cards.title: Translate Nixpkgs into native Jet packages managed only by Hangar
cards.body:
Owner requirement: ingest Nixpkgs through an adapter that translates definitions into the canonical native Jet package/build model. Jetpack owns resolution, builds, installation, updates and removal; Hangar is the only store. No separately installed or bundled Nix package manager, Nix daemon, Nix profile, or Nix store is permitted, including hidden or mounted compatibility stores. Native Jet packages bypass the adapter. Existing Nixpkgs packages use the adapter until converted to full native Jet packages. Out-of-the-box support ships with normal Jet/Jetpack installation. This fixes product ownership, not the adapter implementation; no code implementation is authorized in this stream.

Owner licensing choice: Jet/Jetpack code is MIT. Compatible permissive dependencies may retain their licenses and notices. Managed package payloads may use other licenses and retain their original terms. This is not permission to relicense third-party code. Independently, the Nixpkgs adapter must not depend on Nix implementation executables, libraries, daemons, services or storage.

D-NIX-UPSTREAM1 is superseded unratified. Its old A required an upstream Nix provider; its old B retained a bounded subset. Neither matches the owner’s settled native Nixpkgs-to-Jet-package translation requirement. Do not count this as ratification of either old option. Owner direction and licensing answers are recorded in this card; no replacement choice is needed for that settled boundary.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Ship a Jet-owned Nixpkgs-to-native translator inside Jetpack. Translated and authored packages share one checked package and build model, Hangar is the only store, and there is no Nix executable, library, daemon, profile or store. Owner contract (c1, met): Jet and Jetpack code is MIT; managed packages keep their own licenses.

## Current state
- No translator exists.
- The installed-Nix escape path is still live in Rust (crates/jetpack/src/NixFallbackPolicy.rs:14,158,242) and was carried into the Jet port: Jetpack/Nix/Source/Fallback/FallbackPolicy.jet:7-8 (JETPACK_NIX_FALLBACK_POLICY and _BIN), :139 (`nix build --json`), :176-179 (PATH discovery). This contradicts the card.
- The bounded evaluator is Jetpack/NixEval (#3600).
- The mixed fixture tests/fixtures/jetpack-project/env.jet currently expects native `hello` to realize and `postgres@nixpkgs` to stay an E1272 hole. That is gap evidence, not completion.

## Changes
1. Cutover: delete the installed-Nix fallback from the Jet port and the Rust reference together: Fallback/FallbackPolicy.jet, FallbackImport.jet, FallbackIdentity.jet, the Nix/Tests/Fallback*.jet claims, the env vars, the flags and the callers. Keep no disabled fallback.
2. Translation:
   - Evaluate Nixpkgs sources with Jetpack/NixEval/Source.
   - Translate dependencies, builders, source identities, platform constraints, path and string contexts, and evaluation-triggered builds into native facts in Jetpack/PackageModel/Source/Recipe and Provider plus Jetpack/Provider/Source.
   - Keep upstream provenance so that updates re-translate.
3. Realize and admit only through Jetpack/Store/Source/Hangar:
   - Native builds from translated recipes are the baseline.
   - Build with the #3620 native derivation builder in the sandbox.
   - No /nix/store, mounted store or profile.
   - Any binary reuse separately proves references, integrity, target and license.
4. Preserve:
   - trust, locks, offline mode, precedence and limits;
   - #410's native build-and-boot independence;
   - native packages bypassing the adapter;
   - an ordinary standalone install that needs no Nix;
   - MIT and permissive dependency notices, with no Nix implementation code imported.
5. Unsupported valid packages stay open defects, never silent fallback. Rust crates/jetpack remains reference only.

## Proof
Criterion 11:
1. `JETPACK_WORKER=b19np Tools/agent/jet-env bash Jetpack/Bootstrap/check.sh --tests` -> `JETPACK CHECK OK (check, default run, AOT test)`.
2. The Jet-built jetpack runs a mixed native plus Nixpkgs environment through resolve, build, install, run, update and remove on AOT and default `jet run`, with PATH free of nix. `postgres@nixpkgs` realizes natively instead of raising E1272.

## Batch
batch-jetpack-nix.

## Dependencies
#3600 (evaluator tier proof) and #3620 (native derivation builder).

criteria.text: The settled owner contract is recorded: a Jet-owned translator inside Jetpack, one canonical native package/build model, Hangar only, no Nix implementation dependency, and the selected MIT/permissive project and package-license policy.

cards.title: Complete LSP 3.18 protocol negotiation and lifecycle
cards.body:
## Outcome

Deliver the complete applicable LSP 3.18 protocol contract through the real Jet server, with truthful capabilities and an executable applicability inventory.

## Shared stream contract

This card owns its Outcome, implementation plan, and criteria. The rules below are shared context for the complete idea stream. Sibling cards own the other portions; they are not duplicate acceptance work on this card.

- All current stable LSP 3.18 Jet-applicable capabilities crossed with every applicable Jet construct. Explicit reason for each inapplicable item; no advertised empty/no-op implementations.
- Real end-to-end VS Code, Zed, Neovim acceptance; protocol harness also required. No notebook visual or Canvas-node redesign.

## Origin and authority

Source idea `bhg7rahc`, recorded 2026-09-12T19:16:49.469Z:

Inspect LSP standard to ensure 100% jet support
cards.plan:
**Goal**
The real Jet LSP server implements the complete applicable stable LSP 3.18 protocol and lifecycle contract. It advertises capabilities truthfully, negotiates client support, and ships an executable applicability inventory. Any N/A needs a concrete reason; unknown or unimplemented behavior never counts as inapplicable. Real VS Code, Zed and Neovim acceptance is also required. There is no notebook visual or Canvas-node redesign. The server stays in the Rust CLI host, since LSP is part of the retained host boundary.

**Current state**
- The server is `Source/LSP/Server.rs`. The old path `crates/jet-codegen/src/Source/LSP` is stale. Other LSP modules: `Check.rs`, `Features.rs`, `Completion.rs`, `Position.rs`, `SymbolDB.rs`, `Adapter.rs`, `EnvironmentResources.rs`.
- Dispatch: `Server.rs:354-357` handles `initialize` by calling `configure_workspace_roots` and then `initialize_response(id)`. The response ignores the client capabilities.
- The static capability JSON near :551 carries the MCP-shaped `"protocolVersion": "2025-11-25"` mixed into LSP initialize.
- There is no `positionEncoding` negotiation anywhere (`Position.rs` fixes one encoding).
- Cancellation returns -32800 before and after running (`Server.rs:253-258`).
- `tests/lsp.rs:765` `lsp_initialize_capabilities_have_named_test_coverage` is a source-marker test. The card says to delete it rather than re-pin it.
- #3196 owns overlapping-edit freshness and cancellation release (`tests/lsp.rs:3188`).

**Changes**
1. Add `Tools/lsp/lsp-3.18-inventory.json`, pinned to the official 3.18 spec. It lists every request, notification, capability, option and lifecycle rule, each marked applicable, client-dependent or N/A with a reason and a witness test name. Add `Tools/lsp/check-inventory.mjs` to validate it.
2. `Server.rs`:
   - Parse client capabilities on `initialize`, and advertise only complete handlers.
   - Negotiate `positionEncoding` (utf-16 default, utf-8/utf-32 when offered) through `Position.rs`.
   - Separate the LSP initialize result from MCP initialization data without breaking a distinct MCP consumer.
   - Add dynamic registration where the client supports it, `$/progress` and workDoneProgress, `$/setTrace`/`$/logTrace`, `shutdown`→`exit` ordering (requests after shutdown get InvalidRequest), and correct partial-frame and ContentModified/RequestFailed errors.
3. `tests/lsp.rs`:
   - Delete `lsp_initialize_capabilities_have_named_test_coverage`.
   - Add the `lsp318_*` fixtures: UTF-8/UTF-16 positions over non-BMP text, partial messages, request/notification errors, cancellation races, versioned edits, disconnect, and client-feature negotiation.
4. Update the client-facing 3.17 wording to the exercised 3.18 contract.

**Proof**
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test lsp -- lsp318_` → pass.
- `node Tools/lsp/check-inventory.mjs` → no unknown or unwitnessed row.
- Real-editor acceptance: VS Code, Zed and Neovim session transcripts attached to the card.

**Batch**
batch-host-cli: Source/LSP.

**Dependencies**
#3196 (freshness and cancellation proof, criterion 4).

cards.title: Unify inferred effects, trusted defaults, and restrictive policy
cards.body:
## Current owner direction

This is the existing owner of the effect-policy change, not a new duplicate stream. The owner asked for high-priority delivery during the prep/build interview.

The latest direction changes the default assumed by D-TRUST-LAUNCH1. Preserve that ratified decision as history. Do not implement its old metadata-free prompting rule as the new default.

## Trust prompt rule (owner ruling, 2026-10-01)

The owner rejected the trusted-folder framing and gave this rule in chat (logged on this card 2026-10-01):

- When a program needs trust, Jet asks one question with three answers: Always trust, Once, Cancel.
- Once: run this time only. The next run asks again.
- Always trust: record trust for that target. Later runs never ask again.
- Cancel: do not run.
- A CLI flag that skips the prompt (for example --trusted, or a run-unsafe style flag) answers the prompt as Once. It never records Always.

There is no separate owned-root or trusted-folder concept. Trust comes only from an Always trust answer or from a prompt-skipping flag for that one run. #3705 owns the prompt itself (it absorbed #3419); this card owns the effect model the prompt feeds.

## Requirements stated by the owner

- Always infer and retain effects, including when source omits an effect row. Make the effect facts available for reflection, explanation, and enforcement.
- Do not ask again for a target the user chose Always trust for.
- Provide a deny-by-default restricted mode selected through invocation policy and package/module policy. Enterprise policy can make this the default.
- Positive source effect rows are ceilings. Listing an effect permits it within the source contract but does not prove that the body uses it.
- Authors can explicitly reject effects at package, module, entrypoint, or function scope. Keep positive ceilings and explicit empty ceilings as expert controls.
- In restricted mode, explicit package or function budgets must cover the required effects. Resolve inherited coverage without requiring repeated declarations on every helper.
- Keep implementation source reusable across trust policies. Choosing a policy must not require rewriting function bodies or automatically editing source.
- Dependencies do not inherit trust from the program that uses them.
- Apply one effect model to ordinary execution, shared program preparation, and the AOT build procedure. Keep their effect provenance separate by phase and entrypoint.
- Prep prepares the program for every execution path. For AOT, its results are prepared into the artifact, not rerun as application startup. Build is the AOT procedure for executables, libraries, and linkable objects.

## Model

Keep three facts separate: inferred potential effects, written source ceilings and prohibitions, and approved execution authority (an Always trust record, a Once answer, a prompt-skipping flag, package.jet authority, --allow/--deny, or enterprise policy). A declaration in third-party source never grants itself authority. An outer approved budget can cover unannotated helpers. Inner source can narrow a boundary, not defeat an enclosing mandatory restriction. Enterprise policy is highest.

Always-on compiler tracking is not the same as recording every runtime operation. Static analysis stays conservative for dynamic calls and opaque foreign code: unknown effects are never reported as pure. The owner selected always-available effect provenance and the existing required authorization receipts, with detailed runtime auditing controlled by policy. Enterprise may require that audit; ordinary development does not record every effect occurrence.

No new public spelling is approved by this card. Restricted mode uses the existing --trust/-T axis plus package.jet authority policy; any new syntax needs its own ratification and registry cutover. Ordinary effect trust must not erase independent checks: Secret, FFI, Unsafe, provider consent, environment/package/toolchain trust, and sandbox boundaries stay separate.

## Existing mechanisms

Source inspection, not runtime proof: the Jet homes are Jetpack/PackageModel/Source/Authority/Resolver.jet, Jetpack/PackageModel/Source/Policy/EffectBudget.jet, Jetpack/Foundation/Source/Authority.jet and Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Effects/Checks.jet. The shipped host resolver is crates/jet-foundation/src/Authority.rs plus the Source/CmdCompile.rs launch paths. Reuse these; do not add a second effect system.

Relevant law: D-EFFECT-OMIT1, D-EFFECT-ROW2, D-EFFBUDGET1, D-TEAMPOLICY1, D-TRUST-LAUNCH1 (history), D-SCRIPT-CONFIRM1 (#3705), and D-META-GATE1. Existing source spellings include -[Net]>, -[!Net]>, and -[]>.

## Effect-preserving caching: owner clarification

A cache hit must not suppress an observable effect from a logically invoked operation. A user-written status print remains program behavior. Cache pure computations where valid, but preserve effects and their order at each logical invocation. Do not replace fresh effects with a replay of old console output. Trust selects authority; it does not license an optimizer to remove effects.

Launching an already-prepared AOT artifact does not invoke prep. Shared preparation and compiler-hook details are owned by #3509.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Build one effect-policy model:
- Effects are always inferred and explainable.
- Trust comes from the owner's prompt rule: one prompt (Always trust / Once / Cancel); Once re-prompts next run; Always never prompts again for that target; a prompt-skipping CLI flag counts as Once.
- A deny-by-default restricted mode is selected by invocation or package/enterprise policy.
- Positive rows are ceilings and negative rows are enforced prohibitions.
- The same law applies to run, dev, test, prep and AOT build, with separate provenance for each phase.

## Current state
- Owner ruling 2026-10-01 settles trust establishment (logged on this card). The owned-root ballot in the old plan is withdrawn; no owner gate remains.
- #3705 implements the prompt UI (with #3419's rows). Its own rows still describe the older default-yes confirm; reconcile them with the three-answer rule when that card is worked.

Host mirror: crates/jet-foundation/src/Authority.rs plus Source/CmdCompile.rs launch paths. #3607 ports the PackageModel authority.

## Changes
1. JetSema Effects/Checks.jet: always infer and keep effects, including transitive, generated, callback and opaque calls. Positive rows are checked ceilings; negative or empty rows are prohibitions enforced through reachable calls.
2. PackageModel Resolver.jet / EffectBudget.jet: one resolver. Authority sources, in order: enterprise policy, package.jet authority and --allow/--deny, the Always trust record, a Once answer or prompt-skipping flag (this run only). Enclosing budgets cover inferred helpers. Dependencies never inherit the caller's trust. Package, environment and toolchain authenticity stay separate.
3. Trust store: Always trust writes one record per target; Once and prompt-skipping flags write nothing. Cancel runs nothing and writes nothing.
4. Apply the resolved policy before effects on every run/dev/test/prep/build path. Mirror into Authority.rs and the Source/ launch paths in the same batch (Rust/Jet parity). Prep results persist into AOT artifacts; cache reuse and child execution keep receipts.
5. Migrate the CLI, diagnostics (E1803 family), reflection, examples and tests in one cutover. Coordinate the prompt surface with #3705 and prep capabilities with #3509.

## Proof
Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test authority and --test effects pass, including new cases once_answer_reprompts_next_run, always_trust_never_prompts_again, skip_prompt_flag_counts_as_once, restricted_mode_refuses_uncovered_inferred_effect, negative_ceiling_blocks_transitive_callback and dependency_does_not_inherit_caller_trust; tests/ui E1803 snapshots re-blessed through jet test Compiler --profile ui.

## Batch
batch-jetc-sema: effect inference and ceilings live in JetSema. The resolver and host mirror land in the same build.

## Dependencies
None open. #3705 (prompt UI) and #3509 (prep capabilities) are coordinated, not blocking.

cards.title: Consolidate project-generated files under one selected root
cards.body:
## Outcome

Stop scattering generated files and directories beside input files. The owner prefers one top-level .jet directory that includes build outputs. D-GENERATED-STORAGE2 now recommends the expanded local-root option B; the owner has not ratified a choice. Preserve saved data, required evidence, and safe project/target identity.

## Shared stream contract

This card owns its Outcome, implementation plan, and criteria. The rules below are shared context for the complete idea stream. Sibling cards own the other portions; they are not duplicate acceptance work on this card.

- D-GENERATED-STORAGE2 owns the unresolved storage location. Its revised recommendation puts all default project-generated files under one top-level .jet root, including build outputs. Preserve protected project data and separate project/target identities. Earlier shared-cache planning text is not approval.
- One authored source file is repository-wide default for suitable examples/scaffolds/dogfood/benchmarks. Put necessary metadata/policy in package {}; generated reproducibility locks allowed. Real multi-file apps stay multi-file.
- Gauntlet workflow matched per cell, standalone default; real package cells put all peers in comparable package workflows. No Jet-only preparation.
- Expose first-use setup, cold/warm build, execution and source-to-result totals separately, retaining per-metric losses. Never average away losses or rewrite historical receipts.
- Current internal operational caches .jet may contain saved/audit/sensitive state: classify before migration, preserve protected roots and links, do not blanket-delete. Existing .jet trees outside owned disposable data are not authorized collateral deletion.

## Origin and authority

Source idea `bsl93wcp`, recorded 2026-09-14T18:24:32.543Z:

Consider cleanup for .jet/ dirs EVERYWHERE in the project. So messy, especially compared to all the other types. We also need to prefer single file jet, not separate package files. We want to evaluate parity between jet and other languages in gauntlet, so having packages estabilished for jet but not other languages is not a direct or fair comparison, pick one.

## Owner question and revised proposal

Question qt6cidsa rejects the earlier alternatives and asks for peer-language evidence. The revised ballot includes official Cargo, Dart, Gradle, and .NET comparisons. Option B now includes build outputs and all other default project-generated files, not merely .jet/cache/. The decision remains open; no file migration is authorized by this answer.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Every default project-generated file lives under one top-level `.jet` root (D-GENERATED-STORAGE2=B, ratified). Project and target identities never collide or escape, and protected saved/audit data survives the migration. Criteria 1 and 3 are verified. Criteria 2, 4 and 5 remain open.

**Current state**
- The build root is `.jet/build`:
  - `Source/CmdCompile.rs:9927` `build_output_root`.
  - `:9931` `bin_path` = `.jet/build/<stem(file)>`.
  - `:9942` `build_artifact_path` uses the bare target name.
  - `:9961` test binaries.
  - `:5314` writes `.gitignore` (`.jet/build/`, `.jet/lock`, `.jet/cache/`).
  - Dependencies are at `Source/Fetch.rs:791,916,1228` (`.jet/build/deps/<dep>`), and exec at `Source/CmdExec.rs:161-165`.
  - No `.jet-build` reference remains in `Source/`.
- Open defects from the 2026-09-23 independent review:
  - Final artifacts collide across entries, profiles, toolchains and targets, because `bin_path` keys on the stem only.
  - Locked preflight compares planned generated modules against all same-member provenance.
  - Action-generated sources get no peer-output overlays.
  - An equal-root package can verify or replace nested-member lock rows as if its scope were global (E3512 shared `.jet/lock` provenance).
  - The first CLI regression used retired `--allow-exec/--allow-fs` flags and tested nothing.
- Other owners: `Source/ReceiptStore.rs` (`.jet/receipts`, canonical target identity), `Source/RecordIndex.rs` (`.jet/records`), `Source/ProveReplay.rs` (`.jet/records/saved/<id>`), `Source/ProductionReceipt.rs` (`.jet/reports`), `Source/RunCache.rs` (the external `~/.cache/jet/run` stays global), and the `Jetpack/Store` port.

**Changes**
1. Jet side: `Jetpack/Store` and `Jetpack/CLI` must use the same `.jet/build/deps` and lock layout as `Source/Fetch.rs`. Mirror any path helper in Jet, and add no second layout.
2. `Source/CmdCompile.rs`: key artifact paths by the ballot's identity: entry (project-relative path for equal basenames), profile, target and toolchain. The default host dev build keeps its current `.jet/build/<name>`, and non-default identities get a distinct subpath. Use one helper for build, test, run and doctest.
3. Lock provenance: scope `.jet/lock` rows per workspace member and limit preflight to the same member (the ReceiptStore/Fetch lock readers).
4. Action outputs: overlay peer outputs for action-generated sources.
5. Cleanup: `jet clean` removes only classified disposable subtrees (`build`, `cache`) and never `records/saved`, `receipts` or `reports`. Update ignore rules together.
6. New `tests/generated_storage_root.rs` using the current authority flags.

**Proof**
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test generated_storage_root` → all cases pass.
- `jet test Compiler --profile cases build_entry/ --test package_outputs --test comptime_cli_parity` → still green (default `.jet/build/main` layout unchanged).
- A grep for `.jet-build` and a bare `build/` default writer in Source/ and Jetpack/ → no hits.

**Batch**
batch-host-cli: this is Source/ CLI path/lock/cleanup code, plus the Jetpack store path mirror.

**Dependencies**
None open. #3415 (history FIFO) consumes this root but does not block it.

cards.title: Context: visibility, typed keys, task/FFI edges on top of D-CTX1
cards.body:
Frozen by owner (2026-09-16): "It's not clear to me exactly what we gain from introducing context... put this as a card in the frozen section so we can discuss it at a later time."

## What already exists (facts)
- D-CTX1 Smart Context (ratified 2026-06-22): `#Context(allocator: arena) { … }` swaps an ambient field for a block's lexical+dynamic extent and restores it on exit (return, break, `?`, panic). An explicit allocator argument at a call site beats the ambient. `examples/features/effects/smart_context.jet`.
- D-DEADLINE1 (ratified 2026-06-28): `#Context(deadline: <Int epoch_ms>) { … }`; wait/IO points observe the budget; `examples/features/concurrency/deadline_context.jet` shows a spawned `task` inheriting it.
- Effect rows are inferred; a written row is a ceiling (D-EFF2 flow-through).

## Rejected in the interview
- `+Frame` marker (name and glyph both rejected by owner).
- `with Context{…} { … }` block (no precedent; "weird ctor+block"). The marker block already exists as D-CTX1.
- Fully hidden Odin/Jai `*Context` last argument with TLS binding (web/enterprise foreclosure: TLS bleed across pooled requests, nothing after `await`, vanishes at C/WASM edges).
- Context as an effect that grants permission. Context carries values, never permissions: `context.allocator.alloc` still needs `Mem`.

## Leaned by owner in Round 3 (not ratified; discussion input)
- User fields as typed keys: any package declares `#ContextKey struct RequestId { value: String }`; bind `#Context(RequestId{value: r.id}) { … }`; read `context.get<RequestId>()`. Core fields keep the D-CTX1 named spelling (`allocator:`, `deadline:`).
- Edges: a task captures the ambient at spawn (snapshot, never the OS thread); a foreign-thread entry (GLFW/sqlite callback) sees the program root context; every field has a root default so nothing is ever nil.

## The open fork (visibility)
1. Row entry for direct reads: the word `context` in a body adds `Context` to the inferred row; ceilings must list it; a function without `Context` calling one that has it, outside any `#Context` block, is a compile error (same grant machinery as D-SCAP1 `#Abilities(…) { }`). Runtime knobs (allocator, deadline) stay quiet because `Mem`/`Time` already disclose them. Web and enterprise get visible dependence and package `deny: [Context]`; games and libraries pay nothing.
2. Hidden: D-CTX1 as written; typed keys readable anywhere; forgetting to bind is silent-wrong (root default).
3. Per-key row `-[Context<RequestId>]>`: most precise; new type-argument form in the row.

## Five rooms to re-run when discussed
File loader (which allocator), C callback from a foreign thread, tests (Tracking allocator, reset), one HTTP request (request id, deadline, arena freed at end), game tick (bump reset; `#Hot` lint on `context.allocator` in hot bodies).

## Owner question to answer first
What does a program gain over explicit parameters plus D-CTX1 as it stands? Candidate answer to test: request-scoped values (request id, tenant, trace span) carried through library code that cannot take them as parameters, with a compiler check that the binding exists.

cards.title: Const generics: a compile-time Int as a type parameter
cards.body:
Owner gate from the Jai-vs-Jet interview (comptime ladder rung R4, owner chose "R0-R4 now"). Today a known constant can size an array (`[U8#64]`, `[Float#(@lanes * 2)]`) but a number cannot be a type parameter, so `Packet<64>` and a generic SOA count cannot be written; S26 says comptime does not parameterize a type. The proposal is a narrow amendment: a compile-time `Int` may parameterize an existing type constructor, spelled `Packet: struct<comptime N: Int> { data: [U8#N] }` (D-COMPTIME-WORD1=A), used as `Packet<64>` or `Packet<lanes>`. Monomorphized like `<T>`. Not types-as-values: no use-site type factories, no `SOA(T, n)` in type position, no dispatch on comptime results. `Meta.Const` is named alongside (see D-META-GATE1).

## Exit criteria (after ratification)
1. Parser and sema accept `<comptime N: Int>` declarations and literal / comptime-constant arguments; a runtime value in that slot is a teaching diagnostic.
2. Example: firmware-style `Packet<N>` with `[U8#N]` field runs on O0, O1 and O2 (I9).
3. Spec entry amends S26 narrowly and cites D-META-CONST1.

## Owner scope extension — 2026-09-21

## Outcome

Finish D-CONSTGEN1 without treating const generics as first-class type factories. Implement compile-time Int parameters, substitution, instance identity, constraints and target layout through the existing generic mechanism. Reconcile the latest metadata naming direction with immutable decision history through the contract card; ordinary prepared values do not require repeated @ references outside declared parameter syntax.

## Owned paths and integration

- crates/jet-foundation/src/AST
- crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Types.rs
- crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Bundle/GenericModules
- crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR
- tests/generics.rs

One implementer owns this coherent patch. Main owns integration and closure. Serialize shared AST, Reflect.rs, Driver and pipeline edits with their other owners; do not duplicate those models.

## Scope limits

This is planned implementation, not completed behavior. Standard mode retains level 5; privileged operations require the owner's explicit opt-in contract. No new external dependency, unsafe exception, alternate parser, compatibility alias, or tier deferral is approved. Preserve ratified history and use the latest owner direction for current behavior.

## Proof

Add the `Packet: struct<comptime N: Int>` witness with literal and prepared arguments, distinct sizes and nested use. Exercise O0, O1 and O2. Reject runtime arguments, illegal array sizes, overflow and conflicting instance identities with source snapshots. Inspect the instantiated type metadata from the same program.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Finish D-CONSTGEN1, with the spelling now fixed by D-CONSTGEN2=A: a compile-time `Int` may be a type parameter of an existing type constructor. The declaration is `Packet: struct<comptime N: Int> { data: [U8#N] }` (D-DECL-COLON1=A, D-COMPTIME-WORD1=A), and uses write the plain value, as in `Packet<64>` or `Packet<lanes>` after `lanes: comptime { 64 }`. It is monomorphized like `<T>`.

This is not types-as-values: no use-site type factories, no `SOA(T, n)` in type position, and no dispatch on comptime results. It is comptime ladder rung R4; the owner chose "R0-R4 now".

## Current state
- The grammar and AST have shipped (#3662, logged 2026-09-28 in `Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:7455`; syntax row at `:34`).
  - Jet: `TypeParam.prep: PrepParam?` in `Compiler/JetAst/Source/AST/Items.jet:447-464`, with the parser at `Compiler/JetParser/Source/Parser/Items.jet:531`.
  - Rust: `crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Types.rs:473`.
  - This supersedes the card's older `<@N: Int>` spelling.
- Every `prep` parameter is rejected with E0390 until this card lands:
  - Jet sema: `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Registration/Items.jet:438-441`;
  - Rust sema: `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Casing.rs:120-128`;
  - UI fixture: `tests/ui/prep_number_param_unsupported.jet`.
- There is no substitution, instance identity or layout for number parameters in `Compiler/JetSema` or `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/TypeInstances.jet`.
- Criteria 1-4 and 9-12 (Syntax entry, log entry, grammars, snapshots) are met for the declaration grammar by #3662. Only the E0390 snapshot changes here.

## Changes
1. JetSema (`Registration/Items.jet` plus generic substitution):
   - Replace the E0390 rejection with number-parameter binding. `N` is in scope as a value inside the declaration, including array sizes such as `[U8#N]`.
   - A use-site argument must be an Int literal or a comptime constant. A runtime value in that slot gets a new registered diagnostic with a UI snapshot.
   - Instance identity includes the value, so `Packet<64>` and `Packet<32>` are different types.
2. JetCodegen (`TypeInstances.jet`, `Types.jet`): monomorphize and lay out each instance, with deterministic naming that includes the number.
3. Mirror the change in the shipped Rust sema, TIR and MIR so the goldens run on the shipped binary. Delete the E0390 path in both compilers and retire the row, or keep E0390 only for a non-Int number type.
4. Add `Examples/features/generics/const_packet.jet`: a firmware-style `Packet: struct<comptime N: Int>` with literal and comptime arguments, two distinct sizes and a nested use, printing sizes and bytes.
5. Update `Docs/spec/reference/metaprogramming.md`: S26 is amended narrowly, citing D-CONSTGEN1 and D-CONSTGEN2.

## Proof
- `jet test Compiler --profile golden generics/const_packet`: identical on O0, O1 and O2.
- `jet test Compiler --profile ui prep_number_param`: the old E0390 fixture is replaced by a runtime-argument rejection fixture.
- `jet test Compiler --profile cases generics/`: passes.

## Batch
batch-jetc-sema: substitution and identity are the core. Codegen layout lands in the same build.

## Dependencies
None real. #3520's naming reconciliation was settled by D-CONSTGEN2=A (#3662 shipped).

cards.title: Complete reflection and metaprogramming public contract
cards.body:
## Outcome

Define one complete, versioned public model for metadata, preparation, generated code, compiler sessions and advanced operations. Preserve owner-selected callable metadata roots, ordinary names for prepared values, explicit generation, explicit Runtime modes and function/method/block sites. Preserve ratified Generated values and const-generic semantics except where the latest owner instruction explicitly amends them. Publish exact field/operation catalogs through executable registries, not duplicated prose lists. Record API decisions before implementation; this card owns contracts, not compiler delivery.

## Owned paths and integration

- crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs
- crates/jet-foundation/src/AST
- crates/jet-foundation/src/Registry.rs
- crates/jet-foundation/src/Collections.rs
- docs/spec/reference/metaprogramming.md
- docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md

One implementer owns this coherent patch. Main owns integration and closure. Serialize shared AST, Reflect.rs, Driver and pipeline edits with their other owners; do not duplicate those models.

## Scope limits

This is planned implementation, not completed behavior. Standard mode retains level 5; privileged operations require the owner's explicit opt-in contract. No new external dependency, unsafe exception, alternate parser, compatibility alias, or tier deferral is approved. Preserve ratified history and use the latest owner direction for current behavior.

## Proof

Read every approved decision and compare its chosen interface with the executable registry schema planned by the consumer cards. Require every public fact, operation, phase and failure to have a delivery owner and a behavioral witness; reject holes described as future work.

## Deduplication

#3509 owns this campaign. Existing owners #3147, #3175, #3181, #3199, #3201, #3202 and #3505–#3508 are reused, not replaced. #3418, #3419, #3421 and #3042 remain separate prerequisite owners. Shared specification references alone do not make these distinct implementation outcomes duplicates.

## Complete metadata family ownership

### Type universe and canonical identity

Owners: #3147.

Every AST type form, generic application, recursive reference, alias, trait object, tagged/union, dimensional numeric and fixed-size type.

### Fields, enum cases and access

Owners: #3147, #3524.

Ordered fields, typed defaults, offsets, visibility, captures, active cases and lawful copy/access refusal.

### Callable contracts

Owners: #3522, #3541.

Functions, methods, closures, labels, default expressions, zones, effects, captures, overload and specialization identity.

### Program and typed code

Owners: #3523, #3199.

Definitions, references, selected calls, typed expressions/bodies, imports, graph edges and complete source-version identity.

### Local and memory facts

Owners: #3175, #3523.

Before/after expression state, shadowing, joins, initialization, ownership, moves, views, lifetime, cleanup and typestate.

### Source and provenance

Owners: #3523, #3202, #3533.

Exact source, comments, documentation, source/expanded attributes, lexical/caller origins and generated expansion stacks.

### Package, settings and build

Owners: #3523, #3540, #3527.

Resolved dependencies, package identity, profiles, typed settings, contributions, target/backend and build inputs/outputs.

### Runtime retention and erased values

Owners: #3524, #3532.

Demand-driven per-type and whole-table modes, actual value identity, retained completeness and lawful dynamic access.

### Authority, phases and query failures

Owners: #3520, #3521, #3526.

Explicit checked phase, allowed target scope, unavailable/denied/invalid/stale/truncated outcomes; checked empty is distinct.

### Transformations and tooling

Owners: #3530, #3529, #3533.

Typed immutable snapshots, parsed code, changed contracts, complete recheck receipts, navigation, diagnostics and inspect/explain output.

Completeness is checked against the executable schema, the compiler Type algebra and the semantic-index fact registry. This family list is a planning boundary, not a substitute for per-field behavioral coverage. Do not bless unavailable facts as complete merely because a query returns an error.

Current application amendment (2026-10-07, #27 clarified by #29/#31; Sol writes / Opus reviews #28):

Render full A clause map into every named spec paragraph with amendment links; distinguish standard no rewriting from approved advanced checked changes without deleting universal token/tree/attribute/user-macro/custom-syntax/message-loop/mutable-node/forged-fact bans; keep CONTROL2/OPTIN2 approvals, changed-provider refusal/revocation/handles/dependency grants/non-equivalence; standard type recipes/const generics retained; Hook-Stages text aligns; no new capability/API introduced and unbuilt advanced behavior not falsely marked delivered.
Paths: NO NEW API/OPERATION. Preserve existing compiler.advanced registry/opt-in implementation scope; D-HOOK-STAGES1 change-set gates align; advanced compiler delivery stays existing #3520 consumers
Registry/spec/UI/goldens: Legacy Syntax.rs compiler.advanced rows KEEP, Jet counterpart decision provenance adds D-META-RECONCILE1=A. No new syntax/capability names (NOT Meta.Rewrite/Meta.Expand/Meta.Types); D-GENERIC-TYPEFN1 recipes/const generics remain standard; Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md S26, D-FRONTENDAPI1/D-METAMUTATE1, D-METADEPTH1/2, D-META-GATE1 clause-by-clause amendment links; Docs/spec/reference/metaprogramming.md design boundary; keep universal bans in standard AND advanced; Docs-only reconciliation needs no new diagnostic/snapshot today; existing advanced delivery requires missing root/approval/changed provider/undeclared target/revocation fail before execution fixtures; Update metaprogramming examples to checked atomic ChangeSet with approved root/provider/DeclarationHandles/exact dependency grants; do not claim unbuilt tracing transforms executed; universal no-macro/mutable-node facts remain

cards.plan:
## Goal
One complete, versioned public model for metadata, preparation, generated code, compiler sessions and advanced operations. Its exact field and operation catalogs are published as executable registries in the Jet compiler, not as duplicated prose. This card owns contracts, not compiler delivery.

## Current state
- All four ballots (D-PREP-SURFACE2, D-META-REFLECT2, D-META-PUBLISH2, D-META-CONTROL2) are ratified A, so no decision blocker remains.
- Criteria 6-8 are met: the Syntax.rs entry, the syntax-decisions.md log and regenerated `jet devtools grammars`. Criterion 9 (re-bless snapshots) is open.
- The 2026-09-24 work landed in archived crates/jet-semindex (typed callable facts, schema v20; `callable_signature_facts_keep_typed_and_unavailable_states` passed). tests/semindex.rs:363 pins SCHEMA_VERSION 20.
- Owned paths retarget from crates/jet-foundation/src/{Syntax.rs, AST, Registry.rs, Collections.rs} to Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry (CoreCalls.jet, CoreCallRows.jet, CoreModules.jet, DiagnosticRows.jet), Compiler/JetAst/Source/AST (Comptime.jet, Expressions.jet, Items.jet) and Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet. Docs: Docs/spec/reference/metaprogramming.md and Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md (the old docs/ path is stale).
- Metadata families and owners: type universe (#3147); fields and enum cases (#3147, #3524); callable contracts (#3522, #3541); plus the remaining families listed in the card body.

## Changes
1. Registry: add Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/Metaprogramming.jet (listed in Compiler/Bootstrap/sources.list), with one row per public fact, operation, phase and failure: name, family, availability phase, result/error type, owner card and witness name. Include D-META-REFLECT2's closed result and error types, complete typed field schema, runtime value/table roots and retention operations exactly. Extend the string-only CallableSignatureFact fields from their checker producers, and do not describe them as already complete.
2. AST: Compiler/JetAst/Source/AST/Comptime.jet carries the ratified prep and generation shapes. No discarded spelling survives as a second interface.
3. Docs: metaprogramming.md cites the registry, not a copy of it. Record that default mode stops at level 5 and that opt-in never grants host permissions or unchecked facts. Phase availability, unavailable facts, identity, visibility, receipts and I9 meaning are explicit.
4. Map all forty captured Jai capability families to a contract, owner and proof. Unknown peer details stay blockers.
5. Re-bless the affected snapshots (criterion 9).

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` exits 0.
- A registry completeness check, `rg -c "owner:" Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/Metaprogramming.jet`, equals the row count, and every owner card exists in Tower.
- `jet test Compiler --profile ui meta_` passes.
- `jet test Compiler --profile cases semindex/semindex_schema_version` passes.

## Batch
batch-jetc-front: the registries and AST shapes are front-end foundation data, checked in one compiler check.

## Dependencies
None open. All four ballots are ratified.

cards.body:
## Outcome

Implement the chosen package request, privileged compiler module and explicit provider registration. Standard mode remains level 5. Reuse the existing authority/trust resolver; root ownership, dependency identity, enterprise denial and source scope remain distinct. Freeze effective mode/authority before metaprogram execution. Record mode in toolchain/package/cache/artifact identity. Do not expose raw private Rust stores or authorize mutation merely by import.

## Owned paths and integration

- crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Package
- crates/jet-foundation/src/Policy.rs
- crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/core_call.rs
- crates/jet-driver/src/Driver/mod.rs
- Source/main.rs
- crates/jetpack/src

One implementer owns this coherent patch. Main owns integration and closure. Serialize shared AST, Reflect.rs, Driver and pipeline edits with their other owners; do not duplicate those models.

## Scope limits

This is planned implementation, not completed behavior. Standard mode retains level 5; privileged operations require the owner's explicit opt-in contract. No new external dependency, unsafe exception, alternate parser, compatibility alias, or tier deferral is approved. Preserve ratified history and use the latest owner direction for current behavior.

## Proof

Build the same hook fixture with no opt-in, import only, manifest only, complete approved opt-in, dependency-only request, restricted enterprise policy and no-TTY unknown-root execution. Assert only the authorized registration runs. Attempt self-enablement through settings, manifest writes, generated headers, cache reuse and subprocesses; every bypass must fail without unauthorized effects.

## Deduplication

#3509 owns this campaign. Existing owners #3147, #3175, #3181, #3199, #3201, #3202 and #3505–#3508 are reused, not replaced. #3418, #3419, #3421 and #3042 remain separate prerequisite owners. Shared specification references alone do not make these distinct implementation outcomes duplicates.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement the ratified package opt-in for above-level-five metaprogramming (D-META-OPTIN2=A: a checked package opt-in suffices), the privileged compiler module and explicit provider registration. Standard mode stays at level 5. The effective mode is frozen before any metaprogram runs and recorded in toolchain, package, cache and artifact identity. Import alone authorizes nothing.

## Current state
- D-META-OPTIN2 is ratified A (2026-09-21, "all decisions ratified").
- The owned paths are archived: crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Package, crates/jet-foundation/src/Policy.rs, crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/core_call.rs, crates/jet-driver/src/Driver/mod.rs and crates/jetpack/src. Source/main.rs is the retained host.
- Jet homes: Jetpack/PackageModel/Source/Manifest, Authority/Resolver.jet, Policy and Lock; Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Pipeline.jet and Identity.jet; Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls (CompilerServices.jet, Core.jet).
- Ballot text: registration accepts compiler-issued declaration identities, not display strings. A dependency rewrite needs an approved invocation-root `metaprogramming_targets` entry that matches package identity, the complete source digest and the exact declarations, and any change in grant or source invalidates the approval.

## Changes
1. Jetpack/PackageModel/Source/Manifest: parse the ratified opt-in field. Authority/Resolver.jet resolves effective mode: root ownership, dependency identity, enterprise denial and source scope stay distinct, a dependency can never widen consumer mode, and root and mandatory external denials win.
2. JetDriver Pipeline.jet: freeze `JetDriverMetaMode` before any prep or hook execution. Identity.jet folds it into cache and artifact identity, and Jetpack Lock records it.
3. JetSema Calls/CompilerServices.jet: every above-level-five entry point checks the frozen mode and is refused in standard mode with a registered diagnostic. Hook registration takes compiler-issued declaration identities.
4. Source/main.rs only forwards the mode flag.
5. Host IO, credentials, provider consent and audited Unsafe stay independent of this opt-in.
6. Criteria 7-10: add a syntax-decisions.md log entry, regenerate `jet devtools grammars`, and re-bless the snapshots. The Syntax.rs row goes in the shipped binary's syntax table.

## Proof
- tests/ui/meta_optin_{none,import_only,manifest_only,dependency_only,enterprise_denied,no_tty,self_enable_*}.jet plus one approved fixture: `jet test Compiler --profile ui meta_optin_`.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Jetpack/Bootstrap/check.sh --area PackageModel` exits 0.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` exits 0.

## Batch
batch-jetc-driver: mode freezing and identity are driver-owned, with the manifest and resolver in the same build.

## Dependencies
#3520 (contract) and #3418 (unified effects and restrictive policy, which the resolver reuses).

criteria.text: A metaprogram action above marker expansion (adding declarations outside a marker, rewriting a body, making a type from text) needs a `Compiler` value, and each action checks every applicable `Meta` case (`Generate`, `Include`, `Rewrite`, `Types`, `Raw`) like any effect: denied by written code, otherwise allowed. Without a `Compiler` value the action is refused with a registered diagnostic.

Only the root package's own `build.jet` source can call `b.compiler(output)`; the check uses loader/lock identity, not a caller-supplied name, and a forwarded `Build` cannot get around it. A dependency cannot make or widen a `Compiler` value, and root and organization denials of `Meta` cases win over any grant.

cards.title: Use ordinary constructor defaults in typed package settings
cards.body:
## Outcome

After the settings ballot, migrate declarations from key: Type = value to key: Type{value} if selected. Reuse canonical Jet token/literal/default parsing at a dependency-safe seam; remove the ad-hoc equals split and quote/depth scanners where they misread legal literal payloads. Keep declarations package-only, preserve current scalar/fieldless-enum domain, and leave profile key:value and CLI --set key=value overrides unchanged. Update every current producer/consumer/diagnostic/example; preserve historical ballots and audits.

## Owned paths and integration

- crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Package/mod.rs
- crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Package/Blocks.rs
- crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Items/functions_params.rs
- crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Items/type_methods_fields.rs
- crates/jet-driver/src/Driver/mod.rs
- examples/features/packages/typed_settings
- tests/package_outputs.rs
- editors

One implementer owns this coherent patch. Main owns integration and closure. Serialize shared AST, Reflect.rs, Driver and pipeline edits with their other owners; do not duplicate those models.

## Scope limits

This is planned implementation, not completed behavior. Standard mode retains level 5; privileged operations require the owner's explicit opt-in contract. No new external dependency, unsafe exception, alternate parser, compatibility alias, or tier deferral is approved. Preserve ratified history and use the latest owner direction for current behavior.

## Proof

Extend typed_settings_preserves_tier_parity_and_cli_override and package parser/formatter tests. Cover Bool, signed Int, Char braces/quotes, strings containing commas/equals/comment text, canonical raw/triple literals and fieldless enum values. Reject wrong type, empty/multiple/defaultless forms, aggregates, effectful constructors, old declaration spelling and undeclared profile/CLI keys. Require unchanged effective-value provenance and cold/warm runtime results.

## Deduplication

#3509 owns this campaign. Existing owners #3147, #3175, #3181, #3199, #3201, #3202 and #3505–#3508 are reused, not replaced. #3418, #3419, #3421 and #3042 remain separate prerequisite owners. Shared specification references alone do not make these distinct implementation outcomes duplicates.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Land D-SETTINGS-CTOR2=A (ratified 2026-09-21): package settings declare `name: Type{default}` using Jet's ordinary typed-default form; the old `name: Type = default` is rejected with a registered fix. Profile `settings: { key: value }` and CLI `--set key=value` do not change.

## Current state
- Examples still use the equals form: `Examples/features/packages/typed_settings/package.jet:5-6` (`tls: Bool = true`, `api_base: String = "…"`), `Examples/features/packages/build_contribution/package.jet:5` (`cache_slots: Int = 1`).
- Jet parser: `Jetpack/PackageModel/Source/Manifest/PackageParse.jet:455-469` `pkg_parse_settings` splits on the first `=` (`split_once("=")`), so a `=` or `,` inside a String default is misread. `SettingDecl{ty, default}` is `Manifest/PackageFacts.jet:398-402`.
- Fix text naming the old form: `Manifest/Blocks/BuildProfiles.jet:260` ("declare a typed `settings: {{ key: Type = default }}`").
- Shipped host parser (still what `jet run` uses until the Jetpack cutover): `crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Package/mod.rs:3701-3708` `parse_settings`, same `split_once('=')`.
- PackageModel may use the Compiler front end (`Jetpack/Bootstrap/areas.list:11,13`), so `lex_config` (`Compiler/JetLexer/Source/Lexer/Terminators.jet:554`) is reachable; no second literal scanner is needed.

## Changes
1. `PackageParse.jet` `pkg_parse_settings`: tokenize each entry value with `lex_config`; accept exactly `TypeName { literal }` where the literal is one Bool/Int (signed)/Char/String (incl. raw/triple) token or a fieldless enum case; keep the existing Tier-0 domain check. Delete the `split_once("=")` path and any quote/depth scanning it used. Reject: missing default, empty or multiple payloads, aggregates, constructor calls, wrong literal kind.
2. Old spelling: new `PackageParseError.RetiredSettingDefault(key, ty, value)` mapped in `Manifest.jet` `pkg_manifest_parse_diagnostic` to E1206 with fix text `write `{key}: {ty}{{{value}}}``.
3. `BuildProfiles.jet:260`: fix text says `settings: {{ key: Type{{default}} }}`.
4. Host mirror (required so the shipped binary proves it): `crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Package/mod.rs` `parse_settings` gets the same grammar, reusing `jet_lexer` tokens, with the same E1206 text.
5. Migrate both example `package.jet` files, the syntax registry (`Compiler/JetFoundation/Data/Syntax`) and `Jetpack/Foundation/Source/Syntax.jet` entries, `Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md` log entry, regenerate grammars with `jet devtools grammars`, and re-bless the affected snapshots, all in one change. Historical ballots stay unchanged.

## Proof
- `JETPACK_WORKER=settings Tools/agent/jet-env bash Jetpack/Bootstrap/check.sh --area PackageModel --deps-from-head --tests` → `JETPACK CHECK OK (check, default run, AOT test)`; new PackageFacts claims: Bool/Int(-1)/Char/String containing `,` `=` `//`, fieldless enum; rejections (old form → E1206 fix text, `Bool{}`, `Int{1, 2}`, `Bool{1}`).
- `jet test Compiler --profile cases package_outputs/typed_settings_preserves_tier_parity_and_cli_override computed_build_contribution_records_lock_and_matches_explain_golden` → pass (defaults, profile override, `--set tls=false`, provenance unchanged).
- `jet test Compiler --profile golden packages/typed_settings` → pass.

## Batch
batch-jetpack-pkgmodel: the parser home is Jetpack/PackageModel; the host mirror rides the same post-build retest.

## Dependencies
None open. D-SETTINGS-CTOR2 is ratified (A).

criteria.text: The chosen declaration form has one parser/formatter meaning shared with ordinary Jet defaults, not a second hand-written constructor language.
If constructor form wins, tls: Bool{true} and api_base: String{"https://api.example.com"} work and old equals declarations are not Jet syntax and get no migration diagnostic (owner order).

cards.title: CoreLib foundations: complete Jet ownership
cards.body: Complete every foundational declaration: root carriers, text, collections, math, units, time, encoding, regex, args, files/path, IO/memory, and portable crypto. Migrate callers and generated projections. Rust may remain only as typed provider leaves.
cards.plan:
**Goal.** This is the foundations wave of #3690 (W1 plus part of W2). Each foundational Core member (text, collections, math, units, time, encoding, regex, args, files/path, io/mem, portable crypto) gets exactly one meaning: its Jet body in Core/*.jet, or a declared typed provider leaf. No Rust dispatcher row, JIT shim or interpreter route may duplicate it.

**Current state.**
- `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core.jet` (2412 lines) holds 1,814 `dispatcher_row`s. 693 are in foundation modules, and 657 of those name members the module's `source_module … owns {…}` line already gives to Jet. Those are duplicate meanings and an I9 risk.

| Module | Rows | Jet-owned |
|---|---|---|
| math | 220 | 219 |
| text | 137 | 137 |
| encoding | 124 | 123 |
| collections | 52 | 52 |
| time | 48 | 39 |
| files | 45 | 38 |
| crypto | 42 | 25 |
| regex | 20 | 19 |
| args | 3 | 3 |
| mem | 2 | 2 |

- The remaining 36 unowned rows (crypto 17, time 9, files 7, math/encoding/regex 1 each) need either a Jet body or a leaf declaration.
- The self-hosted routing mirror is `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/{CoreCallRows,CoreCalls,CoreHostSignatures}.jet`, `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/HandleMethods.jet` and `Compiler/JetEval/Source/Routes/`.
- From merged #3517: the text/file source attempts were reverted on 2026-09-21 because the compiler rejected private source paths. `Core/text/string.jet` is now a private source part (`crates/jet-foundation/src/CoreSourceParts.rs:30`).
- c4 is met, but #3584 (building) now requires ALL_CAPS module constants. c7 tracks that.

**Changes (one module per patch, in dependency order).**
1. **F1 route cut, per module:** delete the Jet-owned `dispatcher_row`/`ambient_route` lines in Core.jet. Regenerate with `node Tools/agent/gen-core-tables.mjs --write`, which rewrites `CoreModuleExports.rs` and `CoreCallRows.jet`. Remove the now-dead `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/**` functions and JIT shims. Remove matching routes in `HandleMethods.jet`/`JetEval/Source/Routes`.
2. Order: text + collections (confirm the `Core/text` and `Core/files` private helpers check first), then encoding/regex/args, then math/units/time, then files/path/io/mem, then crypto (hands off to #3667 for seal/open semantics).
3. For each unowned row: write the Jet body, or keep it as a typed provider leaf marked in Core source (F4 once ratified; until then the existing `source_module` leaf convention).
4. Migrate callers/examples/goldens in the same patch. Rename module constants to ALL_CAPS (#3584).
5. Perf: text/collections are gate cells. Rerun the matched text/collections perf cells before deleting the Rust route. A loss keeps that route and goes on a card.

**Proof.**
- The commands in add_criteria.
- `jet test Compiler --profile cases core_surface_ledger/`: passes.

**Batch.** `batch-host-runtime`: deleting Prelude CoreLib Rust rows changes the embedded dispatcher. Proof needs one compiler build and one tier-parity golden pass.

**Dependencies.** Parent #3690. Crypto overlaps #3667/#3668, which own the crypto semantics. None of these block the other modules.

cards.title: CoreLib system: complete Jet ownership
cards.body: Complete archives, networking, process, tasks, events, watchers, terminal, logging, email, and database semantics. Keep host access behind typed provider leaves and prove all applicable tiers.
cards.plan:
**Goal.** This is the system wave of #3690 (W2/W3): archive, process/tasks, event/watcher, term/log/sys, email/db and net transports. Jet source owns protocol, policy, validation and typed failures. Host access stays behind typed, policy-free provider leaves.

**Current state.**
- c4 (sys.expand parity) is met: `tests/corelib_parts/system.rs:461` `core_sys_expand_home_patterns_are_identical_across_tiers`.
- c5 fails. `Core/sys/sys.jet:16` `pub fn set(name, value) -[Env]> { core.sys.set(name, value) }` is infallible. The leaf `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/FSIoEnvOsTesting.rs:677` `jet_std_env_set(...) -> Result<(), EnvError>` runs `jet_env_validate_name/value` in Rust, which is policy in the leaf. The emitted Rust assigns that Result to a `()` MIR slot (E0308; log 2026-09-24). The test is `tests/corelib_parts/system.rs:488`.
- Dispatcher rows in `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core.jet` for system modules: 355 in total, 293 of them already Jet-owned duplicates.

| Module | Rows | Jet-owned |
|---|---|---|
| net | 107 | 107 |
| service | 59 | 5 |
| sys | 52 | 52 |
| log | 28 | 28 |
| http | 27 | 24 |
| term | 22 | 20 |
| sync | 17 | 17 |
| db | 13 | 13 |
| event | 7 | 7 |
| process | 6 | 6 |
| tasks | 6 | 4 |
| email | 6 | 5 |
| watcher | 4 | 4 |

- Sibling owners of sub-contracts: #3594 (process binary streams), #3596 (archive streaming), #3557 (TCP handle shape, building), #3669 (db semantics) and #3665/#3666 (HTTP/TLS).

**Changes.**
1. **c5 first:**
   - Move env name/value validation (empty, `=`, NUL, and the platform length cap) into `Core/sys/sys.jet`.
   - `set` becomes `-[Env]> EnvError!`, matching `unset` at :18, under the ratified typed-failure/no-fake-success law.
   - The leaf `jet_std_env_set` becomes policy-free and returns `()`.
   - Update the provider row (`Core.jet:352`) and regenerate with `node Tools/agent/gen-core-tables.mjs --write`.
   - Update the test witness to `sys.set(key, v) ?? return` and add an invalid-name line.
2. Then, one module per patch: net → sys/log/term → sync/event/watcher/process/tasks → db/email → service. Delete the Jet-owned `dispatcher_row`/`ambient_route` lines and the dead `Prelude/CoreLib` functions and JIT shims (F1). Mirror the removal in `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/*.jet` and `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/HandleMethods.jet`.
3. The 54 `core.service` rows with no Jet owner need Jet bodies over typed leaves. Raw sockets and OS calls stay leaves, using the F4 declaration once ratified.
4. Migrate callers, examples and goldens in each patch.

cards.title: CoreLib data: complete Jet ownership (browser storage moves with the web package, #6445)
cards.body: Complete data loaders, transforms, HTTP, router/forms, reactive, sync, services/jobs, storage, and browser semantics. Remove high-level native policy and prove all applicable tiers.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Finish the data/web slice of Core Jet ownership (parent #3547 is done). Every data, web, reactive, sync, service and jobs declaration has a real Jet body or a typed provider leaf, all policy, validation and error meaning lives in Jet, and each package passes AOT, `jet run` and interpreter proof.

**Current state**
- Building (log 2026-09-24): disjoint worktree lanes for data, HTTP client, web router and sync. Known failures: core/data/database and `is_base64` emit AOT Rust E0308/E0063 (JetErr into typed `DataError` slots). The Core/http/client.jet syntax cascade (E0003 at byte 12789) blocked the http_i9 framing test.
- HTTP/CSRF policy still in Rust: crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/WebServerFn.rs:141-174 (`JetWebServerFnCsrfPolicy`, `JetWebServerFnSpec`) and HTTPServer.rs. Core/http/server.jet:53 `json<T: Encode>` delegates to the provider. The HTTP client/server framing now belongs to #3665 and #3666, so it is out of this card's scope.
- Jobs: Core/jobs/jobs.jet:59-69 `JobQueue` is an in-memory record list (`queue()` builds `records: []`), which shadows the D-DX-QUEUE1=A SQLite provider. Examples/features/concurrency/job_queue.jet has no golden.
- Packages: Core/data (data, loader, stream, arrow, plot, sketch), Core/web (router, forms, query, table, virtual, store, storage, browser, devserver), Core/reactive, Core/service, Core/jobs.

**Changes**
1. Lane data: fix the typed error-carrier emission so `DataError` slots receive `DataError`, not `JetErr`. The fix goes in Compiler/JetCodegen at the result-carrier lowering, mirrored in the Rust emitter only as far as the shipped binary needs. Then fix the Core/data/data.jet `public_parameter` split and Core/web/query.jet `esc_json` UTF-8 defects named in the log.
2. Lane web: move CSRF/retry/idempotency policy from WebServerFn.rs into Core/web (a Jet decision function). WebServerFn.rs keeps only transport leaves.
3. Lane jobs: make `jobs.queue()` open the single SQLite-default durable provider identity with receiver `enqueue`/`claim`/`ack`/`retry`/`delay`/dead-letter. Delete the in-memory `records` shadow, migrate callers and add the job_queue golden.
4. Per package: diff each source declaration against the CoreCallRows and CoreModuleExportNames rows and the actual callers. Delete any route that re-encodes a Jet body. Main alone edits the shared Core.jet and registry rows at integration.
5. Web and browser tier cells stay explicitly pending until exercised.

**Proof**
- `jet test Compiler --profile golden concurrency/job_queue`: passes.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test corelib_http_data -- core_data_`: passes, including database and base64 on AOT.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test ui_backend -- web_` and `jet test Compiler --profile golden web/`: pass.
- A three-tier `jet run` diff for Examples/features/web/query_lifecycle.jet and store_history.jet against their goldens: empty.

**Batch**
batch-core-ui (web/reactive family): most remaining work is Core/web, reactive and jobs. The data carrier fix lands in the same build.

**Dependencies**
None blocking. #3665 and #3666 own HTTP framing and TLS.

cards.title: CoreLib specialized: complete Jet ownership
cards.body: Complete compute/models, UI/TUI/font, games, plugin/mod, compiler/reflect, testing, and remaining host domains. Keep unsafe/provider seams narrow and explicit.
cards.plan:
**Goal.** This is the specialized wave of #3690: compute/models, ui/tui/font/game, plugin/mod, compiler/reflect/testing, and app/build/devtools/perf/rt. Jet source owns authority, error and effect meaning. Vetted engines (GTK, raylib, ONNX Runtime, wasmtime) remain typed Rust provider leaves until F4/F5 are ratified.

**Current state.**
- Specialized dispatcher rows in `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core.jet`: 206 in total, 197 of them already Jet-owned duplicates.

| Module | Rows | Jet-owned |
|---|---|---|
| compute | 64 | 64 |
| ui | 52 | 48 |
| tui | 35 | 35 |
| game | 19 | 18 |
| testing | 14 | 13 |
| app | 11 | 11 |
| perf | 4 | 4 |
| font | 2 | 2 |
| models, plugin, devtools | 1 each | 0 |

- `core.compute.solve` ownership is resolved. Core.jet has `source_module core.compute.solve … owns { dense, lu }`, and `tests/core_compute_solve.rs` has `compute_solve_uses_scale_relative_pivots_and_checked_errors`.
- The core.testing tier fix is proven: `core_testing_histories_error_is_stable_across_i9_tiers`, passing since 2026-09-24.
- Probe failures that must clear first come from #3695: `Core/ui/ui.jet:121,126` E0768 and :141 E1102, clipboard `UiClipboardText`, and `Core/compiler/compiler.jet:30-40` undefined carriers.
- Self-hosted routing mirrors: `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/*.jet` and `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/HandleMethods.jet`.

**Changes (one module per patch).**
1. compute/compute.solve: delete the 64 Jet-owned rows and the matching `Prelude/CoreLib` compute functions and JIT shims (F1). Keep CUDA/Metal/Vulkan device leaves typed.
2. tui, then ui/font/game: delete the Jet-owned rows. GTK/raylib calls stay leaves. Give the 4 unowned ui rows and 1 unowned game row Jet bodies or leaf declarations.
3. testing, app, perf, rt, mod: delete the Jet-owned rows.
4. models, plugin and devtools each keep one unowned row. #3670 owns plugin policy. models `open` stays an ONNX leaf; declare it as a leaf in `Core/models`.
5. Regenerate registries with `node Tools/agent/gen-core-tables.mjs --write`. Mirror the removals in the self-hosted registry and HandleMethods. Migrate examples and goldens in each patch.
6. Measure no performance win unless a matched battery exists (compute cells are gated).

**Proof.**
- The commands in add_criteria.
- `jet test Compiler --profile cases core_surface_ledger/`: passes.

**Batch.** `batch-host-runtime`: the work removes Prelude CoreLib Rust routes and needs one build plus a tier-parity golden pass.

**Dependencies.** Parent #3690. It shares ui/compiler probe fixes with #3695 and plugin policy with #3670. Neither is a hard prerequisite for the compute/tui/testing slices.

cards.title: Audit Python Rust C Zig Go Core libraries against Jet domains
cards.body: Owner instruction 2026-09-24: audit current peer core/standard libraries and select the best safe, low-friction behavior for Jet across appropriate CoreLib breadth and depth. Compare actual Jet source and executable examples, not stale spec catalogs; preserve versioned official peer citations, contextual same-program behavior, failure modes, Jet-style proposed contract, and uncertainty. Route accepted gaps to existing owning CoreLib cards #3548-#3551 or a narrowly scoped card; public API/default/dependency changes need Tower ballots. No absent-feature or world-class claim from documentation alone.
cards.plan: Split read-only source-backed comparisons by disjoint Jet domains (foundations, system, data/web, specialized), covering Python, Rust, C, Zig, and Go for each applicable surface. Reconcile retained prior audit evidence with current source and official peer versions. For every selected gap, record a same-program Jet/peer example, safe beginner API and explicit expert control, source/executable state, reason for inclusion or CoreLib exclusion, owner gate, owning implementation card, focused example/golden/tier criterion and paired performance cell where motivated by speed. Do not close until selected Core gaps are implemented and proved on every applicable tier and performance losses are measured and owned through existing gates.

cards.title: Jetpack in Jet: port the package and environment engine from Rust to Jet
cards.body:
OWNER DIRECTIVE 2026-09-27 (lifts the 2026-08-30 Jetpack-in-Jet pause recorded on #2327): the owner authorizes a full port of Jetpack from Rust to Jet. The compiler port under Compiler/ (#218) runs in parallel as a sibling; follow its conventions. Phases in order: (1) complete code build-out, (2) parity and bug fixing, (3) optimization.

Owner instructions (override default routing in AGENTS.md for this stream):
- Opus 5.5 only: every dispatched subagent runs on Opus 5.5, set explicitly on OMP task/hub. No @implementation, @full_review, @cavecrew, or other default profile/model. If a dispatch cannot run on Opus 5.5, stop that slice and report; never fall back.
- No JetOS work: do not port, stub, test, benchmark or plan crates/jetpack/src/JetOS/, crates/jetos, or any command/provider/image path that exists only for JetOS. Omit JetOS hooks from ported code; exclude JetOS surfaces from the parity harness and performance cells.
- All ported code lives under top-level Jetpack/, laid out as Jetpack/<Area>/Source/... mirroring Compiler/, plus Jetpack/Bootstrap/ with an ordered sources.list and check script modeled on Compiler/Bootstrap.
- Scope (non-test LOC, ~117k, JetOS excluded): crates/jetpack (~100k incl. src/bin helpers), crates/jetpack-bin (~0.2k), crates/jet-nix-eval (~3.8k), crates/jet-store (~3.2k), crates/jet-env-model (~11k), crates/jet-pkg-model (~69k). jet-env-model and jet-pkg-model are shared with the compiler: check Compiler/ ownership first and never create a second copy. Use Compiler/ Jet versions of jet-driver, jet-sema, jet-codegen, etc., not new ports.
- Every Rust module except JetOS maps to a named Jet home; the mapping and progress live in Tower cards only, not docs.
- Phase 1 order: models + Nix evaluator; Store (Nar, Archive, Journal, Cache, Lifecycle, Closure, ...); Trust, TrustRoot, SemanticLock; Provider, ProviderGraph; Services, Shell, Image (OCI only), Recipe; CLI. Idiomatic current Jet, not transliterated Rust (audits list anti-patterns). Port unit/integration tests with each module. Each slice passes the Jetpack bootstrap check and runs on AOT and default jet run (I9).
- Compiler defects/missing Core APIs: file or reuse a Tower card; no workaround inside Jetpack. New syntax/public API/dependencies need an owner ballot. ed25519-dalek and zstd need an approved bridge pattern (I6); no new external deps. No #Unsafe without an audited reason.
- Phase 2: differential harness running Rust jetpack and the Jet build on the same inputs (existing tests such as tests/jetpack_platform, fixtures, real projects), comparing stdout, stderr, exit codes, store contents and lockfiles; drive every difference to zero with root fixes. Rust Jetpack stays shipped until an owner cutover decision.
- Phase 3: strict gate vs Rust Jetpack, Jet/Rust <= 1.05 on every cell: warm jetpack env, store verification, hashing, graph load; record in the canonical manifest. Never trade semantics for speed.
- Operating: Tower only ledger; one writer per path; worktrees only under .agent-worktrees/; commands via scripts/agent/jet-env; scratch in ~/.cache/jet-luna; narrow proofs per card, broad suites at milestones; report exercised receipts.

Done: every non-JetOS Rust module has a ported Jet home under Jetpack/ with tests, the parity harness passes, every performance cell meets the gate; then stop and ask the owner for the cutover decision.
cards.plan:
## Goal
This is the epic for the owner-authorized (2026-09-27) port of Jetpack from Rust to Jet under top-level `Jetpack/`. It runs in three phases: (1) code build-out, (2) parity and bug fixing, (3) optimization. The Rust Jetpack stays the shipped implementation until the owner ratifies a cutover ballot.

## Owner rules (preserved)
- Every dispatched subagent runs Opus 5.5, set explicitly; never fall back.
- No JetOS work of any kind.
- Code lives in `Jetpack/<Area>/Source/…` with `Jetpack/Bootstrap/` (ordered `sources.list`/`tests.list`, `check.sh`).
- The mapping and progress live only in Tower cards.
- Reuse Compiler/ and never create a second copy.
- Compiler defects and Core gaps get Tower cards and no workaround.
- New syntax, public API or dependencies need an owner ballot. ed25519/zstd need an approved bridge (I6).
- No `#Unsafe` without an audited reason.
- Write idiomatic current Jet and port the tests with each module.

## Current state
- About 96k Jet lines across 12 of 13 areas (tracked plus in-flight). Foundation 2.8k, PackageModel 38.9k (32 test files), EnvModel 8.4k, NixEval 5.6k, Nix 2.4k, Store 25.0k (15), Trust 4.5k, Recipe 0.5k, Provider 4.9k (3), Environment 0.4k, Image 0.8k, CLI 2.1k. Services is empty. The area DAG is `Jetpack/Bootstrap/areas.list:9-23`.
- Much of PackageModel/Store/EnvModel is untracked working-tree work after the rate-limit stop (963c3cb09); the slices (#3601-#3615, #3637-#3652, …) own it.
- No differential harness and no Jetpack performance cells exist yet.
- `check.sh` supports `--syntax`, `--area X [--deps-from-head]`, `--each` and `--tests`. It prints `JETPACK CHECK OK (check, default run, AOT test)` and a receipt with `check-unit-sha256`.

## Changes (in order)
1. Build-out (criterion 1): finish every slice card. Each one ends with `check.sh --area <Area> --deps-from-head --tests` green and a receipt.
2. Integrated proof (criterion 2): `check.sh --each --tests` and then a whole-unit `check.sh --tests` on main. Run a `#Unsafe` audit by searching `Jetpack/` for `#Unsafe` and checking every hit for a reason.
3. Parity (criterion 3): a differential harness under `Jetpack/Bootstrap/` that runs Rust `jetpack` and the Jet build on the root `tests/jetpack_*.rs` inputs, fixtures and real projects (JetOS excluded), and diffs stdout, stderr, exit code, store tree and lockfiles.
4. Performance (criterion 4): warm `jetpack env`, store verification, hashing and graph-load cells in the canonical performance manifest, strict gate Jet/Rust ≤ 1.05.
5. Stop point (criterion 5): raise the owner cutover ballot.

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Jetpack/Bootstrap/check.sh --each --tests` → every area prints `JETPACK CHECK OK (check, default run, AOT test)`.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Jetpack/Bootstrap/check.sh --tests` → `JETPACK CHECK OK (check, default run, AOT test)`. Record the receipt and unit SHA.
- The differential harness report shows 0 differences. The perf gate shows every Jetpack cell ≤ 1.05.

## Batch
batch-jetpack-cli: CLI is the top of the area DAG, so its unit closes over every area. The epic's integrated proof is that unit.

## Dependencies
- #3661: the single-unit `jet check` is too slow, so the whole-unit check times out or hits the memory cap.
- #3673: cross-module enums, type imports and constants, needed to split areas into packages.
- #3676: the first ICE of the tier run.
- The Core gap cards #3593-#3598 and the Compiler entry points #3599 stay on the slices that need them.

cards.title: core.files: store-grade primitives for Jetpack (file identity, exclusive create, no-follow, fd-relative ops, advisory locks, xattrs, binary handles)
cards.body:
Found by the Jetpack Rust-to-Jet port mapping (#3590; mapping receipts ~/.cache/jet-luna/jetpack-port/mapping-{A,B,C}.json). The Rust Jetpack uses these through std or crates; the Jet port cannot express them with current Core. Per the owner rule the port does not work around a missing Core API inside Jetpack. Each item is new public Core API, so it needs an owner ballot (AGENTS.md owner gates) with exact names, signatures, errors, effects and tier behavior before implementation. Prove each on AOT and default jet run (I9).

Needed:
1. Stat identity: device, inode, hard-link count, owner uid, nanosecond mtime (Core/files/files.jet samefile currently returns an error at :1046). Used for same-inode, hardlink-count, owner and path-swap (TOCTOU) checks in 16+ files: Store/{Ingest,Lifecycle,Cleanup,Closure,Seal,Reuse,Broker,Archive}, jet-pkg-model Authority/Envelope/SealWalk.
2. Exclusive create (O_EXCL/create_new) with explicit creation mode (17 files).
3. No-follow open and read through a handle (O_NOFOLLOW), and no-follow traversal from a held root directory (10 files).
4. Directory handles and fd-relative operations: openat, mkdirat, renameat, unlinkat, fchmod, fdopendir/readdir (Store/Lifecycle/Directory.rs, Authority, Envelope).
5. Kernel advisory lock (flock LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB / LockFileEx) with try_lock, unlock and crash release; core.files.lock today only creates an O_EXCL marker (RuntimePolicy/Lock, Store journal/transactions).
6. Close-on-exec control.
7. Extended attributes list/get/set (Envelope, Store capture).
8. Binary streaming handles: read a chunk into [U8], write bytes, seek, set_len, fsync on a handle (NAR, archive, cache streaming; existing reader/writer are line-oriented).
9. Directory fsync so renames are durable; atomic rename-exchange (renameat2 RENAME_EXCHANGE / renameatx_np); specified replace-existing + write-through rename on Windows.
10. Sparse-hole detection (SEEK_HOLE/SEEK_DATA) for Envelope.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Give `core.files` the store-grade primitives the Jetpack Jet port (#3590) needs, exactly as the seven ratified decisions define them, with the syscalls as policy-free provider leaves. Two needs that no decision covers go to ballots.

## Current state
- Core/files/files.jet: `samefile` always errors with `file identity requires provider inode/device support` (:1041-1046). `lock` is a host marker file (:759; dispatcher `jet_std_fs_lock` at crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core.jet:322). `truncate` rewrites the whole file (:1157). Byte IO is whole-file only (`read_bytes` :132, `write_bytes` :147).
- There is no no-follow, directory-handle, fd-relative, xattr or binary-handle API. `open`/`create` are host rows (Core.jet:1080-1081), and `stat` is `jet_std_fs_stat` (:301).
- Ratified A: D-CORE-FILEERROR1 (`IOError.AlreadyExists`/`Unsupported(IOContext)`, one mapper); D-CORE-FILESTAT1 (`FileId{device, inode}`, `links`, `owner`, `size_on_disk`, and Instant `modified`/`changed`/`created` replacing `modified_ms`/`created_ms`; `samefile` compares ids); D-CORE-FILEOPEN1 (`create(if_exists: CreateIfExists{.Replace}, mode: Int?{None}, links: LinkPolicy{.Follow})`, `open(links:)`, and FileReader `read`/`chunks`/`seek`/`stat` plus FileWriter `write`/`write_all`/`fsync`/`set_mode`/`stat`, with all handles close-on-exec, which covers need 6); D-CORE-FILERENAME1 (`rename(if_exists: RenameIfExists{.Replace})` with Refuse and Swap, and folder `fsync`); D-CORE-FILEDIR1 (an opaque `Directory` from `open_directory` with no-follow relative-name methods); D-CORE-FILELOCK1 (flock/LockFileEx `lock(path, timeout: Duration?{None})`, `try_lock`, crash release, identity re-check); D-CORE-FILEXATTR1 (three no-follow xattr calls).
- Needs 8 (`set_len` on a handle) and 10 (SEEK_HOLE/SEEK_DATA) have no decision.

## Changes
1. Jet semantics in files.jet: the new enums (`CreateIfExists`, `LinkPolicy`, `RenameIfExists`), `FileId`, the extended `Stat`, `samefile`, the `Directory` path-part validation (reject `..`, `.`, empty and absolute parts), lock timeout and retry policy, and every error message (what, why, fix).
2. Provider leaves only in the retained host (Prelude CoreLib Rust and jet-rt): open flags (O_EXCL, O_NOFOLLOW, O_CLOEXEC, O_DIRECTORY), openat/mkdirat/renameat2/unlinkat/fchmod/fdopendir, flock, the [l]xattr calls, statx, renameatx_np and the Windows equivalents, plus the shared errno mapper.
3. Cutover: remove `modified_ms`/`created_ms` and the marker lock, then migrate every caller in Core/, Jetpack/, Examples/ and tests/. Register the members in Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry (CoreHostSignatures.jet, CoreCallRows.jet) and regenerate with `node Tools/agent/gen-core-tables.mjs --write`.
4. Draft two ballots, D-CORE-FILESETLEN1 (handle `set_len`) and D-CORE-FILEHOLES1 (sparse data/hole query), each with same-program alternatives.
5. New Examples/features/io/files_store_primitives.jet with its .out, one section per decision, covering the failure cells: AlreadyExists, a final link refused, a `..` part refused, Swap with a missing name, try_lock contention, and an xattr on an unsupported filesystem.

## Proof
- `jet test Compiler --profile golden io/files_store_primitives` passes.
- `jet test Compiler --profile golden io/files_store_primitives` passes on O0, O1 and O2.
- `node Tools/agent/gen-core-tables.mjs --check` exits 0.

## Batch
batch-core-files: Core/files plus its provider leaves, retested in one pass.

## Dependencies
None for the seven ratified slices. Needs 8 (set_len) and 10 (holes) wait on the two ballots this card drafts.
