cards.title: core.process: binary streams, exec, process groups, fd inheritance, scoped signals for Jetpack
cards.body:
Found by the Jetpack Rust-to-Jet port mapping (#3590; mapping receipts ~/.cache/jet-luna/jetpack-port/mapping-{A,B,C}.json). The Rust Jetpack uses these through std or crates; the Jet port cannot express them with current Core. Per the owner rule the port does not work around a missing Core API inside Jetpack. Each item is new public Core API, so it needs an owner ballot (AGENTS.md owner gates) with exact names, signatures, errors, effects and tier behavior before implementation. Prove each on AOT and default jet run (I9).

Needed:
1. Binary stdin/stdout/stderr streaming on ProcessChild (today only line streams); Provider and Store feed and read NAR/tar bytes through child processes.
2. exec: replace the current process image (jetpack env/use shell handoff).
3. Child process-group/session placement (Unix process_group(0), Windows CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP) and Windows Job Object containment plus GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent (Services supervision, RuntimePolicy).
4. Hand an inherited file descriptor to a child (clear FD_CLOEXEC) (Store Broker, Services).
5. Scoped SIGINT/SIGTERM handler with a pollable flag and restore of the previous handler (on_signal registers a policy only).
6. core.sys: process start-identity query for pid-reuse guards on macOS/Windows.
Depends on #3591 (core.process currently fails to check).
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement the six ratified core.process decisions the Jetpack port (#3590) needs: binary pipes, process replacement, terminal handoff and groups, kept-open handles, scoped signal receivers, and start identity. Prove each on AOT and default `jet run` (I9). The port may not work around a missing Core API.

## Current state
- `Core/process/process.jet` (349 lines) has only line streams. `stdin_text` (:51-57) writes text, and `on_signal` (:100) registers a policy only. There is no exec, keep_open, `signals()` receiver or identity.
- Process handles are compiler-known: `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/ProcessHandles.jet:292-456` (ProcessChild fields `stdin`/`stdout`/`stderr`/`terminal` at :431-437, and ProcessStdin write/close at :410-412). The registry has `ProcessStdin.close` at `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/CoreCallRows.jet:1601`.
- The host is `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/Process.rs`, which already defaults to a Unix process group and Windows Job containment (per the 2026-09-28 log, around :328-347 and :493-513), plus `ProcessSpec.rs`.
- #3591 is done. All six decisions are ratified A: D-CORE-PROCBYTES1, PROCREPLACE1, PROCGROUP1, PROCIDENT1, PROCINHERIT1 and PROCSIGNAL1. `IOError.Unsupported` comes from D-CORE-FILEERROR1=A (card #3593), which is not yet in `Core/io/io.jet`.

## Changes (Jet compiler first; one sub-slice per decision, landing together)
1. PROCBYTES1: `ProcessStdin.write(bytes) -> Int IOError!`, `write_all(bytes)`, `write_text(text)` (renamed from `write(text)`; migrate `stdin_text` and callers). `ProcessStdoutStream`/`ProcessStderrStream` get `read(limit) -> [U8]`, where `[]` means EOF, and `chunks(size: Int{65536})`. A limit below 1 gives `IOError.InvalidInput` before any read. Sema rows go in `ProcessHandles.jet`, registry rows in CoreCallRows, and host code in `Process.rs`.
2. PROCREPLACE1: `ProcessSpec.replace_process() -[Exec, Time.Wait]> Never IOError!`. It refuses Capture/Stream/terminal/detached/timeout/output_limit/under before execve. On Unix it flushes Jet stdio before execve. On Windows it uses a Job Object stand-in.
3. PROCGROUP1: automatic terminal handoff (setpgid/tcsetpgrp with SIGTTOU blocked, reclaim after wait, refuse a second owner with InvalidInput). On Windows, CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP for non-console children.
4. PROCINHERIT1: `ProcessSpec.keep_open(handle: &&KeepOpen, at: Int?{None})`, where KeepOpen is a core.files handle. Numbers below 3 or duplicates are refused. CLOEXEC is cleared only in the child. On Windows it uses PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST, and `at` gives Unsupported.
5. PROCSIGNAL1: `process.signals(kinds) -[Exec]> Receiver<ProcessSignal>` with a nested newest-wins scope, restore on drop, and one pending value per kind.
6. PROCIDENT1: `ProcessIdentity { pid, start, containment }`, `ProcessChild.identity()`, `process.identity(pid)`, `process.find(saved)` and `RunningProcess` terminate/kill/interrupt. Start tokens: Linux stat starttime, macOS proc_pidinfo, Windows GetProcessTimes. Other targets give `IOError.Unsupported`.
7. Update `Docs/spec` core.process and the Jetpack mapping receipts.

## Proof
- Add goldens `Examples/features/io/process_bytes.jet` (binary round-trip through `cat`, chunks, invalid limit), `process_keep_open.jet`, `process_signals.jet` (self-SIGINT through `sys.kill`, nested restore) and `process_identity.jet` (identity equality, `find` after exit returns None). For each, `jet test Compiler --profile golden io/process_` passes, and `jet run` diffs empty.
- `tests/process_replace.rs::replace_process_execs_and_refuses_capture` passes via `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test process_replace`.
- The terminal handoff is checked in `tests/help_pty.rs` style under a PTY: `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test process_replace -- terminal_handoff`.

## Batch
batch-core-files: the core.process surface plus its sema, registry and host rows, retested with the io/process goldens.

## Dependencies
#3593 (core.files handles and `IOError.Unsupported` from D-CORE-FILEERROR1) is needed for items 4 and 6. Items 1, 2, 3 and 5 can land first.

cards.title: core.http / core.net: capped streaming fetch, redirect policy, pinned addresses, inherited sockets for Jetpack
cards.body:
Found by the Jetpack Rust-to-Jet port mapping (#3590; mapping receipts ~/.cache/jet-luna/jetpack-port/mapping-{A,B,C}.json). The Rust Jetpack uses these through std or crates; the Jet port cannot express them with current Core. Per the owner rule the port does not work around a missing Core API inside Jetpack. Each item is new public Core API, so it needs an owner ballot (AGENTS.md owner gates) with exact names, signatures, errors, effects and tier behavior before implementation. Prove each on AOT and default jet run (I9).

Needed (replacing jet_net uses in Store/Cache.rs, Store/NixCache.rs, Provider/native.rs, Provider/fetch.rs, NixIndex.rs, ToolchainUpdate.rs):
1. Streaming GET response body with a caller-set byte cap (default body limit is 1 MiB) - jet_net::get_stream, get_stream_follow_redirects.
2. Bounded fetch with an explicit redirect-policy callback - jet_net::fetch_bounded_with_redirect_policy.
3. Request over pre-resolved, pinned public-only socket addresses - jet_net::get_stream_pinned + resolve_public_addresses; public-IP classification must match jet_net::is_public_ip (including CGNAT and other special ranges).
4. Adopt an inherited listening socket (socket activation, fd 3) for non-JetOS dev services (see #329 for the JetOS twin).
5. Unix-socket peer credentials (SO_PEERCRED) for the shared-store broker.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement the five ratified Jetpack network needs in Core Jet: a capped streaming body, a redirect host policy, pinned destinations, inherited listeners and Unix peer credentials. The syscalls stay as policy-free leaves.

## Current state
- Core/http/client.jet has no body-limit, stream, destination or redirect-target API. `RedirectPolicy` is `{Disabled, Limited, All}` (:26-29), with a fixed `C_MAX_BODY_BYTES` (:181, :282).
- Core/net/net.jet has no `inherited_listeners` or `unix_peer`.
- Core/net/ip.jet `is_global` (:81-83) and `ipv6_is_global` (:453-455) are narrower than the proposed table (no CGNAT 100.64/10, 198.18/15, documentation ranges or 2000::/3 rule).
- Ratified A: D-CORE-HTTPBODYLIMIT1 (`HTTPResponse.body(limit: Int = 67108864) -> Body`, where Body implements `core.io.Reader`; over-cap gives `IOError.InvalidInput` through the reader or `HTTPError.BodyTooLarge(limit)` inherently; Content-Length above the cap fails before any byte; the Rust `HTTP_RESPONSE_BODY_LIMIT` checks are removed); D-CORE-HTTPREDIRECT1 (`RedirectTarget {AnyHost, SameOrigin, Hosts([String])}` in `Follow{max, same_origin_credentials, to}`, refusing with `HTTPError.Redirect` before connecting); D-CORE-HTTPDEST1 (`HTTPDestinations {Any, Public, Loopback}` and `HTTPClient.destinations(rule)`, resolving once per client, pinning, applying to IP literals and every hop, `HTTPError.Policy`); D-CORE-NETINHERIT1 (`net.inherited_listeners() -[Net, Env]> [InheritedListener] NetError!` under the sd_listen_fds protocol); D-CORE-NETPEER1 (`net.unix_peer(stream) -[Net]> UnixPeer NetError!`).
- D-CORE-NETPUBLIC1 (which addresses count as public) is still open. Recommended: A, the jet_net table.
- The ratified texts name #3665 as the port that merges the Rust transport and the Jet client.

## Changes
1. Net slice (independent; land first): Core/net/net.jet `InheritedListener`, `inherited_listeners` and `UnixPeer`/`unix_peer`, with LISTEN_PID/FDS/FDNAMES validation, SO_ACCEPTCONN and SO_TYPE checks, CLOEXEC and unsetting the variables. The leaves (getsockopt, SO_PEERCRED/getpeereid) go in the retained host.
2. HTTP slice, on the #3665 Jet client: the body cap on every read path, `RedirectTarget` with Location resolved through core.net.url join, and destination pinning (a per-client map keyed by scheme, host and port, shared by clones, bypassing the DNS TTL, ignoring env proxies under .Public/.Loopback, and keeping SNI on the original host).
3. The .Public rule uses the NETPUBLIC1 table once it is ratified. Written for A: `is_global` and `ipv6_is_global` bodies become that table in ip.jet, and nothing else changes.
4. Regenerate with `node Tools/agent/gen-core-tables.mjs --write`.

## Proof
- `jet test Compiler --profile cases network_core_contract/network_core_contract_example_covers_reserved_cidr_and_mime_boundaries` passes, with Examples/features/net/network_core_contract.jet extended with the table rows and 240.0.0.1 still not public.
- New tests: `cargo test --test http_client_law -- http_body_limit_streams_and_rejects_over_cap http_redirect_target_same_origin_and_hosts http_destinations_public_pins_and_refuses_private` pass.
- New tests: `cargo test --test corelib_net -- net_inherited_listeners_sd_listen_fds net_unix_peer_reports_uid_gid` pass on Linux.

## Batch
batch-core-net: Core/http and Core/net.

## Dependencies
#3665 for the HTTP slice. D-CORE-NETPUBLIC1 (open) gates only `.Public`.

cards.title: core.archive: full streaming zstd decoder, streaming gunzip, tar with mode/type/link headers for Jetpack
cards.body:
Found by the Jetpack Rust-to-Jet port mapping (#3590; mapping receipts ~/.cache/jet-luna/jetpack-port/mapping-{A,B,C}.json). The Rust Jetpack uses these through std or crates; the Jet port cannot express them with current Core. Per the owner rule the port does not work around a missing Core API inside Jetpack. Each item is new public Core API, so it needs an owner ballot (AGENTS.md owner gates) with exact names, signatures, errors, effects and tier behavior before implementation. Prove each on AOT and default jet run (I9).

Needed:
1. core.archive.zstd decodes only raw/RLE blocks, whole-buffer, capped at 64 MiB. Store/NixCache.rs streams real zstd NARs (Rust uses the zstd crate approved by D-CODECS1 for the native standard-cache codec). The Jet port needs a full streaming decoder in Core (encoder is test-only in Rust). This is the approved-bridge question for zstd under I6.
2. Streaming gunzip (whole-buffer 64 MiB today).
3. Streaming tar reader/writer with mode, type and link headers (Store/Archive.rs, Image OCI layers).
cards.plan:
## Goal
Give Jetpack (#3590) the codecs it needs, in Jet Core, per three ratified decisions:
- D-CORE-CODECSTREAM1=A: reader adapters;
- D-CORE-ZSTDSOURCE1=A: a full RFC 8878 decoder written in Jet, with no new dependency and the unused zstd crate pin in jet-jit removed;
- D-CORE-TARSTREAM1=A: a streaming tar entry reader and writer.
The port must not work around missing Core inside Jetpack. Every tier runs the same source (I9).

## Ratified surface (new spelling)
```text
gzip.reader<R: io.Reader>(source: &R) -> GzipReader<R>
zstd.reader<R: io.Reader>(source: &R, max_window: Int{134_217_728}) -> ZstdReader<R>
  read(limit: Int) -> [U8] IOError!        // [] = end of decoded data
  chunks(size: Int{65536})
archive.tar_reader<R: io.Reader>(source: &R) -> TarReader<R>
  next(&self) -> TarEntry? IOError!;  read(limit) / chunks(size) for the current entry
archive.tar_writer<W: io.Writer>(sink: &W) -> TarWriter<W>
  add_file(name, body, mode: Int{0o644}, modified: Instant{epoch}) IOError!
  add_directory / add_symlink / add_hardlink / finish() IOError!
TarEntry{name, kind: TarKind, mode, size, modified}
TarKind{File Directory Symlink(String) Hardlink(String) CharDevice BlockDevice Fifo}
```
- Read rules: a limit below 1 is `IOError.InvalidInput`. `[]` comes only at a member or frame boundary; an early end is InvalidInput with cause `truncated`. Source errors pass through, and the adapter never closes its source. Errors carry `IOContext{operation: .Codec, resource: gzip|zstd, cause}`.
- gzip: every concatenated member; FEXTRA, FNAME, FCOMMENT and FHCRC; CRC-32 and ISIZE per member; trailing non-member bytes are InvalidInput. Memory is the 32 KiB window plus one chunk.
- zstd: raw, RLE and compressed blocks; Huffman literals with treeless reuse; FSE sequences in predefined, RLE, compressed and repeat modes; repeat offsets; window and content-size checks; XXH64 checksum; skippable frames skipped. A window above max_window is `Unsupported` with the size and the fix; a dictionary frame is `Unsupported` with the id. Memory is the window plus one 128 KiB block.
- tar: ustar, GNU and PAX. Long names, link targets and PAX size/mtime are applied inside the reader. Sparse files return as `.File` with logical size and zero holes. Header checksum verified; octal or base-256 numbers; names at most 4,096 bytes of UTF-8; at most 1 MiB of PAX records. Volume and unknown flags are `Unsupported`.
- The whole-buffer `decompress` calls keep their names, 64 MiB cap and error enums, and run on the same decoders.

## Current state
- `Core/archive/zstd.jet:57-58` decodes raw and RLE blocks only, whole-buffer. `gzip.jet:36` is whole-buffer. `archive.jet:279-344` has in-memory `tar_add`/`tar_get` without mode, type or link headers.
- Core has no `io.Reader`/`io.Writer` trait. `Core/io/io.jet` has only value buffers, and a grep finds no `trait` declaration anywhere in Core, yet all three ratified signatures bound on them.

## Changes
1. `Core/io/io.jet`: add `trait Reader { fn read(&self, limit: Int) -> [U8] IOError! }` and `trait Writer { fn write(&self, bytes: [U8]) IOError! }`, exactly the read and write contract the ballots state. Implement them for FileReader and FileWriter (`Core/files`), BytesBuf and TCP streams. Flag to the owner when landing, because the trait is implied by the ratified bounds but never named on its own.
2. `Core/archive/gzip.jet`: an incremental inflater state (reuse archive.jet's inflate core) plus `GzipReader`. `decompress` becomes read-to-end over a BytesBuf.
3. `Core/archive/zstd.jet`: the full RFC 8878 decoder and `ZstdReader`. Remove the zstd crate pin in jet-jit.
4. `Core/archive/archive.jet`: `TarReader`, `TarWriter`, `TarEntry` and `TarKind` as above.

cards.title: Core small gaps for Jetpack: isatty, OS-thread parallelism, JSON byte-limited parse, dynamic plugin load, models runtime
cards.body:
Found by the Jetpack Rust-to-Jet port mapping (#3590; mapping receipts ~/.cache/jet-luna/jetpack-port/mapping-{A,B,C}.json). The Rust Jetpack uses these through std or crates; the Jet port cannot express them with current Core. Per the owner rule the port does not work around a missing Core API inside Jetpack. Each item is new public Core API, so it needs an owner ballot (AGENTS.md owner gates) with exact names, signatures, errors, effects and tier behavior before implementation. Prove each on AOT and default jet run (I9).

Needed:
1. core.term: is_terminal for stdin/stdout/stderr (CLI output, prompts).
2. core.tasks: OS-thread parallelism (cooperative only today) for Store verification/hashing fan-out; affects the strict performance cells (store verification, hashing).
3. core.encoding.json: parse with a caller-supplied byte limit (MCP, CompilerExtension, FFI).
4. core.plugin: dynamic-path WASM Component instantiation with bounded fuel/memory (core.plugin.load needs a literal artifact) for the compiler-extension and build-plugin hosts in jetpack-bin (wasmtime today).
5. core.models: ModelPackage/ModelDescriptor/ModelError runtime (jet_rt::model) for jet-pkg-model Model.rs.
cards.plan:
**Goal.** Close five Core gaps the Jetpack Rust→Jet port (#3590) cannot work around. Four are ratified and ready to build. Models waits on its open ballot.

**Current state and decisions.**
1. **Terminal facts.** D-CORE-TERMSTDIN1=A: `StdinHandle.is_terminal() -> Bool`, and `Stdout`/`Stderr` `is_tty()` is renamed `is_terminal()` in one cutover. All three read the existing `jet_term_*_is_terminal` leaves (`Prelude/Term.rs:69-82`). There is no error path and no new effect. `Core/term/term.jet:97-99` has only `terminal_width`/`terminal_height`.
2. **OS-thread parallelism.** This is not new API: `para_*` and task groups are specified on OS threads (`Docs/spec/spec.md:2051-2074, 2171-2175`). The gaps are implementation plus a stale doc line in core.tasks:
   - the JIT runs para callbacks on one worker (`crates/jet-jit/src/Collections.rs:331-361`)
   - the MIR evaluator runs `para_fold` serially (`MIREval.rs:18308-18349`)
3. **JSON limits.** D-CORE-JSONLIMIT1=A: `json.parse(text, limits: EncodingLimits{EncodingLimits.safe()}) -> DataTree EncodingError!`, with the same for `decode`. Fields are validated in order before parsing. `Core/encoding/json.jet:71-74` takes no limits, and `safe_limits()` is at :60.
4. **Plugin.**
   - D-CORE-PLUGINPATH1=A: `plugin.load<I>(path, authority, sha256: String?{None}) -> Plugin<I>`. `I` is an exportable trait whose world is generated at load, and the literal form stays unchanged.
   - D-CORE-PLUGINLIMITS1=A: a `limits: plugin.Limits{Limits.default()}` label with fields fuel 10,000,000 (refilled each call), memory_bytes 16 MiB, table_elements 10,000 and timeout 2000 ms (per call).
   - `Core/plugin/plugin.jet` is a 17-line note today.
5. **Models.** D-CORE-MODELDESC1 is **open**. It covers `ModelDescriptor`/`ModelPackage`/`ModelError` and the pure `models.check`. `Core/models/models.jet` is 18 lines.

**Changes.**
1. Terminal:
   - Add `is_terminal` to the three handle types in the Prelude type table and Jet sources.
   - Rename every `is_tty` caller in Core, Examples, Jetpack and tests.
   - Update the registry with `node Tools/agent/gen-core-tables.mjs --write`.
2. Parallelism:
   - JIT: dispatch para callbacks to the shared worker pool, keeping deterministic result order.
   - `Compiler/JetEval`: evaluate `para_fold` with the same pool semantics, or document it serial-by-design if I9 allows equal results.
   - Fix the core.tasks doc line.
3. JSON: add the `limits` label to `parse`/`decode` using the existing limit validator. `loads` stays the bare form.
4. Plugin:
   - Generate the expected world from `I` and check exports at load, failing closed on imports.
   - Move the limits into `plugin.Limits` in Jet. This lands with #3670's policy port.
   - Jetpack's build-plugin and compiler-extension hosts switch to the new load path.
5. Models: after D-CORE-MODELDESC1 is ratified, implement the chosen types in `Core/models/models.jet` as a separate patch.

**Proof.** The commands in add_criteria.

**Batch.** `batch-host-runtime`: the JIT pool, the evaluator and the plugin load route need one host build plus a tier-parity retest. The term and JSON changes ride along.

**Dependencies.**
- Models waits on the D-CORE-MODELDESC1 owner ballot. The other four items proceed.
- Plugin shares `plugin.jet` with #3670, so land them together or rebase.

Four of the five gaps have ratified API decisions and none is implemented: core.term has no is_terminal, JSON has only fixed safe limits, core.plugin is a 17-line intrinsic stub, and core.models is an 18-line stub. OS threads need implementation only. Models waits on the open D-CORE-MODELDESC1. Evidence: Core/term/term.jet:97-101 (terminal_width/height only, no is_terminal); Core/encoding/json.jet:60-79,470,499 (safe_limits only, no caller limit); Core/plugin/plugin.jet:12-17 (literal-artifact intrinsic only); Core/models/models.jet (18 lines); decisions D-CORE-TERMSTDIN1/JSONLIMIT1/PLUGINPATH1/PLUGINLIMITS1 ratified A, D-CORE-MODELDESC1 open

Two short ballots submitted ready: D-CORE-TERMSTDIN1 (is_terminal on std streams; is_tty renamed in one cutover), D-CORE-JSONLIMIT1 (json.parse/decode with EncodingLimits). OS-thread parallelism is NOT new API: para_* and task groups already run on OS threads (spec.md:2051-2074, 2171-2175); the remaining gap is implementation (JIT runs para callbacks on one worker, jet-jit/Collections.rs:331-361; MIR evaluator runs para_fold serially, MIREval.rs:18308-18349) plus a stale core.tasks doc line. core.plugin/core.models ballots are being drafted by ArchivePluginBallots.

Each ratified item has a same-program witness with identical AOT and default-run output (interpreter too where applicable), run as `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=<dir/name> cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run`:

cards.title: Foundations: value and ref memory model, soundness fixes, and compiler-owned stack layers
cards.body:
One home for the 2026-09-27 foundations review, so these critical items do not scatter across the board. Evidence and design live in Docs/proposals/memory-model-foundations-2026-09-27.md (findings F1-F10 with repro programs, proposals, and the stack-replacement analysis). The owner asked for every owner decision to be balloted here. Self-hosting is done and every ballot here is ratified (16 of 16), so implementation proceeds.

Soundness defects found (not owner choices, still critical): F1 generic code bypasses the task sendability check (check passes, jet run runs, AOT ICE 101); F2 the JIT tier has no second checker and documents a stale stack-slot hazard in crates/jet-jit/src/Concurrency.rs. Conflicts with ratified text: F3 recursive Shared types rejected by E0221; F4 #Policy(gc) stores copy, contrary to D-OPTGC1=A; F5 storing a Shared handle consumes it; F6 ~ on Cell aliases; F9 misplaced #Unsafe site diagnostic after an earlier error.
cards.plan:
## Goal
This is the single home for the 2026-09-27 foundations review (Docs/proposals/memory-model-foundations-2026-09-27.md). It fixes soundness defect F1 now, puts the F2 differential oracle into the #217 soundness campaign, and turns each ratified memory ballot into its own build card. F3-F6 and F9 are resolved against ratified law.

## Current state
- Ballots: 15 of 16 are ratified A (D-MEMREF1, -LIFE1, -EXCL1, -TASK1, D-RAWPTR2, D-AUTOPIN1, D-DENY-COST1, D-REACT-REF1, D-INVALIDATE1, D-OPTIMISTIC1, D-RESUME1, D-WIRESKEW1, D-HOTSTATE1, D-STACKBOUND1, D-SECRETEDGE1). D-SYSSCHED1 (parallel game systems from their data access) is open with recommendation A. That is the only reason the phase is `deciding`. The plan below assumes A.
- F1 (proposal :64-90): `fn spawn_with<T>(value: ^T) { task ^value {…} }` called with a `Cell` passes `jet check`, prints 1 under `jet run`, and fails AOT with ICE 101 (rustc: `Rc<JetCellInner>` is not Sync). The same defect exists in the Jet compiler. Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Ownership/Crossings.jet:176 returns None (sendable) for any generic parameter, and thread confinement is a hand-kept name list (:102-106 core.mem and Browser types, :232-237 Cell and SharedGuard). The Rust twin is `sendability_problem_inner` in crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerOwnership.rs.
- F2: crates/jet-jit/src/Concurrency.rs `jet_jit_sender_send` documents a stale stack-slot hazard, and nothing checks JIT runs a second time.
- The owner's condition on waiting for self-hosting (#218) no longer applies, because Compiler/ is the primary target.

## Changes
1. F1, Jet compiler: at each generic instantiation that reaches a crossing (task spawn, channel send, shared storage), check sendability of the concrete type argument instead of skipping the parameter at Crossings.jet:176. Use the instantiation bindings from Calls/Inference, and report E1102 at the call site with the generic path in the note. Replace the name lists with a `ThreadConfined` fact on the type's registration (opt-out, like an auto trait), set in the declaring Core module.
2. F1, Rust mirror: the shipped binary executes this unsoundness, so mirror the check in CheckerOwnership.rs.
3. F2: add the differential oracle to #217. For generated programs, when sema accepts and rustc rejects, the harness records a sema bug card.
4. Open one build card per ratified ballot, each linking this card and the proposal. Link F3 (recursive Shared, E0221), F4 (#Policy(gc) copies, contrary to D-OPTGC1=A), F5 (storing Shared consumes it), F6 (`~` on Cell aliases) and F9 (misplaced #Unsafe site after an earlier error) to those cards, or fix them against current law.
5. After D-SYSSCHED1 is ratified, open its build card.

## Proof
- Add tests/ui/generic_task_sendability.jet (the F1 program) with E1102: `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/generic_task_sendability cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots`.
- `~/.cache/jet-luna/safe-jet.sh run tests/ui/generic_task_sendability.jet` reports E1102 and no longer prints 1.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` exits 0.
- The F2 oracle's first run is recorded on #217.

## Batch
batch-jetc-sema: F1 is a sendability rule in JetSema plus its mirror. The remaining work is card creation.

## Dependencies
D-SYSSCHED1 (open owner ballot) blocks criterion 1 only; F1, F2 and the build cards can proceed now.

Notes: Batch MEM of the 2026-10-28 board consolidation (TowerDedup). One worker (opus), one build, one proof run: per-card criteria; B01/B02 soundness batches are its first slices. Order: #4620 #4756.
Decisions so far: D-DENY-COST1 (ratified=A) on #3645; D-AUTOPIN1 (ratified=A) on #3645; D-HOTSTATE1 (ratified=A) on #3645; D-INVALIDATE1 (ratified=A) on #3645; D-MEMREF-EXCL1 (ratified=A) on #3645; D-MEMREF-LIFE1 (ratified=A) on #3645; D-MEMREF-TASK1 (ratified=A) on #3645; D-MEMREF1 (ratified=A) on #3645; D-OPTIMISTIC1 (ratified=A) on #3645; D-RAWPTR2 (ratified=A) on #3645; D-REACT-REF1 (ratified=A) on #3645; D-RESUME1 (ratified=A) on #3645; D-SECRETEDGE1 (ratified=A) on #3645; D-STACKBOUND1 (ratified=A) on #3645; D-SYSSCHED1 (ratified=A) on #3645; D-WIRESKEW1 (ratified=A) on #3645; D-LINK-ITEM1 (ratified=A) on #4620; D-METHOD-FOOTPRINT1 (ratified=A) on #4620; D-LINK-SIBLING1 (ratified=A) on #4620; D-MAP-SLOT1 (ratified=A) on #4620; D-PARAM-CONST1 (ratified=A) on #4620; D-COPY-WORD1 (ratified=A) on #4620; D-DROP-ASAP1 (ratified=A) on #4620
Fog: no criteria yet on #4620 (proposals in consolidate-plan.json no_criteria).
Out of scope: cards outside this list; other batches of the consolidation plan.

2026-10-27 F1 still reproduces on the Jet compiler (s1 at caa6a2945c + bd23): fn spawn_with<T>(c: ^T) -> Int { t :: task keep(^c); ^t.join() ?? 0 } called as spawn_with(^greet) with a closure checks clean and runs (prints 1), while the same send through a channel is E1102 (tests/ui/unsendable_send). Repro q/f1/a.jet in the Main lane. A sound fix needs a per-function summary of the type parameters a generic body sends across a task, checked at each instantiation (transitively through generic callees); a plain 'type parameter crossing is E1102' rule would reject Core's generic parallel adapters. Side bug: the same program warns L0102 'parameter c is never used' although c is passed to the task call.

C1 requires a linked build card for each ratified outcome. D-SYSSCHED1=A (game systems run in parallel from their access) has no linked build card; its build is #238 C10 ([#820] '... conflict-safe scheduling live in Jet'). Link #238 as the D-SYSSCHED1 build card. Evidence: systems-perf SP-26 / SD-LO-03; Unreal tick-aggregation and deferral evidence is attached on #238.

Measurement question for the memory-model review: Rust keeps Rc and Arc separate so single-threaded code never pays atomic refcount updates (7_o-YRxf_cc 33:00-35:40). Jet merges them into Shared<T>, which is always lock/atomic guarded (spec.md:1108-1111). Record the cost of Shared<T> on a value that never crosses a task (matched cell under the strict gate) before D-MEMREF-TASK1 build work; if material, the compiler can elide synchronization when sendability analysis proves no crossing.

Correction (2026-10-02, owner direction): the mining probes p1-p12 ran on target-rel/release/jet built 2026-10-01 22:14, which the owner says is obsolete. Every probe-based claim in the earlier 2026-10-02 mining log on this card is withdrawn until it is reproduced on a fresh build. Ratified D-RAWPTR2=A (p.offset(n), byte_offset, cast, mem.window(p, len), copy, fill; provenance checked in dev/hardened builds) already answers it, so ballot D-PTR-CHECKED1 was withdrawn after adversarial review. Live probe J8 on HEAD 1aca7cfe2: `p + 1` on *Int is E0109 and `p.offset(1)` is E0102 'Ptr has no method offset' with a fix telling users to define it inside struct Ptr (wrong advice for a Core type). Zig evidence: *T cannot step, [*]T steps by elements, slices are checked (probe Z4). Also: Docs/spec/reference/prior-art.md still lists 'unchecked pointer arithmetic' as rejected; update it when D-RAWPTR2 ships.
All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.

Phase 0 triage 2026-09-28 (toolwebmem1b, Opus 5.5): D_OWNER. 15 of 16 attached ballots are ratified; only D-SYSSCHED1 is open. F1 (generic code bypasses task sendability) and the F2 differential oracle no longer need to wait for #218, because Compiler/ is now the primary target. Evidence: `tower decision show D-SYSSCHED1` shows status open with rec A. The other 15 decisions are ratified A (card DEC list). The proposal is Docs/proposals/memory-model-foundations-2026-09-27.md. Owner question: D-SYSSCHED1: should game systems run in parallel automatically from their parameter access?

CORRECTION to the 2026-09-28 review log entry: the review agent named AstraBallotReview did NOT run on GPT-6 Astra. Its session log records model_change openai-codex/gpt-5.6-luna (thinking max), because ~/.omp/agent/config.yml routes the default task agent to @implementation. The agent self-reported 'GPT-6 Astra' and Pip repeated it without checking. The eight ballots the owner ratified on 2026-09-28 (D-DENY-COST1, D-AUTOPIN1, D-HOTSTATE1, D-INVALIDATE1, D-RESUME1, D-SECRETEDGE1, D-STACKBOUND1, D-WIRESKEW1) were reviewed by Luna 5.6, not Astra. No GPT-6 Astra review has run on any ballot on this card.

16 ballots raised (short profile, recommended option A first). Owner authorized one GPT-6 Astra review instead of the two-agent review. Fresh agent AstraBallotReview (GPT-6 Astra) ran a beginner-plus-adversarial pass on all 16 and repaired current-pane facts, undefined names, and option wording. Pip then re-verified its claims: kept Secret/Credential/E0722 (true per Prelude registry), but corrected its wrong claim that !Mem.Alloc(above: N) limits one allocation — MemoryFacts.rs sums bytes along the call path, so it bounds total heap per path; D-STACKBOUND1 now adds only !Mem.Stack. D-MEMREF1 options are three spellings of one value/link model per owner direction (owner rejected ref T): A *T link, B &T fields, C generalized Shared<T>. Other memory ballots use A's spelling and defer to D-MEMREF1. Proposal: Docs/proposals/memory-model-foundations-2026-09-27.md (uncommitted; checkout has another writer's rename in progress).

criteria.text: F1 is fixed at the root: generic code cannot move a thread-confined value across a task boundary. Proof: a tests/cases row reports E1102 on the generic `spawn_with(c)` program (spawn_with takes `&&`) under jet check, and `jet run` on it exits with the same diagnostic (no output `1`), on O0, O1 and O2 (was c5; tests/ui/generic_task_sendability is not on dev).
F3-F6 and F9 are each resolved, either by a ratified D-MEMREF outcome's build card or fixed against current ratified law, with UI snapshots and tier proofs.
criteria.evidence: dev d6c30e99a2 (G10Safe-unsafe-after-parse-error) plus master c5876bcc77 (#4500 c5-c7 build rows). F3 (recursive Shared refused by E0221): D-MEMREF-LIFE1=A, #4500 c6; under current law E0221 fires only at a cycle-closing write, proof cases shared_graphs/shared_graph_building_matches_aot_and_default_tiers. F4 (#Policy(gc) copies instead of tracing): D-OPTGC1=A, #6295 c2. F5 (storing a Shared consumes it) and F6 (copying a Cell aliases): D-MEMREF1=A, #4500 c1. F9 (E0355 cascade after a parse error): holds on current law, pinned by jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter unsafe_block_after_statement_parse_error PASS 1.

criteria.text: Taking the raw address of a list element inside #Unsafe (`*list[0]`) either compiles to a pointer into the list's storage or is rejected with a registered diagnostic; today it is an internal compiler error ("raw address of a temporary"), which violates I2. A census probes every place-expression form under * (list, array, field, nested index, view) at O0, O1 and O2, and each lands as a case. Found by the 2026-11-05 Doom port investigation (dev 0ccdff27ea).

D-AUTOPIN1=A is built: every automatic choice (storage form, browser or server placement, collection, copies, inlining, update notifications) is sound by default; `jet inspect choices` and editor hovers show it with its reason; a marker or effect denial locks it; a later change that breaks a lock fails the build naming the fact that changed. Proof: a golden per choice kind and a UI snapshot for a broken lock.

D-RAWPTR2=A is built: `?mem.Ptr<T>` (null is None), `p.offset(n)`, `p.byte_offset(n)`, `p.cast<U>()`, `mem.alloc_raw(size:, align:)`, `mem.free_raw(^p)`, `mem.window(p, len)`, `mem.copy` and `mem.fill`, all inside #Unsafe and keeping the pointer's origin; dev-mode and hardened builds still check range, liveness and alignment. Proof: a golden on O0, O1 and O2 and a UI snapshot for a use outside #Unsafe.

D-STACKBOUND1=A is built: `jet inspect memory` prints worst-case stack and heap per entry point from backend frame sizes and the call graph; `!Mem.Stack(above: N)` enforces a stack limit and `!Mem.Alloc(above: N)` the total heap any call path may allocate; recursion needs #MaxDepth(n) and dynamic calls a sealed target set. Proof: a golden of the report and a UI snapshot per refusal. (was #3239 c35)

Found 2026-11-09 (G6Lead, probes $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/G6Lead/ballots/probes/cycle/s19 and s20): a strong edge hidden in a closure is accepted and leaks. A feed owns a Close stream and a listener closure captures the feed strongly; E0221 accepts it, the program prints "end" and never "closed 7". Cause: SharedCycles.jet treats a `.Lambda` as a fresh value and skips places of function type. Safe code that forms such a cycle is refused by sema (or freed, if the type opts into collection), on O0, O1, O2 and web; a case proves the refusal, the weak-capture form (s22) still runs and closes, and a UI snapshot shows the diagnostic.

Found 2026-11-09 (TlsLead): `mem.address_of(shared[0])` on a mutable Shared list fails in lowering with "ir.build unlowered: write place StaticCall of Shared<[Int]>". Sema either accepts the program and it lowers and runs the same on O0, O1, O2 and web, or refuses it with a registered diagnostic and a UI snapshot; a case proves it.

cards.title: jet check is too slow for a large single unit: 9.2k Jetpack lines take 329 s (NixEval 5.5k = 195 s alone)
cards.body: Measured by the Jetpack port (#3590) with target/debug/jet (built 2026-09-26), each under a cgroup cap. jet check src/jetpack.jet on the assembled Jetpack unit: NixEval area only (5,539 lines) 195 s, 680 MB peak; Foundation+PackageModel only (3,663 lines) 79 s; both together (9.2k lines, master 31b1e0bf3) 329 s, 800 MB peak, 0 errors, 199 lints. Receipts: ~/.cache/jet-luna/jetpack-bootstrap/lead-c3e0b738ad/check.receipt and 5efbbecdee/check.receipt. The port targets ~120k lines in one unit (mirroring Compiler/Bootstrap); at this rate a single check would take far longer than an hour, which blocks the per-slice proof loop and later the build-time performance cell. Note the binary is a debug build; release timings are unmeasured. Needs: profile where check time goes on this unit (the unit is available by re-running Tools/agent/jet-env bash Jetpack/Bootstrap/check.sh) and a root fix.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Make `jet check` on a large single unit roughly linear in source size, and stop it running out of memory. Today it blocks three things: the Jetpack per-slice proof loop (#3590), stage zero of self-hosting (#218 criterion 12), and later the build-time performance cell.

## Current state
Measured with the debug `target/debug/jet` (built 2026-09-26), under a cgroup cap. Release timings are unmeasured.

| Unit | Lines | Wall | Peak memory |
|---|---|---|---|
| Jetpack NixEval only | 5,539 | 195 s | 680 MB |
| Foundation + PackageModel | 3,663 | 79 s | — |
| Both (master 31b1e0bf3) | 9.2k | 329 s | 800 MB (0 errors, 199 lints) |
| Compiler front slice (70 files, 2.93 MB) | — | 39 min single-core, OOM-killed | 8 GB, no verdict |
| EnvModel unit (185 sources) | — | exceeds the 6 GB cap in ~8 s | — |

- The lexer slice (94 KB) takes 25 s. Receipts: `~/.cache/jet-luna/jetpack-bootstrap/lead-c3e0b738ad/check.receipt` and `5efbbecdee/check.receipt`.
- Root-cause lead (`~/.cache/jet-luna/jetpack-port/jet-packages-study.md` §3): cost follows content, not size. The NixEval prefix timings are:
  - Text (225 lines): 0.5 s.
  - Adding API types and NixJson (825 lines): 37.4 s.
  - Adding the Lexer and Parser (1,588 lines): 69.6 s.
  - Adding `Jetpack/NixEval/Source/Evaluator/Values.jet` (260 lines of recursive `NixEvalValue`/`NixEvalNative`/`NixEvalThunk` enums and impls): 180.2 s, i.e. +110.6 s.
  - Adding 1,796 lines of evaluator methods: only +15.9 s.
- Splitting into files or packages does not help: a 5-line app over NixEval takes 207.6 s on the first run and 209.7 s on an unchanged rerun.
- Receipts are never reused under systemd-run. The environment identity at `Source/ReceiptStore.rs:3566-3573` ignores the Nix temp variables but not `INVOCATION_ID`.
- The bootstrap assembles one compiler unit on purpose (`Compiler/Bootstrap/sources.list`), and `Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Identity.jet` carries the whole module graph into checking.

## Changes
1. Profile first. Run `perf record` (or the sema phase timers) with a release `jet check` on `Jetpack/NixEval` and on a synthetic recursive-enum fixture. Name the pass whose cost grows with the recursive type graph times its use sites; likely suspects are drop/copy/derive/structural-recursion or type-identity walks without memoization.
2. Fix it at the root in the shipped checker (`crates/jet-sema`, the bootstrap checker used for stage zero). Memoize per type identity, or compute the fixpoint once per SCC. Then make the same fix in `Compiler/JetSema` so the self-hosted checker never inherits the algorithm.
3. Add `INVOCATION_ID` to the receipt environment-ignore list (`ReceiptStore.rs:3571`) as an immediate fix. #2517 later deletes ReceiptStore and replaces it with per-module memoization.
4. Add the scaling regression `recursive_enum_check_scales_linearly` in `tests/cli_compiler_speed.rs`. Checking N and 4N use sites of a three-way recursive enum must take at most 5x the time, with a fixed memory ceiling.

## Proof
- `jet test Compiler --profile cases cli_compiler_speed/recursive_enum_check_scales_linearly`: passes.
- Measurement with a release build: `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Jetpack/Bootstrap/check.sh --area NixEval` finishes in under 20 s (today 195 s on a debug build) and stays under 1 GB peak. The receipt is recorded.
- `bash ~/.cache/jet-luna/slice-scaling.sh target/release/jet after lexer parser front`: the front slice finishes under the 6 GB cap with a verdict.
- An unchanged rerun under systemd-run replays the receipt.

## Batch
batch-jetc-sema: the root cause is in the checker. The Rust bootstrap checker and Compiler/JetSema get the same fix in one build.

## Dependencies
None. This card unblocks #3590 and #218 stage zero.

Evidence: Card log: JetPackagesStudy prefix timings (Values.jet +110.6 s); Source/ReceiptStore.rs:3568-3573 (env-identity ignore list lacks INVOCATION_ID); Compiler/Bootstrap/sources.list + Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Identity.jet (single-unit assembly)

Scale data point (JetCompilerRunPath): Rust jet check of the Jet compiler front slice (70 files, 2.93 MB) ran 39 min single-core and was OOM-killed at 8 GB without a verdict; a 94 KB lexer slice takes 25 s. This blocks stage zero of self-hosting (#218 criterion 12), not only Jetpack.

Triage 2026-09-28 (Luna 5.6 high legwork, Pip reviewed): RETARGET_JET. This is a compiler-loop performance defect, not Jetpack implementation policy: the Jet bootstrap intentionally assembles one compiler unit (sources.list:1-4) and its Driver carries the complete module graph into checking (Identity.jet:109-147). The measured regression is reported and still actionable, but release performance is unverified (bugs-4.json:64-80). Evidence: The card reports 329 seconds for a 9.2k-line assembled check and 195 seconds for the 5.5k-line NixEval slice at ~/.cache/jet-luna/triage/bugs-4.json:64-80; release timing is unverified. ; Compiler/Bootstrap/sources.list:1-4 defines one unqualified Compiler unit and says the list is the only assembly order. ; Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Pipeline.jet:1-2 identifies the Jet front-end as parse, check, lower, and assemble. Jet target: Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Pipeline.jet, Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Identity.jet, Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/CheckProgram.jet, Compiler/Bootstrap/sources.list.

Also: check results are never reused between runs under systemd-run because the receipt environment identity includes INVOCATION_ID (ReceiptStore.rs:3568-3573 already ignores Nix temp variables for the same reason), and receipts are not stored for ../ path deps.

Root-cause lead from JetPackagesStudy (report ~/.cache/jet-luna/jetpack-port/jet-packages-study.md section 3): check cost follows content, not size. NixEval prefix timings: Text 225 lines 0.5 s; +API types/NixJson 825 lines 37.4 s; +Lexer/Parser 1,588 lines 69.6 s; +Values.jet (260 lines: recursive NixEvalValue/NixEvalNative/NixEvalThunk enums and impls) 1,848 lines 180.2 s (+110.6 s); +1,796 lines of evaluator methods 196.1 s (+15.9 s). Splitting into files or packages does not help: a dependency is re-checked in full every time and nothing is reused between runs (5-line app over NixEval: 207.6 s first run, 209.7 s unchanged rerun). Suspect a whole-unit pass that scales with the recursive enum/type graph times use sites. A PhaseTiming profile is the next step.

criteria.text: [retarget] A profile names the super-linear pass in the Jet checker (Compiler/JetSema) on the recursive NixEval enums, and a check of a fixture with 4N use sites takes at most 5x the N-site time with bounded memory.
Release `JET=jet jet Jetpack/Bootstrap/Check.jet --area NixEval` finishes in under 20 s and under 1 GB peak (from 195 s / 680 MB debug), with its receipt recorded.

[#3951] The original 30-variant named-payload `#Comparable` enum program (Examples/features/types/enum_many_variants) builds on every level within the compile-speed budget, with generated code size linear in variant count. Derived equality, compare, Debug and cleanup bodies no longer explode (PreludeDerives.jet). There is a receipt for the 12-variant and 30-variant cases.

[#2533] Each retained generated-code compile-cost lever (derive trimming, explicit types or backend-specific trimming) has a before/after backend time on the corpus, a keep/drop decision and a passing level differential.

Receipt write cost of jet check (#6629): A jet check of a small program returns within 1 s of its result being known, even on a contended disk, and its receipt stays durable. Today one check writes .jet/receipts and records as 4 objects plus a records index, each made durable separately: 0.35 s of compile, then 49-84 s of fsync under lane load on $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT (after_close_reader, 11-07). Make the write cost one barrier per check: the objects first, then one fsync of the directory and index, or the write handed off with the next command waiting on it. A measured row pins the time under write load, and a kill during the write leaves either the old index or the complete new one. (was #6629 c2)

cards.title: Compile-time surfaces leave prefix @ so @ can mean a live link
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-09-28: use `@` for checked live links (D-MEMREF1) and migrate completely away from `@` for compile time. The owner asked for a full suite of questions, including alternatives such as dunder names.

Inventory of current `@` uses (Syntax.rs, syntax-decisions.md, Examples):
1. Compile-time values and blocks: `@name :: expr`, `@ { }`, `#Static @LIMIT`. D-PREP-SURFACE2 already moves these to `prep { }` plus ordinary names; #3505 and #3520 own that cutover.
2. Compile-time branch and loop: `@if`, `@loop`, and declaration templates (S57, D-STRUCT-ONCE1).
3. Metadata roots: `@TYPE`, `@FUNCTION`, `@METHOD`, `@CLOSURE`, `@PROGRAM`, `@PACKAGE`, `@SOURCE`, `@VALUE`, `@TYPES`, and `@PHASE` (D-META-REFLECT2, D-PREP-SURFACE2).
4. Fact members: `T.@layout`, `@name`, `@fields`, `@range`, `@dimension`, `@measure`, `@exactness`, `value.@origin`, and `f.@effects`, plus the overlapping `T.reflect()` (D-LAYOUT-FACTS1, D-FACT-READ1, D-TRACK-ORIGIN1).
5. Build facts: `@build.os`, `profile`, `package.name`/`version`, `settings.*`, and `stamp.*` (D-ONCE-AT1, D-CONF-MODULE1).
6. Const generic binder: `<@N: Int>` (D-CONSTGEN1, #3505).
7. Fences: `@[ … ]@` (D-EACH1, D-FENCE-GLYPH1, D-FENCE-RANGE1).
8. Compile-time function marker: `@fn` (D-FOUND-LITERAL1).
9. Non-compile-time uses: infix package refs `target@provider#version`, `host@root`, and the command home files `@run.jet`, `@build.jet`, `@dev.jet`, and `@test.jet` (D-JPK-REF1, D-JPK-OSHOST1, card #1866). D-ONCE-AT1 also reserved an infix 'at a machine' form.

The ballots here pick the family and each item's spelling. After ratification, one coherent cutover migrates the parser, sema, formatter, grammars, diagnostics, examples, and spec together (greenfield rule). It sequences with #3505/#3520 and the self-hosting port (#218).
cards.plan:
## Goal
Take every compile-time meaning off prefix `@`, so that in code `@` means only a D-MEMREF1 checked live link. Do it in one cutover of parser, sema, formatter, grammars, teaching diagnostics, examples and spec.

## Current state
- Ratified and landed: D-PREP-SURFACE2, D-PREP-BRANCH1, D-PREP-FN1 (`prep { }`, `prep if/loop/fn`), D-FENCE2 (`<: … :>`), D-CONSTGEN2 and D-AT-INFIX1. The Jet parser teaches E0388 for the retired `@if/@loop/@fn/@ { }` (`Compiler/JetParser/Source/Parser/Statements.jet:374-392`).
- Still open with recommended option A: D-COMPILER-NS1 (the family: plain word `prep` plus a `compiler.` namespace), D-META-ROOT3 (`compiler.type/function/method/closure/program/package_info/source/value/types/phase`, marked facts become record fields, `T.reflect()` retires, `reflect.of(value)` stays), D-BUILD-FACT2 (build facts) and D-NAME-SPLICE1 (computed declaration names and declaration metadata).
- Remaining prefix-`@` code paths in the Jet parser: `@name ::` comptime constants (`Parser/Entry.jet:148-150`, `Parser/Items.jet:994-998`), `@` marker metadata (`Parser/Declarations/Markers.jet:54-58`), and the `@`-headed prep recovery arms (`Statements.jet:233-236, 399, 431`; `Declarations/Markers.jet:150`). Metadata roots (`@TYPE` …), fact members (`T.@layout` …) and `@build.*` still exist as described in the card inventory.
- Non-compile-time infix uses (`target@provider#version`, `host@root`, `@run.jet` home files) are out of scope and keep their meaning.

## Changes (written for option A on all four ballots)
1. After ratification, record the complete old-to-new mapping in `crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs`, `Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md` and the Jet syntax registry under `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry`.
2. `Compiler/JetLexer` and `Compiler/JetParser`: parse `compiler.` roots as ordinary calls, marked facts as fields, build facts per D-BUILD-FACT2 and computed names per D-NAME-SPLICE1. Retired `@` forms are not Jet syntax and get no teaching diagnostic; E0388's teaching is removed under #4148 c4. Prefix `@place` parses as a D-MEMREF1 link.
3. `Compiler/JetSema`: resolve the `compiler.` namespace through the prelude (`#NoPrelude` opts out) and route it to the existing metadata path (#3520).
4. Mirror the parser in `crates/jet-parser` so the bootstrap still parses the corpus. Migrate the formatter, `jet devtools grammars`, `Examples/`, `Core/`, `Docs/` and UI snapshots in the same commit.

## Proof
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/at_compile_time_retired.jet cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots` passes.
- `cargo test --test selfhost_parser` passes.
- Jet slice check: `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` reports no diagnostic in `Compiler/JetLexer` or `Compiler/JetParser` (map through `~/.cache/jet-luna/compiler-bootstrap/compiler.map.json`).
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=comptime cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` and `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=reflection cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` both pass with identical AOT and `jet run` output.
- `jet devtools grammars` regenerates with no remaining `@` compile-time rule.

## Batch
`batch-jetc-front`: a lexer/parser surface cutover plus the Rust parser mirror.

## Dependencies
Owner ratification of D-COMPILER-NS1 first, then D-META-ROOT3, D-BUILD-FACT2 and D-NAME-SPLICE1 (recommend A for all four). Sequence with #3505 and #3520, which own overlapping paths, and with the #218 port.

cards.title: Core HTTP client in Jet, including checked header names and values
cards.body:
Owner 2026-09-28: the standard library must be written in Jet under Core/; port whatever the Rust Prelude files still own. Evidence: ~/.cache/jet-luna/jetpack-port/prelude-core-gap.json (Opus 5.5 study, file:line citations). Move every semantic item (validation, defaults, formats, protocol logic, limits, error meaning) into the named Core/*.jet home; keep only policy-free provider leaves in Rust (raw syscalls, socket I/O, vetted TLS/SQLite/Parquet/Wasmtime engines). Migrate every route (AOT emit, JIT, interpreter, web where applicable) to call the one Jet meaning (I9) and delete the duplicated Rust policy in the same cutover. Proof needs a compiler build that embeds the edited Core sources, so this is blocked by #3663 (master does not compile) and #3591.

Files: crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Prelude/HTTP.rs.
Homes: Core/http/{client,http,h1,h2,hpack,cookie}.jet. Resolve the retry divergence (Jet retries PUT/DELETE, Rust only safe methods) to one documented rule. Delete dead client-handle builder code and JetHTTPAmbientDeadline::push if no caller remains.

**Goal.** The HTTP client's meaning moves into Core:
- HTTP/1.1 framing, HTTP/2 framing and HPACK
- cookies with public-suffix rules
- redirects, proxies, pool/per-origin limits, DNS TTL, phase timeouts
- header/form/multipart encoding and retries

It lives in `Core/http/{client,http,h1,h2,hpack,cookie}.jet`. Rust keeps socket I/O, TLS (rustls) and gzip inflate leaves only.

**Current state.**
- `Core/http/` has `client.jet` (518 lines), `http.jet` (1227) and `server.jet` (91). There is no `h1`/`h2`/`hpack`/`cookie.jet`.
- `crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Prelude/HTTP.rs` (5534 lines) holds the policy. The card body lists 18 semantic items with line ranges, which this plan keeps:
  - ambient deadline :18-67, limit constants :68-78, pool :104-276
  - client builders :283-700, cookies/PSL :704-1118
  - H2 :1180-1660/:3915-4224, DNS cache :1746-1785, PEM :1842-1941
  - timeouts :2088-2166, send parts :2167-2530, forbidden headers :2531-2588
  - form/multipart :2589-2644/:5413-5534, redirects :2645-3020, proxy :3021-3078
  - H1 write :3180-3511, head parse :3774-3914, body framing :4225-4562, HPACK :5003-5412
- Retry divergence: `Core/http/client.jet:232` `retryable_method` retries GET/HEAD/OPTIONS/TRACE/PUT/DELETE, while Rust retries safe methods only.
- `Core/http/http.jet` already has `valid_header_name`/`has_ctl` (:1043/:1051), `form_encode`/`query_encode` (:716-769) and `parse_response`/`content_length` (:474/:870).
- #3663 was fixed in 6fc6f3862.

**Changes (one sub-module per patch).**
1. `h1.jet` (new): request encoding, upload body writing, the streaming head reader, and `BodyFraming` (content-length/chunked/close) readers over a byte-stream leaf.
2. `hpack.jet` (new): static table, integer/string/Huffman codec and the decoder dynamic table. `h2.jet` (new): frame read/write, connection settings/flow control and the response body reader.
3. `cookie.jet` (new): `CookieJar`, date parse, domain/path match, and the PSL `registrable_domain` over a generated constant table (F2).
4. `client.jet`:
   - pool/origin limits, the DNS TTL cache and phase timeouts
   - redirect follow with body-replay rules, and proxy/no_proxy selection
   - reconcile the limit constants with the existing `C_MAX_*`
5. `http.jet`: the forbidden-request-header list and multipart encoding.
6. Retry rule, kept as the one documented rule: RFC 9110 idempotent methods (current Jet `retryable_method`), and only when the body is replayable and no response bytes arrived. The Rust safe-only branch is deleted. Document it in the `client.jet` doc comment.
7. PEM helpers move to `Core/net/tls.jet`, shared with #3666.
8. Delete the ported Rust, the dead client-handle builders and `JetHTTPAmbientDeadline::push` if uncalled, plus the Jet-owned `core.http` dispatcher rows. Regenerate the tables.

**Proof.**
- The commands in add_criteria.
- `jet test Compiler --profile cases http/` and `cargo test --test http_dependency_audit`: pass.
- A perf cell is required only if the matched networking battery covers the client. Rerun it and keep the Rust route on any loss.

**Batch.** `batch-core-net`: Core http/net source and its Rust Prelude twin, needing one build and the net retest.

**Dependencies.** None open. It shares the PEM parser with #3666, and whichever lands first owns `Core/net/tls.jet` PEM.

cards.title: Project jobs: core.process, job graph, and job parameters broken on the default tier
cards.body:
Three owner-reported defects (2026-09-28) plus three found while fixing them. Fixed in the working tree by pip; not yet committed.

1. `use core.process` failed to compile (10 errors in `Core/process/process.jet`). Private helpers called from `which` (`?String`) and `getstatusoutput` (`!IOError`) had implicit `!Err` contracts. Fix: mark the infallible helpers `!Never`, matching Core convention; regenerated only the `core.process` row of `crates/jet-foundation/src/CoreModuleExports.rs`.
2. `after:` was ignored on `jet jobs` / `jet run -- <job>` (default and `--interpret`). The host swapped the entry point and never ran the Prelude job graph (I9 divergence from AOT). Fix: `Source/Interpreter.rs` `run_job_graph` checks every job in the root's closure, then hands the Prelude `jet_job_dispatch_specs` one spec row per MIR job with a host invoke/validate trampoline. The Prelude owns order, skip, cache, cwd, cancellation, and events. Root argv is validated before any predecessor runs (`jet_jit::validate_entry_argv`).
3. Jobs with plain parameters (`fn migrate(to: String{"latest"})`) were listed but failed with E1321 at invocation. Fix: `Driver::swap_entry_point` gives such a job a compiler-generated `#[CLI, Decode]` record with the same field names, types, and defaults as the checked job schema.
4. Found: bare `#Job` (no marker args) produced no MIR job row, so it could not be a graph predecessor. Fix: `artifact_plan::lower_job` uses default metadata.
5. Found: job argument rows had empty help and a re-spelled `Type::Named("String")` type, so any `#Job(...)` with parameters hit a MIR legality ICE on every tier. Fix: rows take the lowered parameter type and `#CLI`-field shape rules; a single `#CLI` record parameter uses the record's field inputs like a record entry.
6. Found: AOT job wrappers never used the record decode path. Fix: `MIRRust::emit_jobs` passes `record_inputs` for a single `#CLI` record parameter. UNVERIFIED: every AOT build currently ICEs (`::jet_jit::SourceSharedInterop`), owned by another stream.

Also noticed, not fixed: the embedded copies of `core.reactive` and `core.web.table` in `CoreModuleExports.rs` are stale against committed Core sources, and `crates/jet-foundation/build.rs` only hashes `Core.jet`, so this staleness is not caught.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Land the working-tree fixes for project jobs (`use core.process`, the `after:` job graph, scalar job parameters, bare `#Job`, job argument rows, and AOT record decode). Then prove `jetpack_tasks` and AOT job-dispatch parity.

## Current state
- The fixes are uncommitted in the working tree, touching `Core/process/process.jet`, `Source/Interpreter.rs`, `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/mod.rs`, `crates/jet-foundation/src/CoreModuleExports.rs` and `tests/jetpack_tasks.rs`.
- `Source/Interpreter.rs:749` `run_job_graph` hands the Prelude `jet_job_dispatch_specs` one row per MIR job.
- `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/mod.rs:1953, 3582` `strip_source_shared_interop_jit` removes the AOT `::jet_jit::SourceSharedInterop` ICE region.
- `tests/jetpack_tasks.rs:201` `jet_jobs_after_runs_predecessors_and_scalar_args` exists. Criteria 1-3 are met.
- Rust job lowering: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/artifact_plan.rs:1136` `lower_job`, `TIR/mir.rs:2452` `lower_job_argument`, and `MIRRust.rs:10746` `emit_jobs`.
- The Jet compiler still has fix 5's bug. `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/JobTestArtifacts.jet:31-48` `jet_codegen_lower_job_argument` re-spells the type as `Type.Named(argument.ty)` and emits empty `help`. `:102` `jet_codegen_lower_job_fact` needs checking for the bare `#Job` default-metadata case (fix 4).
- Also noticed and not owned here: the stale embedded `core.reactive` and `core.web.table` rows in `CoreModuleExports.rs`, and `crates/jet-foundation/build.rs` hashing only `Core.jet`.

## Changes
1. Integrate the working-tree fix as one commit, owned only by this card's paths.
2. Jet compiler mirror, in `JobTestArtifacts.jet`: argument rows take the lowered parameter type and `#CLI` field shape/help. A single `#CLI` record parameter uses the record's field inputs. A bare `#Job` produces a job row with default metadata.
3. AOT: `MIRRust::emit_jobs` passes `record_inputs` for a single `#CLI` record parameter, as already in the tree.
4. `tests/jetpack_tasks.rs`: add `jet_build_job_dispatch_matches_default_and_interpreter`. Build the `after:` + scalar-parameter fixture with `jet build`, then dispatch `seed` through the binary's emitted job entry. Its output must match `jet jobs seed` and `jet run --interpret -- seed`. It covers three cases: predecessor order, stop on a failing predecessor, and E1331 with exit 2 for a bad root argument before any predecessor runs.

## Proof
- `jet test Compiler --profile cases jetpack_tasks/` passes all tests (criterion 4).
- `jet test Compiler --profile cases jetpack_tasks/jet_build_job_dispatch_matches_default_and_interpreter` passes (criterion 5).

## Batch
`batch-host-runtime`: host job dispatch plus AOT/run/interpreter parity.

## Dependencies

cards.title: Jet sync engine: Convex/Linear-grade local-first data with proven query, mutation, and action kinds
cards.body:
Owner note (2026-09-28): "I want a jet-native tool that functions like convexdb as an excellent, world class sync engine" (linked video https://youtu.be/pRf8_40EDtM is Tom Delalande's Linear case study, not a Convex video).

Harvest (mine-for-jet report mine-for-jet-2026-09-28):
- Linear (video 4:12-8:26): the client downloads the workspace once, then every read and write is local; one observable state re-renders views; the engine turns local changes into transactions and streams remote changes over a socket, so local and remote changes look identical; the server accepts or rejects each transaction and the client rolls back on reject; large workspaces forced lazy loading and a partial bootstrap; engineers can switch sync off to prototype locally; there is no plug-and-play engine, and it takes several full-time engineers to maintain.
- Convex (https://docs.convex.dev/functions/runtimes): queries and mutations must be deterministic (seeded Math.random, Date.now frozen per call) so the system can retry and re-run them; non-deterministic work such as fetch lives only in actions.

Jet already ratified most of the mechanism: D-LIVEQUERY1 (footprint-tracked live queries over -[DB.Read]> functions, #Transact write-set invalidation, pushes to Signal<T>), D-EFFDBREAD1, D-SYNC1 (CRDT values over the live channel), D-DBPOLICY1 (row policies below app code), D-DX-QUERY1 (optimistic mutation with rollback), D-DX-SERVERFN1 (typed calls derived from App actions), D-QUERY-LIVE1 (incremental maintenance). Jet's advantage Convex cannot copy: effect rows can prove at compile time that a query only reads, that a mutation is replay-safe, and that only actions touch the network; the same Jet validation code runs on client and server (I9).

Current state is far from that: the shipped example does not compile, Core/app is string-keyed, and app/web duplicate the surface (#3700, #3701).
cards.plan:
**Goal**
A Jet-native local-first sync engine at Convex/Linear grade (owner note 2026-09-28: "a jet-native tool that functions like convexdb as an excellent, world class sync engine"). It covers client cache and partial bootstrap, local reads and writes as transactions, server accept or reject with rollback, socket fan-out, an offline queue and a local-only mode. Query, mutation and action are compiler-checked effect classes.

**Current state**
- Ratified mechanism: D-LIVEQUERY1 (footprint-tracked live queries over `-[DB.Read]>`, `#Transact` invalidation, `Signal<T>` push), D-EFFDBREAD1, D-SYNC1 (CRDT values), D-DBPOLICY1, D-DX-QUERY1 (optimistic mutation plus rollback), D-DX-SERVERFN1 and D-QUERY-LIVE1.
- Code: Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/Database.jet:31-41 tags `query`/`query_one`/`live` as `DB.Read` and `execute` as `DB.Write`. Effect checks are in Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Effects/Checks.jet. Core/sync/sync.jet exists. Core/app is string-keyed, and the D-LIVEQUERY1 example does not compile (#3700). app and core.web duplicate the surface (#3701).
- Harvest: Linear (4:12-8:26 of https://youtu.be/pRf8_40EDtM): one bootstrap, then local reads and writes, identical local and remote change paths, accept or reject with rollback, lazy partial bootstrap, and sync-off prototyping. Convex runtimes: deterministic queries and mutations (seeded rng, frozen clock); only actions do non-deterministic I/O.

**Changes**
1. After #3700 and #3701, write Docs/proposals/sync-engine.md covering cache and bootstrap, transaction upload, accept/reject, rollback, socket fan-out, offline queue and local-only mode, each tied to the decisions above (criterion 1).
2. Effect classes (no new syntax): a query is a fn whose inferred row ⊆ {DB.Read}; a mutation is a `#Transact` fn with no Net, Exec or irreversible effect; an action is anything else. Add the checks in Effects/Checks.jet, register two diagnostics in Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/DiagnosticRows.jet with UI fixtures tests/ui/sync_query_writes.jet and sync_mutation_calls_net.jet, and mirror them in the Rust sema only as far as the shipped binary needs.
3. Ballots before implementing each: frozen clock and seeded rng inside queries and mutations vs explicit Clock/Rng injection (D-DET1); the concurrent-mutation conflict policy (serializable retry vs CRDT merge); client persistence defaults.
4. Add Examples/features/web/sync_two_clients plus its golden: two clients, one edits offline, both reconnect and see each other's change, and the server rejects one write, which rolls back.
5. Add a gauntlet cell under Tools/gauntlet against Convex and one other engine before any battery claim, under the strict performance gate.

**Proof**
- `jet test Compiler --profile ui sync_`: both snapshots match.
- `jet test Compiler --profile golden web/sync_two_clients`: passes on O0, O1 and O2. `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test web_build -- sync_two_clients`: passes on the web tier.

**Batch**
batch-jetc-sema: the first buildable slice is the effect-class checks. The proposal and ballots come before it.

**Dependencies**
#3700 (live-query example and ICE) and #3701 (app/web owner ballot).

cards.title: Diagnostic readability sweep: rewrite every active diagnostic in plain words (Opus 5.5 workers)
cards.body:
What is wrong: many diagnostics explain grammar or internal state instead of
the learner's problem. A census of crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/
Diagnostics.jet on 2026-09-28 found 813 active rows, of which:

- 218 have the placeholder Why "The registered <stage> rule applies here";
- 297 have a What that repeats the internal Meaning verbatim;
- 287 put decision IDs (D-…, S…) in user-facing what/why/fix text.

Example (report F17, probe p08): a function that returns only for `n > 0`
and `n < 0` gets E0114: "its final statement produces no value … statements
and semicolon-terminated expressions yield unit". Ordinary Jet has no
semicolons, "unit" is jargon, and the message never says "when n is 0,
`sign` reaches the end without a value".

Research basis: Becker et al. 2019 guidelines (readability, low cognitive
load, context, positive tone, hints, logical argument, right time); Barik et
al. 2018 (argument structure plus a resolution); Ko et al. 2004
(understanding barriers were 34/38 insurmountable).

Owner direction: a comprehensive sweep, implemented by Claude Opus 5.5
(`opus-worker` agent). The orchestrator integrates.

Owner instruction (chat, 2026-09-28): the owner reviewed the learnability report and directed that this fix be carded at P0. This card records that direction; it is not a ballot.

Probe sources live in the report's Appendix A. They ran from a directory with its own package.jet granting [IO, Mem.Alloc], on the working-tree debug binary of 2026-09-28 13:07 (HEAD 68e1f8fb plus another stream's uncommitted compiler edits). Re-run each probe on a fresh build before starting; a probe that no longer reproduces is recorded on the card, not silently dropped.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Owner-directed P0 (2026-09-28, learnability report F17). Every active diagnostic reads in plain words:
- **What** names the learner's specific problem, using the names in their code.
- **Why** gives the reason in one or two plain sentences, with no placeholder.
- **Fix** gives a concrete edit or command.
- No internal vocabulary: decision IDs, constant names, "unit", "source bytes", byte offsets, key=value dumps, stage names. That material moves to `jet explain CODE --verbose` and `--json`.

The rubric is enforced so the sweep cannot regress.

## Current state
- The authority is `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Diagnostics.jet`. `Compiler/Bootstrap/generate-diagnostic-rows.mjs:9-10` generates `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/DiagnosticRows.jet` from it.
- The 2026-09-28 census found 813 active rows: 218 with the placeholder Why "The registered <stage> rule applies here" (for example `Diagnostics.jet:7-8`, E0001/E0002), 297 whose What repeats Meaning, and 287 with decision IDs in human text.
- E0114 (probe p08) still says "its final statement produces no value … statements and semicolon-terminated expressions yield unit" (`tests/ui/missing_return.stderr`, `tests/ui/total_guard_missing_value.stderr`). It is produced only in Rust (`crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Registration.rs:969`, `CheckerCore/blocks.rs:199`); JetSema has no E0114.
- `tests/diagnostics_format.rs` already checks row completeness and sentence case (`:13-75`), but not placeholder text or decision IDs.
- Rows owned by other open P0 cards are sequenced first: #3715 (E0121), #3718 (authority errors) and #3719 (unclosed delimiter).

## Changes
1. **Docs.** Write the rubric into `Docs/spec/diagnostics.md`.
2. **Validator.** Add `every_active_diagnostic_reads_in_plain_words` to `tests/diagnostics_format.rs`, and apply the same checks in `generate-diagnostic-rows.mjs` so generation fails on a violation.
3. **Rewrite.** Rewrite the rows in `Diagnostics.jet` using disjoint code-range lanes run by `opus-worker` (Claude Opus 5.5), with one integration owner. Update the dynamic message builders in `crates/jet-parser` and `crates/jet-sema` that fill those rows, then regenerate `DiagnosticRows.jet`.
4. **E0114.** Add E0114 to JetSema (the final-statement check in the block/return analysis) and have it name the uncovered path's condition. Mirror the path-naming in `crates/jet-sema/.../blocks.rs` for the shipped binary.
5. **Snapshots.** Re-bless every affected UI snapshot one fixture at a time (`JET_UI_FILTER=<f> UPDATE_EXPECT=<f>`, with `UPDATE_EXPECT_REASON`). The orchestrator reviews each change as text.
6. **Probes.** Re-run the report's Appendix A probes on a fresh build. A probe that no longer reproduces is recorded on the card.

## Proof
- `cargo test --test diagnostics_format`: all tests pass, including the new rubric test, which is the census. Log its counts on the card.
- `cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots` and `cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots lint_snapshots`: pass after reviewed re-blessing.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/missing_return.jet cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots`: pass.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh`: exit 0.
- Every lane returns `Tools/agent/lane-check.sh` `CHECK OK`, and the lanes are listed on the card.

## Batch
`batch-jetc-sema`: diagnostic registry text and sema message builders, proven by the UI/format suites in one retest pass.

## Dependencies
#3715, #3718 and #3719 (all P0, ready) own overlapping rows and land first.

cards.title: Last use moves everywhere; kept parameters inferred; x.move() and x.copy() are the exact pins
cards.body: D-COPY-DEFAULT1=A (ratified; owner comment: 'Compiler chooses if unmarked, programmer can manually put sigils where desired for exact. full control'). Parent #3741. Evidence: probe p34/p35 — storing a read parameter deep-copies even at the caller's last use (~20% slower builder).
cards.plan:

cards.title: Principle: a value can owe a transition (one debt concept for must-use, single-use, and tasks)
cards.body:
Elegance principle hunt, 2026-10-01. Jet checks several kinds of value debt with separate rules, words, and escapes: `#MustUse` (E0419, discard `.drop("reason")`), `#SingleUse` (E0140-E0143, discard `consume(x)` inside `#Unsafe("reason")`), and a bound task that owes a join (L1101, discharge `.join()` or `.detach()`). Ratified D-CONC-UNIT1=A already moved tasks onto the single-use obligation checker. Typestate and taint already share one flow store, `Facts

` (`crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/FlowFacts.rs:1-80`). `GateKind` already has `DutyDrop` and `StateTransition` (`crates/jet-foundation/src/Authority.rs:671-672`). Users cannot declare a debt for their own types. Closed-book prediction test: 6 hit, 0 near, 0 miss. Owner choice: ballot D-OWES1.
cards.plan: After ratification: add the ratified debt declaration, express #MustUse, #SingleUse, and task join as instances, unify the diagnostic sentence, and make `.drop("reason")` the single abandon gate per the ratified option.

Vale's answer is that the callee inherits the duty. Also relevant: Vale's linear key (insert returns a key that proves the entry exists; remove consumes it) and the observation that 'remember to' comments mark missing debts.

cards.title: One lane type: width-parameterized and scalable SIMD vectors
cards.body:
Owner request: start from what hardware can do and turn it into high-level constructs, keeping both a bottom-up and a top-down path. Mojo defines every scalar and vector as one library type `SIMD[dtype, width]` (`Int = Scalar[DType.int]`, Modular commit 99e3a880 `std/simd.mojo:115-240,443-468`).

Today Jet has a closed family of named lanes (D-SIMD3=B: F32x4, F32x8, F64x2, F64x4, I32x4, I32x8, I64x2, I64x4, U8x16, U8x32; Examples/features/lowlevel/simd_wide.jet). A width cannot be a parameter, so generic code over "the widest native width" cannot be written, and vector-length-agnostic hardware (Arm SVE, RISC-V V) has no spelling. Const generics (D-CONSTGEN1=A, #3505) make a parameterized lane type possible.

Ballot D-LANES1 decides the lane surface.
cards.plan: Owner decides D-LANES1. Implementation waits on #3505 const generics; then define the lane type in Core over compiler intrinsics, migrate the named family in one cutover, and add SVE/RVV lowering where the target supports it.

cards.title: Use newer CPU instructions in one binary: multiversioned functions and typed intrinsics
cards.body:
Owner request: leverage what hardware can do now (bottom-up), give experts direct access to machine instructions, and stay forward-facing for new hardware.

Today D-FFI-ASM-CPU1=B builds for the target baseline and needs explicit CPU flags for newer instructions; a shipped binary cannot use AVX-512 when present and fall back otherwise. Experts can reach instructions only through audited `#FFI(asm)`; the compiler-only `__core_intrinsic` namespace (D-CORE-CALL1) is closed to users. Prior art: Rust `#[target_feature]` + `is_x86_feature_detected!` + `core::arch`; GCC `target_clones`; Google Highway dynamic dispatch; Mojo `CompilationTarget` queries and `comptime if`; Odin `@(enable_target_feature=...)` and `base:intrinsics` (265 procedures).

Ballot D-CPU-DISPATCH1 decides how code opts into newer instructions.
cards.plan: Owner decides D-CPU-DISPATCH1. Then add the chosen target-feature function form, a per-process feature probe in the Prelude, safe typed intrinsics in Core for the chosen ISAs, and dispatch on every tier.

cards.title: Co-editing one program from text and Canvas (EYG shared-tree lesson)
cards.body:
Owner request: EYG sends the AST over the wire, which could let a text editor and a visual blueprint editor edit the same program at once; Mojo has no traditional AST and parses straight to MLIR. Take the best of both: a lighter compiler and blueprint-style editing.

EYG's IR is a closed node list encoded as DAG-JSON with content-addressed references; text is one optional parser (commit 75f09475, `packages/gleam_ir/src/eyg/ir/tree.gleam:15-44`, `spec/README.md:44-92`). Mojo's parser emits the MLIR `lit` dialect (MojoCompilerWalkthrough.md:136-138). Jet parses text to an AST without lossless trivia (formatter re-emits canonical syntax), Canvas edits go through source transactions (D-CANVAS-RAD1=A), and no stable node identity crosses the LSP boundary.

Ballot D-PROGRAM-FORM1 decides the shared program form.
cards.plan: Owner decides D-PROGRAM-FORM1. If A wins: on a stale Canvas revision, resolve the edit's anchors in the newest revision, replay, format, re-check, publish atomically; report anchor conflicts. The self-hosted front-end shape (Mojo's no-AST lesson) stays an internal implementation choice.

cards.title: C header import depth: read real headers with a full C front end
cards.body:
Owner request: use Zig's cross-compatibility as a wedge: import C headers directly, act as a drop-in C/C++ compiler, build foreign projects in Jetpack, and export C ABI libraries.

Today `jet cc`/`jet c++` exist and use the pinned Jetpack toolchain (`crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs:1333-1349`); `#Export(c)` exists (Examples/features/packages/library_loadable); foreign builds are on #1347; cross toolchains on #758/#1058/#1060. The weak link is header import: `crates/jet-pkg-model/src/CBind.rs:1-12` is a focused std-only parser that maps scalars, strings, pointers, slices, and layout records, and skips the rest. Zig's `@cImport`/`translate-c` reads real headers through a full C front end, including macros, unions, bitfields, function pointers, and variadics; Zig probe Z6 cross-compiled C to Windows and AArch64-musl from one host.

Ballot D-CIMPORT1 decides the header engine.
cards.plan: Owner decides D-CIMPORT1. Then extend the binder, run it against a corpus (zlib, sqlite3, libcurl, SDL3) for every supported target, and report unmapped declarations with registered diagnostics.

cards.title: Portable sandboxed app format: what Jet ships to run anywhere (Docker/Nix/WebAssembly replacement)
cards.body:
Owner direction (2026-10-01): Jet should be portable and better than WebAssembly, and replace Docker and Nix. EYG ships a checked program and lets the host supply effects.

Jet today: native binaries (trusted code), OCI images projected from environments (D-ENV-IMAGE1=A), wasm32-wasip2 (D-WASISRV1=A, #1914), sandbox components (--target=sandbox), Wasmtime plugins (D-PLUGIN1=A, D-DEP-WASM1=A), Hangar store and build-step sandbox (D-JPK-SANDBOX2=D). Output.Bundle is the closed catch-all kind for distributables (D-ECO-OUTPUT-KINDS1=A). The portable-platform proposal (JPM/1, JPH/1) is unratified with no prior card.

Ballot D-PORTABLE1 decides the portable app form of Bundle.
cards.plan: Owner decides D-PORTABLE1. Then specify the .jetapp layout, host selection, confinement reporting (confined/verified/TRUSTED), and grant storage; paired cell against an OCI container and plain wasmtime on startup, size, and throughput.

Folded #4762 "Extensible hardware requirements with trusted scan, target facts and pre-entry admission" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root task step of parent #4195 (Portable sandboxed app format: what Jet ships to); 1 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: D-HOST-CAPS1=A Proposes Core Hardware, HardwareKind, HardwareRequirement, HardwareProbe and ScanContext as specified in the explainer. Hardware contains main memory, storage and typed device entries. Target gains hardware; every Output gains target, requires and uses. Package-defined kinds use pure type-owned satisfies/coarse methods; scan probes are separately trust-granted. $build.hardware shares D-CONF's typed fact plane and merge law; $build.cpu remains the CPU entry. Host observations, grants and kind/probe package identities determine launch admission/cache identity, never a producer's asserted facts. Free amounts are checked before each GPU job. Implementation areas: Core hardware typ

Independent witness (Blow, cKyrT8OVbDo 00:00-09:40): untrusted plugins should share structured data without serialize/parse, get write permission only to chosen memory without a separate process, and a plugin that crashes inside shared lock-free code after incrementing a counter leaves the host unrecoverable; containers exist because the OS stopped reliably rerunning programs; wanted: one portable, sandboxed, backend-neutral instruction format. Today D-PLUGIN1=A / D-DEP-WASM1=A accept copied boundary values as a loss; the portable proposal (Docs/proposals/jetpack/portable-platform-specification.md H-ISP-002, L-11a, CV-15; unratified) already specifies sealed zero-copy and trap termination, which this corroborates. Research lead for C2 measurement (not verified): in-process hardware write isolation (x86 protection keys, Arm permission overlays) for verified guests, with known limits (few keys, no speculative-read protection). Local IPC culture serializes to JSON even on one machine (CK-07): include a large structured value crossing the boundary in the C2 measurement against wasm and OCI.
All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.
