criteria.text: A compile-throughput cell measures `jet check` and `jet build` (O0 and --release) of a representative million-line corpus in lines per second on the reference machine, recorded every wave.
Each compiler phase has a lines/s budget, and the budgets compose to 30M lines per second end to end; every phase over its budget names its root on a card.
End metric: `jet build` of the corpus runs at 30M lines per second or faster, with output identical to the slower build.

Guards walk the tree once. A tests/guards run builds one shared file index of the tree in process (each path with its kind and size, and contents read on demand and held only for that run), walked once and handed to every guard. None of the 43 guards that walk the tree walks it itself. Acceptance: the guards pass unchanged, a source scan proves no guard calls a directory walk, and the 4-shard tests/guards run takes under 30 s cold on a dev export, down from about 75–90 s, measured before and after. Owner: Lander2, after the Land.jet census SUB.

Plan step 0, stop the bleeding: every train records its compiler build's CPU-s and per-phase seconds against the previous seed and fails past +10% (the train speed gate). The 2026-11-11 regression (sema.bodies 5.0 -> 52.1 s, comptime.precheck 0.3 -> 19.2 s between a0.0.43 and seed-t22) is bisected to its commits and fixed at the root, and the #6527 slide from a0_021 (53.6K lines/s, 54 CPU-s) is undone. Gate: at least 55K lines/s and at most 60 µs of CPU per line. Measured by the c1 cell: cold and uncached, `jet build` of Compiler plus Core on the reference machine (32 hardware threads), n=3 median, recording wall, user+sys CPU-s, CPU-ns per line, average parallelism (CPU-s / wall) and peak RSS. Output is identical to the previous stage's build (chain fixed point plus goldens).

Plan step 1, use the machine: average parallelism goes from about 5 to at least 24 of 32 threads. Modules stream through the pipeline as soon as their dependencies are checked (no phase-wide barriers), comptime runs in parallel, work queues are wait-free, and the allocator keeps per-thread arenas so threads take no global lock. 32 threads beat 16. Gate: at least 400K lines/s. Measured by the c1 cell: cold and uncached, `jet build` of Compiler plus Core on the reference machine (32 hardware threads), n=3 median, recording wall, user+sys CPU-s, CPU-ns per line, average parallelism (CPU-s / wall) and peak RSS. Output is identical to the previous stage's build (chain fixed point plus goldens).

Plan step 2, data-oriented core: every compiler name, symbol, type and function is an interned u32 id (no String keys in maps). AST, types and IR are flat struct-of-arrays columns, compiler data lives in per-phase arenas freed in bulk, and compiler data carries no reference counts. Peak RSS falls under 1 GB (#5910). Gate: at most 5 µs of CPU per line and at least 5M lines/s. Measured by the c1 cell: cold and uncached, `jet build` of Compiler plus Core on the reference machine (32 hardware threads), n=3 median, recording wall, user+sys CPU-s, CPU-ns per line, average parallelism (CPU-s / wall) and peak RSS. Output is identical to the previous stage's build (chain fixed point plus goldens).

Plan step 3, fused per-function pipeline: each function goes parse -> check -> lower -> select -> encode while its data is still in cache, with no whole-program intermediate copy, and a direct executable image writer replaces the object-then-link path. Gate: at most 1.5 µs of CPU per line and at least 20M lines/s. Measured by the c1 cell: cold and uncached, `jet build` of Compiler plus Core on the reference machine (32 hardware threads), n=3 median, recording wall, user+sys CPU-s, CPU-ns per line, average parallelism (CPU-s / wall) and peak RSS. Output is identical to the previous stage's build (chain fixed point plus goldens).

Plan step 4, the compiler compiled well. Starts only once the language is mostly stable (the major syntax, semantics and Core churn is done), so tuning isn't wiped out by later cutovers: Jet's own release code generation (register allocation, inlining, bounds-check hoisting, SIMD selection) and a SIMD lexer at 1 GB/s or more close the gap to hand-written machine code on the compiler's five hottest loops, each with an asm-parity ceiling cell (Tools/perf/asm-parity). Every gain is general, applies to all generated code (owner, 2026-10-23), and is proven on a second program. Gate: at most 1 µs of CPU per line and at least 30M lines/s end to end, which is c3. Measured by the c1 cell: cold and uncached, `jet build` of Compiler plus Core on the reference machine (32 hardware threads), n=3 median, recording wall, user+sys CPU-s, CPU-ns per line, average parallelism (CPU-s / wall) and peak RSS. Output is identical to the previous stage's build (chain fixed point plus goldens).

Running one test costs about that test's own time. The testkit's fixed startup cost is measured phase by phase (building or loading the kit, compiling the harness, scanning the corpora, loading Core, starting workers), each phase is listed with its time, and everything that is not the test itself is cut, cached or done once, so a run filtered to one golden entry at --jobs 1 finishes within 0.5 s of that entry's own compile-and-run time. Today a single golden entry pays about 35 s of fixed kit overhead (2026-11-04 gate run: cli_args.jet 3.1 s and fidelity.jet 5.5 s alone, plus about 35 s each run). This also speeds every agent's A/B proof run.

Jet's test runner is the fastest of any language, shown by a peer-matched cell in the canonical performance manifest. The same test corpus (a few thousand small unit tests with assertions, plus a set of whole-program golden tests) is written in Jet and in each peer (Rust with cargo test and nextest, Go with go test, Zig with zig build test, TypeScript with Bun test and Vitest, Python with pytest), and the cell measures, per peer: a cold full run, a warm full run, and the edit-one-test-and-rerun loop, in wall time and peak memory on the same machine. Jet/peer is below 1.00 for every peer in every metric, per the AGENTS performance gate; any loss stays logged here.

Runtime deadlock (found by TestSpeedLead 2026-11-05): with more running tasks than about (cores+8)/2, nested joins hang. Every thread waits in futex_wait on a task that never gets a worker, because the scheduler adds at most 8 workers to cover blocked waits (Compiler/JetRuntime Scheduler.jet:1097). Reproduced by a testkit pool whose entries each join a child and its resident watcher task, on the AOT and run tiers; JET_SCHEDULER_THREADS=256 avoids it. Met when a join on a child that hasn't started yet runs that child on the joining thread (or an equivalent that never deadlocks), a cases fixture nests joins inside a task group whose limit is at least the core count and finishes on O0, O1 and O2, and the testkit's default pool no longer needs its workaround.

log.text: Decision (Main, 2026-11-13), child signal dispositions: Core process spawn keeps POSIX exec semantics. Ignored signals are inherited and caught handlers reset to default (HostSpawn.jet jet_rt_process_spawn_child; SIGPIPE is reset, as in Rust std). This matches Rust std, Go and Python, and is what nohup and shells rely on. cards.title: Scripting measured against every peer: the ScriptBench gate, the run phases and the peer audit
cards.body:
Owner ruling, 2026-10-28. This replaces the old rule where a `#!` first line silently granted every permission.

In plain words: a Jet script gets no extra powers just by having a `#!` line. The first time it needs one (reading files, the network, and so on), Jet asks you in the terminal, once. Your answer is remembered for that exact script. If you already wrote `-A` (allow all), Jet does not ask. Printing, arguments, stdin, time, randomness and exit are always free.

Behavior:
1. A `#!` launch line no longer grants anything implicitly (today `jet_cli_source_invocation` in Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Authority.jet sets `all = true` for any `#!/` file).
2. `-A` (or `--allow=...`) written on the launch line, e.g. `#!/usr/bin/env -S jet -A`, applies as if typed. `./script` and `jet run script.jet` behave the same. `-A` on the command line works as today.
3. Ask once: when the run needs a permission it was not given and stdin/stderr are a terminal, Jet asks before the program starts. Sema already knows the required effects, so one prompt lists every missing permission and its resource, for example "read files under ./data" or "connect to the network". It offers allow once, always allow this script, and no. "Always" is remembered against the script's content hash in the project's single top-level `.jet/` (or the user cache for loose scripts). If the content changes, Jet asks again.
4. With -A present, Jet never asks. Outside a terminal (CI, pipes), Jet never asks either: it fails with the exact-grant error (5).
5. Exact-grant errors name the smallest grant (e.g. `--allow=FS.Read:./data`) and also say that `-A` grants every effect. `jet fix` writes the chosen grant onto the launch line (scripts) or into package.jet (packages).
6. Free basics: stdout/stderr printing, args, stdin, env-free time reads, randomness and exit never need a grant.
7. `--verbose` under -A prints one line listing the effects the run actually used, so users learn what to narrow.

One meaning on every tier (I9): the prompt and grants live in the shared CLI authority path, not per backend.

cards.title: Install Jet with one tested command: release tarball, installer script and a Nix flake package
cards.body:
Today a new user cannot install Jet. The install page says to use Nix, but the repository flake ships no `jet` package, so the documented command cannot work. This card gives Jet one documented install path that a CI job proves on every release.

Evidence (audit 2026-10-28, DOC-01): Docs/site/dist/install.html names Nix only; flake.nix exports rust-musl-toolchain and musl-linker, no jet package. The channel is chosen by ballot D-INSTALL1 (drafted, filed when this card leaves `later`).

Related: #4154, #5068, D-SEED-DIST1=A (seed published as a release asset for CI and Nix).

criteria.text: D-INSTALL1 is ratified, and the install page documents only the channel it picks.

On a clean Linux x86-64 container with no Nix and no Jet, the documented install command installs `jet`; `jet new hello && cd hello && jet run` then prints the greeting. The release gate runs this on every release.
`nix run github:<org>/jet -- --version` prints the release version: flake.nix exports `packages.<system>.default` built from the pinned seed release asset.
The install page is generated from the tested install script; no page names an install command that the release gate does not run.
The installed `jet` runs `jet run hello.jet` with JET_TOOLCHAIN_ROOT and JET_COMPILER_IDENTITY unset: Core ships inside the binary or the install root (test unsets both).
The same one-line install works on macOS arm64 and on Windows x64 (`irm … | iex`), and `jet run hello.jet` prints the greeting on both, checked by the release gate.

cards.title: New GPU and accelerator support arrives as a library: a public device-provider interface
cards.body:
Jet should run fast on any chip, including chips that do not exist yet. Today each GPU family Jet knows (CUDA, Vulkan, Metal, WebGPU) is wired into Core, so supporting a new accelerator means changing Jet itself. Mojo shows the better model: a hardware vendor ships a library that teaches the language a new device. This card makes Jet work that way.

Owner direction 2026-10-28: replaces the audit's "restore AI/ML / re-scope #3955" proposal. The shape is ballot D-ACCEL-LIB1, hosted here.

Builds on ratified decisions: D-CORE-BOUNDARY1=A (CPU chip instructions are Core library entries, #4565), D-HOST-CAPS1=A (packages add hardware kinds, #4195), D-GPU-PACKAGING1=A, D-COMPUTE1=D and D-COMPUTE-BACKEND1=D (Core owns the compute contract with a CPU reference). Related: #3026, #3028, #4731, #4762, #3955.

log.text: Frozen by owner direction (2026-11-01): cross-platform work is frozen for now. Remaining criteria need CUDA, Metal, Vulkan, Android and iOS device providers.

Merged #3028 "GPU provider matrix and actual cross-target dispatch" into this card (GPU and accelerator providers as a library); its 14 open item(s) are carried as "(was #3028)" criteria. Owner ruling 2026-10-30: merge duplicate and superseded cards into one survivor.

FutureAudit 2026-10-28, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/FUTURE.md T25: KernelIR + DeviceProvider proposal (D-KERNELIR1 and its epic card) folded here by owner direction; no separate ballot or card. Four layers, no MLIR: typed device facts (D-HOST-CAPS1) replace the string devices in Core/Compute/Solve.jet:83-84; #Kernel stays the restricted subset with a CPU reference (D-COMPUTE-KERNEL-SURFACE1=B); a provider implements caps, lower, load, launch, alloc and copy over a public, versioned kernel IR; Core.Compute tensors, autodiff and tiles target that interface. First providers are mined from the Rust-era backends #1144-#1146. Shader stages (#3027) use the same interface.

criteria.text: D-ACCEL-LIB1 is ratified.
criteria.evidence: CardClose-1 2026-10-31 (wave 9b tree): tower.json decisions: D-ACCEL-LIB1 (cardId = #5964) status=ratified outcome=A ratifiedAt=2026-10-28

criteria.text: A package outside Core adds a test accelerator (a provider that runs kernels on the CPU through the provider interface) with no compiler or Core change; device selection finds it from the package's hardware description and runs the CPU-reference conformance suite against it.
The existing CUDA, Vulkan, Metal and WebGPU providers use the same public interface; no provider uses a private path.
A provider that fails the conformance suite is refused at selection with a named failure and is never used silently.

core.compute selects a device by a typed `Device` value built from the hardware description; the string device names in Core/Compute/Solve.jet are gone, and an unknown device kind is a compile error with a registered UI snapshot.

Providers lower from one public, versioned kernel IR (a subset of the compiler IR; no MLIR dependency); `jet inspect` prints a kernel's IR and its version, and a provider that declares an unsupported IR version is refused at selection with a named error (test).

The CUDA, Metal and Vulkan/WebGPU providers are ported from the Rust-era backends of #1144-#1146 (code mined, not re-authored) and pass the CPU-reference conformance suite where the device exists; without the device, selection reports unavailable and never falls back silently.

(was #3028) The existing provider family runs authored compute and graphics across all required Linux/Windows/macOS/browser/Android/iOS routes without adding HIP or a second public API merely for vendor coverage.

(was #3028) Supported NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Apple and Android mobile GPU routes have actual device execution/readback or presentation evidence. Every required platform has a successful supported route; hardware absence does not count as completion.

(was #3028) CUDA is correctly compute-only; Vulkan, Metal and browser WebGPU carry the matching graphics routes. Receipts identify the actual provider/device/program/profile rather than a generic GPU label.

(was #3028) All adapters consume the same checked program, resource and numeric facts. F32Strict/Reproducible compute and the graphics contract agree with their references across applicable execution tiers.

(was #3028) Loader/capability absence, unsupported precision/format, device loss, queue/allocation failure and invalid lifetime produce bounded typed failures. No implicit CPU/headless replacement or fabricated success occurs.
(was #3028) Existing Tensor .Auto, provider-issued unsafe contracts, system-loader trust, backend lifetimes and I6 dependency boundaries remain intact.

(was #3028) The canonical matrix records exact applicability, source/binary/device identity and focused results. Unsupported but required cells remain open; later broad campaign proof does not replace this card's complete matrix.

(was #3028) [#3207] A 16-op chain on resident F32 input reports exactly one allocation, upload and readback (compute_residency test). There is no hidden f64 roundtrip. Kernel-only and end-to-end timing are reported separately.
(was #3028) [#3208] Examples/features/web/compute_errors.jet (wrong rank, out of bounds, bad reshape, matmul mismatch) gives identical output on native and browser. There is no second JS checker.
(was #3028) [#3209] W3: compute writes an RGBA resource that graphics consumes on one identified device, with every copy disclosed.
(was #3028) [#3210] The matched W0–W6 GPU matrix runs with compiler, device, driver, policy and cache recorded, separating kernel-only and end-to-end timing.
(was #3028) [#3211] Golden tooling/compute_ml_handoff: W4 dtype, shape, stride, device and owner, plus custom-op/autodiff composition, with every copy disclosed (D-DATA-BRIDGE1).
(was #3028) [#3222] An authored kernel traces from source, proof and cache identity to the provider program (`compute_parity -- kernel_trace_`), with typed source and device failures.
(was #3028) [#3220] Selecting a non-CPU device without its component returns the D-GPU-PACKAGING1=A actionable missing-component result (golden). Each named dependency goes to its own ballot.

cards.title: Workspace roots: check, test, fmt, doc and build act on members; status and parts list them
cards.body:
A workspace is one folder holding several packages. Today `jet check`, `jet test`, `jet build` and `jet doc` at the workspace root refuse with "ambiguous" and exit 2, `jet status` shows a phantom `target run.jet`, and a failing dependency hides its own errors. This card makes the root useful. What root commands act on is ballot D-WORKSPACE-CMD1, hosted here.

Evidence (audit 2026-10-28, LAY-04, mono_probe.sh / notes/mono_probe.log).

log.text: All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.

criteria.text: D-WORKSPACE-CMD1=A is built: at the root of a three-member workspace `jet check`, `jet test`, `jet doc` and `jet build` behave as it decides with `-p <member>` narrowing; `jet run` still asks which program to start.
`jet status` at a workspace root lists members and their entries (no phantom `target run.jet`), and `jet project parts` lists the members.
E0626 for a failing dependency prints that dependency's own diagnostics inline.
criteria.evidence: jet check of a package importing a failing dependency prints that dependency's own errors inline (E0113 at shapes/shapes.jet:2:5), then its E0626 (tests/ui/dependency_package_errors PASS, ui-liveui-n21ui.txt); a failing workspace member's errors print once (workspace_check_covers_every_member_without_picking_an_entry asserts count = 1, PASS); jet run of net/backend_battery prints the underlying E2104 (service.tree #4957 at Batteries/backend/backend.jet:271:21) before E0626

cards.title: Lockfile: committed, machine-independent, and outside the disposable `.jet/` folder
cards.body:
A lock file pins the exact dependency versions so every machine builds the same thing. Today the lock lives in `.jet/lock`, which `jet new` tells git to ignore, and it stores a build timestamp, so it would churn on every commit. This card makes the lock reproducible and places it where ballot D-LOCKFILE1 (hosted here) decides.

Evidence (audit 2026-10-28, LAY-02, LAY-06): generated .gitignore = `.jet/build/ .jet/lock .jet/cache/` (Host.jet:1478); `[build.stamp]` in the lock. Related: D-LOCK1 (spec), D-GENERATED-STORAGE2=B, #3421.

All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.

criteria.text: `jet new` writes the lock where D-LOCKFILE1=A puts it, plus the .gitignore it specifies. Proof: a jet new case (`jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter jet_new`).
The lock holds no per-machine state: building the same project on two machines gives byte-identical locks; build stamps live under `.jet/build/`.
The spec lists every `.jet/` subpath and whether it is disposable; files meant to be committed live outside `.jet/`.

(was #2218 c1) Lock changes print a changelog-shaped diff with version moves, added/removed counts, and net size delta; jetpack lock diff shows the same on demand [precut audit: no dev test, golden, case or snapshot proves this today]

cards.title: Tables for data analysis: a dataframe type over Arrow column batches
cards.body:
A dataframe is a table with named columns that you can filter, group and join, like a spreadsheet in code. Data analysts expect one, and Jet has none. Whether Core ships it is ballot D-DATA-FRAME1, hosted here.

Evidence (audit 2026-10-28, DOMAIN gaps). Builds on D-COMPUTE1=D (dataframes integrate through the compute operation family), D-COLUMNAR-BOUNDARY1 and D-DATA-READER1 (scan into column batches).

criteria.text: Reading a CSV into a frame and running filter, group-by with a sum, join, sort and select by column name works and matches Polars on the same file (golden).
Frame operations run through the shared compute operations; no second kernel path.
In a frame built from `csv.decode<Row>`, a misspelled column name or a column type mismatch is a compile error; the paired Polars and pandas programs fail only at run time (test pairs).
Columns can carry units: adding a `Meters` column to a `Seconds` column is a compile error (test).
`jet notebook` shows a frame as a table and draws `frame.plot(x, y)` with no package install (test).
(was #2449 c1) The typed plot plan implements checked marks, channels, scales, axes, legends, facets and layers in source [precut audit: no dev test, golden, case or snapshot proves this today]

(was #2449 c3) The inspector derives selections, values, schema and transformation facts from the same typed plot/table source [precut audit: no dev test, golden, case or snapshot proves this today]

(was #2968 c1) Checked Arrow ownership, typed DataLoader/stream consumers and native and Web provider context are implemented, proven by tests and goldens on every applicable tier.

cards.title: One manifest per project: fold env.jet and workspace.jet into package.jet sections
cards.body:
A manifest is the file that describes a project. Jet projects can carry package.jet, env.jet and workspace.jet, and a user must learn which setting goes where. Removing the legacy pkg.jet is already decided (D-JPK-LEGACY1=A, #5075). Whether the remaining files become sections of package.jet is ballot D-MANIFEST-ONE1, hosted here.

Evidence (audit 2026-10-28, LAY-05). Related: D-CONF-NAME1 (members live in package.jet).

log.text: Test finding (DeclTypes-3, w22-wave cases, q/sg/cases-w22-wave.txt): 3 env_hook cases FAIL with 'capture prefix line missing': export_changed_definition, export_failed_reload and export_unchanged_directory. A 'module env.dev {prompt}' counts as a typed env (EnvironmentHash.jet:115, environment_names > 0), so an untrusted non-tty export prints 'env.jet here is not trusted' and emits no JETPACK_ENV_HASH line. Whether a prompt-only env needs trust is a trust-law question for this manifest card, not a small fix. The other 16 env_hook rows pass once a jetpack binary is present.

Merged #5980 "Map: Package model: workspaces, lockfile, one manifest, environments" into this card (one manifest per project and the package model); its 1 open item(s) are carried as "(was #5980)" criteria. Owner ruling 2026-10-30: merge duplicate and superseded cards into one survivor.
All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.

cards.title: Map: Wrong-meaning bugs: values, patterns, comparisons and checked arithmetic
cards.body:
Destination: Each listed program computes the documented value on every tier.
Notes: Batch B04 of the 2026-10-28 board consolidation (TowerDedup). One worker (opus), one build, one proof run: cd <worktree> && JET=$JET Tools/agent/jet-env jet test Tools/testkit "suite cases" with one regression case per card (o0,o1,o2 agree). Order: #3838 #4909 #4679 #4726 #4906 #4929 #5020 #5940 #5941 #4156 #4721 #4745 #4976 #4977 #5037.
Decisions so far: D-PAT-NAMED-NEST1 (ratified=A) on #3838
Fog: no criteria yet on #5940 #5941 #4929 #4679 #5020 #4976 #4977 #4745 #4721 (proposals in consolidate-plan.json no_criteria).
Out of scope: cards outside this list; other batches of the consolidation plan.

log.text: c4 ruling (Main, 2026-11-13): the canonical typed comparison (equal_unordered, used by core.testing.compare and the history supplier) compares two Dyn.Number lexemes by exact decimal value, with arbitrary precision and never through binary64: "1.0" equals "1.00", "1e2" equals "100.0", "-0.0" equals "0.0", and "1e400" equals "10e399". Int, Float and Number stay distinct variants. Dyn == stays exact. Spelling preservation (encoding-decisions, JSON numbers) governs rendering only. Found by G12Docs-4 on b14, where these pairs compared unequal.

c29 decision (Main, 2026-11-13): the plugin wire budget is PG_MAX_WIRE = 1 MiB per string argument and result. It is declared beside PG_FUEL, PG_MAX_PAGES (256 pages, 16 MiB), PG_MAX_TABLE and PG_MAX_FRAMES in PluginHost.jet and enforced the same way (pg_failure, Budget(.Wire), PG_LIMIT_WIRE), so it adds no second mechanism. 1 MiB is 1/16 of the memory budget, so an over-budget result is still in bounds and only the wire budget refuses it. Neither the criterion nor spec.md named a number; spec.md now records this one (SUB G3Core-c29-wire).

c25/c27: ballot D-COMPONENT-TUPLE1 posted (author G12Docs-4; non-author adversarial review ReviewComponentTuple, Claude Opus, which respelled A from _0/_1 to part0/part1 after probes showed _0 fails E0357 and breaks D-NAME-SIGIL1, and rebuilt D on the #Import overlay model). Recommendation A (part0, part1). c25b needs four edits if A is ratified.

c8 reproduces on seed-b13 (D-SCRIPT-HELPERS1 authoring, 2026-11-12, probes in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/ballots/probes/D-SCRIPT-HELPERS1): a closure that writes a captured := local loses the write when passed as a callback, so each(...) leaves the value at 0 (p13, q09). A task that calls such a closure compiles and loses the write (q12), while writing the name directly in the task is refused with E1101 (q11), so the same write is refused in one spelling and silently dropped in the other. Closures also copy values they only read (q16, q18), against spec.md 'shared read access' (Docs/spec/spec.md:1167-1181). Rerun: sh run.sh p13.jet q09.jet q11.jet q12.jet q16.jet q18.jet in that directory.

c2 items 1-4 are proved by G3Core-t1b (7dfa3007a5, PASS 1 each); item 5 (files.map(p).path ICE) is still open with G12Docs-4. c10 items b and c pass as fallback_break_keeps_later_locals_in_scope_on_every_tier and equality_with_a_constant_payload_compares_on_every_tier.

G3Core-t1 (tests only, direct land) map from G12Docs-4. c2, the #4721 CliSeams1 items: 1 resource_returned_from_a_temporary_result_match_stays_open_on_every_tier; 2 advisory_lock_closes_through_a_moved_value_on_every_tier; 3 borrowed_file_writer_writes_through_a_fallible_function_on_every_tier; 4 optional_success_result_fallback_agrees_across_execution_tiers. Item 5 (MappedFile path field) still fails on seed-b13: files.map(p).path is an ICE, "ir.build unlowered: field of core.files.MappedFile", at O0/O1/O2, so c2 stays open until G12Docs-4 lands that fix. c3: the bare_none case covers a bare None returned from a T? E! function. `?? None` refused on T? E! is the spec rule (spec.md:1408-1412, ?? yields the innermost payload and its right side must be that payload), not this bug. c35 is covered by the recursion-stop case.

c38 shares its root with #6281 c41: a flat 1024-arm match is refused with E1403 (nests 257 levels) because arm chains reach sema as nested Expr.If. One iterative else-chain walk in sema, lowering and IR closes both.
Deconfliction 2026-11-06: reworded to match D-DECL-COLON1=A (`name: value`, no `::`); I9 tiers O0, O1, O2 and web (D-EXEC1, D-EXEC2=A: no interpreter or JIT).

Main-13 scope note (Builder3, 2026-11-04): the seed compiles Core and the compiler, and it rejects wrapping(T{x}) with E1005, so Main-13 moves only the 33 runtime narrowing sites. The 10 Core sites stay plain T{x}. Each narrows a value that is masked or built to fit, so the new E3010 stop never fires and their meaning is unchanged. The census found no compiler sites. The Core sites move under c34, once the seed has rotated past Main-13.
Held-work citation moved into the repo (#6563 c2, landed 446b49726a; see Tools/tower/held/README.md). The scratch patch lanes/Main/unitarg/Main-13-parked.patch now lives at Tools/tower/held/5971/.
c12 wrap-around spelling moved from a card question to ballot D-FIXED-WRAP1 (recommends T.wrapping_from(x), destination-owned per S42). Parked patch Main-13 waits on its ratification.

c12 patch (Main-13: sema routes an unheld fixed-to-fixed narrowing through the exact Int and CheckedIntToFixed; case tests/cases/numeric_widening/fixed_narrowing_stops_like_int; golden Examples/features/math/fixed_narrowing_stop.jet) is PARKED, not landed: wave 37 on 26fa6cd102 found 2 real regressions. tests/cases/web_build/web_decimal_and_grouped_formatters_use_shared_helpers and tests/cases/checked_text/html_composition_matches_aot_jit_interpreter_and_web fail on the wave and pass on base (rerun on both). Root, from the node wasm stack: Compiler/JetRuntime/Source/Int.jet:146 int_fits does U64{int_limb(value, at)} (an I64 to U64 conversion), which is now checked and calls jet_int_checked_fixed, which calls int_fits: infinite recursion. Native passed only because its runtime pack is still built by the older compiler; the next seed would break native too. Verified correct: I64{U64{max}} stops with E3010 on none, basic and full. To finish c12: (1) the runtime's own bit-pattern conversions (about 35 non-literal fixed conversions in Compiler/JetRuntime, e.g. Int.jet:146, Iter.jet:697, IterNumeric.jet:4-8, NativeByteList.jet:12-17) need an explicit wrap-around conversion, and Jet has none (to_bits/from_bits are Float-only; wrapping(...) is ratified for arithmetic operators only), so this needs an owner-ratified spelling or a sanctioned runtime-internal raw cast; (2) the widen-to-Int-plus-runtime-call lowering should become an inline bounds check so hot paths do not pay a call per conversion. Parked patch: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/unitarg/Main-13-parked.patch.

Folded #5941 "Sema's loop-never-exits verdict can disagree with the lowered CFG and silently drop the code after the loop" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #5971 (Map: Wrong-meaning bugs: values, patterns, comparisons and checked); 1 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Before 1158a1548f (#5940 b), sema_stmt_refutable_expr_can_break did not walk the arm values of a value-position if/match, so a loop whose only exit is a 'break' inside a value match arm ('event :: if &scanner.next() == { .Val(v) -> ^v .None -> { break } ... }') was judged exitless. Destination: Collections and codecs are linear-time, one-meaning and typed (DataTree/Dyn, #Codable).
Notes: Batch C04 of the 2026-10-28 board consolidation (TowerDedup). One worker (opus), one build, one proof run: cd <worktree> && JET=$JET Tools/agent/jet-env jet test Core (collections, json, encoding, data suites) plus serde/* goldens. Order: #3236 #3280 #4295 #4306 #4472 #4602 #4626 #4667 #4884 #3271 #3272 #4412 #4499 #4520 #4682 #4739 #4757 #4781 #4789 #4828 #4886 #4611.

Folded #4886 "List.replace does not have the ratified D-ONCE-VERB1 swap meaning (it clones to a new list)" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #5976 (Map: Core data, collections and codecs); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Found by CopyPareto1. Ratified D-ONCE-VERB1=A (Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:7049): 'replace keeps only the List swap meaning'. Today List.replace is a pure clone-to-new-list in both the registry and the Rust Prelude (~Prelude:3041), not the in-place swap that returns the old value. Fix both tiers to the ratified meaning (in-place replace returning the old element) and migrate every caller in one cutover; regression on both tiers. Check the exact ratified signature first (Tower card for D-ONCE-VERB1).

Folded #4884 "List.sort_by must be O(n log n) on the JetIR route" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #5976 (Map: Core data, collections and codecs); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Found by CopyPareto1 (goal 10), confirmed by NativeReview2 / NativeLead24-2: native O0 List.sort_by computes insertion positions over an index permutation (O(n^2)) and then allocates a replacement element buffer once (Lower/Combinators.jet:523-698/713); it may have replaced an older O(n log n) canonical index-merge. Every native program sorting a large list pays quadratic time. Main-admitted fix: make the canonical List.sort_by kernel a stable O(n log n) sort by reusing the existing canonical stable index-merge + swap-cycle (no second sort implementation), same stability / comparator semantics on every tier; regression with a large list + a stability case + a timing bound. Order: CopyPareto1

Folded #4667 "json.parse is about 460 times slower than V8 on a 2.4 MB document" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #5976 (Map: Core data, collections and codecs); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Proven: 30,000 records, 2,366,671 bytes; default jet run parse about 12.3 s wall versus Node JSON.parse 26.5 ms (json_probe.jet, node_json.js). Fix: byte-level parser without per-character String/DataTree churn, or a native provider; add a JSON throughput budget (for example 50 MB/s on this shape) to the performance gate. Related: csv.to_string and JSONWriter grow a String by self-interpolation in a loop (csv.jet:77-80, json.jet:208-212), a quadratic copy; collect and join once.

criteria.text: D-NET-READINTO1=A is built. `read_into(buffer, limit)` appends up to `limit` bytes to the caller's `[U8]` and returns the count, as an inherent method on TCPStream, UnixStream, TLSStream and file readers, with a deadline form. It returns 0 at end of stream, and a limit below 1 is invalid input. The Reader trait is unchanged. The HTTP server, the HTTP client and the TLS record reader switch to it. A paired two-program cell (a read(4096) loop against read_into: wall time, allocations per read, peak memory) is in the measurement manifest, and read_into strictly wins it. Goldens run on O0, O1 and O2.

D-WS-ROUTE1=A is built. `mux.websocket(pattern, handler)` and `#Server.WebSocket(path)`: the server runs authentication and Origin policy, then validates and upgrades, and the handler returns nothing. One route-table adapter and handshake serve TCP and TLS. The route owns GET, so an equivalent GET registration is refused, HEAD gets 405 without an upgrade, and OPTIONS lists GET. Upgraded tasks stay inside the server limits and shutdown. Protocol close codes are kept; an application failure may send 1011 only before the transport closes. OpenAPI describes handshake responses only. This depends on the concurrent serve loop (#4635). Goldens on O0, O1 and O2, plus a TLS case.

Merged #5041 "No implicit copies: native codegen and compiler source copy only where the source explicitly asks (.copy()), every copy justified" into this card (drop glue and moves: moves never copy, no implicit copies); its 5 open item(s) are carried as "(was #5041)" criteria. Owner ruling 2026-10-30: merge duplicate and superseded cards into one survivor.

Folded #5906 "A Close temporary passed to a borrowed parameter is never closed: sink(S { id: 5 }) skips close" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #5989 (Map: Drop glue and moves: Close always runs,); 1 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Repro (fc382a23cd discovery jet, jet run): struct S { id: Int }, impl S.Close { fn close(^self) { print("close {self.id}") } }, fn sink(x: S) { print("sink") }, fn run() { sink(S { id: 5 }); print("end") } prints 'sink', 'end' and never 'close 5'. The same happens with a generic fn sink<T>(x: T). With fn sink<T>(x: ^T) and sink(^S { id: 5 }) it prints close 5. So a temporary with a Close impl bound to a read parameter is never closed after the call (a secret would not be scrubbed, a handle not released). Files: $JET_RUN_ROOT/Main/cv/g92b.jet, g92.jet. Acceptance: the temporary closes exactly once after the call on run and build; a golden example in Examples/features/memory proves it.

Folded #5821 "A task closure keeps its captured arguments alive after the body moves them out" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #5989 (Map: Drop glue and moves: Close always runs,); 1 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Found by RustOut's Sglue slice (2026-10-23): with `task f(x)`, the closure environment keeps x alive for the task's whole life, so moving x out inside the body (or dropping it) frees nothing. In the compiler, ir_merge_runs(parts[at]) shared each IR part with its task, the merge rewrite then copy-on-write copied the functions (+0.24 GB at ir.build) and ir.opt copied them again (+0.55 GB); the x64 'free on a task' never freed anything before link. Workaround in the slice: pass tasks only keys and counts. Fix: a moved or last-use capture must transfer ownership out of the task environment (or the env must release a capture at its last use), same meaning on every tier (I9). Proof: an example whe

A Close value read out of self or out of a struct field is a move: after `lease := self` in a method, or after a field is consumed while its struct stays in scope, the original no longer holds the resource, and it closes exactly once when the moved value drops. A case proves that a FileLock taken this way is released before the next statement that probes it, on O0, O1 and O2.

Each FileLock is released before the next probe and closes once (found by G6Meta-4).

cards.title: Scripts may read the file you name on the command line, and use a private temp folder, without a prompt
cards.body:
When you type `./wc.jet notes.txt`, you have already said which file the script may read. This card lets that act count as the permission: a `#CLI` field of type `Path` grants reading exactly the path you passed, and a private per-run temp folder (`files.temp_dir`) needs no prompt. Everything else still asks once, as owner ruling #5949 says. Ballot D-SCRIPT-DESIGNATE1, hosted here, decides; this card builds the winner.

Source: FutureAudit 2026-10-28, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/FUTURE.md T11 items 2 and 3 (the powerbox model: a file picker grants the file the user picked). Writes are not designated; they keep the #5949 prompt.

Related: #5949, D-SCRIPT-CONFIRM1=A (#3705), spec.md "Command registry and typed inputs" (`Path` is a supported #CLI scalar), core-library.md `temp_dir`.

log.text: All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.

criteria.evidence: CardClose-1 2026-10-31 (wave 9b tree): tower.json decision D-SCRIPT-DESIGNATE1: status=ratified outcome=A (typed paths are granted) ratifiedAt=2026-10-30; the card's criteria follow option A

criteria.text: `./wc.jet notes.txt`, where wc.jet takes a #CLI struct with a `Path` field, reads notes.txt with no prompt and no flag; reading any other file still prompts (pty test).
The grant covers exactly the passed path after resolving `..` and symlinks, and only for reading: writing the passed path still prompts (tests for both).
A script that calls `files.temp_dir(prefix)` gets a fresh directory under a per-run root with no prompt, and the root is removed at exit, also after a failure (test).
`jet run --verbose -A` and the prompt list designated paths as granted by argument; the spec and the #5949 basics list are updated in the same change.

cards.title: Run-time checks for #Unsafe code and foreign edges: the hardened profile (D-MEM-HARDEN1=A) and every aliasing and undefined-behavior class, like Rust's Miri
cards.body:
Rust has Miri: a slow interpreter that catches memory mistakes the type checker missed, such as reading past a buffer inside unsafe code. Jet should have the same safety net. This card adds an opt-in checking run at O0 that tracks extra state for every value and stops with a named error on any aliasing, bounds, release, race or uninitialised-read mistake, including inside `#Unsafe` blocks and at foreign edges.

Source: FutureAudit 2026-10-28, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/FUTURE.md T06 ("new card for the O0 checking mode if #4726 does not cover it"; #4726 lists results, not a checker).

Related: #4309 (static IR ownership verifier, a compile-time check; this is its run-time partner), #4620 (memory model), #4726 (defined-behavior ledger), D-MEM-HARDEN1=A (shipping run-time checks for unsafe islands and foreign edges).

The row stays known-failing until `jet test --profile hardened` is built.

BoardPlanner review 2026-11-09 (dev 6a06b917cb). Retitled: this is the card for run-time checks of #Unsafe code. New row: D-MEM-HARDEN1 (from #3239 c35). Gained #6418 c96 (the hardened-profile catch; its zero-overhead clause is G11 #2858). c2: hosted CI is removed. c1's new opt-in spelling is an owner choice (C-G10-1: reuse --profile=hardened, recommended).

criteria.text: Under `--profile=hardened` (D-MEM-HARDEN1=A, on `jet build` and `jet test`; no new spelling), every #Unsafe operation and foreign edge stops with a named runtime code and the source location on: out-of-bounds access, use after release, double release, a data race on shared memory, a read of uninitialised memory, and writing through an aliased mutable view.

A planted-bug corpus with one program per class, each inside `#Unsafe` or a foreign edge, stops in checking mode with a named runtime code and the source location, and runs without a report in normal mode; the corpus runs in the verify batch.
All in-repo `#Test`s pass under checking mode in a nightly job.

First slice of c1 (bounds): under --profile=hardened (D-MEM-HARDEN1=A), an out-of-bounds read or write through an #Unsafe pointer or raw slice stops with a named runtime code and the source location at O0, O1 and O2. The normal profile emits no extra check (pinned by an O2 dump or a byte-identical build). A planted-bug case proves both.

cards.title: `jet test` tries many task orders: seeded schedules over the replay recorder find races and deadlocks
cards.body:
A concurrency bug often appears only in one rare order of task steps, so a test passes a thousand times and fails in production. Rust needs extra tools (loom, shuttle) to search those orders. Jet already records task message and lock order for exact replay (D-REPLAY-ORDER1=A, built in the Rust era as #4252). This card lets `jet test` run a concurrent test under many seeded orders and print the seed of a failure, so it replays exactly.

Source: FutureAudit 2026-10-28, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/FUTURE.md T07 and T21. The Rust-era replay recorder is a capability row on the not-built census card and must be ported first.

Related: #3239 (task outcomes), #4637 (fair turns), #5468 (stop edges in tasks).

log.text: Moved from G1 to G15 (testing toolkit) by owner order 2026-11-06: G1 keeps only hand-off and durability.

c1 spelling is an owner gate: TestProfiles drafts D-TEST-SCHEDULES1 (#Test marker argument vs jet test flag vs body call); Main posts it after an adversarial pass. The seeded single-worker scheduler / replay recorder port (D-REPLAY-ORDER1=A) proceeds ungated

criteria.text: A concurrent `#Test` can ask for schedule exploration with a run count (spelling recorded in Docs/spec); `jet test` runs it under that many seeded task orders and reports the result per seed.
A planted lost-update race and a planted lock-order deadlock in the test suite each fail within the default run count; the report prints the seed and the interleaving.
Re-running with the printed seed reproduces the same failure through the replay recorder three times in a row (test).

D-TEST-SCHEDULES1's reruns: spelling lands with its Data/Syntax registry row, a syntax-decisions.md log entry, editor grammars regenerated by jet self devtools grammars and re-blessed snapshots, and the syntax-ratification chore check passes.

D-TEST-SCHEDULES1=A: #Test("…", reruns: N) with N an Int >= 1 (below 1 is a registered compile error with UI snapshot); also reruns: on TestProfile, t.reruns(n) in fn test and --reruns=<n>, which change only tests that ask for reruns; small order trees run exhaustively depth-first; reruns run in parallel on virtual time; deadlock and suspected livelock are reported failures; --seed replays one order; property tests with reruns: are a compile error; spec.md deadlock text (2872-2888) updated

cards.title: Forwarding derive: a distinct type takes its base type's traits in one line
cards.body:
Rust's orphan rule forces wrapper types, and each wrapper must re-implement every trait by hand. Jet's distinct types (`Die: distinct Int(1..6)`) meet the same chore. A forwarding derive lets a distinct type take its base type's traits (equality, ordering, printing, hashing, codable) in one line, through the ratified derive-request law (D-ONCE-DERIVE1=A, D-CORE-DERIVE-HOME1=A). Library API inside existing law; no new marker.

Source: FutureAudit 2026-10-28, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/FUTURE.md T30.

Related: #3505 (const generics), #4609 (cross-module generics, P0).

cards.title: Registry publish policy: short-lived identities instead of stored tokens, and a runnable example per public function
cards.body:
Two rules decide what it takes to publish a package. First, how the publisher proves who they are: in 2025 a worm spread through npm by stealing long-lived publish tokens, and trusted publishing replaces them with a short-lived identity from the CI job. Second, what a package must contain: pages with only type signatures leave users guessing, so each public function could be required to ship a tested example. Ballots D-TRUSTPUB1 and D-REGISTRY-EXAMPLE1, hosted here, decide; this card builds the winners.

Source: FutureAudit 2026-10-28, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/FUTURE.md T15 and T20. Already ratified and not reopened: the transparency log, TUF metadata and transactional publish (D-JPK-REGISTRY1=D), signing (D-PKGSIGN1), the trust root (#2199).

cards.title: Remote builds and shared cache work with existing build farms
cards.body:
Big teams speed up builds by running steps on a shared farm of machines and sharing a cache of results. Jet has ratified who may use a remote builder and how it is bound (D-JPK-REMOTE1=D: `build.remote` grants, `jet remote bind`), but not the wire protocol. Ballot D-REAPI1, hosted here, decides between the open protocol existing farms speak and a Jet-only one.

Source: FutureAudit 2026-10-28, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/FUTURE.md T22.

cards.title: Infrastructure as typed Jet: a first-party package where the plan is a value tests can check
cards.body:
Teams describe servers, databases and networks in tools like Terraform, then apply that description to a cloud. Those tools have their own languages, keep secrets in a state file, and make plans hard to test. A first-party Jet package could describe infrastructure in typed Jet, with the plan as a value that tests assert on and apply running only under Net and Secret authority. Ballot D-INFRA1, hosted here, decides whether to build it and whether to reuse Terraform/OpenTofu providers.

Source: FutureAudit 2026-10-28, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/FUTURE.md T24. Sequenced after the HTTP client and server (audit card 3: #3665, #4957), hence `later`. Fleet and OS deployment are epoch e9 and out of scope.

cards.title: Write a typed Jet config out as JSON, YAML or TOML for other tools
cards.body:
Many tools read settings from JSON, YAML or TOML files. Jet lets a project write configuration as typed Jet and can already export a JSON Schema from a type (D-CORE-JSON-SCHEMA1=A). Hand-copying the values into those files repeats them, and the copies drift. Ballot D-CONFIG-EXPORT1, hosted here, decides whether a command writes a checked Jet config value out in those formats. It is not hosted on #4275, whose ratified scope forbids new ballots.

Source: FutureAudit 2026-10-28, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/FUTURE.md T23.

With the schema option, the command writes the JSON Schema for the value's type from the same codec metadata, and a value that fails its type is never exported (test).

cards.title: Complete the marker API as a metaprogramming rung: every target, typed reflection, one shared API with derives and fn build, library diagnostics, expand/test tooling
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-10-28: markers are a rung on the metaprogramming ladder and need a solid, comprehensive API for building and using them; fix the gaps.

Findings (MarkerScout, dev be55563b38, read-only):
(1) User marker bodies expand only on structs, top-level functions and text blocks (Compiler/JetSema Registration/UserTemplates.jet:417-458). Enums, variants, methods, fields, modules and packages are not wired, although built-in markers reach them.
(2) Reflection lacks module and package info and markers on enum variants. Marker arguments come back as untyped MarkerInfo{name, args} (Comptime/Reflection.jet:340), not as the marker's declared typed parameters.
(3) Marker bodies, derives and fn build do not share one reflection and emit API.
(4) There is no way for a library or user marker to register its own diagnostic codes with what/why/fix text (I4).
(5) There is no expand or inspect view or test helper for marker output; jet emit is unwired (#6038).
(6) Wrapping or around behaviour (decorator-like) is absent by design (D-METADEPTH1/2, D-PROCMACRO1), which is a ballot question.
(7) The Data/Syntax Markers.jet name list (25) duplicates part of the Prelude registry (81).
The ladder is: comptime expression, comptime fn, marker, derive, fn build. They share the same reflection and emit API, differing only in scope (philosophy pillar 4).

cards.title: Memory checks accept every safe program: no over-strict rejections
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-10-28: if a program is memory safe, Jet must accept it. Checks must be neither over-strict nor under-strict; only `#Unsafe` blocks opt out.

Known over-strict case: E0221 rejects a type that could form a strong loop at its declaration. It rejects a plain linked list (`next: Shared<Node>?`) and a tree with weak parent links and strong `kids` (probes in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/ballots2/probe/family2.jet). A strong loop can only close when a strong field of an existing shared value is written with a value that reaches it. Building by construction (prepend, a new child) never loops.

Scope: every memory, ownership, borrow, aliasing and resource diagnostic.

cards.title: Upgrades need no hand edits: every breaking change ships a `jet fix` rewrite, and last release's code builds on the new one
cards.body:
Scripting audit 2026-10-28 (row D28). `jet --version` on commit 8fbf094 prints "release readiness: not-ready" and "1.0 compatibility policy: future-1.0 (planned; not active)". Go 1 (compat promise plus `go fix`) and Perl 5 are best in class: old code keeps running. Python 2 to 3 took twelve years because most changes needed hand edits.

Design that beats them. Jet keeps greenfield freedom (AGENTS.md) but makes every break mechanical: a change that makes accepted source fail `jet check` must register a `jet fix` rewrite in the same change. CI proves it on the previous release's Examples/ and on a fixed corpus of scripts. Go fix covers a subset of changes; Jet's rule covers all of them, so users never hand-edit to upgrade. No card owns this: #5071 removes editions and retired forms but does not gate migrations. Map: #5982.

cards.title: Port the Python bridge and the PyPI/npm providers to the self-hosted toolchain: `use py.X` in a loose script, each foreign package fenced by its grant
cards.body:
Scripting audit 2026-10-28 (row D06, ecosystem size). Python has 600k+ PyPI packages and JavaScript 3M+ npm packages; Jet's own registry has no public content, so Jet loses on reach by count. The ratified design already answers this. D-FFI-PY1=A (Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:4166): `use py.X` talks to a supervised sidecar CPython with a typed message boundary and the `-[FFI.Py]>` effect; `py@embed` is the opt-in in-process mode. D-JPK-EXTPROV1=A (:4185): PyPI, npm and SwiftPM are first-class providers, fetched, hash-pinned and offline after the first fetch. D-DATA-BRIDGE1=A (:5964) reserves the `py.*` and `r.*` roots. Both were built in the Rust era (#180, #937 done) and never ported: probe on commit 8fbf094, `jet run -A b/pyuse.jet` with `use python.numpy as np` gives E0603 "The imported module is not present in the package source snapshot". No open card owns the port (#5984 is a map with no criteria).

Why this beats every peer rather than tying. Reach becomes a superset: PyPI plus npm plus Jet packages, where Python reaches only PyPI and Node only npm. Safety is better than at home: a PyPI package runs in a sidecar whose OS access is fenced by the script's grants, so a package that reads ~/.ssh is refused unless FS.Read for that path was granted. pip, uv and npm run package code with the user's full authority. Mojo also imports Python modules but runs them in-process with no fence.

Scope: the self-hosted `py.*` binder (sidecar default, `py@embed` opt-in), the PyPI and npm providers in the resolver behind #4833's fetch path, typed stubs from `.pyi` files where present, and the authority wiring. The R bridge (D-FFI-R1) follows the same sidecar path and is out of scope here.

criteria.text: A loose script with `use py.numpy as np` and `print(np.mean([1.0, 2.0, 3.0]))` prints 2.0 under `jet run`; the first run fetches and hash-pins numpy from PyPI, the second run works with the network disabled (test). Today E0603 (probe `jet run -A b/pyuse.jet`, commit 8fbf094).

Reach census: of the 100 most-downloaded PyPI packages, at least 90 import and pass a one-call smoke test through `use py.X` on Linux x86-64 (script and table checked in; the failing ones are listed with the reason).

Fence test: a fixture PyPI package that opens ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 at import is refused with an authority error naming FS.Read and the path, unless that grant was given; the same package under `pip install` plus `python3 -c 'import fixture'` reads the file (paired test).
The #5949 prompt lists `FFI.Py` and the Python package names when a script first uses `py.*`, and a dependency update that adds a new Python package asks again (#5459 rules).

Call cost: with `py@embed`, 100k calls of a small pure Python function finish in less than 1.5x the time of the same calls made inside CPython; with the sidecar default, the median round trip is below 20 microseconds (numbers logged per release).

A manifest dependency in the D-JPK-EXTPROV1 form (`leftpad: npm@"1.3.0"`, syntax-decisions.md:4186) fetches, pins and is called through its typed first-party stub package (:4220); the second run works offline (test).

cards.title: Benchmark Jet's build and package system against Nix, and beat it
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-10-28: Jet's build and package system must be lightning fast, substantially faster than Nix, more powerful, and easier to use, audit and reason about. Nix is a required peer for the build, package and configuration cells.

Compare like with like: the same project or package set built hermetically by both, on the same machine, cold and warm. Nix evaluation and store operations count, and so do Jet's check, store and cache.

log.text: BoardPlanner review 2026-11-09 (dev 6a06b917cb). Speed card: G11 by the owner's 2026-11-09 ruling (speed and size are G11).

KitSpeed first receipt 2026-10-28 (5 samples, interleaved; Jet/Nix medians with the SemanticIndex O(n²) fix): eval 0.77, noop 20.4, incremental 4.87, cold_cache 5.21, scratch 3.88 — all lose. Causes: 73% build-plan query (whole-package Interpreter check, eager ProgramInfo, third Doc-mode recheck); no build stamp or artifact cache (JET_CACHE_DIR unread); Core rechecked per process (~150 ms). Fix plan: build stamp, plan cache + per-module interface/object caches, CAS under JET_CACHE_DIR, build-program closure scoping + one shared check + lazy ProgramInfo, persisted Core interface. Receipt: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/land/kitspeed-nix-peer-receipt.txt

criteria.text: The canonical performance manifest lists Nix as a required peer with paired cells: config evaluation (`nix eval` vs `jet check` of the build program), no-op rebuild, one-file incremental rebuild, cold build from a populated cache or substituter, and a from-scratch hermetic build of the same medium project; each cell has a harness and committed receipts.
Every cell meets the gate (Jet/Nix below 1.00) and the evaluation, no-op and incremental cells reach Jet/Nix at most 0.25; losses stay on cards with their cause.

A side-by-side note shows the same project in Nix and in Jet: lines and concepts a reader needs, how each declares and audits inputs and effects, and reproducibility (bit-identical output on two machines or two clean stores).

cards.title: `Set` is a sorted array with a memmove per insert
cards.body:
ScriptBench 2026-10-28 root cause R3 (cells: w13 wall/CPU). Report: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/scripting/bench/BENCH.md.

Cause: `Set` is a sorted array (`Compiler/JetIR/Source/BuildSets.jet:1-7`). Each insert shifts the tail with memmove (`ir_set_insert_body`, `:65-95`, memmove `:77-88`). Building a set of 2 M lines is O(n²) moves.

Evidence: perf: `jet_rt_mem_move` 80.0 %, `jet_rt_string_compare` 5.8 %. Timed warm: jet-bin 18,666 ms vs PHP 733.1 ms, Python 1,363.8 ms.

log.text: HELD by owner order 2026-11-11 (no small optimizations until the language is mostly stable; architecture and regression fixes go first, per #5479 c5-c8). These criteria stay open and unworked: c2 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c).
BoardPlanner review 2026-11-09 (dev 6a06b917cb). Speed or size card: moved from G4 to G11. Owner order 2026-11-09: all speed and size work is G11.

W13 root (CardClose-1, perf on a 200k-line subset, base s1 release): jet_ir_set_insert → jet_rt_mem_move is 88.5% self, string_compare 4.0%. Set<String> is a sorted array (Compiler/JetIR BuildSets.jet:65-95, ir_set_insert_body). Each new key is binary-searched, then the tail is memmoved, so n distinct keys cost O(n^2) shifting: 200k keys take 3.5 s, 2M lines 87 s. Fix: a hashed Set index like BuildMaps' hash/capacity, or insert-then-sort for bulk adds.

ScriptBench w13 on dev 69a987b5a6, wave-21 s1 (CardClose-1, sbench/w13-dev.json): LOSS against every peer. jet-bin 86.9 s wall, 79.1 s CPU, 220 MB RSS. Wall ratios: 249x python, 78.6x ruby (the closest), 241x php. jet run 56.5 s; that run may have overlapped other jobs, so it is not yet evidence of an inversion. The root is not profiled yet.

criteria.text: The cause above is removed at its root, and the probe cited in the evidence scales linearly or shows the gap closed (receipt with the command and numbers).

PASS: collections_and_methods/set_inserts_by_hash_in_linear_time (TIMEOUT on a0_035, PASS on the candidate).

cards.title: JSON decodes through a `Dyn` tree and refuses typed input over 16 MiB
cards.body:
ScriptBench 2026-10-28 root cause R4 (cells: w06 wall/CPU/RSS). Report: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/scripting/bench/BENCH.md.

Cause: JSON parses to a `Dyn` tree first, then decodes the tree to the typed records in a second pass (`Core/Encoding/Json.jet:93`). Typed `json.decode<T>(text)` refuses input over 16 MiB (`Json.jet:81`, `:718`), so a 44 MB file must take the two-pass path. Every node is allocated and freed.

Evidence: perf: `jet_rt_alloc_8` 12.5 %, `jet_rt_free_8` 10.4 %, `jet_rt_alloc` 6.2 %, `jet_rt_dyn_to_native` 4.2 %, `jet_rt_dyn_from_native` 3.7 %. Timed warm: jet-bin 9,785 ms and 1,950,092 KB peak vs Bun (TS) 395.8 ms / 289,728 KB, Python 1,502 ms / 403,264 KB.

log.text: Safety finding (Main, 2026-11-12): on seed-b13 a one-key Dyn write on a non-Object value crashes with SIGSEGV instead of a program stop (I1). G11Speed-dk1 makes it an exit-70 stop and covers it in case encoding_parity/dyn_object_key_write_reads_only_the_keys, as well as making the write native (c3); held behind probe g11-c3dyn.

HELD by owner order 2026-11-11 (no small optimizations until the language is mostly stable; architecture and regression fixes go first, per #5479 c5-c8). These criteria stay open and unworked: c2 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c).
BoardPlanner review 2026-11-09 (dev 6a06b917cb). Speed or size card: moved from G4 to G11. Owner order 2026-11-09: all speed and size work is G11.

G1Lead b7ff715849 fixes the a0_039 gate regression from option D (c1dd8c7b26). A migration block now loads core.encoding, and E0105 never names a generated __ helper. G1Lead proof on a dev-built compiler: golden Examples/Data/Migrations/run.jet PASS on O0, O1 and O2; ui migration_change_via_ok PASS; ui marker_module_ambiguous PASS on its original snapshot; all 12 ui migration* and 6 marker_module* rows PASS; golden CryptoMigration, DecodeMigration and DBMigrationProof PASS on O0 to O2; cases filter migration 6 PASS and 3 known, decode 30 PASS and 8 known. Main re-cuts a0_039 at this commit.

G1Lead landed option D as dev c1dd8c7b26: typed json.decode<T> reads the document in place through one generated reader per type; decode(tree) is the same body over the tree source. Worker verify: check/build/selfcheck rows 0; filters encoding_parity 27, json 91, codable 13, serde 4, decode 29, corelib_parts_encoding_streams 4, all PASS. General-mechanism proof on a second program (package index, 50k+100k packages, identical output): 1648-1719 ms / 444 MiB vs 2922-3268 ms / 1.20 GiB. w06: 1633-1822 ms / 505 MB vs 3593-4058 ms / 1.46 GB. Main runs the c1/c2 peer measurements with the next seed.

Owner correction 2026-11-08 (to Main), superseding the process in the previous entry: NO ballot. The owner ratifies D directly: engineer away the downsides (hand-written impl migration, Flatten/untagged without a second semantics, error-order parity with the tree path, public Decode change size, code size and compile time), then build D. A design pass that removes each downside comes first inside the build; no owner gate before building.

Owner direction 2026-11-08 (to Main): option D. The generated Decode body reads an abstract format-neutral reader interface; Dyn is one reader and a JSON byte cursor another, so there is one copy of the decode rules (SerdeItems) and every format streams with no intermediate tree. The downsides must be engineered away before presentation: the migration of hand-written Decode impls (adapter or one cutover), Flatten and untagged enums (buffering or lookahead without a second semantics), the size of the public Decode change, the beginner surface, and error-order parity with the tree path. Process: a ballot draft with exact surface and same-program alternatives, then an adversarial design review in Docs/audits (serde Deserializer/visitor and Swift Decoder as the strongest existing designs, with measured probes), then a redesign until it holds, then owner ratification, then build. Options A/B/C are superseded.

Main 2026-11-08 06:10 c1 is owner-gated. Every #Codable decode is a Sema-generated body over `tree: Dyn` (Registration/SerdeItems.jet: field lookup, defaults, presence/E2410, DenyUnknownFields, validate, Flatten, migration, tagged/untagged enums). JetIR ir_dyn_decode only dispatches to it, so a one-pass decode needs a second, generated, per-type decoder over a byte cursor. Options (G1Lead scoping): (A) a hidden codec slot on the Prelude Decode trait, `__decode_json(cursor)`, whose default materializes the subtree and calls decode. SerdeItems emits the streaming body beside decode with shared helpers, and Flatten, untagged, migration and hand-written impls use the fallback, unchanged. This changes a public trait shape (Prelude Traits.jet, the OwnedTraitRows ratchet), so it needs a ballot and an adversarial review. Recommended. (B) a compiler-generated free function per type over a Core-private cursor. It needs a privacy exemption for generated items in Sema/Calls/Core.jet, which is frozen, so the freeze must be lifted. (C) JetIR synthesizes the readers from type rows plus TSerdeAttribute, duplicating the SerdeItems semantics in IR. That is a second mechanism (I8), the largest and riskiest; not advised. Any option must keep per-field errors in declaration order, and a syntax or duplicate-key error anywhere must replace the field errors, as the tree path does. Separately in scope now: dropping the 16 MiB typed-decode refusal (typed decode over 16 MiB then works through the tree path). That is not the root fix.

Main 2026-11-08 00:00: PortsLead-2 found c1 needs a streaming Decode path. The Prelude trait is decode(tree: Dyn) and SerdeItems derives it, so every typed decode builds the Dyn tree first. Meeting c1 needs a language-level change to the Decode trait and its derive, not a library fix. It needs a design (and a ballot if it changes the public trait) before code. Deferred out of the overnight G4 push.

W06 root (CardClose-1): json.parse_with_limits (Core/Encoding/Json.jet:93 → parse_value/object/array, 392-672) builds the whole 40 MB document as a Dyn tree: one allocation per value and key, plus a positions map per object. Person.decode then walks it again (dyn_to_native, string_clone). Typed json.decode<T> refuses input over 16 MiB, which forces this path. Fix: a typed streaming decode from bytes straight to the target type, with no Dyn tree.

Correction (CardClose-1, perf stat -r 3, sbench/w06-evsym.txt): there is no O0-vs-full inversion. --release 4.06 s, 18.0G cycles; --optimize=none 4.06 s, 17.5G; jet run 5.22 s, a third of it compile. The earlier jet-bin 5961 ms was load noise. Root: per-value allocation and the Dyn round-trip. jet_rt_alloc_8, free_8, alloc, dyn_from_native, string_drop and free make up about half of all cycles, all in the runtime pack, which --optimize does not touch.

ScriptBench w06 on dev 69a987b5a6, wave-21 s1 (CardClose-1, sbench/w06-dev.json): LOSS against every peer. jet-bin 5961 ms wall, 5640 ms CPU, 1.26 GB RSS. The closest peer is python (4.09x wall, 3.93x RSS); bun is 46.6x wall and 9.0x RSS. jet run (4468 ms) beats the optimized binary, the same inversion seen on w05.

cards.title: CSV builds fields byte by byte, re-validates UTF-8 per field and materializes every row
cards.body:
ScriptBench 2026-10-28 root cause R5 (cells: w05 wall/CPU/RSS). Report: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/scripting/bench/BENCH.md.

Cause: CSV pushes each byte into a `[U8]` (`Core/Encoding/Csv.jet:341-441`), then makes each field with `String.from_bytes(field.copy())`, which validates UTF-8 again per field (`:382`, `:390`). All rows are materialized before the caller sees one, so peak memory grows with the file.

Evidence: perf: `core_encoding_csv_parse_rows_with` 12.7 %, `jet_rt_free_8` 10.3 %, `unit_numeric_int_parse` 7.5 %, `jet_rt_alloc_8` 6.8 %, `unit_text_bytes_utf8_error` 5.4 %. Timed warm: jet-bin 1,976 ms and 719,540 KB peak vs LuaJIT 498.8 ms / 2,768 KB, Python 2,136 ms / 11,848 KB.

cards.title: Waiting for a child process polls in 1–10 ms slices (~10 ms per spawn)
cards.body:
ScriptBench 2026-10-28 root cause R6 (cells: w07 wall). Report: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/scripting/bench/BENCH.md.

Cause: Waiting for a child polls. The collector waits in 1 ms slices (`Compiler/JetRuntime/Source/ProcessExecutionCollect.jet:190`); the waiter yields in 10 ms scheduler waits (`:225-229`, comment: "polling remains the seed's 10ms scheduler wait"). About 10 ms per child; w07 runs 100 children.

Evidence: Timed: jet-bin warm 1,057.9 ms (≈ 10.6 ms per child) vs Bun 129.3 ms, Python 141.2 ms. CPU is much closer (jet-bin 216 ms vs Bun 132 ms), so most of the wall time is waiting.

log.text: HELD by owner order 2026-11-11 (no small optimizations until the language is mostly stable; architecture and regression fixes go first, per #5479 c5-c8). These criteria stay open and unworked: c2 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c).

Owner cut the agent count to 2. MechD-3 stopped. Unlanded: its c2 (w07) work and inline-run drafts in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/MechD (patch-g5 landed as c639365c56). c2 is not started.

c1 follow-up (MechD-3): on the CardClose-54 base c66f96253f, strace -f -c over 1000 run() calls shows 1000 poll calls, one per run, each returning on pipe HUP or pidfd readiness, and 0 nanosleep or clock_nanosleep. The 1-10 ms sleep slices are gone.

c2 remeasured on 2ba0d540c4 (base jet, ScriptBench copy $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/sb/scriptbench with imports migrated to 'use X :: core.X'; bun is 1.3.13 because 1.4.4 is no longer substitutable; receipt $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/sbench/w07w11.json). w07 FAILS, so c2 stays open. jet-bin 110.8 ms wall, 5920 KiB; jet-run 116.3 ms, 9684 KiB. Losses: php wall 1.09 / cpu 1.14 (php 101.6 ms); perl cpu 1.01 and rss 1.00; rss vs lua 1.35, luajit 1.34, bash 1.16. jet-run also loses to python cpu 1.01, bun wall 1.02, perl wall 1.01, php wall 1.14, and rss vs perl, lua, luajit and bash. Roots: per-spawn cost (about 1.1 ms vs php's 1.0 ms) and a 5.9 MiB resident floor against 4.4-5.1 MiB for lua and bash.

2026-11-01 c2 measured on 360e470044 (BENCH.md, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/CardClose/sbench/h360-report.md): FAIL. jet-bin 192.9 ms loses wall/cpu to php 1.30/1.33, perl 1.12/1.10, python 1.11/1.11. Root: run_spec starts a collector thread (192 MiB stack, clone/join), 3 pipe2 pairs capturing unread stdio, /dev/null, 23 extra parent syscalls per child; peers inherit stdio.

ScriptBench w07 on dev 1620f05362 + tools (wave-27 tree s2, BENCH.md method, 2026-11-01 12:35): still FAIL c2. jet-bin 191.1 ms wall / 187.4 ms cpu / 4140 KiB for 100 children; loses to php 146.3 ms (1.31x) and perl 175.4 ms (1.09x); jet-run also loses on rss to perl and lua. The 1-10 ms poll is gone (c1); the remaining ~0.45 ms per child is spawn-path CPU (the child already uses clone(CLONE_VM|CLONE_VFORK)). Log: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/sb-w07w10.log

Landed on dev at undefined in CardClose-54 (patch row: criterion/count 1): Root removed (tsc s1, runtime pack 827b3c1660d49fda = dev 69a987b5a6 + d4f3932172): the waiter's park slot is woken by the collector when it sets done, and the idle collector sleeps on the child's pidfd instead of 1-10 ms slices. Probe: 1,000 sequential run_spec(cmd(["true"])) take 11165 -> 3815 ms under strace, and timed park waits ending on the timeout fall from 1291 to 261 (re-parks; 0 lost wakes). Correction (CardClose-1): process_execution_env_remove (ProcessExecutionPrepare.jet:26) is about a third of the jet process's own samples, or 17.4% of all samples, not 38%. No other jet function is above 4%.

Each spawn builds the child environment twice: once to prepare (Compiler/JetRuntime ProcessExecutionPrepare.jet:240) and once for the receipt identity, only to read PATH (ProcessExecutionReceipt.jet:250). Each build copies the inherited environment through process_execution_env_set (ProcessExecutionPrepare.jet:45), which removes by key linearly for each var. With 169 vars that is about 14k string_eq per build, plus 4 allocations per var: 38% of user samples. The inherited keys are already unique, so the fix is to move-push them and read PATH directly. Pinned to one CPU, jet equals python (0.23 s); php and bun remain ahead. Handoff: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/CardClose/HANDOFF-scriptbench.md.

cards.title: `para_map` runs one worker per 64 items and ignores `limit:`
cards.body:
ScriptBench 2026-10-28 root cause R8 (cells: w11 wall). Report: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/scripting/bench/BENCH.md.

Cause: `para_map` splits work into fixed 64-item ranges (`Compiler/JetRuntime/Source/Parallel.jet:24-26`, `:90`) and starts at most one worker per range (`:94`). w11 has 100 URLs, so only 2 workers run, each doing up to 64 blocking GETs in a row, whatever `limit:` says.

Evidence: Timed: jet-bin warm 1,356.9 ms vs Bun 222.5 ms, Python 312.5 ms; 64 × 20 ms server delay = 1.28 s.

log.text: HELD by owner order 2026-11-11 (no small optimizations until the language is mostly stable; architecture and regression fixes go first, per #5479 c5-c8). These criteria stay open and unworked: c2 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c); c6 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c); c8 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c); c9 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c); c10 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c).
BoardPlanner review 2026-11-09 (dev 6a06b917cb). Speed or size card: moved from G4 to G11. Owner order 2026-11-09: all speed and size work is G11.

Owner ruling 2026-11-08 (Q19): A. Public Core gets core.tasks.cpu_ns() -> Int (CPU time used by the current task) and core.tasks.current_task() returns a real task id; the compiler trace uses that public surface rather than a private route.

SchedLead commit 1/7 landed as afe2acc8c8: tasks run on fibers that park instead of blocking their worker thread; closed InlineAsm rails X64_FIBER_SWITCH and X64_GS_BASE_WRITE, gated by IRProgram.asm_rails. Its receipt: precommit rc=0, VERIFY OK, LaneCheck CHECK OK; focused task/cancel/generator/para/deadline/sleep cases and the concurrency goldens equal to baseline. #6403 r08: the quick task finishes in 98.7 us (base 2.9 s). 100000 cancel/timer/wake race rounds all accounted on every tier (base hangs). No leak over 3 x 10000 cancelled parked tasks. About 5.7 KB per parked task. w11 still loses to bun on wall (105.95 vs 94.66 ms); the root is the para_map limit cap at the core count, which is commit 2. Open: the ~32k live-fiber cap (vm.max_map_count) must degrade or diagnose, never crash; a 100k-task case is requested. #6403 c4 names a function that was removed; it gets reworded to the offload stats at c6.

Owner decision 2026-11-08 (to Main): build the async-I/O scheduler redesign now, no ballot. Tasks are multiplexed on few threads, with the epoll wait run on the waiting thread (the D-PARA-LIMIT1 path) instead of an OS thread per in-flight wait plus a poller-thread hop. Scope covers the same root in #6403 (a blocked task holds its worker) and #6440 (generator yield is a park/wake, about 20 us). Engineer away the downsides (task/channel/cancellation semantics unchanged on every tier, blocking foreign calls and OS waits offloaded, fairness and deadlines, I9 parity, debuggability), then build. Target: w11 beats every peer on wall, CPU and RSS (bun 9.25 ms CPU; jet 19.5 ms after fixes 1-4).

Main 2026-11-08 04:55 w11 fix 3 landed bee6af85ed (inet_pton for literal hosts, no getaddrinfo): perf task-clock -r30 25.4 -> 21.2 ms CPU, hyperfine user+sys 20.7 -> 17.7 ms, wall unchanged at 87 ms (G1Lead). Fix 2 (persistent epoll registration, 21.2 -> 20.9 ms) is queued in lane-commit; fix 1 (wake after unlock, 20.9 -> 20.3 ms) passed VERIFY and is next. bun stays at 9.25 ms CPU; c2 still fails pending the scheduler redesign.

Main 2026-11-08 04:40 w11 c2 profile (G1Lead, dev at 15e01b1474, perf stat -r30, nice 19, busy box): bun 9.25 ms CPU and 89.2 ms wall against jet-bin 25.8 ms CPU and 87.2 ms wall, so Jet wins wall unpinned and loses CPU 2.8x. Pinned to 12 cores Jet wall is 187 ms (para_map worker cap). Breakdown: 25 para workers spawn and join in 1.6 ms. 100 sequential GETs take 11.1 ms, about 110 us per request against about 40 us for bun, from 22 syscalls per request: 6 futex poller hops, 4 epoll_ctl ADD/DEL on every wait, 4 setsockopt, and a musl getaddrinfo mmap/munmap even for 127.0.0.1. Parallel overhead adds about 9 ms: 1401 of 2090 futex calls hit the HostNetPoller root mutex, which is held while waking ParkSlots and around epoll_ctl. The server delay adds about 4 ms. Approved bounded runtime fixes, to land after the next seed, in this order: Jet-side IP literal parse, register once with MOD re-arm, wake after unlock (prototype 25.8 -> 24.5 ms), then shard the root lock if still hot; estimated 19-21 ms total. The verdict: bounded fixes cannot reach bun 9 ms. The floor of the current model is one OS thread per in-flight request plus a poller hop (2 context switches) per wait. Closing c2 needs the D-PARA-LIMIT1 async-I/O path (waits multiplexed on few threads, epoll on the waiting thread): a scheduler redesign needing owner scope.

Main 2026-11-08 04:15: 7bf10da106 by PortsLead-2 does not meet c2. It resolves IP literals through getaddrinfo AI_NUMERICHOST on the caller thread, adds a word-sized Int division fast path for boxed operands, and reads the clock through vDSO clock_gettime with the replay env parsed once. w11 jet-bin instructions:u 104.4M -> 32.8M, task-clock 45.1 -> 24.7 ms; jet run 164.6M -> 92.4M; clones 126 -> 26, clock_gettime 2909 -> 0. On a loaded machine (15 runs, wall/CPU ms): jet-bin 85.5/19.2, jet-run 99.0/33.2, bun 87.1/8.1, deno 112.8/38.6. Still loses to bun on CPU; the rest is futex/thread-park, about 14 ms of system time, which is a scheduler redesign. A quiet-window measure is queued in proofq as Main-PortsLead-w11-measure.sh.

Spreading receipt for 9177db37e4, same compiler (seed-built from d405d4cb6c). Probe $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/burn/para/para16.jet: 16 items of a 20M-step LCG kernel; under the old 64-item chunks all 16 ran on one worker. Built with jet build --release: ser wall 0.430 s (cpu 0.44 s); para_map wall 0.042 s (cpu 0.50 s), 10.2x. jet run (O0): ser 1.139 s, par 0.068 s. Every mode prints total 6472. c2 (ScriptBench w11) waits on the ScriptBench rebuild.

dev 9177db37e4 (Main): an unlimited para_map, para_filter or para_partition now passes PARA_EVERY_WORKER (1073741824) instead of -1 (BuildParallel.jet). The runtime caps it at the available parallelism, so chunks are the items spread over the pool, at most 64, and a short list of costly items reaches every worker. para_fold keeps -1 and its 64-item chunks (merge-tree contract). Compile-time code keeps cap 1, so the same value. The Parallel.jet comment and core-library.md core.tasks were updated; 4df47ce6da has the c5 paragraph. Proof is queued for the dev s1 batch: the 16-item probe at $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/burn/para/para.jet should show the parallel run well under the serial one, with every result 508760, plus goldens Concurrency/Parallel and ParallelIter.

Finding for c2 (Main 2026-11-07): an unlimited para_map over fewer than 64 items is one chunk, so it runs on the caller thread (Parallel.jet:22-26 keeps 64 items per chunk when limit < 0). 16 items of a 20M-step kernel: built binary par (map+fold) real 0.893 s, user 0.992 s = serial x2. para_fold's 64-item grouping is its contract (BuildParallel.jet:570-573), but para_map, para_filter and para_partition could spread a short list over the pool the way the limited path does (parallel_chunk_size). w11 passes limit: 32, so it already takes the spreading path.

Deconfliction 2026-11-06: reworded to match I9 tiers O0, O1, O2 and web (D-EXEC1, D-EXEC2=A: no interpreter or JIT); the Rust-free toolchain (Jet suites and tests/cases rows replace cargo tests and .rs sources).
#6563 c1 precut audit re-added 3 criteria from archived #3672: each was not proven on 9c7ddf1359. Row verdicts and reasons: Docs/audits/precut-2026-11/PRECUT-AUDIT.tsv (ff5dd7fd7b).

c2 remeasured on 2ba0d540c4 (same setup and receipt as #6084: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/sbench/w07w11.json; bun 1.3.13). w11 FAILS, so c2 stays open. jet-bin 106.8 ms wall, 21.8 ms cpu; bun 93.4 ms wall, 21.2 ms cpu: jet-bin/bun wall 1.14, cpu 1.03. jet-run/bun wall 1.23, cpu 1.45; jet-run/deno wall 1.03. All other peers are wins.
