cards.title: `fs.walk` collects and sorts every entry before yielding
cards.body:
ScriptBench 2026-10-28 root cause R10 (cells: w02 wall/CPU/RSS). Report: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/scripting/bench/BENCH.md.

Cause: `fs.walk` collects every entry, then sorts the whole list by path (`Core/Files/Files.jet:1501-1530`, sort at `:1529`). The program then stats each file again for its size.

Evidence: perf spread over `core_files_walk_impl`, `jet_rt_string_compare`, alloc/free. Timed warm: jet-bin 113.6 ms vs Lua 59.6 ms, Bash 65.6 ms, LuaJIT 65.6 ms.

log.text: HELD by owner order 2026-11-11 (no small optimizations until the language is mostly stable; architecture and regression fixes go first, per #5479 c5-c8). These criteria stay open and unworked: c2 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c).
BoardPlanner review 2026-11-09 (dev 6a06b917cb). Speed or size card: moved from G4 to G11. Owner order 2026-11-09: all speed and size work is G11.

412154ebff (G1Lead): fixes the I2 ICE at its root, in JetIR ir_call_row. An argument widened to a union is boxed as the callee parameter's own union, registered by the callee signature, rather than a union respelled in the caller's scope. New case core_path_foundations/core_path_calls_core_files_on_every_tier passes on O0/O1/O2 (9 core.files.path functions plus missing paths); seed a0_038 fails it with 8 ir.build faults. A census of Core union parameters (String|Path 46 sites, [String]|HTTPCorsOrigins 1, Int|ServiceWorkflow 7, LocalDate|DateTime 1) is covered by the same fix. Open structural finding, I8: Core declares Path twice (the Core/Compiler/Lang.jet builtin and core.files.path), so user code `files.exists(path.of("x"))` fails with E0112. Making it one Path is a Core API design call that waits for a ballot. Also seen: CoreSurfaceLedger --check fails under the seed on core.files.__walk_release (seed against tree; it clears with the next seed).

Lander gap closed (Main, 2026-11-08): the precommit census (the lander's census-snap.sh) checked Compiler/JetCli but never Core, unlike Land.jet census selfcheck-core, so a Core spelling no compiler accepts landed in 863e3d6b4e. The census now runs `jet check --threads 12 Core` with keep-going using the compiler it just built, and precommit requires `selfcheck-core rc=0 rows=0`. Probe: dev Core gives rc=0 rows=0; a copy with the old Path.jet:410 spelling gives rc=1 with the same 2 rows (E0047, INCOMPLETE) the a0_039 preflight reported; about 3 s per run.

cd58a15b81 (G1Lead): Core/Files/Path.jet walk unwraps each entry with `entry ?? return Err(err)`. The old `entry?.path` spelling checks under no compiler (E0047 on a0_038 and on dev sema), and it landed because precommit does not gate selfcheck-core; that lander gap is Main's. A Core census under a0_038 and B2 is clean after the fix (0 rows), and the walk cases pass 11/11. Found while fixing it: no case calls core.files.path walk, and every core.files.path function passing path.raw to a `String | Path` parameter ICEs in ir.build ("union String | core.files.path::Path without a definition") on a0_038 and on dev, an I2 violation. Routed to G1Lead ahead of #6082 D: fix the root in lowering, add an O0/O1/O2 case, and census the other Core parameter unions.

Phase 2 landed as 863e3d6b4e (62 files, lane-commit precommit passed). G1Lead reports peak RSS, old vs new, of 13.4/40.2/160.6 MB vs 15.0/15.0/14.4 MB on 20k/80k/323k entries, identical path order, and the Iterable-loop authority fix (E1803/E0740). Main could not re-check this with the a0_038 seed: a probe built inside the dev checkout came out byte-identical to one built outside any checkout and still reported no FS requirement, so the seed does not pick up the checkout Core. c1 is to be measured with a compiler built from 863e3d6b4e or later, in the next batch verification. Scripts: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/walk6086/ab2.sh.

Owner decision 2026-11-08 (to Main): option A, no ballot. walk/walk_files become lazy, with per-entry results: each entry or its own IOError is yielded as the walk goes, break/drop closes the handles, and memory is bounded by depth. One greenfield cutover migrates every caller (G1Lead census: 52 files: Examples using .len()/index, Path.walk() -> [Path], the L0522 lint, docs); collecting is explicit. Engineer the downsides away in the build (error visibility for callers that only want a list, ordering identical to today, the beginner path), then build.

Main 2026-11-08 05:45 c1 is owner-gated (public API). Since e3e314c953 the walk is depth-first and sorts one directory at a time, so the collect-then-sort-everything cause is gone; what remains is the collected result in the public signature: walk/walk_files return [WalkEntry] !IOError (core-library.md). Today a failed directory drops its subtree, the walk continues, and the earliest failure is the Err of the whole walk. A stream cannot keep that contract, because it has yielded entries before the Err exists. Options (G1Lead census, 52 files touched by A: Examples using .len()/index, Path.walk() -> [Path], the L0522 lint, docs): (A) walk/walk_files become a lazy per-entry-fallible stream, and every caller migrates in one cutover; (B) keep the list API and add a streaming twin (new surface, against I8 one mechanism); (C) keep the list: linear time per e3e314c953, peak memory proportional to the tree, and c1 is reworded to time-linear. Needs an owner ballot (with an adversarial review before A/B is built). G1Lead builds whatever is ratified.

MechD-3 stopped (2-agent cap); nothing of this landed. Its proposed design: add fs.walk_iter(root, ignore:) and walk_files_iter, which return an Iterable of Result<WalkEntry, IOError>, walk depth-first keeping only the open directories on the current path, and sort siblings per directory, so the order is by path component (the order __walk_before uses for errors, and walkdir's sort_by_file_name). walk and walk_files keep their signatures and collect over it, which removes the BFS queue and the global string sort. Visible change: 'a/b' now sorts before 'a.txt' and 'a-c'. walk_iter is new public API and the order change is product behavior, so this needs an owner ballot before it is built.

cards.title: Plain `jet run` keeps an unoptimized program, slower than `--release`
cards.body:
ScriptBench 2026-10-28 root cause R15 (cells: `jet-run` warm cells that do real work (w03, w05, w06, w14)). Report: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/scripting/bench/BENCH.md.

Cause: Plain `jet run` builds with the stock options; only `--release` adds `optimize: full` (`Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Front.jet:755-757`, `:777`, `:799-801`). So the kept script program is unoptimized, and a warm `jet run` is slower than the `--release` binary of the same file.

Evidence: Timed warm, jet-run / jet-bin: w03 18,572 / 14,790 ms (1.26), w05 2,747 / 1,976 ms (1.39), w06 12,223 / 9,785 ms (1.25), w14 135.7 / 74.1 ms (1.83). (w09 13.8× and w10 2.3× are mostly R12 start-up; w04 0.83 and w13 0.99 are within their ± 34 % / ± 11 % spread.)

BoardPlanner review 2026-11-09 (dev 6a06b917cb). Added G11: the card is a run-speed defect (c2, ScriptBench w03 and w14). It keeps G4 for c11 (the D-BUILD-TIER1 run tier) and the c5/c6 output rows. Owner order 2026-11-09: all speed and size work is G11.

Owner ruling 2026-11-09 (later the same day, replacing 'always full'): jet run is O0; jet build defaults to full, with an O1 flag for a faster compile. D-RUN-TIER2 (always full) is withdrawn; RunTier2Review found it NOT CLEAN. The replacing ballot is D-BUILD-TIER1.

Owner ruling 2026-11-09 (BoardPlanner C-G4-2): jet run always builds the program at full optimization (the Go model), superseding D-RUN-TIER1=B and the O0 rule for jet run in AGENTS.md I9; compile-time code is unchanged. ScriptLead writes the replacing ballot D-RUN-TIER2 (exact behavior: first-run cost, what is kept, jet dev), which gets an adversarial review and is posted before it is built.

Main 2026-11-08 04:05 regression (blocks the a0_037 release): a kept program reused by plain jet run runs as a child of a waiting jet run that does not forward SIGINT, so `kill -INT <jet run pid>` leaves the program running. A fresh compile runs the program in-process, and SIGINT ends it. Lost cases: corelib/core_os_interrupt_delivery_matches_aot_jit_and_interpreter and core_os_interrupt_callback_forms_match_dev_tiers. Repro: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/intr/probe2.py. G1Lead is fixing it by making the kept launch take the same in-process path, one mechanism.

Main: c6's tier-trace test and interp/deopt rows have no meaning without an interpreter; c6 now proves native byte-exact runs on every level. c8's 'evaluator' is compile-time code, which runs natively at O0 (I9). CardCleanup Q(c).
Deconfliction 2026-11-06: reworded to match I9 tiers O0, O1, O2 and web (D-EXEC1, D-EXEC2=A: no interpreter or JIT).
#6563 c1 precut audit re-added 7 criteria from archived #2862, #2864: each was not proven on 9c7ddf1359. Row verdicts and reasons: Docs/audits/precut-2026-11/PRECUT-AUDIT.tsv (ff5dd7fd7b).

ScriptBench w15 on dev 69a987b5a6 (CardClose-1): the jet run path costs 16.8 ms CPU and 9.5 MB RSS to launch the kept program, against 1.8 ms and 0.25 MB for the built binary. jet-run cells therefore lose to luajit (CPU 7.01, RSS 3.75), perl (CPU 4.23), php (CPU 2.69) and bash (RSS 1.30), while jet-bin beats every peer. These cells are report-only under D-PERF-RUNCELL1=B. The root is the run-path launch overhead this card and D-RUN-TIER1 cover.

Ballot D-RUN-TIER1 drafted (A: jet run at basic; B: first run at none, a reused script is rebuilt once at full; C: keep, use --release), rec B, at $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/ballot-run-tier1.json. Not posted yet: it needs the cross-family adversarial review pass first.

Ballot input (UiGreen-1, INFERENCE, not measured): (b) costs one kept --release image per script (it replaces the none image, so the net cost is the size difference) and one full-optimize rebuild per script source, about a jet build --release, on the first reuse (2nd run) or in the background after the 1st; the cold run is unchanged. Card warm ms, jet run (none) / jet-bin (release): w03 18572/14790 (1.26x), w05 2747/1976 (1.39x), w06 12223/9785 (1.25x), w14 135.7/74.1 (1.83x).

UiGreen-1 2026-10-31 23:50: owner gate. Plain jet run optimizing none is ratified (Docs/spec spec.md:3815-3816, D-BUILD-DEFAULT1=B, syntax-decisions.md:5713). Fix options for a ballot: (a) jet run stock = basic (cold compile cost; run cases re-key); (b) cold jet run stays none, and the kept script program (ScriptCache) is rebuilt at full once warm (tier-up on reuse, same meaning per I9); (c) keep as is. UiGreen-1 leans (b). Parked until the owner rules; Main is preparing the ballot.

cards.title: Every lazy-iterator pull locks a global mutex to charge comptime fuel
cards.body:
ScriptBench 2026-10-28 root cause R18 (cells: w10 jet-bin wall/CPU vs Lua and LuaJIT). Report: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/scripting/bench/BENCH.md.

Cause: After R17, the rest is text splitting and iteration. Every pull of a lazy runtime iterator calls `jet_rt_iter_charge` (`Compiler/JetRuntime/Source/Iter.jet:277`), which locks and unlocks a global mutex to charge compile-time fuel even when no compile-time evaluation runs (`IterCharge.jet:4-21`).

Evidence: `perf record` of the timed w10 binary: `jet_rt_native_iter_string_split` 12.1 %, `jet_rt_iter_charge` 8.8 %, `main_run` 6.3 %, `jet_rt_alloc` 5.4 %. Timed: jet-bin cold 4.3 ms / warm 5.3 ms vs LuaJIT 2.7 / 2.7 ms, Lua 4.8 / 3.4 ms; every other peer is slower.

The global fuel mutex is gone (c1); the rest is line/word splitting cost. Log: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/sb-w07w10.log

cards.title: Effects on types: packages, targets and the compiler as effect-typed types (end-state proposal)
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-10-29, after a talk by Simon Peyton Jones on types that control which effects they may interact with and how: "if we can define the usable and not usable effects on a type, then we can make packages and the compiler types themselves, which then echoes effects on types." This is the mechanism behind pillar 5, "The Language Is A Library", but it is not itself a pillar (owner, 2026-10-29).

The owner wants the exact end state first: every semantic rule and every spelling, as it will look once built, so he can fix it before any work starts. Main writes the proposal in Docs/proposals and links it here. The owner then corrects it, and the corrected surface becomes ballots on this card.

log.text: c66: jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter E3413 on seed-b8 (dev 8ed6cef36e) gives ERROR selection: no matching corpus entries. No E3413 UI snapshot exists on dev, so c66 is unproven and E3413 breaks I4 (every diagnostic has a UI snapshot). Routed to G8Scope-3.

Proof-line refresh (G8Scope-3 sweep on b5, 2026-11-11). c32: `grep -nF 'LibraryEffectListDenial: struct' Compiler/Prelude/Diagnostics.jet` hits; aaced3ca08 renamed LibraryEffectNotKernel. c33: `grep -nF 'E0756. Inside its package the name is bare' Docs/spec/spec.md` hits; the spec rewrapped. c34: the Effect enum moved to the generated Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/EffectRoots.jet; `grep -nF '#FX(Net, FS)' Core/Effects/Effects.jet` hits; `jet Tools/agent/CoreSourceRows.jet --check` is current. The ui library_effect_* (5/5) and golden ScopedEffects (o0/o1/o2) proofs exist and pass on b5; earlier reports of them missing were a sweep-planner miss.

Many criteria cite the same fR3 range and six fix commits; the review's ledger maps each criterion to its original implementation commit. Owner: G8Scope, top priority.

Jetpack records each dependency effect row in the lock and reports widening, and --locked refuses it (syntax-decisions, authority rows). It must not follow proposal §7.2, where jet add writes grants, because met c18 rules that out. A grant-widening check on upgrade does not exist today. Expert half: waits on D-TARGET-DECL1.

c37 is partly done by G8Lead2-24 (landed 973d760c89): the four compiler.advanced.* spelling rows and their constants are removed, with no shim, and the lexical ledger is regenerated (58 rows). c37 stays open for the rest.

Decision (Main, within ratified scope) for c36, c37, c39 and c44. No new ballot is needed: D-META-LADDER1=A (2026-11-09) and D-REFLECT-EXPANDTYPE1=A settle them. (1) The rows use LADDER1's Meta effect family (Meta: enum { Generate, Include, Rewrite, Types, Raw }, implementing Effect, declared in Core's compiler package under D-EFFTYPE-KERNEL1, not in Prelude/Effects.jet). Read access is watching, which needs no Meta effect, so a read-only lint has an empty Meta row. The criteria's Compiler.* spelling reads as Meta.* under LADDER1. Compiler is the root-only value that only the root's own source makes. (2) c37: the advanced API is gated by Meta effect rows plus the root-only Compiler value. The compiler.advanced.* spellings in Spellings.jet are deleted with no shim, and a test proves that a grant enables the API and its absence refuses it. (3) c39: the example custom lint is read-only, with an empty Meta row; the example marker is typed -[Meta.Generate]>. Each has golden output on O0, O1 and O2. (4) c44: the row for Marker.expand(self, target: Target) and Derive.expand(target: Target) is Meta.Generate, since expand only adds generated members (Rewrite stays for existing-code transforms under D-META-OPTIN2). Docs/proposals/effect-types-2026-10-29.md section 9.1 is amended to match. c21-c24 and the expert half of c30 wait on D-TARGET-DECL1, which is in the ballot queue.

Decision (Main, 2026-11-09) for c27 (G8Lead2-17): the closed_lists duplicate guard measures each pair's shared-member count, not the overlap ratio, so deleting a unique member can never fail it and adding a shared member always does. Known debt left open: Jetpack HermeticBuildError and the compiler's BuildSessionError share 27 members; the shared vocabulary would live in jet_foundation as a generated list once there is a card for it.
c6 is met with E0749, the ratified ceiling code for a type row outside its cap; E0712 in older text is not the code. c54 waits for G8Lead2-15 (its case pins E0227) in train 2.

Decision (Main, 2026-11-09) for c25-c27, within the owner-reviewed proposal's rule that an action with ambient effects is never reused: an effect is ambient when its result is not fixed by the action's declared inputs. Net is ambient unless every fetched byte is pinned by a content hash in the key (a mismatch fails the action); FS is not ambient for declared input paths and the action's own output directory; Exec is not ambient for a declared tool identified by content in the key, and ambient for a PATH lookup; Env is ambient unless declared with its value in the key; Time.Now, Rand and other processes are always ambient; Time.Wait is not. These readings hold only where the sandbox enforces denial of undeclared FS, Env, Net and Exec; elsewhere every cap counts as ambient, and a case proves an undeclared read is refused. c27 removes ActionCache (Cached/UncachedPhony) and ActionSpec.uncached_phony, renames ActionSpec.cached to ActionSpec.new, and reuse becomes exactly: no ambient effect.

D-EFFTYPE-MODEL1 A ratified by the owner 2026-10-30: #FX above a struct, enum or trait caps everything done in the type's name (methods, trait impls in any package, closures inside them, inherited default methods and Close impls). Method rows may only tighten it, and parameter work belongs to the caller, so there is no tail rule. C9 rewritten; C31 added.

Owner direction 2026-10-29: implement effects on types in the near future; ballots for the proposal's choice points are attached to the cards they govern. Check code reachable from each artifact's entry against that artifact's target row (new code, proposal E0763). Expose target facts as `$build.target.*`.

Compute each dependency's inferred row and check it against the depending package's `grants` (new code, proposal E0762) with the call path and the version that widened it. Implement the ratified `jet add` behavior (ballot C6). Retire the unenforced `policy: { effects: … }` in one cutover.

Body: Design: Docs/proposals/effect-types-2026-10-29.md (section 6 and ballot C2; supersedes the module rung of D-EFFECT-RUNGS1). Owner direction 2026-10-29: implement effects on types in the near future; ballots for the proposal's choice points are attached to the cards they govern. Module values stay named-only unless ballot C2 on this card says otherwise.

Merged #6134 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Effects on types: trait rows bind every impl and make trait-value calls precise. Body: Design: Docs/proposals/effect-types-2026-10-29.md (section 5). Owner direction 2026-10-29: implement effects on types in the near future; ballots for the proposal's choice points are attached to the cards they govern. A call through a trait value uses the trait's row; without one, the union of the built program's impls.

Every diagnostic: §12 table, E0749/E0712/E0747 widened plus new E0760-E0765. Absorbed, kept or retired mechanisms: the §11 table, e.g. `policy: { effects: { deny } }` Retired, advanced compiler opt-in Replaced by `Compiler.*`.

cards.title: Ballot: are Core's generic bodies checked against the selected target?
cards.body:
Finding B10 of the #6128 census (Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md; line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f). Core's generic bodies are checked without the selected target's no_os fact; user bodies are checked with it (Sema/Scopes.jet:492-498).

Pillar 5 (Docs/spec/philosophy.md): Core is ordinary Jet that uses only mechanisms any package can use, and every tool calls the compiler library instead of keeping its own copy of a language rule. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with a registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). The same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9).
cards.plan: Implement the ballot's answer and delete or publish the exemption.

cards.title: Ballot: does Core ship as a versioned package?
cards.body:
Finding B15 of the #6128 census (Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md; line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f). Core comes from the toolchain beside the package graph (JetDriverCompileRequest.core_sources, Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Identity.jet:180-218), is keyed by `<corelib>/` (Sema/Diagnostics.jet:20-22, Loader.jet:2659), and has a private core.<area>.runtime namespace (E1001, Loader.jet:3616-3625) that packages cannot mirror.

Pillar 5 (Docs/spec/philosophy.md): Core is ordinary Jet that uses only mechanisms any package can use, and every tool calls the compiler library instead of keeping its own copy of a language rule. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with a registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). The same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9).
cards.plan: Implement the ballot's answer. Under A, Core resolves through the package graph with a version, and the `<corelib>/` predicates are deleted once F01-F12 land.

The core.<area>.runtime privacy uses a rule any package can use (UI snapshot for the refused import).

cards.title: Core declares its own host leaves; delete the compiler's twin of Core's API
cards.body:
Finding F01 of the #6128 census (Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md; line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f). The compiler keeps a twin of Core's API. Core members are typed and dispatched by compiler tables (Compiler/Prelude/Core.jet:1-4, CoreCallExtensions.jet; generated Registry/CoreCallRows.jet:10 with 1,998 rows; hand-written Registry/CoreSignatures.jet:88, CorePlatformSignatures.jet:229, CoreHostSignatures.jet:22, CoreValueSignatures.jet). A native row wins over the Core declaration (Sema/Calls/Core.jet:264-270). A package can reach the host only through C FFI.

Pillar 5 (Docs/spec/philosophy.md): Core is ordinary Jet that uses only mechanisms any package can use, and every tool calls the compiler library instead of keeping its own copy of a language rule. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with a registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). The same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9).
cards.plan: Add one public declaration for a host-provided function, usable by any package, whose signature, effects, failure and sink facts are read from the declaration. Move every Core member that has a CORE_CALLS row to that declaration in Core source. Delete Compiler/Prelude/Core.jet's member rows, CoreCallExtensions.jet, the generated CoreCallRows table and the hand-written signature tables in one cutover. The spelling of the declaration is ballot A on this card.

OWNER 2026-10-30 asked what Compiler/Prelude/Core.jet is ('looks nothing like jet ... some weird kind of table or config file'). Merged #6163 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Build core.build and the fn build host on the public compiler library. Body: Finding F16 of the #6128 census (Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md; line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f). core.build is implemented inside the compiler: Compiler/JetBuildSession/Source/Session.jet:1-4 (private compiler service linkage), Keys.jet:1-5 (Rust v2 key contract), Declarations.jet:1-2 (Rust runtime_bridge positional contract); Compiler/JetEval/Source/BuildServices.jet:1-3; Build and BuildPlan methods are dispatched by member-name strings in Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/BuildAdapter.jet:36-81. Pillar 5 (Docs/spec/philosophy.md): Core is ordinary Jet that uses only mechanisms any package can use, and every tool calls the compiler library instead of keeping its own copy of a language rule. cards.title: Odin-level array programming: element-wise array operators, swizzles on any small array, matrices
cards.body:
Owner 2026-10-29 (direct): Odin's built-in array support (array arithmetic with + - * / that just works, swizzling, strong support for 3D and graphics) must ALL be added to or verified in Jet. This amends D-VECARITH1 (element-wise operators closed to compiler-provided lane and linalg types) and widens D-SWIZZLE1.

Today: swizzles work only on five hard-coded Core type names (F32x4, F64x2, Vec2, Vec3, Vec4; Sema/Expressions/Places.jet:679), with x/y/z/w only and no rgba. Element-wise arithmetic is limited to compiler-provided lane and linalg types. Fixed arrays `[T#N]` (S76/D-FIXARR1) get no element-wise operators or swizzles.

Odin reference set to audit row by row: fixed arrays of numbers with element-wise + - * / % and bit ops between arrays and with a scalar (broadcast), and unary minus; == and !=; swizzles .xyzw and .rgba for N<=4 (read, write and repeat-read); swizzle on the result of an expression; built-in matrix types with * as matrix product, matrix-vector product, transpose and the like; quaternions; #simd vectors; #soa struct-of-arrays layouts; array-to-slice conversion; `len` as a compile-time constant; and compile-time evaluation of all of the above.
cards.plan:
1. Audit: write a table of every Odin array, matrix, quaternion, simd and soa feature (cite the Odin docs/spec) against Jet today, with each row PASS, PARTIAL or MISSING and a probe program. Send the table to Main before implementing; any new spelling needs an owner ballot (I7).
2. Implement every MISSING and PARTIAL row whose spelling is already ratified or needs no new syntax: element-wise operators on [T#N] numeric fixed arrays (array op array, array op scalar), swizzles on [T#N] with N<=4 plus rgba on every swizzleable type, driven by a type fact instead of hard-coded Core names.
3. One runtime meaning on all tiers (I9), with lowering to SIMD where the backend has it.
4. Examples/features/lowlevel goldens; UI snapshots for length mismatch, a non-numeric element and an invalid lane.
5. Pair each new performance-relevant surface with a two-program perf cell against the plain loop (AGENTS.md performance gate).

log.text: Array ballots on Tower: D-ARRAY-CORENAMES1, MATRIX1, KEYED1, LAYOUT1. Drafted by KitSpeed-2; adversarial reader Ballots-4. Ratified conflicts fixed (card #1437 matrix family INDEX1=E, MUL1=F, LIT1=E, BCAST1=E, SOLVE1=B, HOME1=D; D-LANES1=A; D-SPACE-GEOMETRY1=A; ..= is E0318). Readings for the owner to confirm: MATRIX1 treats Matrix*Vec as the transform product, with BCAST1 limited to repeating operators; LAYOUT1 says push through a window is refused where visible and stops otherwise. Main replaced alias declarations in MATRIX1 with the #6176 form.
Correction to the audit counts (KitSpeed-2): 87 rows, of which 25 PASS, 6 PARTIAL, 55 MISSING and 1 bug.

Audit (KitSpeed-2, 2026-10-29, 78 probes at O0 and full on 25f9dee): 19 PASS, 7 PARTIAL, 49 MISSING, 1 bug. SIMD S1-S11 is ratified but unbuilt (E2104 cites #5984). Swizzle write is broken (lowlevel/swizzle.jet FAILs on all tiers). Rows needing no new syntax are in implementation; B0-B10 go to owner ballots.

criteria.text: A dated audit in Docs/audits lists every Odin array/matrix/quaternion/simd/soa feature with Jet status and probe; every row is PASS or has a linked card or owner ballot.

Numeric fixed arrays [T#N] support element-wise + - * / % and bit operators with another [T#N] and with a scalar, unary minus and ==, as goldens on O0/O1/O2; length or element mismatches are registered diagnostics with UI snapshots.

Matrix and quaternion operations the audit marks as Odin built-ins have a Jet equivalent proven by goldens, or a linked card or ballot.

cards.title: Portable wasm seed: bootstrap Jet from the repo alone with a C compiler (jet compiler as wasm + tiny C wasm interpreter)
cards.body: Split from #4154 step 3 (owner-approved plan, 2026-10-01; split approved by Main, 2026-10-29). #4154 closes on steps 1–2 (the tagged chain and per-release seed binaries). This card owns the third leg: a portable seed checked into the repo and refreshed occasionally, like Zig's zig1.wasm. It is the Jet compiler built to WebAssembly plus a tiny C wasm interpreter, so any machine with a C compiler can bootstrap from the repo alone, with no downloads and no older Jet binary. Today the self-hosted backend emits only x86-64 (Compiler/JetBackend/Source/X64). The wasm32 target triples exist only as target-machine facts (TargetMachine.jet wasm.browser / wasm.wasi), with no wasm code emitter. So the first prerequisite is a JetIR → wasm32 core-module emitter. The wasm decoder and validator from the plugin engine (#5487, Docs/proposals/plugin-wasm-engine-2026-10-29.md) are reusable for checking the emitted seed. Related: #5455 (bootstrappability from a small seed as the trusting-trust answer).
cards.plan: 1. A JetIR → wasm32 core-module emitter (wasm 1.0 + bulk memory + multi-value), with a minimal WASI-like host import set (args, environ, fd read/write/seek, path open/stat/readdir, clock, exit) that is exactly what jet build needs. 2. Build the compiler (Compiler/ workspace, JetCli) to jet.wasm and check it with the #5487 validator. 3. A small C99 wasm interpreter (one file, no dependencies) that implements that import set over POSIX. 4. A bootstrap script: cc the interpreter, run jet.wasm to build native s1 from the repo, then s2 = s3 fixed point against the released seed. 5. Check the seed in (compressed, with recorded sha256) and document the refresh: who regenerates it, and when.

Body: Part of the portable wasm seed card (#4154 step 3 split; q/cards/owner-1029b/wasm-seed.json). Today the self-hosted backend emits only x86-64 (Compiler/JetBackend/Source/X64). This step lowers JetIR to a core wasm module and builds the compiler itself. Estimate 80-120 h. Plan: Reuse Compiler/JetWasm's types, binary encoder and validator. Lower JetIR functions, calls, linear memory, globals, data segments and the function table (indirect calls) to wasm 1.0 + bulk memory + multi-value. Define the stack and heap layout and the C-ABI-like call convention. Add `jet build --target=wasm32-wasi`. Grow coverage from the golden examples up to the Compiler workspace.

cards.title: Value passing is physically optimal: named-tuple returns in registers, last-use moves are true moves, and large read-only values pass by address
cards.body: Owner direction (2026-10-29): multiple returns (Jet named tuples) and value passing must be maximally performant, optimal and efficient. Last-use moves are ratified (D-COPY-DEFAULT1=A, D-CALLSITE-MARK2=A; spec.md ~1103-1150). Calls carry no marks; a take is declared && in the signature (D-MOVE-SIGIL1=A) and an early move is written x.move(), including for fields, values with cleanup, type parameters and lambda captures. Nobody has verified that the generated code actually achieves this. The nbody profile (#3039 C6) already showed hidden heap boxes and copy/drop helpers on hot paths.
cards.plan: Write a small benchmark and inspect corpus (jet inspect code, D-CODE-INSPECT1) at O1/O2: (1) functions returning small named tuples (2-4 scalar fields): the result must come back in registers, with no heap and no stack round-trip beyond the ABI; (2) last-use moves of List/String/struct locals into take parameters and receivers: no copy, no extra retain/release; (3) large read-only struct parameters: passed by address, with no copy; (4) the `^`-required exception cases: confirm each is required for meaning, not for a codegen limitation. Fix every gap in the backend and IR. Add each case as a paired perf cell against the C/Rust equivalent per the performance gate.

log.text: HELD by owner order 2026-11-11 (no small optimizations until the language is mostly stable; architecture and regression fixes go first, per #5479 c5-c8). These criteria stay open and unworked: c4 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c); c7 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c); c8 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c); c9 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c).
Owner deconfliction 2026-11-06: D-CALLSITE-MARK2=A supersedes D-CALLSITE-MARK1=A's ^ exceptions.

Retargeted c4 (owner order 2026-11-02: an invalid criterion is retargeted to a valid one). Old text: Each case has a perf cell at parity or better against C/Rust (Rust <= 1.05) Why: AGENTS.md performance gate: Rust has no parity band (Jet/Rust must be below 1.00 like every peer) and every required cell needs a machine-ceiling reference. The old 'Rust <= 1.05' band is retired.

C4 measured on f75020e91d (IrTypes-2, one build slot, 7 runs pinned to CPU 31, clang-21 -O2 / rustc 1.97 -O3, loaded machine): LOSES. Jet/Rust and Jet/C at O2: multi-return 2.86 / 3.12, recursion-aggregate 2.82 / 2.85, fixed-return-64 1.50 / 2.79, destructure-move 0.82 / 3.02. At O1: 3.15/3.44, 5.16/5.24, 2.40/4.45, 0.66/2.45. Table: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/IR/IrTypes/perf/m1.txt, runner perf/fb.sh. multi-return's O2 IR is fully scalar-replaced, so the gap is arithmetic: floordiv/mod use idiv plus a floor fixup, % 13 gets no magic multiply, every division has a trap check, and every loop iteration has a stop_poll. That work is #6205.

cards.title: Research: modularity, scalability and extensibility of every layer of Jet, then one extension-architecture design
cards.body: Owner direction (2026-10-29): every level, semantic, syntax, feature and scope of Jet must be analysed through the lens of modularity, scalability and extensibility, so that every domain can grow indefinitely the way D-CORE-BOUNDARY1 makes hardware a library change and D-INFRA1 makes infrastructure typed Jet code. Hardware and FFI are two drops in that ocean. A dedicated research agent (owner-approved) does this.
cards.plan: Write a dated research document in Docs/research that covers every layer: lexical/syntax, the type system, semantics (effects, memory, errors, concurrency, evaluation, comptime), the compiler pipeline, the runtime, tooling, build/packages, every standard-library domain, deployment/targets, and evolution over time. For each layer: what is closed today and where (file:line, measured), the possible extension mechanisms, prior art with citations, costs (performance, tooling, readability, safety, I8 one mechanism, I9 tiers), and what the evidence favours. Then draft one extension-architecture design meeting the ballot rework bar, and specify a 'no closed lists' gate.

cards.title: Native struct layout is physically optimized (reordered and packed) on every type, and C interop works with that optimized layout
cards.body: Owner direction (2026-10-29): always keep the compiler's memory-layout optimization, unlike Rust where #[repr(C)] turns field reordering off. C interop and FFI must be confirmed working with the optimizations on. Current state (Main probe on dev bb9c74e522): a default struct reports kind "default", guarantee "physical layout unspecified" and no size fact (Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Comptime/Reflection.jet:682-723; `Mixed.$layout.size` is empty). The same 5-field struct {U8, Int, U8, Int, U8} under #Layout(c) is 40 bytes, while the optimal order is 24. Runtime record glue (e.g. JetRuntime/Source/DataPlotFlat.jet:68-92) stores each field in its own 8-byte word in a jet_rt_alloc block. That suggests default records are heap blocks with a word per field, the same cost the nbody profile showed for [T#N] (#3039 C6).
cards.plan: 1. Measure the real native representation of default structs (stack vs heap, word-per-field vs packed) at O0/O1/O2. 2. Make the default layout physical and optimal: fields ordered by alignment then size, small fields packed, niches used for optionals (D-MEM-UNBOX1), inline (not heap) for value structs, and a defined $layout size/offset fact. 3. C interop with optimization on: a Jet type exported to C emits its C declaration in the optimized field order, so C sees the same bytes with zero copies. A type imported from a C header keeps that header's layout because it is a C type. Today's 'wire mirror' copy at the boundary (syntax-decisions D-PLACE1 text) is removed wherever the layouts already coincide. 4. #Layout(c) remains only for matching an externally fixed layout; if its public meaning changes, that part goes to the owner through the ballot bar. 5. Prove it with a C round-trip test: C reads and writes Jet-exported optimized structs, on every tier.

log.text: HELD by owner order 2026-11-11 (no small optimizations until the language is mostly stable; architecture and regression fixes go first, per #5479 c5-c8). These criteria stay open and unworked: c4 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c); c6 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c).

OWNER RULING 2026-10-30 (verbatim): 'keep field order unchanged' for hand-written #Layout(c) structs that mirror an outside layout. Final rule: every struct defined in Jet source is layout-optimized, including ones exported to C (C gets a generated declaration in Jet's order). #Layout(c) marks a layout owned elsewhere and keeps its written field order, as do C types imported by use from a header or C source.

OWNER DIRECTION 2026-10-30 (verbatim): 'if we define the layout in our source, then we should optimize it. If we are pulling it from elsewhere we shouldnt change it.' Applied: every struct defined in Jet source is layout-optimized, including ones exported to C (C gets a generated declaration in Jet's order). Types pulled from elsewhere, such as C structs imported from a header or C source by use (D-FFI-CINPUT1 A), keep the foreign layout unchanged. Open edge sent to the owner: hand-written #Layout(c) structs that mirror an outside layout (Jetpack HeaderParser structs, embedded MMIO register blocks) count as 'defined in our source' by the literal reading, which would reorder them.

Landed bc8aba3913: C1 C2 C3 C5 met. C4 (perf cell vs C/Rust for the packed layout) stays open; the struct-packed cell is ready in IrTypes-2's tree, measurement paused by the owner's overnight priorities.

Main reading of the owner direction (reported for confirmation): every Jet-owned struct gets the optimized layout, including structs exported to C, which get a generated C declaration in offset order (C3). #Layout(c) keeps C declaration order, because it marks layouts the foreign side owns (Jetpack HeaderParser structs and the embedded MMIO register blocks); reordering those would break them. No new marker is added. If the owner wants #Layout(c) reordered as well, the foreign-owned layouts would need a different spelling, which is a ballot.

Correction from IrTypes-2's measurement (e6, jet emit --ir at none/full plus O2 objdump): default user structs are NOT heap. They are one IR Aggregate in a stack slot on every tier, laid out in declaration order with natural C alignment (Mixed {Bool, Float, U8, I32, Float} = 32 B; reordered and packed = 24 B). The word-per-field heap glue is the runtime's 163 hand-written jet_rt_record_new_*/jet_rt_handle_* shims for specific Core types (boxed records at the Core/runtime boundary), not user structs. Read-only by-value params already pass by address. Returns copy from a frame temp into the caller's sret (#6201 C6). The remaining scope of this card is reordering/packing, the  size fact, C export in the optimized order, and whether those boxed runtime records should become plain aggregates.

cards.title: Lambda is an unnamed function: `fn(n: Int) -> Int { n * n }` (ballot D-LAMBDA-FN1)
cards.body: Owner idea (2026-10-29): a lambda is a function without its name, just as `A | B` is an unnamed enum (D-UNIONTYPE1). Today `->` starts the result type in `fn f(x: Int) -> Int {}` and in the type `fn(Int) -> Int`, but starts the body in a lambda `(n: Int) -> n * n`. So `(n: Int) -> Int { n * n }` silently parses `Int{n * n}` as a typed value, and adding a line makes it E0399. Census at d345e35902: 4,768 lambdas in 1,194 files, 59.1% relying on E0801 inference. Ballot D-LAMBDA-FN1 decides the form.
cards.plan: After ratification: parser (fn + `(` in value position parses an unnamed function, reusing the callable signature parser), sema (written result/error types checked against the expected type; the declaration rules apply when there is no expected type), a `jet fix` migration of all lambdas, and updates to the spec, the syntax registry, editor grammars, examples and diagnostics in one cutover.

cards.title: Debug info for optimized builds: DW_TAG_inlined_subroutine entries and location lists for locals at -O1/-O2
cards.body: Found by RustOut7-2 while probing lldb on a native jet build at 236cd9310c for #6221 P1. At the default optimization level, inlined functions (e.g. `area`) leave no inlined_subroutine entries, and most locals have no location, so `--release` binaries can't be debugged meaningfully. #6221 P1 covers aggregate type DWARF and makes `jet debug` build with optimize=none/inline=off. This card covers the optimized tiers, which C compilers support (gcc/clang -O2 -g).

cards.body: Found by BallotDesign (probes $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/q/bd/probe/ext). Compiler/Prelude/core/prelude.jet:21-22 declares `fn check(text: String) Error! -[]>` and `fn encode_hole<T: Printable>(value: T) String -[]>`. In user code `String -[]>` is E0003 (only `-[]> String` is accepted), and user traits cannot declare bodiless methods at all (E0081 '`fn name` has no body'). Pillar 5: Core may use no form a package can't write.
cards.plan: Make the Prelude use the user grammar (`-[]> String`). Decide whether user traits may declare required (bodiless) methods; if the ratified trait design allows required methods, lift E0081 for trait declarations. Otherwise the Prelude must use the same form users use. Cutover in one patch.

c180 scope ruling (Main, 2026-11-11): the rule counts entries, not the name run. An entry is the load's entry file or any file a package or project declares as an entry or binary: a `run: fn` entry or a script body. Within one load graph, package or project, entries are all script bodies or all `run` entries, and a script-style scope has exactly one script file. Library functions that happen to be named run (Core/Game/Game.jet:23 game.run(scene, …), Core/Tasks/Tasks.jet:230 tasks.run()) only run when called, so they don't count and are not renamed (a public API rename would be owner-gated). A UI case proves importing core.game from a script stays legal.

Clarification of the D-FILE-STATEMENTS1 withdrawal (owner, 2026-11-11: run fn and script style are both allowed, and mutually exclusive within one file). This is the rule as built. From MemDesign #6385 research (2026-10-30): an unknown static method on a builtin number type (for example U8.from_int) reports a misleading E0107 "Nothing named `U8`"; it should report E0311 naming the type and the method. Folded here as part of C22 instead of a new criterion on #6389.

Merged #6183 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: A local trait implemented through `impl labels.Tag.Mine` passes coherence, but calling its method gives E0102. Body: Found by IrTypes-2 while working on g10 (#6170/#6171/#6172, 2026-10-29) on jet-u13 / dev 36825b7a15; the repro is in the IrTypes-g10 msg. Not fixed by g10. A local trait implemented with a module-qualified head (`impl labels.Tag.Mine`) is accepted by coherence, but a call to its method is refused with E0102, so the impl can never be used. Plan: Reproduce from the g10 msg. Make method resolution find impls registered under a qualified head, using the same key that coherence uses. Add a case test.

Merged #6181 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: `Mat3<Int>(...)` silently ignores its type argument; a missing static method on Mat3 reports E0107 "Nothing named Mat3". Body: Found by KitSpeed-2's #6177 Odin array audit (2026-10-29; probes in kitspeed/w6177/probes, run at O0 and full on 25f9dee, with both tiers agreeing). (1) Writing a type argument on a non-generic Core math type, `Mat3<Int>(...)`, is accepted and the argument is silently discarded, so the program builds a Float matrix. It should be a registered diagnostic. (2) Calling a static method that doesn't exist on Mat3 reports E0107 "Nothing named `Mat3`" instead of E0311 naming the missing method. Plan: Reproduce with the audit probes. In sema, reject type arguments on non-generic types (registered code, UI snapshot), and route missing static methods on an existing type to E0311.

Merged #6285 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: `[T]{}` means the empty list in an expression but is E0003 as a field default (`values: [DBValue]{}`). Body: Found by BallotDesign (probe $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/q/bd/probe/ext/holes_b_default.jet). A field default `values: [DBValue]{}` is E0003 'Expected a value'; only `[DBValue]{[]}` parses. In expressions, `[DBValue]{}` is the empty list. The same text should mean the same thing in both places. Plan: Accept `[T]{}` as the empty-list default in field position (one grammar rule shared with expressions). Migrate any `{[]}` defaults if the ratified spelling is `{}`.

Merged #6284 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: A static trait method cannot return `Self`: `-> Self` gives E0108, and `-> Cypher` gives E0913. Body: Found by BallotDesign (probe $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/q/bd/probe/ext/self_static.jet). In an impl of a trait whose static method returns Self, writing `-> Self` and returning `Cypher{...}` reports E0108 'This needs Self, but the value is Cypher'; writing `-> Cypher` reports E0913 (signature mismatch). Self must be the implementing type inside an impl. Plan: In sema, resolve Self to the impl's target type in static trait methods (signature and body), consistently with instance methods. Add a golden and a ui snapshot for a true mismatch.

Merged #6283 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Two spellings of unit success: `Ok(())` and `Ok()` in the corpus. Body: Found by BallotDesign: Examples/ has 13 lines of `Ok(())` and 12 of `Ok()` (for example web/state_surface.jet:42). Reaching the end of an `E!` body already succeeds. One meaning needs one spelling (I8). Plan: Pick the canonical form from the ratified decisions (or ballot it if none decides), migrate every caller in one cutover, and make the other spelling a diagnostic with a jet fix.

Merged #6282 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Impl methods do not inherit the trait method's declared effect row (E0907 asks to restate `-[]>`). Body: Found by BallotDesign (probe $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/q/bd/probe/ext/unit_norow.jet). An impl of CheckedText.check without `-[]>` gets E0907 'must be pure. Declare this CheckedText method pure', even when the body is pure. The trait's declared row is not used as the impl's row. Under D-EFFECT-OMIT1 rows are inferred, and an impl should take its row from the trait (a pure body checks; an impure one reports E0907 at the effect). Plan: In sema, an impl method with no written row takes the trait method's declared row as its ceiling and checks the body against it. Update the E0907 snapshot to point at the offending effect.

Merged #6257 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Is Float Comparable? The generic bound `T: Comparable` admits Float, but `#Comparable` on a Float field is E0905 and Solver.jet:258 says Float isn't Comparable. Body: Found by Ballots-4 for #6174 (probes $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/q/b4/p74/gen2.jet, gen3.jet). TypeRelations.jet:1168 treats Float as a member of the scalar family at generic bounds, so min/max over Float work and NaN propagates. Deriving #Comparable on a struct with a Float field is refused (E0905), and the solver has a Float-specific 'isn't Comparable' fix text. One meaning (I8) needs one answer: either Float is Comparable everywhere, with NaN-propagating comparisons (the generic-bound behaviour min/max now relies on), or nowhere (and min/max over Float need a separate ordering such as total_cmp). Plan: Pick the meaning that matches the ratified Comparable contract (Docs/spec, D-CORE-LAWS1 laws for Comparable). Make the bound, derive and solver diagnostics agree, and add UI tests for each path. If the contract is silent and a choice is needed, it is an owner ballot.

Merged #6252 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: `return` inside a braced lambda passed to generic `map` is checked against the enclosing function (E0113) instead of the lambda. Body: Found by Ballots-4 while probing for D-LAMBDA-FN1: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/q/b4/lamp/p12.jet. A `return` inside a braced lambda body passed to a generic `map` is type-checked against the enclosing fn's result type and reports E0113. The retired Rust test sort_comparator_early_return_is_local_to_lambda expected `return` to be local to the lambda, and spec S47 says return leaves the lambda. Plan: Make lambda bodies a return scope in sema for every call shape, including generic callees whose result is solved from the body. Port the Rust test as a case/golden.

Merged #6199 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: A comma between enum cases gives a misleading E0003 ("Expected a name for a variant name", fix "e.g. `main`"). Body: Found by Main (2026-10-29, dev bb9c74e522). `enum Color { Red, Green, Blue }` reports E0003 "Expected a name for a variant name, found `,`". The Why is "Names start with a letter or `_`" and the Fix is "e.g. `main`, `count`, `_tmp`". The real cause is that enum cases are separated by whitespace or newlines, not commas, and every user coming from Rust, Swift, TS or C writes the comma. The diagnostic must name the actual rule and offer a machine fix that drops the commas. If the owner changes the separator rule (enum comma question, 2026-10-29), this card follows that outcome instead. Plan: In the enum case parser, detect a `,` where a case name is expected after a case and report a dedicated registered diagnostic (what/why/fix: enum cases are separated by spaces or newlines; remove the comma) with a structured fix. Add a UI snapshot. Re-check after the owner's separator ruling.

criteria.text: Owner ruling 2026-11-09 (language review): a callable's signature always puts its arrow before the result: parameters, then `->` or the effect row `-[…]>`, then the result type, then the error contract. The error-first order (`fn(path: Path) IOError! -[FS.Write]>`, 455 signatures in Core on dev 6a06b917cb) is not valid Jet: a unit result is simply omitted after the arrow (`fn(path: Path) -[FS.Write]> IOError!`). The parser refuses the old order with a registered diagnostic and a UI snapshot, jet fmt or jet fix rewrites it, and every signature in Core, Compiler, Jetpack, Tools, Examples and tests is migrated in the same cutover.

Owner ruling 2026-11-09 (language review): a file of top-level statements just runs. A file whose top level holds statements is a program and its statements are its entry, in order; a file with `run: fn` is a program; a file with both is an error with a registered diagnostic and a UI snapshot; a file with neither is a library. E0621 no longer refuses `print("hi")` alone in a file, the first-hour guide drops that lesson, and cases prove the same meaning on O0, O1 and O2 for jet run FILE, jet -e and piped input.

criteria.text: Owner ruling 2026-11-09 (language review): Jet has no warnings. A style point that jet fmt can rewrite is rewritten by jet fmt and never reported (the final-return and positional-Bool lints that print thousands of lines when Jet's own runtime compiles are of this kind). Everything else that matters is an error. To stay friendly to someone in the middle of building, tidiness errors (an unused binding, an unused import, unreachable code) never stop jet run or jet dev: the program runs and they are not printed; jet check and jet build list every one and exit non-zero, so the list works as a todo list. The L-code class is retired or re-registered under these three rules, each with its UI snapshot, and the whole repository is clean under jet check.

Owner ruling 2026-11-09 (language review): `shared` is a type, not a keyword. A shared holder is built like every other typed value, `Shared{value}` (T inferred from the value), in a binding, a field initializer or a module-level declaration; the `shared value` keyword form is removed from the parser and the syntax registry with no teaching diagnostic and no jet fix rule for the old spelling (the old form gets only the parser's ordinary error, as for any unknown word), and every use in Core, Compiler, Jetpack, Tools, Examples and tests is migrated in the same cutover. Behavior (locking, handle copies, task crossing, the cycle rule) is unchanged by this criterion.

criteria.text: Owner ruling 2026-11-09 (language review): a module-level `name: value` is a guarantee, not a try. It is always evaluated while building; one that fails while building, or that cannot run then because it has effects, is a build error with a registered diagnostic and UI snapshot whose fix names the three ways out (move it into `run`, make it lazy explicitly, or use a pinned build input such as embed_file). No code runs before `run`. Today `BAD: 10 / zero()` at module level passes jet check and jet build and stops at first use with E3010 (probe, seed a0_042). Inside a function a plain `name: value` still only tries to fold; in a file of top-level statements the lines are the program and run in order. Cases prove the same meaning on O0, O1 and O2, and every module-level binding in Core, Compiler, Jetpack, Tools, Examples and tests is clean under the rule in the same cutover.

criteria.text: D-LANG-MIGRATE1=A is built. Every breaking language change lands with a registered rewrite: one codemod plan per change in Compiler/Migrations, named by toolchain version, each with an old-spelling fixture the suite replays. `jet fix` applies every rewrite since the toolchain in the lock, or since `--since`. criteria.text: D-API-SURFACE1=A is built (owner ratified 2026-11-11): `jet check` compares a package's public promises (signatures and effects) against its recorded package.api sheet and reports a changed promise with a registered diagnostic (what, why and fix, plus UI snapshot) that tells the author to accept it. `jet check --accept-api` rewrites package.api. `jet registry publish` computes the minimum semantic version from the promise diff (a new required effect on a released function is a major bump), and the author may raise it but never lower it. Goldens or CLI #Tests cover an unchanged API, an added function (minor), a function newly needing Time (major) and an author raise.

Owner order 2026-11-11: a program is EITHER script style OR a single run entry, never mixed, with no workaround at any scope. If a `run: fn` exists anywhere in the program's load graph, its package or its project (any module, nested module, re-export, import rename such as `use { run: other.main }`, or code a marker or template generates), then top-level executable statements anywhere in that scope are refused, and the reverse also holds. A script-style program has exactly one file with top-level statements, its entry, and no `run: fn` anywhere. Today E0621 covers only both in one file and E0620 covers only an imported script body, so an entry script whose imported module or package declares `run: fn` is not refused. One registered diagnostic (what, why and fix, plus a UI snapshot) names both sites. UI cases cover the same file, an imported module, another module of the same package, a renamed import, a re-export and generated code. Before landing, sweep every Jet source in the repository (Core, Compiler, Jetpack, Tools, Examples, tests and fixtures) and migrate every hit in the same batch.

A grant naming one library doesn't cover another library in the same language, and the ballot program prints 7. Owner: G6Decl. criteria.text: A ?? fallback that returns a value built from err.copy() keeps the left side's type. cards.title: Rebuild Tower in Jet: the board's CLI, store, server and web UI become a Jet web application (stress test for Jet as a web domain language)
cards.body: Owner order 2026-10-30: 'Rebuilding tower in jet rather than TS/JS will be the goal as a stress test for jet as a web domain language.' Tower today is a Node application under Tools/tower (63 .mjs/.js files: CLI tower.mjs, app/store.mjs, app/server.mjs, the web UI and tests). The rebuild uses Jet's web stack end to end (Core web, HTTP server, routing, live UI, storage), so every gap it finds is a Jet defect or missing capability, recorded as a criterion here or a gap card. The board data in Tools/tower/.tower/ keeps its format unless the owner rules otherwise, so the cutover needs no data migration. The owner runs tower serve; agents use the CLI.

log.text: Owner order 2026-11-11: Tower is not to be rebuilt in Jet any time soon. Removed from G9 and given no goal, so no lane works it. Tower stays on node.

BoardPlanner review 2026-11-09 (dev 6a06b917cb). Tagged G9: Tower rebuilt as a Jet web application is the web goal's stress test. c9-c54 are Node Tower behaviors folded in; they are the parity list for c2/c3.

criteria.text: A gap census: every capability Tower uses (HTTP server and routing, file-backed JSON store with atomic writes and locking, CLI argument parsing, live web UI, markdown rendering, the test suite) is mapped to a Jet Core API that exists or to a named gap, committed under Docs/research with file:line evidence.

The Tower CLI is a Jet program with the same commands, flags, output and exit codes; Tools/tower's own test suite, ported to jet test, passes against it, and the board files it writes are byte-identical to the Node version's on the same operations.
tower serve is a Jet web application serving the same board UI and live updates; a scripted browser test drives the main flows (cards, criteria, decisions, ballots, questions) on the Jet server.
Cutover: Tools/tower holds no .mjs/.js/.ts outside generated browser output (per the #5201 rule); AGENTS.md, skills and docs name the Jet commands; nothing falls back to Node.
A Tower workload cell in the perf manifest compares the Jet server with the Node one (request latency and memory) under the performance gate.

cards.title: Cache control and visibility: give programs control over L1/L2/L3 use and show where code leaves cache for RAM or disk
cards.body:
Owner question 2026-10-30 (verbatim): 'Cache hits are critical -> how can we give control over L1,2,3 cache, visualize when we are no longer in cache & go to RAM or HDD/SSD?'

Starting facts: D-CACHE-CONTROL1 A is ratified (mem.prefetch(place, .Read|.Write, level: .L1), mem.stream_store, the build fact for the cache-line size, each needing a paired gauntlet cell). #Layout(c, align(N)) and D-PLACE1 cover alignment; #Layout(columnar) covers SoA. Whether any of this is implemented is unproven; this card measures it.

log.text: HELD by owner order 2026-11-11 (no small optimizations until the language is mostly stable; architecture and regression fixes go first, per #5479 c5-c8). These criteria stay open and unworked: c4 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c).

Update: the full original cache-control1-wip.patch is recovered (31 files, 71,012 bytes, the same size as the original): $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/recovery/6312/cache-control1-wip.patch, with SOURCES.md. Recover integrates it under c5.

It applies to 67fd7fdc47 and conflicts in 7 files on dev; generated rows are to be regenerated. The Recover lane integrates it under c5, and its landing also corrects Tools/tower/held/6312/README.md, which still says the compiler half is gone.
The 3 surviving cache-control test files are now in the repo at Tools/tower/held/6312/ (landed e07c1b85ae). c5 integrates them; the Recover lane is rebuilding the missing compiler half now.

Lost-work status (owner 2026-11-04: recover it, or record it as incomplete so it is never reported done): cache-control1-wip.patch (31 files, 783 lines, base 67fd7fdc47; D-CACHE-CONTROL1 A) is gone. Its three test files survive in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/MemDesign/t1: Examples/features/memory/cache_line_padding.jet, Examples/features/memory/stream_store.jet and tests/conformance/corpus/core/mem/stream_store.jet. The compiler half (IR StreamStore, the x64 movnti plus sfence encoder, registry and Core rows, the Core/Mem wrapper, the $build.cpu.cache_line fact and #Layout align() parsing, E1105 text) is missing; the search of agent transcripts and git objects continues. No criterion was met by that patch; the implementation is tracked by the criterion added today.

Missing: mem.prefetch with the D-CACHE-CONTROL2=A index-gather cell; no CHECK OK; base predates dev 215 + wave 8. work-1.patch and gen.patch in the same dir are earlier cuts it supersedes. Inventory: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/MemDesign/HELD.md. Next owner: finish prefetch, rebase, lane-check, drop.

Unbuilt work in progress for C4 (D-CACHE-CONTROL1 A): $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/MemDesign/cache-control1-wip.patch (31 files, 783 lines, base 67fd7fdc47). It adds $build.cpu.cache_line (registry fact, align() parser, E1105 text) and mem.stream_store (IROp.StreamStore, x64 movnti plus sfence, Core rows, conformance fixture, two examples, core-library.md). Never built; missing s1-s3 build, o0/o1/o2 goldens, lane-check and AOT paired cells (the surface pair harness must learn AOT pairs first).
