cards.title: Type conversions: make explicit conversion clean (owner asks about Int{myFloat}-style constructor casts)
cards.body:
Owner question 2026-10-30 (verbatim): 'Type conversions generally need casts, how can we make this clean? Should casting be done by wrapping the value to cast in a type literal constructor? like Int{myFloatVar}?'

Starting facts: D-SHAPE-CONVERT1 A (ratified 2026-07-14, #566) makes conversion destination-owned: Target.from_source(value) (U8.from_int(n) ?? return, UserId.from_int(raw)); checked narrowing is fallible; safe widening is implicit; casts, to_* and convert() are refused. D-JAI-SMALL1 A adds #As member conversion. Type{...} braces already mean typed literals and field defaults (String{""}, ANSI{"..."}), so Int{x} would overlap them.

log.text: Deconfliction 2026-11-06: reworded to match the owner order that a retired spelling gets no teaching diagnostic, UI snapshot or jet fix rule.

Owner 2026-10-30 on float to int: 'for integer, let's do the swift/rust style. we have advanced APIs with variadics and optionals and defaults and named vs positional etc. but dont think we really use them, but this may be a good place for that.' Direction for the ballot: separate exact conversion (fails unless the value is whole and in range, like Swift Int(exactly:) and Rust TryFrom) from the deliberate lossy forms (truncate, round, saturate), and use Jet's named, defaulted and optional parameters for the lossy choices.

OWNER 2026-10-30 (verbatim): 'what about casts as a kind of generic trait that can be implemented? then using the Int{myFloatVar} would detect that you are trying to construct an int literal and detect the type of the internal type, then use the implemented conversion trait implicitly? Thoughts'. Main's findings: Type{x} conversion already exists for scalar heads under D-DOTCTOR3 and its 2026-09-28 amendment (#3739; syntax-decisions.md:1187-1229): Float{n}, U8{i}, F32{v}, Int{I64{v}} work, and Int{myFloat} is deliberately E0112. Those rules are compiler-builtin while from_* (about 2821 call sites) is a second mechanism. The #6313 ballot leads with the owner's trait design.

criteria.text: A dated Docs/research note answers the owner's question: the current rule and how it reads in real code (counted call sites in Core, Examples and Compiler), the pain points with evidence, how Int{x} would interact with typed literals, field defaults and checked text, which conversions are lossy (float to int rounding, narrowing, sign) and how each must be spelled, and prior art (Rust as/From/TryFrom, Swift Int(x), Zig @intCast, Odin cast, Go T(x)).
criteria.evidence: Docs/research/2026-10-30-type-conversions.md (SurfaceDesign-docs.patch): current rule with file:line (BuiltinStatics.jet:175/212, Checked.jet:389), probes m6313/m6313b/m6313c/m6313p o0=o1=o2; lossy cases (float->int truncation, Float.from_int rounding, narrowing wrap, sign); typed-literal and checked-text interaction; census of from_float/from_int/_rounded/round sites in Core, Examples, Compiler; prior-art table (Rust as/From/TryFrom, Swift, Zig, Go, C, Java, C#, Python, Kotlin, JS)

criteria.text: A ballot-ready Tower decision presents same-program alternatives (keep Target.from_source; Int{x}; Int(x); others the research finds), each with exact spelling for widening, checked narrowing, rounding, saturating and wrapping, and the beginner and expert paths; it states which earlier decisions it amends.
criteria.evidence: D-CONVERT-TRAIT1 added to Tower on card #6313 (ballot-ready: Tower decision add validation passed, readycheck READY, plaincheck PLAIN OK, recommendation losses []).

criteria.text: D-CONVERT-TRAIT1=A is built: From(S) is a Core trait with one method from(value: S) -> Self; impl Celsius.From(Float) makes Celsius{x} and Celsius.from(x) work; To(T) is only a bound (prep S: To(Float) means Float.From(S) exists), and writing impl X.To(Y) is an error whose fix writes impl Y.From(X). Every caller, example, test and doc is migrated in one cutover, the old spelling is not Jet syntax and gets no diagnostic, UI snapshot or jet fix rule (owner order 2026-11-06), and the examples pass on O0, O1 and O2.

impl Celsius -> Float no longer gives the self-contradicting E0113 naming the internal errconv_Celsius_to_Float; after ratification the declaration follows the D-CONVERT-TRAIT1 outcome with a user-facing diagnostic and a UI snapshot.

D-FLOAT-INT1 = A is built. Int{f} converts a whole, finite, in-range Float and otherwise stops with a registered error that names math.trunc, floor, ceil, round and round_even; a literal body is checked at compile time. New math.round_even(f) -> Int rounds ties to even. checked(Int{f}) gives None where Int{f} would stop, and saturating(Int{f}) truncates, clamps and maps NaN to 0, on every integer head (Int, I64, U8, I16, ...); no from_float or saturating_from method exists. math.round and round_even stop on NaN, infinity and out of range. Every in-repository caller is migrated, and each form has a UI snapshot and a golden example on O0, O1, O2 and web. (was #6151 c51)

cards.title: Custom allocators and struct-of-arrays: native, complete support and its interactions
cards.body:
Owner questions 2026-10-30 (verbatim): 'How can jet support custom allocators? What does this feature intefere with? Does this overlap with anything? Can we just support it natively? what about soa data types? We should support those.'

Starting facts: D-REGION1/D-ALLOC1/D-ALLOC2 (mem.Arena, scope-bound views, E0631/E0632), D-FIXED-BACKING1 (mem.Fixed), D-ALLOCFAIL1 (try_alloc family, AllocError), D-ALLOC-DEFAULT1 A (Jet-written size-class mem.Heap), D-TARGET-ALLOC1, D-SOA1/D-SOA2A-D (#Layout(columnar), whole-struct only, E1107-E1109), D-SOA-SITE1 A and D-SOA-TIER1 A. Core/Mem/Mem.jet declares empty struct Arena {}, Bump {} and Pool<T> {}. #6109 (Arena/Bump .alloc) closed; #6310 is an allocator-view ICE; #5042/#5043 are allocator speed cards.

log.text: Unlanded work, recorded 2026-11-12 (dead-lane sweep, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/sweep/deadlanes/REPORT.md). Staged in Main/inbox from the dead G3Ctx lane and not on dev: G3Ctx-5/6 (c3), G3Ctx-9 (c9, the ICE 101 fix), G3Ctx-10..14 (c8), and G3Ctx-16/16r and 17/17b (c3 slices 2a and 2b). G3Ctx-18 (c3 completion: a user mem.Allocator value as a #Context(allocator:) carrier) is only work in progress, saved as $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/sweep/deadlanes/G3Ctx-t9.patch, with its draft message at $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/G3Ctx/g3ctx18.msg. Each is rebased on dev and re-proved before landing. Owner: G12Docs-4 (G3), after #5971.

Ballot NEW-D-ALLOC-MIGRATE1 withdrawn 2026-11-11 after an adversarial rewrite (owner order: confusing or parallel ballots are redone, and questions an existing mechanism answers are decided rather than balloted). Decided: Migrate through ordinary recoverable error propagation: infer AllocError, admit it into typed domains unless an explicit nonallocating conversion exists, and retain Never only after proof or explicit handling. It extends: origin/dev:Core/Mem/Mem.jet:16-20 defines AllocError. D-ALLOC-FAIL1=C, read in full, requires ordinary allocation failure, typed admission or conversion, and proof or handling at Never boundaries. origin/dev:Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/CheckProgram.jet carries the ordinary failure solve; no allocation-specific failure system is needed. The full record is $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/ballots-v4/NEW-D-ALLOC-MIGRATE1/verdict.md. Withdrawal decides the direction; it does not mean the build is done.

Amends Main's 2026-11-11 c8 migration-form log, after G3Ctx's measured census ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/G3Ctx/c8/census.mjs, a name-based call-graph over-approximation on t4). Of 81,415 function bodies, 58,136 reach a growth call. Under the propagate rule, 21,549 Never! functions would drop Never! (Compiler 9,768, Core 5,495, Jetpack 4,416, Tools 1,607, tests 248), and 8,691 typed-domain functions would widen `E!` to `(E | AllocError)!` across about 300 error types (StoreError 703, IOError 461, SSLError 310), which breaks the field reads in `.Err(e)` arms. D-ALLOC-FAIL1=C says typed domains 'admit or convert' and does not choose between them, and the choice reshapes about 30k signatures and Core's public error types. That is public API at a scale the ballot did not measure, so it goes back to the owner as NEW-D-ALLOC-MIGRATE1 (admit as a union, convert with one impl AllocError -> E per type, or a mix by rule; and the Never! form: drop Never! and propagate, or keep it and handle once per function). D-ALLOC-FAIL1=C stays in force. Meanwhile the work that every outcome needs proceeds: the nonallocating AllocError -> Err (G3Ctx-10), fallible IR and runtime routes for every growth operation (List insert/extend, Map add/add_new/setdefault/update, String push_str), an inline fast path for plain push with a fallible slow path plus a paired perf cell, and the codemod with each outcome as a mode and a --census. The cutover itself waits for the vote.

c8 migration form, decided by Main on 2026-11-11 within D-ALLOC-FAIL1=C (no new ballot). G3Ctx measured the reach on t4: 27,821 growth call sites (Compiler 15,345, Jetpack 5,095, Core 4,147, Tools 3,234) and 22,279 Never! lines. The ratified text fixes the form: "first reduce plumbing through ordinary inference and propagation, then choose stopping once at a boundary"; Never! must prove or handle failure, and no flag silently changes a contract. The cutover is a program SUB (a codemod run on the composed train tree, with a --check mode), not a static patch. Its order: (1) an unannotated function infers AllocError, and nothing is written; (2) a typed-contract function whose domain admits it gains mem.AllocError in its contract, written in the source; (3) a Never! function that allocates loses Never! and propagates, unless it is a real no-failure boundary, which handles it once with `?? panic("no memory")` at its outermost call, never at each growth site; (4) entry points (the jet driver main, tool main and run functions) are the stopping boundaries. A per-call `?? panic` is used only where the codemod cannot find a boundary, and the SUB lists those sites. A paired perf cell (propagating growth against the pre-cutover build on a growth-heavy workload) proves the cost before ratification closes, and the census of the whole repository runs collect-all before the train.
D-SOA-SITE1 A retired the #Layout(columnar) marker in favour of Columns<T>; the criterion named the retired spelling.

criteria.text: A dated Docs/research note answers each owner question with evidence: what is ratified versus implemented (each allocator and columnar surface probed on o0/o1/o2, file:line), whether a user can write their own allocator today and through which trait, what custom allocators interfere or overlap with (ownership and drop, collections, Close resources, threads and tasks, FFI, the GC opt-in, comptime, the runtime heap), and prior art (Zig allocators, Odin context allocator, Rust Allocator API, C++ pmr, Jai SoA, Odin #soa).
criteria.evidence: Docs/research/2026-10-30-custom-allocators-and-soa.md (MemDesign.patch): allocator and columnar surfaces probed o0/o1/o2 (a1-a14, s1-s12, api/ 22 ops) with file:line; user allocator today (no trait); interference: regions, Mem effect, try_, drops, tasks, FFI, Close, GC opt-in (D-OPTGC1), comptime, runtime heap; prior art Zig, Odin context and #soa, Rust Allocator, C++ pmr, Jai SOA, Zig MultiArrayList.

criteria.text: Ballot-ready Tower decisions for every owner choice found, for example a public Allocator trait users implement, how collections take an allocator, and any SoA surface beyond #Layout(columnar) (per-field columns, SoA slices, partial SoA), each drafted to the ballot bar with same-program alternatives.
criteria.evidence: Ballots $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/MemDesign/ballot/D-ALLOC-TRAIT1.json and $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/MemDesign/ballot/D-ALLOC-SITE1.json; plaincheck-file.mjs -> PLAIN OK for both; SoA beyond whole structs has no ballot by evidence (Columns<T> absent: s3 E0003, s8 E0302), stated in the note section 3.

criteria.text: Every ratified allocator and SoA surface is implemented natively in Core and the compiler: a user-written allocator backs List, Map and String, and Columns<T> (D-SOA-SITE1 A, which retires #Layout(columnar)) supports the full logical-list API; each has examples with golden output on o0/o1/o2.

A dated Docs/research note compares Jet with Zig's MultiArrayList and SoA practice: layout, field-slice access, append and grow cost, iteration codegen (vectorization), and the ability to take a pointer or reference to one element's field inside a column and mutate through it; each probed on o0, o1 and o2 with timings.
criteria.evidence: Docs/research/2026-10-30-soa-vs-zig.md (landed 1b8925fb9f): layout and growth (lines 15-18), field-slice access (20-), references to an element field probed o0/o1/o2 (ref1-ref8, E0204/E0220, lines 51-63), append/sweep/update timings at n=2M best of 5 (73-102), vector-code counts (108-111).

criteria.text: Any owner choice the Zig comparison raises (for example element references into columns and their safety rule) is a ballot-ready Tower decision with recommendation.losses = [].
criteria.evidence: No owner choice raised by the Zig comparison: every gap is implementation under ratified D-SOA-SITE1 and D-ARRAY-COLUMNS1; stated with evidence in Docs/research/2026-10-30-soa-vs-zig.md section "Owner choices".

criteria.text: D-ALLOC-FAIL1=C is built. A refused allocation is recoverable by default, through one name and one stable error route, core.mem.AllocError, carried on the ordinary failure rail. The same code works whatever handlers surround it, and `?? panic("…")` is the explicit stop. The ballot program (load: fn() -> Int mem.AllocError! pushing three rows) prints 3, and prints 0 under a test allocator that refuses, on O0, O1 and O2. List, Map and String growth and reserve report AllocError through the same route, with no second error type. An unhandled AllocError has a UI snapshot, and the spec describes the route.

I2 defect found by G3Ctx, 2026-11-11, on seed-t20: passing a raw-pointer dereference as a borrowed place is ICE 101, "ir.build unlowered: write place Deref". The trigger is `bump(pointer.*)` where `bump: fn(c: &Counter) { c.n += 1 }` and `pointer := mem.from_addr<Counter>(mem.address_of(c))` inside #Unsafe. A generic `pointer.*.bump(by)` through a trait `&self` method fails the same way. The repros are $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/G3Ctx/probe/derefw.jet and a2fn.jet. IR lowering handles a Deref write place (a borrow of the pointee) on O0/O1/O2, and both repros become cases that print the bumped value.

D-REGION-ALLOC1=F is built (owner ratified 2026-11-11): a value built inside `#Context(allocator: arena)` that escapes the context is placed in its final owner's memory from creation, through the existing Context allocation route (Compiler/JetIR/Source/BuildTransact.jet:253-260), with no silent escape copy and no `_in` API family. An escape that can't be resolved is refused with a diagnostic naming the explicit repair. The ballot program prints ada;lin. Owner: the G3 lane. Proof: an example golden on O0, O1 and O2 printing the ballot's intended output, a UI snapshot for every diagnostic the form adds, and every in-repo use migrated in the same batch (greenfield, no old spelling kept).

cards.title: Terminal control API: broad, deep core.term so no external terminal library is needed
cards.body:
Owner order 2026-10-30 (verbatim): 'I want to ensure it is easy to use Terminal "commands" like "execute(term.clear_buffer, term.enable_raw_mode, term.enable_alternate_screen, term.hide_cursor)" with an excellent, broad and deep API so external libraries would not be needed'.

Starting facts: Core/Term/Term.jet (64 fns) and Core/Tui/Tui.jet (62 fns) exist; D-TUI-ANSI1 A (ANSI{...} checked text plus cursor, clearing, alternate-screen and mouse helpers returning one checked value), D-TERM-INCREMENTAL1 A (one lossless key decoder), D-CORE-TERMSTDIN1 A (is-a-terminal), D-CORE-PROCGROUP1 A. #6147 is an open ballot on whether the terminal UI leaves Core; this card's API must agree with its outcome. A grep finds no raw-mode or alternate-screen function in Core today.

log.text: Deconfliction 2026-11-06: reworded to match I9 tiers O0, O1, O2 and web (D-EXEC1, D-EXEC2=A: no interpreter or JIT); the Rust-free toolchain (Jet suites and tests/cases rows replace cargo tests and .rs sources).

#6563 c1 precut audit re-added 10 criteria from archived #1751, #2049, #2468, #2469: each was not proven on 9c7ddf1359. Row verdicts and reasons: Docs/audits/precut-2026-11/PRECUT-AUDIT.tsv (ff5dd7fd7b).

criteria.text: A dated Docs/research note maps the full capability set of crossterm, termion, ncurses, notcurses, Go tcell/bubbletea and Python blessed/prompt_toolkit (raw mode, alternate screen, cursor, clear, scroll regions, colors and styles, size and resize events, keyboard and mouse events, bracketed paste, focus, synchronized output, hyperlinks, images, Windows console) against Core/Term and Core/Tui with file:line, and lists every gap.
criteria.evidence: Docs/research/2026-10-30-terminal-control-api.md (SurfaceDesign-docs.patch): Core/Term and Core/Tui with file:line, runtime mode primitive RouteTerm.jet:252/282, capability map vs crossterm, termion, ncurses, notcurses, tcell/bubbletea, blessed/prompt_toolkit with every gap; probes m6315 (PTY t01/t03 OK o0/o1/o2), m6315b/t05 (variadic enum commands OK), m6315r (#Live leaves icanon/echo on)

criteria.text: A ballot-ready Tower decision fixes the command API (for example term.execute(...) taking a batch of command values, flushed once), raw-mode restore on every exit path including panic and signals, and how it composes with D-TUI-ANSI1 ANSI values, with same-program alternatives.
criteria.evidence: Ballot $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/SurfaceDesign/ballot/D-TERM-COMMANDS1.json: plaincheck-file.mjs PLAIN OK, readycheck.mjs READY; A term.execute(...Command) one write + restore ledger on exit/panic/signals/SIGTSTP/faults, B screen guard, C ANSI text + set_raw; composes with D-TUI-ANSI1 (ANSI moves to core.term, cursor/clear/alt/mouse helpers become Command cases) and D-TERM-INCREMENTAL1 (term.events)

criteria.text: The ratified API is implemented in Core with no gap left from the research list on Linux, macOS and Windows targets: each command has an example with golden output on o0/o1/o2 (driven through a pseudo-terminal), and raw mode is restored after a panic in a test.

The ratified but unbuilt terminal decisions are implemented: D-CORE-TERMSTDIN1 (Core/Term/Term.jet:43,64,84 still say is_tty) and D-TERM-INCREMENTAL1 (term.keys(); read_key retired), with examples driven through a pseudo-terminal on o0, o1 and o2.

(was #2049 c2) Each surface scored against named interaction patterns (responsiveness, keyboard model, progressive disclosure, color/NO_COLOR discipline, resize behavior) with concrete gap list [precut audit: no dev test, golden, case or snapshot proves this today]

cards.title: Binary size: Jet's default build must produce the smallest output of any language, for every program, by design rather than per-program tricks
cards.body: Owner (2026-10-30): 437 KB for hello world is far too big. Measured by Main on this machine (x86-64 Linux, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/q/hello): Zig 0.15.2 ReleaseSmall 10,720 B (static), Zig ReleaseFast stripped 18,744 B, C gcc -O2 stripped 14,440 B (dynamic glibc), C musl static stripped 17,696 B, Rust 1.97.1 -O stripped 394,032 B (dynamic). Jet with #6106 C1 (per-function sections plus gc): 437,416 B with .text 387,880 B (IrTypes-2 measurement); dev before #6106 C1: 5,210,576 B. A hand-written static ELF hello is a few hundred bytes. The size comes from runtime code that startup and print reach (allocator, task and thread setup, panic and formatting machinery), not from the program.
cards.plan: Step 1a of the owner-ordered speed program; the full ordered plan is the plan of #5479. c22 (precompiled checked Core and Prelude in the jet binary, ruled toolchain not cache) is the top item, owned by G11Speed-4, in slices S1-S8 listed there. Size criteria c2-c6 ride the same root fixes.

log.text: Main 2026-11-13 (G11Speed-4 finding): Dyn arm pruning (D1-D3) is not done: it is unsound without a complete census of Dyn producers. The msf twin builds Dyn natively (jet_rt_record_new_dyn_text/array, seq_list_rec_dyn_push, jet_rt_dyn_from_native at record crossings), route results and record fields carry Dyn handles, and Dyn place edits round-trip through the runtime, so a missed producer becomes a silent Unreachable trap. The gain is at most 6.4 KB on Timer. R6 poll coalescing is not done for the same reason: the msf polls follow runtime calls on the stop list (alloc failure). Either needs a sema-owned Dyn producer fact first. Next: c28 (sha256 links only SHA-256).

c22 S5 split (G11Speed-4, 2026-11-12). Route: rebase rows on load, not identity-keyed rows everywhere (those are #5479 c7). The record keeps its own module indexes and DeclTable; each reached Core module is appended to the graph and its RowRefs and DeclIDs are rebased. criteria.text: A size breakdown of the Jet hello binary at o0, o1 and o2 lists every runtime symbol and data object over 1 KB with the root that keeps it alive (startup, print, panic, allocator, tasks), recorded in a dated Docs/audits note.
criteria.evidence: Docs/audits/2026-10-30-hello-size.md: hello 437,416 B, identical at default/o0/o1/o2/--release; all 111 runtime functions over 1 KB listed, each with its size, held bytes and root path (startup, init_array, _start/EH, print, exit); no data object reaches 1 KB; liveness recomputed over jet_runtime.pack.o matches the binary (749 sections)

criteria.text: Runtime startup and print pull in only what the program uses: a program that never spawns tasks, allocates or formats links none of that machinery, by liveness and lazy initialization, with one meaning on o0, o1 and o2 (I9) and no change to panic or error behavior.

Jet's default build (jet build, no size flags) of hello and of every required perf workload is strictly smaller than each peer's smallest output for the same program (Zig ReleaseSmall stripped, C musl static -Os stripped, Rust opt-level=z stripped, Go -ldflags=-s -w, Odin -o:size), measured on the same machine; o0 (jet run/jet dev output) and --release are smaller still or equal, never larger.

Final binary size is a required metric in every required perf cell of the canonical manifest, and the gate fails any cell where Jet's default build is not strictly smaller than every peer; a hello-world cell and a small CLI cell are among them.

The size win comes from the root design (pay-for-what-you-use runtime, lazy runtime initialization, liveness through every runtime and Core layer, no unconditional startup machinery), with no hello-world special case, no per-program flags, no stripping or compression tricks that peers are denied, and no change to panic, error, safety or I9 behavior; the receipt shows the same mechanism shrinking a non-trivial program.

For every program in the size corpus (hello, one program per required perf cell, and every landed #5072 tool twin, each with a hand-written, optimized x86-64 assembly reference committed beside it that delivers the same features, fault reporting included), the default jet build holds only the code the program reaches: its size is at most the assembly reference size (Jet/ceiling at most 1.00 in bytes). Every byte category above the reference is listed with the root that keeps it and the card that removes it.

Hash reach: a program calling only crypto.sha256 links only SHA-256. Measured by Main on seed-b13, 2026-11-12 ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/bin14/sha): 229,680 B with 183 KB .text, of which __core_crypto_md_compress (21.6 KB), md_hash_finish (16.5 KB), ripemd160_blocks (11.8 KB), md_hash (9.3 KB), sha512_blocks (6.7 KB) and keccak_absorb (6.7 KB) are other algorithms or a generic dispatch over all of them. The fix is in the general mechanism (a call whose algorithm is known statically reaches only that algorithm, through every Core layer), proven on sha256 alone and on a second program using a different hash family member.

Per-function code size: no Core or generated function carries code its callers cannot reach or expansion a hand-written version would not. Measured by Main on seed-b13, 2026-11-12, default jet build: core_encoding_json_parse_string 21,323 B, __core_encoding_stream_jcs_number 37,759 B, core_regex_scan 35,189 B, unit_unicode_upper_mapping and lower_mapping 28-29 KB each, and MemorySafetyFuzz_run_memory_safety_fuzz_axis 58,080 B. A dated breakdown names, for each function over 4 KB in the tool-twin binaries, what the bytes are (inlined callees, unrolled loops, tables as code, checks) and the general codegen or Core rule that shrinks it; each fix shows the gain on two programs.

Tool twins as binaries: every landed #5072 tool twin is recorded with its default jet build size, its function count and its run wall and peak against its original, beside the hand-written reference of c6. Baseline by Main on seed-b13, 2026-11-12: memory-safety-fuzz 1,850,952 B (1,141 functions, 1.51 MB .text), run-policy 757,008 B (700), timer 752,464 B (848 functions; it links base64, SHA-2 and JSON writers it does not need for a process timer); the hello floor is 37,648 B (56 functions, 24 KB .text, of which the production receipt renderer, writer and publisher are 3.5 KB).

cards.title: A portable target better than WASM: a Jet bytecode or IR plus a hardware-capability API so sandboxed code can use tensor cores, SIMD and GPUs
cards.body: Owner, 2026-10-30: "Mojo has a bytecode/VM effectively which supports portability. One of Jet's goals is to effectively replace WASM as a portable target, so we need to investigate deeply. One issue with WASM is that it doesn't expose the hardware, like tensor cores, so it is a lowest-common-denominator system. We need to improve on that: some kind of metadata API that lets portable code leverage the hardware capabilities exposed by the host running the Jet sandbox." cards.title: FFI v3: build the ratified boundary design for calling and being called by almost any language
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-10-30: a terse but thoroughly engineered, robust proposal for a theoretically perfect FFI that beats every existing one, designed greenfield with no Jet limitations, then judged for adoption into Jet. It must follow the composition principle: a complete primitives layer that can express everything, plus high-quality wrappers for the common cases.

**The proposal:** Docs/proposals/ffi-perfect-boundary-2026-10-30.md (commit e99e795e4c). Section 9 maps every idea onto Jet; three owner ballots follow from it: D-FFI-PRIMS1 (public primitives layer), D-FFI-ISOLATE1 (isolation as a placement option) and D-FFI-EXPORT2 (rich exports).

## Plain summary

- **The idea.** Every foreign boundary is described once, as a *boundary
  contract*. That is a typed list of functions and types, plus the facts a C
  header cannot say: who owns memory, how long a view lives, how errors come
  back, which thread may call, and whether a call is async.
- **Readers and writers.** A reader package builds the contract from whatever
  the other side has (a C header, a Rust crate, a `.d.ts`, a WIT file, a JVM
  class, Windows metadata, a GPU shader). A writer package turns the same
  contract into bindings for whoever calls *us*. Both directions share one
  model, so N languages cost N readers plus N writers, not N×N bridges.
- **Two layers.** A small, complete, unsafe *primitives* layer can express
  every boundary: layout, symbols, calls, memory, callbacks, errors, threads,
  async, isolation. Pareto *wrappers* sit on top: `use "png.h" as png`,
  `#Export`, and typed imports for Rust, Python and JS. Every wrapper
  expands into primitives that you can inspect, so the expert path is a ladder,
  not a cliff.
- **Safe by default.** A call is safe when its facts are checked, vouched for
  in a named `#Unsafe("reason")`, or *isolated*. Isolated means the same import
  runs in a wasm sandbox or a separate process, with no source changes.
- **Zero cost.** A crossing whose types already match costs one direct call.
  When the foreign source is visible, the optimizer can inline across the
  boundary.
- **For Jet.** Most of this is already ratified: header import, C source import,
  binder packages, ownership sigils at the border, vouches, both embedding
  artifacts, and the hardened profile. The new pieces are a public primitives
  layer, isolation as a placement option, and rich exports. Each is one ballot.
  Inline C stays, and becomes a thin wrapper over C-source import, which
  removes the "two ways to bring in C" loss that D-FFI-ONE1 recorded.

This builds on, and does not replace, the boundary audit
[`Docs/audits/ffi-owned-source-and-boundaries.md`](../audits/ffi-owned-source-and-boundaries.md)
(#2933), which covers project arrangements and workflows. This document is the
mechanism underneath them.

Foreign effects are derived by the compiler, never declared by hand (D-FFI-FACTS1=A): for a locked foreign artifact, the compiler reads its imported symbols and internal call graph (from machine code, or from source when Jet builds it), maps each libc and system-call entry to a Jet effect through one table, and propagates through the foreign call graph with the same solver as Jet code. Unknown reach (raw system calls, callbacks into unknown code, dlopen, JIT) stays every effect. Facts are bound to the artifact hash. Proof: cases where libc abs() is admitted under !Net; a C library calling connect is refused under !Net with the chain into the library named; a library with a raw syscall instruction stays every effect; changing the artifact re-derives its facts.

cards.title: API design principle: strong composable primitives first, pareto wrappers on top, full use of variadics and named/positional arguments
cards.body: Owner direction 2026-10-30: wrappers solve some problems but often make everything outside their case harder. Jet's APIs need a very strong primitives layer that can express everything, then pareto-level high-quality wrappers for the common work. Jet's API tools (variadics, named and positional arguments, defaults) are barely used today and should be, to make APIs more powerful and more streamlined. This must become a fundamental design element of the project, with a review that checks the APIs follow it.

cards.title: Build `reject(Diagnostic)` (D-MARKER-DIAG1=A): library compile-time checks raise their own error codes
cards.body: Found by #6385 on dev 59213de00f. cards.title: A task blocked in an ordinary OS wait or foreign call holds its worker thread, so ready tasks stall
cards.body: Found by MemDesign-5 for #6376 (release-notes research: Java 21 virtual threads pinned their carrier inside synchronized and native calls, which made libraries rewrite their locks, until JDK 24's JEP 491; Go releases the P on every syscall and cgo call). D-ASYNCRT1=A promises Go's model: "blocking calls yield automatically; no call-site annotation". Only runtime park points call `scheduler_blocking_wait_enter` (Condition, Shared, Task, TaskGroup, Realtime, Generator, AsyncEvents, SharedTransactions, Scheduler). Raw host calls do not: `jet_sys_waitpid_raw` issues wait4 directly (Compiler/JetRuntime/Source/HostProcess.jet:166-177), and foreign calls have no hook. Repro $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/MemDesign-4/probes/rel/r08_child_wait_block.jet: 96 tasks each run `sleep 1` through core.process, then one trivial task is spawned and joined. On jet 03c64ad0c4 (soft address-space limit raised to 16 GB, see the 192 MiB stack card) it prints "quick task done after 3023780905ns". Compensation costs a thread start today (Shared.jet:46-50 notes hundreds of thousands of such threads in one compiler pass), so the fix has to be cheap on short calls, like Go's hand-off after a call has blocked for a while.

log.text: Owner instruction 2026-11-10 ~16:10, verbatim: "remember for script performance we are targeting being approximately at hand optimized machine code level (as well as for regular programs). that work should go in the size/speed goal, not script. script goal should not have any speed size work" Applied: #6087 and #6403 now belong to G11 (Speed and size) only, and #5072 c41 (peak RSS) moved to #6639. #6639 gains the machine-ceiling target for scripts. #5072's port bars still measure wall time and peak memory as switch bars (AGENTS.md), but the work that makes Jet faster or smaller is G11's.

t14a landed PerfLead-6403c6a (53805444ba..01b86931e7): c6 stage 1 of 2 (TaskGroup stack:, per-size fiber pools, E3012 names stack:). c6 stays open for stage 2. JetParser/Tests have 2 fails that the base shares (generated_jet_call_arguments_match_native_parser_contract, derive_generic_type_holes_stay_in_the_template_ast).

Sizing by G1Lead-3 on 973d760c89. c2 is open on both paths: 96 tasks in libc sleep(1) through #Import c.c delay the quick task 2898 ms on 32 carriers and 11901 ms on 8, and 96 FIFO readers deadlock (rc 124, 60 s timeout), because foreign calls and raw host reads hold the carrier. There is no hand-off today. Plan (runtime-only, no API): a monitor thread is armed only when work is queued and no idle carrier is left. It marks a carrier blocked when the carrier fiber-switch counter and its thread CPU clock have both stood still for ~5-10 ms, then starts one compensation carrier per blocked carrier; extra carriers retire when idle. CPU-bound tasks are not compensated. This costs nothing on the C-call path, so c3 should hold at ≤1.00. Estimate 3-4 h; G1Lead-3 owns it after 6281f.

Worktree cleanup by Main on 2026-11-09 at 22:58. G1Lead-2 is gone, and its four detached worktrees under $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/G1Lead-2/{r1,t4,t5,w4} held unlanded work. Each file whose bytes dev c057ea659d does not already hold was saved as a patch against that worktree HEAD, in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/hold/G1Lead-2-{r1,t4,t5,w4}.patch.
- t4/t5 (base 0f193199cc) and w4 (base 6a06b917cb) carry the program-thread stack work for c6 (Thread.jet, Scheduler.jet, Cli Front/Host, Sema Effects/Checks, the fiber_liveness program_stack(s) cases and the spec text). They wait on ballot D-THREAD-STACK1; whoever builds the ratified option starts from them.
- r1 (base 6a06b917cb) carries an O0 IR-optimizer trace/lint hook in Cli Host.jet and ir_try_from_or/ir_fallback_reads_error in JetIR BuildExpr.jet (a narrowing conversion?? fallback that never reads the error builds no Result), plus spec text. It is unsubmitted and has no named card; it goes to the #5971/#6700 owner as a candidate SUB.
The worktrees are removed after this log.

Correction (Main): the compiler cannot call a core.sys __ row, because the lexer refuses __ names outside Core (E0067, JetLexer Payload.jet identifier_respelling). Every remaining route to a process-local 192 MiB floor for the compiler only is an owner gate: a Compiler exception to the __ rule, a public core.sys call, or a package.jet field. c6 waits on ballot D-THREAD-STACK1. Its options also cover keeping 192 MiB for every program and making the compiler not need the floor (#5910). c6b2, c6b3 and c6b4 stay withdrawn; c6a (in train 2) does not change behavior.

Decision (Main) on c6 replaces the earlier rlimit plan: the compiler never changes RLIMIT_STACK, because every child (jet dev's program, jet test binaries, core.process spawns) would inherit it. The runtime gets a process-local worker-stack floor reached through an internal core.sys.__ row (not public API; Host.jet already calls core.sys.__rlimit the same way). Program default: soft RLIMIT_STACK with an 8 MiB minimum. The compiler sets a 192 MiB floor for its own compile. Staged as G1Lead-3-6403c6f1 (runtime plus row, train 3) and c6f2 (Host.jet call plus case rows for run, dev and test children, on the next seed). c6b2, c6b3 and c6b4 are withdrawn.

Decision (Main) on c6: the compiler raises its own soft RLIMIT_STACK to 192 MiB only for the compile, using the existing core.sys.set_stack_limit, and puts it back before the run step (G1Lead-3-6403c6b3: no public API, no C import, no __thread_stack_floor row). Children started during a compile (jet dev's program) get the user's original soft limit, through an internal X64Launch rlimit record in Loader.jet (G1Lead-3-6403c6b4) with a case row. Every program sees the user's own limit, on every tier.

cards.title: core.compute port: devices, streams, sparse tensors and transfer receipts need storage in the registered compute vocabulary
cards.body: The R1 port of core.compute to Jet source (Core/Compute/Compute.jet) cannot express on_device and transfer to non-CPU placements, transfer_show, streams, sparse CSR, VJPRun or deserialize receipts. The registered types have no storage for them (core-library.md:4289-4291 makes the registered vocabulary their only owner). ComputeDevice, ComputeStream and SparseTensor are opaque to users today (E0119 on a literal, E0302 on field access), so their storage is added as private core_only field rows. Tensor is a 5-field literal that users can read and assign today (a.requested = "Metal" changes compute.placement), so where its reason and transfer receipts live is the owner ballot D-COMPUTE-TENSOR-STORE1 on this card.

cards.title: Run time: default codegen must be borderline equal to hand-written optimized assembly for every program
cards.body: Owner order, 2026-10-30: performance should be borderline equal to hand-written assembly with default codegen, not with flags or per-program tricks. Binary size has the same goal, and #6328 owns size. This card owns speed. Every program in the perf corpus (one per required perf cell plus the codegen kernels: loops, bounds-checked indexing, string length and iteration, slices, calls, closures, records, allocation, I/O write) gets a hand-written, optimized x86-64 assembly reference, committed with a harness that measures cycles and instructions (perf stat, best of N, pinned CPU). The gap is closed in the code generator and runtime design (instruction selection, register allocation, bounds-check elimination, inlining, layout), never by weakening safety, semantics or diagnostics (AGENTS.md performance gate).
cards.plan: Hill-climbing (G13), not current. Owner 2026-11-12 evening: finish the rest of the goals before trying to get to perfect codegen. When G13 starts: the kernel catalog worked backwards from hand-written code (c15), gaps closed largest first (c35), then every cell Jet/peer < 1.00 and Jet/ceiling <= 1.00 (c22, c29). The compile-speed program lives in the plan of #5479.

log.text: c15 progress: G11Speed-G8 e8e4e2b21c and G8b 60ade4f48a landed, proved. Tools/perf/CodegenCeiling.jet catalogs 9 kernels including the allocator leaves, fails on any count above golden, and is a required --check line for JetIR/JetBackend/JetRuntime SUBs and a census codegen pass. Seed-b4 hot-loop gaps: list_sum 254/5 (11 loop versions), gather 273/8, stride 71/6, collatz 180/11, point 213/9, byte_count 119/7. Roots: loop versioning re-copies inlined callee versions (G11Speed-G9 staged, measured in the window), and index spills (next). c15 stays open until the catalog covers every listed shape and names each extra instruction's root.

Owner order 2026-11-11: build c15 now (with c30) as a systematic codegen ceiling gate. A kernel catalog per code shape, each with a hand-written optimized x86-64 reference. A deterministic checker compares the emitted hot code with the reference and names each excess instruction's root. Machine-code goldens at O1/O2. The gate is a required proof line for every SUB touching JetIR, codegen, lowering or the runtime, and runs on every batch compiler. Cycle checks run in full-suite sweeps. Owner ruling 2026-11-08 (chat, Q17): SpeedLead takes run-time codegen (#6414, #6478, #6472, and the TlsLead and G1Lead roots logged here) when it finishes the build.jet work on #6682. No new lead.

Evidence from G1Lead (#6688 c4, 7639370892 and b53d287e41; Jet libm against musl with identical bits, O1 perf-stat cycles per call: sin 81.8 vs 64.8, cos 80.5 vs 64.7, exp 56.7 vs 39.9, log 63.4 vs 41.1, pow 169.3 vs 113.9). Roots, all general codegen: (1) index math on a proven-small Int keeps an inline add plus jo overflow test, 2 to 3 per access; a comptime table read goes through its static list header (len and data-pointer loads) with a bounds check and a list_bounds_stop call with xmm spills, about 15 instructions per access (exp 2, log 4, pow 5 accesses). (2) FloatBits and FloatFromBits (BuildLibrary ir_reinterpret) and Float abs (BuildRoutes:3489) go through a stack store and reload instead of movq; 14 percent of pow samples sit on one reload. (3) At O1, Float and shifted constants are neither folded nor hoisted: movabs plus movq at every use. (4) A || chain is materialized as bools through stack slots, about 25 instructions at pow entry. (5) A small struct return (LibmReduced) goes through sret, and a small helper (libm_rem_pio2_near) is not inlined. Same family as the TlsLead hash findings above; ownership is owner Q17.

Evidence from TlsLead (#6694 S1, b53a78981d), the emitted x64 of core_crypto___jet_hashes_dcompress (portable SHA-512 compress, about 935 ns per block against about 280 ns for mbedtls): (1) 4670 instructions, 2564 mov and 1209 rbp spills, about 6 GPRs used (#6478); (2) no rol or ror: a constant rotate lowers to a shift-by-cl pair plus and 0x1f, and there are 107 shl or shr 0x20 U32 zero-extends; (3) per call 65 jet_rt_list_bounds_stop, 76 jet_ir_stop_poll inside fixed-trip loops (#6472), 32 cleanup enter and leave, 43 jet_rt_int_drop; (4) wrapping(U8{x}) from an out-of-range Int costs about 260 ns (global masks, boxed-Int drops, jo checks) against 9 ns for U8{x %% 256}; (5) list copy and push cost 1.5 to 2 ns per element; (6) a fixed-list global is re-materialized on every access (64 stores); (7) hash_start plus Close costs about 256 ns. Each is a general codegen root; the crypto engine is the second program for the perf rule.

Codegen-1 root list 2026-10-31 (O2 asm of isum 8.38x and sieve 4.63x vs Rust, after Codegen-1-9): R1 register allocation: X64Alloc uses only the 5 callee-saved GPRs, linear scan with no splitting, spill choice by total weight not weight per range length, so hot-loop values live in the frame (isum reloads total, n, len, data pointer from rbp every pass; sieve fill loop 12/24 instructions are spill traffic). R2 bounds checks not proven away (len(xs)==n, cycle(n).to_list length facts never reach the range pass), blocking vectorization. R3 loop-invariant Int inline checks and the ranged-for step-sign test run every pass (no versioning on step>0). R4 accumulator overflow/inline checks (3 per pass) need R2/R3 facts. R5 no vectorization or unroll (Rust vectorizes isum and the sieve count). Order: R1 (spill weight per length, then caller-saved registers for call-free ranges), then R2/R3, then R5.

Work backwards from hand-optimized machine code (owner direction 2026-11-11). A kernel catalog covers each common code shape: counted and iterator loops, list sum and map, text scan and compare, struct copy and move, enum match, option and error return, hash lookup, bounds-checked index, call and return, allocation and drop. Each kernel has a small Jet program and a hand-written, maximally optimized x86-64 reference that does the same work with the same safety checks. For each kernel, a checker compares the hot code that `jet build` emits with the reference: instruction count, spills, loads and stores, checks, and calls. Every extra instruction is named with its root (bounds check not hoisted, value spilled, copy not elided, loop not vectorized, call not inlined, or atomic reference count). Each root is fixed once, in the general lowering, never per kernel, and is proved on a second program that uses the feature differently. Each kernel then gets a machine-code golden that pins the emitted hot loop at O1 and O2, so a regression fails the gate. The gate fails any kernel whose emitted hot code is over its reference in instructions or cycles. Every new codegen feature adds its kernel and reference before it lands.

cards.body: CoverPort census of the wave-6 ui suite (2026-10-31; table $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/CoverPort/out/report5-nodiag.tsv with count, code, stage, registry meaning, Jet emit files and example ids): 157 tests/ui rows expect an error diagnostic that the Jet checker never reports (lint rows L0xxx belong to #6006). Each is a missing sema check, not text. Two kinds: (1) the code has a Jet emit site that misses this case (largest: Sema/Ownership/Checks.jet E0204 x10, E0121 x6, E2305 x5, E0209 x4; Effects E3403 x6; Calls E0112 x5; Control E2402 x5; Registration E3203 x5; E0119, E0926, E0999, E2960 x4 each; E0907, E1206 x3); (2) whole families with no Jet emit site (E1293, E2806, E2807, E1402, lint-policy E1201/E1208/E1211/E1212/E1213/E1216, E0619, E0996, E0997, E2967, E-OSTARGET-*, E-WEB-RUN, a11y E2931). Until each check is ported, its rows are known-failing on this card.

cards.title: Each generator yield is a scheduler task park and wake, about 20 us per value
cards.body: Measured by IrTypes-3 2026-10-31 (IrTypes-25b timing): a generator pull hands off through the task scheduler (park the consumer, wake the producer, and back), about 20 us per yield. The iterloop kit case does 3M yields plus 1.28M channel pulls and takes 79 s. A generator that runs on the consumer thread needs no scheduler: a direct stack switch or a compiled state machine costs nanoseconds, and C/Rust/Zig iterators cost one call or less. This is a structural cost on every program that iterates a generator. Related: #6089 (lazy pulls charging comptime fuel through a global mutex).

log.text: HELD by owner order 2026-11-11 (no small optimizations until the language is mostly stable; architecture and regression fixes go first, per #5479 c5-c8). These criteria stay open and unworked: c1 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c).

criteria.text: A generator pull that stays on the consumer thread costs under 50 ns per value (a direct switch or a compiled state machine, no scheduler park/wake), measured same-run on the iterloop kit case and a 10M-yield microbench; every generator golden is unchanged on O0/O1/O2.

cards.title: stdin reads one byte per syscall: cat-style programs run ~3,300x slower than Rust
cards.body: Floor-1 same-run measurement on df84 (2026-10-31, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Floor/out/pareto-speed.md): the cat cell is about 3,300x Rust by task-clock, because terminal/stdin reads go one byte per read syscall (Compiler/JetRuntime/Source/RouteTerm.jet:19-51). stdout writes need the same check. Fix the root in the one shared runtime: buffered stdin and stdout with correct flush semantics (line-buffered for a TTY, block-buffered otherwise, flush at exit, flush before reading interactive input), with one meaning on every tier.

log.text: Deconfliction 2026-11-06: reworded to match the AGENTS.md Performance gate (Jet/peer < 1.00 with no Rust band, then the asm-parity ceiling).

Main-34 folds print's LF into host_stdout_write (one locked write per print line). cat cell vs rust-O3, perf stat medians: HEAD 7c67280960 runtime 435M cycles / 94.3 ms task-clock (Rust 395M / 89.3 ms: 1.10x cycles, 1.056x task-clock); with Main-34 430M / 93.3 ms (about -1.1%). Output byte-identical; cases --filter stdout|print match the HEAD baseline; golden suite adds no new failures versus HEAD (18 missing-stream rows are #6538, stack_overflow o2 tier-split is pre-existing at HEAD). Rejected: a 16-byte unroll of stdin_line_scan (+3.8% cycles). Remaining gap per profile: sync_sole_enter about 14% (about 15 cycles per elided call), copy about 14%, SWAR scan about 10%, stdout write about 22%; mostly runtime codegen quality (stack spills) and call overhead. Card stays open: the gate requires Jet/peer < 1.00.

Main 2026-11-01 09:05, dev 367eaf8f0d base jet, release build of Floor cells/cat/run.jet on a 200,000-line (10.7 MB) pipe input: output byte-identical. strace shows 165 stdin reads (64 KiB each) and 1,398 stdout writes (about 7.6 KiB each), so the one-byte read root is gone. hyperfine -N, 40 runs, load average 18: Jet 33.2 ms (user 25.7), Rust O3 20.1 ms (user 9.8), C gcc O2 3.9 ms. Jet/Rust is 1.65, down from about 3,300. Criterion 1 is still open. The remaining cost is per-line user time: lines() makes one String per line, UTF-8 is checked per line, and print adds its own work. Next: a borrowed line view or a bulk copy for the lines-to-print path, still with one meaning on every tier.

AsmPar-1 2026-11-01 01:05: the one-byte read root is fixed on wave 18 (strace of the cat cell: 1,086 reads of 64 KiB for 71 MB). The cell is still 3.3x Rust in cycles (0.78G vs 0.24G); the remaining gap is a per-line alloc/free in the lines iterator plus stdio_checkpoint.

Floor cat cell, jet --release: 6,485 M instr / 252-312 ms -> 3,963 M / 150.6 ms task-clock; matched Rust peer (cells/cat/main.rs, now BufRead::lines + BufWriter) 752 M / 58.8 ms, so Jet/Rust is 2.56x (the raw block copy moved to cells/catblock). CRLF transcript byte-identical to the old chomp on 5 inputs, default and --release; 88 stdin/terminal/prompt/io_/print cases have the same status as on IrTypes-30. Left: per-line Result/Option boxes and the String alloc in the lines iterator (codegen, sent to Codegen-1).

Landed on dev at undefined in IrTypes-30 (patch row: criterion/count 1): PARTIAL, criterion NOT met (card stays open): IrTypes-30 buffers stdin (one shared 64 KiB buffer under the stdin lock) and stdout (print flush 0: line-buffered on a tty, 8 KiB blocks otherwise; flushed before stderr, every stdin read, children, exit). Floor-1 cat cell: jet --release 35,612 ms -> 252 ms task-clock (wall ~= task), rust-O3 10.2 ms, zig 9.3 ms same run, so Jet/Rust ~24x, not <= 1.05. strace: stdin reads max 65,536 B, mean 65,424 B (1,086 reads; was 1 B each); stdout 9,198 writes (was 833,335). Every stdin/stdout/prompt/terminal/print/io_/no_args/runtime_stop_goldens/build_option_ case has the same status as the pre-patch jet (cases/repl/ differs only by the harness's E2104 stdin-write race); terminal/stdin_lines_emit_before_eof and stdout_write_bytes_ordered_with_print pass by hand on default and --release. The remaining ~300 ns/line is the per-line String (Core StdinHandle.read_line: checkpoint, jet_stdin_line_raw copy, stdin_chomp's [U8] round trip, alloc/drop), which needs a borrowed line view in the lines loop to reach Rust's raw 64 KiB copy.

Main 2026-10-31: IrTypes-30 (wave 11) buffers stdin/stdout: cat cell 35.6 s -> 252 ms, 64 KiB reads, corpus 52/52 identical. The Floor-1 Rust peer was an io::copy block copy, so it was not matched. Against a matched BufRead::lines + BufWriter Rust (64 ms, 752M instr), Jet is 4.2x in time and 8.5x in instructions (7,894 vs 928 Ir per line). Roots: Core stdin_chomp round trip 30%, jet_stdin_line_raw 27% (UTF-8 validated twice), per-line lazy_line_next boxes 18%, print 8%, String drop 5% ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/IR/IrTypes/c6328/d44/cg/ATTRIB.md). Next: runtime strips CR/LF (IrTypes-31); per-line boxes and String alloc go to Codegen-1. Criterion 1 is not met yet.

cards.title: The gauntlet measurement manifest has no slot for a matched Rust peer, so Jet/Rust ratios cannot be gated
cards.body: Found by Codegen-1 on 2026-10-31. Tools/gauntlet measurement-manifest.json entries carry jet and python programs only, and axes need a status and harness. There is no field for the matched Rust peer, so the AGENTS.md performance gate (Jet/Rust <= 1.05 per cell and metric, strictly below 1.00 against every other peer) cannot be encoded in the manifest, only in prose and lane notes (Floor cells, Codegen-1 corpus). The manifest must name every required peer per entry, with the matched program, and the gate must fail any required cell where a peer is missing or the comparator fails.

log.text: Main 2026-10-31: the gauntlet matrix gives each cell exactly one owning entry (measurement-manifest.test.mjs:744), and matrix.json is owner-approved. So the wordfreq 200k-unique-key variant (Codegen-1: gen.py seed 42, input sha256 43e32ccc…, matched Rust collect+sort_by) cannot be added as an entry without a new matrix cell plus a loss_owners source card. Until the owner approves a text.kernel scale-variant cell, its numbers live in the Codegen-1 Map patch msg as lane evidence. Baseline: Jet 26.45 s vs Rust 0.08 s at 200k; Jet 0.63 s vs Rust 0.05 s at 10k (wave-11 s1, --optimize=full).

criteria.text: measurement-manifest.json names the matched Rust, C, Zig and Go peers per entry, where they apply; the gate script fails a required cell whose peer is missing, unmatched, or fails the AGENTS.md comparator; wordfreq 10k/200k and cat are recorded with matched peers.

cards.title: Machine-ceiling references: a hand-written, maximally optimized machine-code reference for every required gauntlet cell
cards.body: Owner order 2026-10-31: peers are the initial benchmark; hand-written, maximally optimized machine code is the final one (Jet/ceiling <= 1.00 in cycles and bytes per required cell). The manifest encodes it (strict_performance_policy v3 ceiling block, CardClose-8). Of 28 required cells only numerics.int-kernel (sieve) has a reference today; the 27 others report uncovered and fail the gate. Each reference lives in Tools/perf/asm-parity (cells.json entry naming its gauntlet cell ids, plus ref.S), gives the identical output, and uses the best known technique for the workload (SIMD, algorithmic, syscall-level), not a transliteration.

cards.title: Function-local Result/Option boxes from runtime routes stay heap-allocated (binparse 25% alloc/free)
cards.body: binparse run builds a jet_rt_alloc(16,8) Result box around each reader route (4 per record in the loop) that never leaves run. perf on the register-return build: free_8 12.4% + alloc_8 8.8% + alloc 4.3% = 25.5% of 257M cycles (~66M). The register-return pass does not reach these boxes. Fix: escape analysis in JetIR: a function-local box used only by Load/Store at offsets, the unique test, free and Drop becomes a stack slot, and scalar replacement then puts it in registers. General: applies to every non-escaping small heap allocation. Full text: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/IR/IrTypes/c6328/d53/CARD-REQUEST-local-box.md.

cards.title: Sound quiet-runtime-route table so no stop poll follows a runtime call that cannot stop
cards.body: Every runtime route except the hand list in Build.jet ir_route_can_stop is followed by a stop poll. RUNTIME_STOP_EXPORTS cannot decide it as generated: it is the named-call closure from scheduler_panic_publish_record only (cancel/deadline publish via scheduler_native_publish; dynamic code-word calls excluded; 24 scalar route exports such as jet_time_sleep_until are not Jet runtime exports). Generate the closure from scheduler_control_publish, seed every function calling through a non-rail code word, and emit the complement (quiet exports), in both gen-runtime-stop-exports.mjs and RuntimeGenerators.jet. Then ir_route_can_stop answers from that table and the hand list goes. Full text: wave/16/in/Codegen-1-27.msg.

cards.title: Cross-package IR inlining of small Core bodies (runtime-routed Core leaves are opaque to OptInline)
cards.body: Runtime-routed Core leaves (jet_std_math_*) are prebuilt in the runtime pack, so OptInline never has their IR; OptInline also refuses cross-file callees holding located (stop-capable) ops because the trap site is tied to the source file. Ship the IR of small Never! runtime leaves with the runtime pack (or compile them from Core source into the module), and carry the source file per located op so an inlined cross-file op keeps its trap site. Measured motive: fft/tensormap still call Core fabs via to_bits/from_bits after the ir_leaf_route table (-9.1% instead of 12-16%). Full text: wave/16/in/Codegen-1-27.msg.

cards.title: Hoist constant Regex{} construction out of every evaluation

cards.title: Register allocator: live-range splitting so density-based spills keep hot loop values
cards.body: IrTypes-37 (floats in xmm2-15) found that a pure density spill rule wins nbody (1.65G -> 0.62G cycles) but evicts collatz hot loop variables for short temporaries (6.97G -> 10.82G instructions). The landed safe rule (evict only lighter ranges) keeps collatz exact but gives nbody only -36% (1.64G -> 1.05G). Split long live ranges around hot loops so the density rule can keep both. cards.body: Owner order 2026-10-31: once every program meets the hand-written asm ceiling in cycles and bytes, the next goal is to BEAT it. Survey with sources: the Goose language (its claimed speedups over Rust and C, what mechanisms produce them, which are verified, and which fit Jet semantics and I9), whole-program specialization and monomorphization budgets, superoptimization of hot blocks, automatic data-layout transforms (AoS/SoA, field reordering, small-value packing), allocation elision and region inference, comptime evaluation of input-independent work, and cache-aware code layout without PGO. Output: Docs/research/beyond-asm-ceiling-2026-10-31.md ranking each idea by expected gain across ALL programs (not one example), implementation cost and semantic risk, with cards proposed for the top items. No claim without a source or a measurement.

That maximum is not only optimized machine code, but the best result the problem allows, reached by rethinking phasing, ordering, logic and advanced techniques. For real-world cases, hit the real-world maximum. The owner chose "Record it": every required cell gets a written, reviewed theoretical bound; reports show Jet against the peers, the hand-written reference and the bound; the gate stays peers plus the reference; the design targets the bound. Each technique that adds user-visible behavior still needs its own ballot and adversarial review.

criteria.text: The survey lists every technique known to beat expert hand-written assembly (Goose-style stack-based execution, whole-program specialization, superoptimization, data-layout transforms and others), each with sources and a runnable probe.
Each technique that wins its probe gets a card with a paired two-program cell under the performance gate rules.
End metric: required cells beat their asm-parity ceilings (Jet/ceiling below 1.00 in cycles and bytes) with identical output, and every cell that does not is on a card.

Every required gauntlet and ScriptBench cell has a written theoretical bound per metric, derived only from the workload's stated contract: wall time from the critical path (unavoidable latencies and dependency chain); CPU time from the larger of bytes moved over memory or disk bandwidth and minimum operations over machine throughput; RSS and bytes from the minimum working set and image. The derivation is committed beside the cell and reviewed adversarially, so a bound cannot be made easy.

The performance reports show, for each cell and metric, Jet against the best peer of each tier, Jet against the hand-written reference, and Jet against the theoretical bound, on the binary and on `jet run`. The bound ratio is the design target and never relaxes the gate (every peer below 1.00, the reference at most 1.00).

The survey covers the schedule-level techniques that move Jet toward the bound and that typical runtimes do not apply by default: effect-aware early I/O (sema-known opens, DNS, connects and fetches issued at process start); concurrent execution of effects sema proves independent, longest expected chain first; syscall batching (io_uring, writev, readahead) and zero-copy; elimination of unread outputs and stage fusion; compile-time initialized startup images; speculation limited to repeatable effect-free reads. Each gets a probe, a paired two-program cell, and observable behavior preserved (output, the order of visible effects, workload limits such as "at most 32 in flight"; no caching of results the program must compute).

cards.title: FFI v3 gallery: C libraries (libm, zlib, libpng)
cards.body:
Three complete programs that call C through `use c.<lib>`. None contains `#Unsafe`, a pointer or a binding file.
The `cbind` package (root `c`) reads each header with pinned clang, derives facts with evidence, and writes a Jet
module. Outputs are design targets, not observed runs. Design: `ffi-v3.md` in the FFIDesign v3 lane, sections 4
and 5; ballots D-FFI-LANG1, D-FFI-PRIMS2, D-FFI-FACTS1.

## Simple: libm

What it shows: a system library, scalar rows, zero overhead. Each call lowers to the same `call` C emits.

```jet
use m: c.math

run: fn() {
    print(m.cos(0.0))
    print(m.hypot(3.0, 4.0))
    print(m.fma(2.0, 3.0, 1.0))
}
```

```text
1.0
5.0
7.0
```

What the binder wrote (`jet inspect bind math --row hypot --expand`):

```jet
#ffi.Facts(Effects([]))                       // link evidence: libm imports nothing with effects
hypot: fn(x: F64, y: F64) -> F64 {
    ffi.cross("hypot")
    ffi.extern<fn(F64, F64) -> F64>("hypot", EV_MATH_H_168).call(x, y)
}
```

## Medium: zlib file compression

What it shows: lists passed as pointer and length from `counted_by` facts; a C status turned into a Jet error by
the reviewed zlib pack; owned output; text copied from a static C string.

```jet
package: {
    name: "squeeze"
    deps: { z: c@nixpkgs:zlib }
}

use z: c.zlib
use fs: core.files

squeeze: fn(path: String) -> Int !z.ZError {
    data: fs.read_bytes(path)
    packed: z.compress(data, level: 9)          // pack: compressBound + compress2, status -> ZError
    fs.write_bytes("{path}.z", packed)
    restored: z.uncompress(packed, size: data.len())
    assert(restored == data)
    packed.len()
}

run: fn() {
    print("zlib {z.version()}")                   // const char*, static: copied once
    size: squeeze("notes.txt")
    print("compressed to {size} bytes")
}
```

```text
zlib 1.3.1
compressed to 1184 bytes
```

If the zlib pack were absent, `z.compress` would still exist in its raw-but-safe shape:
`compress2(dest: &[U8], dest_len: &U64, source: [U8], level: I32) -> I32`, because zlib's header documents
lengths for both buffers through its `uLongf *destLen` and `uLong sourceLen` pairs and the binder's pairing rule
matches them. Only the error mapping and `compressBound` sizing come from the pack.

## Complex: libpng thumbnailer

What it shows: a reviewed pack giving handles with `Close`, `setjmp` error handling turned into Jet errors, a
refused row with its fix, a project overlay supplying a missing fact, and the audit.

```jet
package: {
    name: "thumbs"
    deps: { png: c@nixpkgs:libpng }        // c-png-pack is found by header hash
}

use png: c.png
use fs: core.files

#Import module c.png {
    // The project states the length fact for one row; Jet checks it at the call.
    #ffi.Facts(Count(row_pointers, num_rows))
    png_read_rows: fn(r: &Reader, row_pointers: &[[U8]], display: ?&[[U8]], num_rows: U32)
}

thumbnail: fn(path: String, out: String, scale: Int) !png.PngError {
    img: png.Image.read(path)               // pack: png_create_read_struct + png_destroy_read_struct as Close
    small := png.Image.blank(img.width / scale, img.height / scale, img.format)
    loop y in 0..<small.height {
        loop x in 0..<small.width {
            small.set(x, y, img.pixel(x * scale, y * scale))
        }
    }
    small.write(out)                          // longjmp inside libpng becomes PngError via the pack's error hook
}

stream_rows: fn(path: String) !png.PngError {
    reader: png.Reader.open(path)
    rows := [[U8]]{}
    loop i in 0..<reader.height -> rows.push([U8].zeroed(reader.row_bytes))
    png.png_read_rows(reader, rows, .None, reader.height)    // checked: rows.len() >= height
    print("read {rows.len()} rows")
}

run: fn() {
    loop f in fs.list_dir("photos") {
        if !f.ends_with(".png") -> next
        thumbnail("photos/{f}", "thumbs/{f}", 4) ?? print("skipped {f}")
    }
    stream_rows("photos/cat.png")
}
```

```text
read 480 rows
```

Without the overlay, the `png_read_rows` call would stop the build:

```text
Error [E3241]: `png_read_rows` takes pointer `row_pointers` with no known length.
  --> thumbs.jet:31:5
 Why: Jet cannot tell how many elements C will read or write through it.
 Fix: Use `reader.read_rows()` from the libpng pack, or state the length with
      #ffi.Facts(Count(row_pointers, num_rows)) in #Import module c.png.
```

The audit of this program (`jet audit foreign thumbs.jet`) lists `png_read_rows` with
`Count(row_pointers, num_rows)  source overlay thumbs.jet:8`, and every pack row with its reviewers and the header
hash it was checked against.

### Best competitor equivalent

```zig
// Zig: one line to import, then raw C everywhere; setjmp errors need a C shim.
const c = @cImport(@cInclude("png.h"));
var png_ptr = c.png_create_read_struct(c.PNG_LIBPNG_VER_STRING, null, null, null) orelse return error.Png;
defer c.png_destroy_read_struct(&png_ptr, &info_ptr, null);
c.png_read_rows(png_ptr, rows.ptr, null, height);      // no length check
```

cards.title: FFI v3 gallery: isolation (wasm, process, hardened profile)
cards.body:
Three complete programs that move foreign libraries out of the program's memory with one `isolate:` line and no
call-site change (D-FFI-PLACE1). `.Wasm` compiles a source library to wasm and runs it inside the process with its
own linear memory. `.Process` runs a closed binary in a supervised child and batches calls through a shared-memory
ring. Jet already has the pieces: the wasm plugin host (`PluginHost.jet`) and the worker supervisor
(`WorkerSupervisor.jet`). Costs are inferences from published sandbox reports, marked as such. Outputs are design
targets.

## Simple: a C image decoder in wasm

```jet
package: {
    name: "avatars"
    deps: { stb: c@nixpkgs:stb_image }
    isolate: { stb: .Wasm }
}

use img: c.stb_image

run: fn() {
    pic: img.load("upload.png")                     // same call as in-process
    print("{pic.width}x{pic.height}")
    evil: img.load("crafted.png")                   // a heap overflow inside stb traps in its sandbox
    print(evil.width)
}
```

```text
640x480
Error [IsolateError.Trapped]: stb_image trapped: out-of-bounds memory access
  in wasm  stb_image.h:4877   stbi__parse_png_file   [placement .Wasm]
  -- crossing: c.stb_image load  (binder cbind 3.0.1, rule emit_plain) --
  in Jet   avatars.jet:10:13  run()
```

Jet memory is untouched; the sandbox is discarded and recreated on the next call. Cost: about 1.1 to 1.5 times
the native decode time inside the library [INFERENCE from RLBox reports], nothing at the call.

## Medium: a closed codec in a child process

```jet
package: {
    name: "transcode"
    deps: { codec: c@"vendor/oldcodec" }   // a local directory: library plus header
    isolate: { codec: .Process }
}

use codec: c.oldcodec
use fs: core.files

transcode: fn(path: String) -> Int !(IsolateError | codec.CodecError) {
    dec: codec.Decoder.open(path)                   // a handle living in the child; Close sends the release
    out: fs.create("{path}.raw")                 // a Close file handle
    frames := 0
    loop {
        frame: dec.next_frame() ?? break            // Bytes cross through the shared ring, no copy per frame
        out.write(frame)
        frames += 1
    }
    frames
}

run: fn() {
    print(transcode("clip.old"))
    // If the child crashes, the call fails with IsolateError.Crashed, the supervisor restarts it,
    // and handles from the dead child fail with IsolateError.Stale instead of touching freed memory.
}
```

```text
2400
```

Effects are enforced: the child runs with only the grants the codec's link evidence needs (`FS.Read` on the input
directory). A codec update that adds a `connect` import shows up as a lock diff before it can run.

## Complex: hardened profile and audit

```jet
package: {
    name: "upload_service"
    deps: {
        stb: c@nixpkgs:stb_image                  // source
        zlib: c@nixpkgs:zlib                      // source via nixpkgs
        codec: c@"vendor/oldcodec"
        exif: py@"exifread==3.0"                    // pure Python
        pillow: py@"pillow==11.0"                   // native extension
    }
    isolate: { stb: .Wasm, codec: .Process }
    profile: { release: { foreign: .Hardened } }
}

use img: c.stb_image
use z: c.zlib
use codec: c.oldcodec
use exif: py.exifread
use pil: py.PIL.Image
use fs: core.files

handle: fn(upload: Bytes) -> Bytes !(IsolateError | codec.CodecError | z.ZError) {
    tags: exif.process_bytes(upload)                       // in-process: pure Python
    pic: img.load_memory(upload)                           // .Wasm
    thumb: pil.from_rgba(pic.width, pic.height, pic.pixels).resize([128, 128])   // .Process under .Hardened
    z.compress(thumb.png_bytes(), level: 6)                  // in-process, hardened clang build
}

run: fn() {
    out: handle(fs.read_bytes("upload.jpg"))
    print(out.len())
}
```

```sh
  codec     .Process     closed binary sha256:44c1…         effects enforced: [FS.Read]
  exifread  in-process   pure Python                        effects proven:   []
  pillow    .Process     native extension, hardened profile effects enforced: [FS.Read]

```

cards.title: FFI v3 gallery: Python (statistics, numpy, pandas with matplotlib)
cards.body:
Three complete programs that call Python through `use py.<package>`. The `pybind` package (root `py`) runs the
pinned CPython with its `jetpy.describe` module to read type hints, stubs (`.pyi`), classes and exceptions, and
emits Jet types. Typed functions get Jet signatures; untyped ones get `Dyn` values that decode on use. Placement is
decided by facts (D-FFI-PLACE1): pure Python runs embedded in-process; native extensions run in-process by default
and in a child process under the hardened profile. Outputs are design targets.

## Simple: the standard library's statistics module

```jet
use stats: py.statistics                     // ships with the pinned CPython; no dependency line needed

run: fn() {
    xs: [2.0, 4.0, 4.0, 4.0, 5.0, 5.0, 7.0, 9.0]
    print(stats.mean(xs))                       // list[float] hint -> [F64]
    print(stats.pstdev(xs))
    print(stats.median(xs))
    print(stats.mean([]))                       // StatisticsError -> stats.StatisticsError
}
```

```text
5.0
2.0
4.5
Error [stats.StatisticsError]: mean requires at least one data point
  in Python  statistics.py:430   mean()
  -- crossing: py.statistics mean  (binder pybind 1.0.3, rule emit_call) --
  in Jet     main.jet:8:11  run()
```

## Medium: numpy arrays shared, not copied

What it shows: PEP 3118 buffers over Jet list memory, so numpy reads and writes Jet data in place; dtype and shape
facts from numpy's stubs; in-place operations take a writable input in the binding's signature, so the call stays plain.

```jet
package: {
    name: "signal"
    deps: { numpy: py@"numpy==2.1" }
}

use np: py.numpy

run: fn() {
    wave: loop i in 0..<1024 -> (Float.from_int(i) * 0.05).sin()
    samples := wave.copy()
    spectrum: np.fft.rfft(samples)                  // reads samples in place; returns an np.Array<Complex128> handle
    peak: np.argmax(np.abs(spectrum))
    print("peak bin {peak}")

    np.multiply(samples, 0.5, out: samples)          // writes into Jet memory through the buffer
    print(samples[20])

    m: np.Array<F64>.from(samples).reshape(32, 32)   // an owned ndarray handle
    print(m.shape)                                      // [32, 32]
    print(np.linalg.det(m.slice(0..<3, 0..<3)))
}
```

```text
peak bin 8
0.4207354924039483
[32, 32]
-0.0
```

## Complex: pandas report with matplotlib, async I/O and a placement choice

What it shows: a DataFrame as an opaque handle with typed column access; Python exceptions as Jet errors;
an `async def` turned into a wait point; a Jet callback passed to `DataFrame.apply`; the hardened profile moving
native extensions to a child process with no call-site change.

```jet
package: {
    name: "sales_report"
    deps: {
        pandas: py@"pandas==2.2"
        mpl: py@"matplotlib==3.9"
        aiohttp: py@"aiohttp==3.10"
    }
    profile: { release: { foreign: .Hardened } }       // pandas, numpy and matplotlib run in a child process
}

use pd: py.pandas
use plt: py.matplotlib.pyplot
use http: py.aiohttp

#Codable
Rate: struct {
    currency: String
    to_usd: F64
}

fetch_rates: fn() -> [Rate] !http.ClientError {
    session: http.ClientSession.new()                 // async with -> Close at scope end
    resp: session.get("https://rates.example/today")  // coroutine -> wait point
    resp.json<[Rate]>()                                 // coroutine -> wait point; decoded into Jet records
}

run: fn() {
    rates: fetch_rates()
    df: pd.read_csv("sales.csv", parse_dates: ["day"])
    df.assign_column("usd", df.apply((row) -> {          // call-scoped Jet callback
        currency: row.get_text("currency")
        rate: rates.find((r) -> r.currency == currency)?.to_usd ?? 1.0
        row.get_f64("amount") * rate
    }, axis: 1))
    monthly: df.groupby(pd.Grouper(key: "day", freq: "ME")).sum_column("usd")

    fig: plt.figure(figsize: [8.0, 4.0])
    ax: fig.add_subplot()
    ax.bar(monthly.index_text(), monthly.values_f64())
    ax.set_title("Revenue (USD)")
    fig.savefig("revenue.png", dpi: 150)
    print("months: {monthly.len()}, best: {monthly.idxmax()}")

    bad: pd.read_csv("missing.csv")                    // FileNotFoundError -> pd.FileNotFoundError
    print(bad.len())
}
```

```text
months: 12, best: 2026-07
Error [pd.FileNotFoundError]: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'missing.csv'
  in Python  pandas/io/parsers/readers.py:1026   read_csv()
  -- crossing: py.pandas read_csv  (binder pybind 1.0.3, rule emit_call, placement .Process) --
  in Jet     report.jet:46:12  run()
```

`jet audit foreign report.jet --placement` shows pandas, numpy and matplotlib in `.Process` (native extensions,
hardened profile) and aiohttp's pure-Python parts in-process.

```mojo
def main():

# Julia PythonCall.jl is similar: pyimport, Py values, conversion with pyconvert.
```

cards.title: Package diagnostics, lints and rewrite rules as values; retire hand-written marker name switches
cards.body:
The registry has 874 diagnostic rows; 80 carry a structured fix and 71 a lint name (DiagnosticRows.jet). Marker names are matched by hand in the parser (Compiler/JetParser/Source/Parser/Items.jet:1593) and in sema (Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/MarkerRules.jet:918), and re-declared as strings (Compiler/JetFoundation/Data/Syntax/CoreSurface.jet:160). Packages cannot register codes.

Done when: `impl T.Diagnostic` and `impl T.Lint` register package codes; `syntax.rewrite(pattern, template)` declares a structured fix that `jet fix` applies; the marker switches read the declared markers (D-MARKER-REFLECT1).

Research: Docs/research/declarative-jet-2026-10-31.md (card #6513). Citations are at dev 68c87ae07b. Section 3.11.

criteria.text: The parser and sema marker switches read the declared markers (D-MARKER-REFLECT1); the hand-written name matches at Parser/Items.jet and Sema/MarkerRules.jet are gone.

NEW-D-LINT-DECL1=A is built (owner ratified 2026-11-11): Diagnostic stays the only finding carrier and gains `tier` and `structured_fix`, while `fix` stays literal help text. A package lint is a checked compile-event subscriber over resolved calls (the NoPrintInLib example fires only on the resolved print symbol inside the opted-in library). syntax.rewrite takes resolved callable identities, keeps argument subtrees and refuses incompatible argument or return types. Importing a package never turns its lints on; a root enables the package's lint group once. Goldens and UI snapshots prove the NoPrintInLib lint, a structured fix applied by `jet fix`, the refused incompatible rewrite, and that a dependent's import stays silent.

cards.title: `#Test` declares properties, fuzz targets and bench budgets
cards.body:
Snapshot, golden and property testing are calls inside test bodies (Core/Testing/Testing.jet:102, 136, 517-532). `#Test` (Compiler/Prelude/Markers.jet:180) has no parameters for generation, fuzzing or budgets, and there is no bench marker.

Done when: a `#Test` function with typed parameters is run as a property with derived generators and shrinking; `fuzz: true` on a `[U8]` parameter registers a fuzz target for D-TEST-MUTFUZZ1's engine; `bench: perf.budget(...)` is a D-WD14 gate.

Research: Docs/research/declarative-jet-2026-10-31.md (card #6513). Citations are at dev 68c87ae07b. Section 3.9.
