cards.title: Self-compile wall regressed from the best measured 9.62 s; get it back below, then keep improving
cards.body: Owner 2026-10-31: the best measured self-compile was 9.62 s. Track major regressions and fix them through the ongoing optimization work. History, from seed rotation s2/s3 builds of the compiler at the default level on a reserved slot: a0_019 (Oct 24) 11.3/9.4 s; a0_020 (Oct 28) 10.7/11.1 s; a0_021 22.6/16.8 s; a0_022 (Oct 30) 12.9/12.4 s; wave 17 chain s2 (Oct 31) 22.8 s. Today's dev compiler (wave 17 s2), fresh tree, 24 pinned CPUs, load 35-48: O0 19.9 s wall/56.5 user-s/6.6 GB; O1 (default) 54.7 s/91.9 user-s/6.9 GB; O2 175 s/143 user-s/5.3 GB, binary 83.4 MB (O1 69.0 MB). Wall far above user/cores means contention, so absolute numbers are inflated; the same-run interleaved A/B (a0_019 on its own source vs dev s2 on dev, 3 rounds, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/selfab) gives the real delta. Plan: bisect across seeds and waves with the stage store, attribute by phase (Tools/perf/budget trace), fix the roots as general compiler/runtime wins, and add a per-wave self-compile A/B against a pinned reference compiler so a regression over 5% is flagged in the wave REPORT.

log.text: Owner of the remaining load-reach work, 2026-11-12 01:3x: G4Ports-1, under #6759 c2. CoreReach.jet (steps 1-3, through 5d60ee4241) is module-granular: on seed-b10, hello plus x.abs() still loads 38 modules in 1043 ms, because Encoding Stream and Cbor reach core.math. The next step makes reach per declaration (lexer item runs as the unit, use targets loaded only when a reached run names the alias, conservative closure over impls and globally registered items, with the core_demand safety net kept), extending CoreReach.jet rather than adding a second mechanism. One SUB meets #6759 c2 and this card's c10.

Main, 2026-11-11: c10 step 3 is on dev as 5d60ee4241 (G8Scope-45 rev 3, landed as G5DevX-g8s45r). core.math loads by use, so sqrt1.jet checks 1364 functions instead of 1785, in 734 ms instead of 915. c10 is still open: it needs the per-phase breakdown on the batch compiler, each root fixed and proven on a second script, and the PortBars speed and memory pass. The cold-compile roots measured on the port twins (comptime.bodies, Core load, sema.finalize) are on #6759, whose c2 is the same load-by-reach rule.

c5: inspect_structure_text_and_json_expose_the_three_rows (G11Speed-4t) PASSes on seed-b8 (meet-reproof1), but it doesn't prove c5's acceptance, which is that every untraced build step of the c1 cell is traced and takes at most 2 s of wall. That needs a timed build trace. Not met.

c8 scope widened (Main, 2026-11-11): besides the layout-directory fsyncs, a cold build with seed-t23 waited 458 s in jbd2_log_wait_commit before its first span, because the build executor publishes its CAS blobs (put_blob -> publish_blob) and action records (put_record -> publish_action) durably, 15 puts about 25 s apart under a busy journal (Jetpack/Store/Source/Build/ArtifactStore.jet). The executor already reads a missing blob or bad record as a cache miss (Build/Cache.jet:239, :535), so G11Speed-7b makes those executor-only publishes non-durable (native-runtime and receipt publishes stay durable), with a miss-not-fault test, or skips them when caching is off. c8 is met by -7 plus -7b with the n=3 cold-store measurement.

G11Speed-1 (CheckedText impl index, fixes root F, c4) measured on the c1 cell, n=3, default mode, 750,411 lines, CPUs 20-31, --threads 12, cold and uncached, arms back to back on a contended host (load 51-96). Median before (seed-t22): 160.94 s wall, 820.3 CPU-s, 4,662 lines/s, 1,093 us CPU/line, parallelism 5.1, RSS 8.73 GB. After: 85.17 s, 236.7 CPU-s, 8,811 lines/s, 315 us CPU/line, parallelism 2.8, RSS 8.72 GB. sema.finalize 59.6 to 10.0 s wall; comptime 30.5 to 1.9 s. Next largest: ir.opt (21 s wall, 100 CPU-s, root B, c6) and 31 s outside the trace (root C, c5). The #5479 c5 gate (60 us/line) is still 5.3x away. Table: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/G11Speed/cell-n3.md.

Wave 24 (a34ef0affd) carries AsmPar-21 (int-sum leaf 8 lanes: isum release 314.2M -> 288.3M cycles), AsmPar-22 (nested short circuits branch directly: wordfreq release -7.1% cycles) and AsmPar-23 (negated inner short circuits; self-compile s1 byte-identical). Same-run interleaved A/B 21:36-21:40 (24 CPUs 4-15,20-31, load 23-43, default level, fresh trees, 3 rounds; $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/selfab/summary.txt): a0_019 on its own source (77b18e4f00) wall 25.6/27.8/22.4 s (median 25.6), user 58.6/60.7/51.1 s (median 58.6), RSS 6.24 GB; dev s2 (68c87ae07b) on dev wall 20.9/22.6/21.9 s (median 21.9), user 70.0/74.2/77.1 s (median 74.2), RSS 7.35 GB. Under this load, wall is 15% better but CPU work is +27% and peak RSS +1.1 GB (+18%); the source also grew between the two commits. Next: a quiet-slot run plus per-phase trace and lines/s to separate source growth from per-line cost; bisect user-CPU across seeds a0_019..a0_022 and waves 16-18.

criteria.text: Root F (proved by G11Speed's bisect, 2026-11-11, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/G11Speed/report-bisect.md): 9afa7da76b (#6206 c22 CheckedText Hole/build) dropped the Distinct-only guard of sema_expression_checked_text_target, so every typed literal and Type.method() call walked every impl with string-cloning name lookups (77.9% of samples on seed-t22). It was amplified by 8c02016476, af8d3e09d0 and 8eaf6f17cc. Fixed by G11Speed-1, which indexes CheckedText impl rows once at registration (same rows, same order). Acceptance: the c1 cell's default-mode CPU-s on the t22 tree is at most 1.10x a0.0.43's per corpus line; comptime.precheck and sema.bodies wall are each at most 1.10x a0.0.43's; and perf shows sema_expression_checked_text_target under 1% of samples. Measured on the fix (n=1, basic): 749 to 164 CPU-s, 6.7K to 14.8K lines/s.

Root C: 42d3bedfe8 and d17bb32500 (2026-11-08) made `jet build Compiler` build the whole toolchain (runtime pack, IDENTITY) and regenerate the Prelude copies and keyword spans, about 23 s of untraced build steps per build (wall 36 to 74 s with CPU flat). Acceptance: every untraced step of the c1 cell is traced phase by phase and takes at most 2 s of wall, or becomes part of the traced compile.

Root B: bb770de593 (2026-11-01, the default level also versions small loops, runs the SSA round trip and the reductions) took ir.opt from 1.2 to 8.9 s wall. Acceptance: ir.opt at the default level costs at most a0_021's per-line cost (1.18 s wall over 646K lines) times 1.10 on the c1 cell, or each pass over that bound has its own named root. Architectural only (owner order 2026-11-11: no small tuning during language churn): the fix is pass scheduling or structure, not per-pass tweaks.

Root A: the a0_021 to a0_022 jump (2026-10-28 to 10-30, 54 to 89 CPU-s, compiler side +21% across trees) is attributed by the c1 cell's per-phase CPU on the a0_022 tree, both compilers, to named commits, and each named root is fixed or carded here.

A cold artifact store opens without per-directory fsync stalls, and the open is traced. Found by G11Speed on 2026-11-11 ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/G11Speed/b30/hang-finding.md): Jetpack/Store/Source/ArtifactStore/Store.jet (~964-971) creates the layout directories cas, ac, lto, locks, leases, quarantine, build-records and records through store_artifact_ensure_dir (Codec.jet:277), which fsyncs the parent after each mkdir. On a busy ext4 that cost 22.55 s across 8 fsyncs in one bench30k build (63 s total), all in an untraced gap between sema.finalize and ir.build; at 4G, 8 of 8 builds stalled. Fix: layout directories are recreated by any later run, so they aren't synced (per Codec.jet's own rule); durable records keep their sync; and a store.open trace span covers the work. Proof: a cold-store jet build of bench30k on the scratch disk ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT), n=3, shows store.open under 0.5 s in the trace and no untraced gap above 1 s, and the store crash-safety tests still pass.

Build reuse and the jet build binary store are off by default, per the standing caches-off order. Found by G11Speed on 2026-11-11: Executor.jet:324 restores any reusable step unconditionally, BuildExecute.jet:188 always opens the store when a build has steps, and Cli/BuildCache.jet:29 keeps the binary store on by default, with no switch (cli.md:504 documents made-or-reused). Fix (G11Speed-7c): a default build opens no store and puts nothing; opting in uses only an existing switch, or the executor API for tests if none exists, and any new public opt-in spelling goes to a ballot. cli.md and the BuildExecutor action-reuse test are updated in the same cutover. Proof: a test shows a default build opens no store; the opted-in reuse test passes; and cold and warm jet build Compiler are measured n=3 before and after.

Cold script cost: `jet file.jet` for a script importing core.process compiles and runs from cold, with no reuse, in less wall time and peak memory than the original tool it replaces. Today (ScriptAPI-2, PortBars outputs, 2026-11-11) b4 pays 1.1-1.6 s and 355-388 MB per run, against originals of 37-1700 ms and 5.8-57 MB, so all 7 measured tool twins fail the speed and memory bars (e.g. census-snap2 21086 ms / 422 MB vs 1117 ms / 47.5 MB). Acceptance: a per-phase CPU and peak-RSS breakdown of that script on the batch compiler names each root (parse/import/sema/lowering/emit/link of Core modules the script does not reach, eager whole-module work, arena sizing); each root is fixed in the general path and proven on a second script; the PortBars speed and memory bars pass on the census-snap2 and roots-mjs entries with cold compile counted. Reuse is not the fix: the standing order counts cold compile time.

Checking a root never needs gigabytes. With seed-b6 at d97d742871 and MemoryMax=6G, `jet check` was OOM-killed on 8 roots: Compiler/JetBackend/Tests, Compiler/JetCli, Compiler/JetCli/Commands, Compiler/JetCli/Commands/Tests, Compiler/JetCli/Tests, its GateProjection.fixture and RustForeign.fixture, and Compiler/JetDriver/Tests. Other scopes peaked at 6.0-6.8 GB. A collect-all census records the peak RSS of `jet check` for every in-repo root, and each phase's memory owner (parse, register, comptime, sema, IR) is named from a profile of the worst root. Every root's peak is then at most 3 GB, with no caching or reuse.

[#2534] No BuildCache, RuntimeCache, RunCache, ReceiptStore, BuildPlanReplay or JET_TIMING/JET_RUN_TRACE/JET_RECEIPT_BYPASS/JET_CACHE_DIR/JET_RUNTIME_CACHE_DIR remains. Every new note and tool error is registered with a UI snapshot. architecture.md, compiler-speed.md and the syntax-decisions ledger describe the graph, store, units and levels as shipped. (moved from #2514 c16)

cards.title: Core #Test blocks have no runner: tests inside Core modules never execute
cards.body: Found 2026-11-01 00:10 (GoldC-3, #6457). Core modules carry #Test blocks (for example Core/Data/Data.jet:2785), but nothing runs them. jet test Core/Data/Data.jet stops with E0067 on __-prefixed names, testkit has no core suite, core-conformance.mjs runs a corpus under tests/conformance, and core-module-check.mjs only runs jet check per module. So every Core #Test is unexecuted, and card criteria that cite them cannot be proven. Fix: one runner (a testkit core suite or jet test over Core with Core-internal names allowed) that executes every Core #Test on o0/o1/o2, gated in lane-check or the wave report, plus a census of the blocks that fail today.

log.text: c2 gating: Admit.jet compares the published seed with the candidate on each suite, and seeds up to a0_040 have no core profile, so "core" joins SUITES once the first seed containing e2118b654e is published (the release after it gates on core).

Main 2026-11-08: priority raised. The ports under #6687 (TlsLead #6694, SqliteLead #6695, G1Lead #6688) need it to prove private Core parts, and 73 Core files hold #Test blocks that never run. Assigned to QuickLead after #6686. Until then, port vectors go in tests/cases.

cards.title: Startup cost: dynamic symbol binding, setlocale and env capture dominate short programs (hello 8.8x, taskfile 22x asm)
cards.body: asm-parity on dev 45ab3b5ef5 (perf record cycles:u, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/asmpar-45ab/hot.sh): hello's cycles are ld.so symbol binding (do_lookup_x 24%, _dl_lookup_symbol_x 23%, _dl_check_all_versions 15%) and glibc tunables init (24%). taskfile spends 14% in check_match, 13% in _nl_intern_locale_data (a setlocale/locale load), 12% in jet_rt_host_env_capture, 12% in strcmp and 12% in record_in. Every cell pays this startup cost. Within the current dynamic-libc model (static linking is the owner ballot #5088): import only the libc symbols the program reaches, avoid eager binding of unused imports, don't load locale data the program never uses, and capture the environment lazily (#6493 is in wave 22). Proof: asm-parity hello and taskfile cycles columns drop, no cell worse in bytes or cycles, and output is identical.

log.text: HELD by owner order 2026-11-11 (no small optimizations until the language is mostly stable; architecture and regression fixes go first, per #5479 c5-c8). These criteria stay open and unworked: c1 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c); c2 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c).

BoardPlanner review 2026-11-09 (dev 6a06b917cb). Speed or size climb: moved from G13 to G11. Owner order 2026-11-09: all speed and size work is G11. It stays a horizon card under the 2026-11-08 rule: it blocks no card, milestone, release or gate, and its targets are not pass/fail criteria elsewhere.

Linux syscall leaf loads its arguments straight into the syscall registers (no push/pop glue): asm-parity hello 2942 -> 2681 instructions:u (-8.87%) default and release on a34ef0affd + this patch; REF-SAME 48/48; lane-check CHECK OK (jet-lane-check.z6u8Iv) Landed in wave 25 as dev 367eaf8f0d (Codegen-1-47).

jet_rt_alloc_init maps the allocator root and size-class table in one mmap (one startup syscall fewer per process) and the JET_CHECKED_ALLOC envp walk no longer spills its cursor; REF-SAME 48/48 and asm-parity bytes -8/-16 default on a34ef0affd + this patch; lane-check CHECK OK (jet-lane-check.mGwHm2) Landed in wave 25 as dev 367eaf8f0d (Codegen-1-46).

Jet-owned main indexes envp on the first environment read instead of at startup: asm-parity taskfile default 2,715,178 -> 1,394,992 instructions:u (-48.6%), release -48.9%, every runtime-linked cell -220K, on a34ef0affd + this patch; REF-SAME 48/48; lane-check CHECK OK (jet-lane-check.WJt5mR) Landed in wave 25 as dev 367eaf8f0d (Codegen-1-45).

CORRECTION (Codegen-1): the ld.so, tunables and locale rows in Main's hot.sh came from the taskset wrapper (perf record -- taskset BIN profiles taskset's own dynamic startup before exec). The asm-parity binaries are static, with no dynamic section and no libc. Real hello cost: 7,212 cycles:u / 2,642 instructions, about 1,200 of them the JET_CHECKED_ALLOC env scan that environment.md requires; the rest is syscalls and page faults (TLS, 12K stdout buffer, 256K sigaltstack, 4 sigactions, ioctl). taskfile: host_env_capture (#6493), alloc/free, stop_poll and thread_attach. The scope of this card is now those real startup costs. The long-running cells' profiles (fft, wordfreq, nbody, binparse, tensormap) are unaffected; taskset is negligible there.

cards.title: Function-value copy: does f.copy() of an escaping closure share its captured state, give an independent copy, or get refused?
cards.body:
Question (owner/ballot): spec.md:889-905 ("Captures and escaping lambdas") says an escaping lambda owns its captures. Copy values are copied at closure creation, clonable values are cloned, and owned non-clonable values move. It never says what a *function value* does when it is copied (`alias: counter.copy()`) or bound twice.

Witness: tests/cases/run_regressions/shared_and_closure_owner_topology_is_preserved.case, fixture tests/fixtures/shared_owner_topology.jet:82-87.
  counter: make_counter(live)   // returns `(value: Int) -> { bucket.values.push(value) ... }` over a `:=` Bucket it owns
  alias: counter.copy()
  print(counter(1)); print(alias(2)); print(counter(3))
The ORACLE-LITERAL output (run_regressions.rs:174, never re-bless) is 102 / 202 / 302. bucket.values.len() grows 1, 2, 3 across counter and alias, so the alias **shares** the one captured environment, as a refcounted closure would.

Today: sema refuses with E0211 "`fn(Int) -> Int` can't be copied" (360e470044).

Alternatives:
- A: A function value is a cheap handle. `.copy()` (and implicit copy) shares the captured environment, as `Shared<T>` handles do (spec.md:1426-1431). Matches the oracle 102/202/302. Needs closure env refcounting in IR/runtime and a spec sentence.
- B: `.copy()` deep-clones the captured environment, so each copy has its own state. Requires every capture to be clonable, or E0211. The oracle would become 102/102/202 (re-blessing an ORACLE-LITERAL needs owner sign-off).
- C: Function values that own mutable captured state are not copyable (today's E0211). The spec gains that sentence, and the case's alias line is removed with owner sign-off (oracle lines 11-12 change).

Acceptance: spec.md "Captures and escaping lambdas" states the chosen rule. The fixture then runs on every tier with the decided output, and shared_and_closure_owner_topology_is_preserved passes (or is rewritten per C with a cited spec line).

Related fixture repairs already staged by CardClose-1 (CC-66 follow-up, not yet landed because this blocks the run):
- bare-block scopes become helper fns (S6-R, syntax-decisions.md:3949)
- `fn(Int) Int` becomes `fn(Int) -> Int` (spec.md:857)
- `String!` becomes `Err!` (E2417)
- untyped-lambda `return x` becomes the tail value
- SharedSnapshot `.value` becomes `.value()` (Main ruling, SharedOwner.jet:429)
- `!= .None` now type-checks (CC-66 sema fix, D-FLOWTYPE1)

cards.title: Jet web framework: full breadth and depth parity with the best frameworks, with their downsides designed out
cards.body:
## Outcome

Owner direction: Jet ships a first-class, native web framework (the Core web modules, compiled by Jet, with no JavaScript runtime or wrapped library). It has full breadth and depth parity with every element of the best frameworks, and every known downside of those elements is engineered away in the Jet design rather than inherited. The framework has no brand of its own (D-WEB-NAME1=C, 2026-11-04): it is Jet's web library, named by its module; no repository path or user-facing text keeps a third-party framework's name.

## Scope

Parity is judged element by element against the best framework for that element, not against one framework. The reference set covers at least: TanStack (Start, Router, Query, Form, Table, Virtual, Store, DB, devtools), Next.js, Remix / React Router, SvelteKit, SolidStart, Qwik, Astro, Nuxt, Angular, Phoenix LiveView, Rails (Hotwire), Laravel (Livewire), Django, Leptos and Dioxus, htmx and Elysia/Hono. Elements include routing and typed search params, data loading and caching, mutations and optimistic updates, forms and validation, tables and virtualization, state stores, rendering modes (SSR, SSG, ISR, streaming, islands, resumability, CSR), server functions and actions, real-time and live views, auth and sessions, i18n, images and assets, styling, testing, devtools, error boundaries, deployment and edge targets, and the dev loop.

## Method

1. A dated audit (Docs/audits) with one row per element: the best framework for it, what Jet has (by code path and executable example, not prose), the gap, and each known downside of the best implementation with the Jet design that removes it.
2. One ballot per owner choice the audit raises (new syntax, public API, product behavior), with same-program alternatives.
3. One child card per gap, each closing with an executable example and golden output on every applicable tier (I5, I9), and a performance cell where the element is performance-relevant.

## Known downsides to design out (seed list, the audit extends it)

Hydration cost and mismatch bugs; client bundle growth; waterfalls between nested loaders; cache invalidation by hand; stringly-typed routes and search params; server/client boundary leaks of secrets; framework lock-in to one host; slow dev rebuilds; runtime-only type errors in forms and APIs; opaque magic in file conventions; duplicated validation between client and server.

## Current state

Examples/features/web/tanstack_start/run.jet is a reference app over the Core web modules (router, query, forms, table, virtual, store). Its web build is being repaired under #5990 c13. It is evidence of coverage breadth only; depth parity is unaudited.

log.text: BoardPlanner review 2026-11-09 (dev 6a06b917cb). Correction to the log above: c14's ballot is not missing. D-DX-BROWSERTEST1=A (ratified 2026-09-04, from #2498) chose "extend jet test" and the spec carries its flags (spec.md:4004-4007), so c14 is met and c15-c18 (scaffold, UI mode, trace viewer, matrix and reporters) are build work inside that contract. Only a new command or a new jet new template name for the scaffold would need its own ballot; adding a browser #Test to the existing web template does not.

BoardPlanner review 2026-11-09 (dev 6a06b917cb). Body: D-WEB-NAME1=C (2026-11-04) chose no brand, so "its own Jet name" is gone. Owner gates: c14 waits for a browser-test ballot (scaffold, UI mode, trace viewer) that is not drafted; c2 is the standing rule that every audit choice gets a ballot. c30's ballots are ratified and archived with #4282: D-WEBAPP-SERVE1=D (2026-07-28) and D-WEBRUN1=A (2026-08-27). Merged: c21 into c22, c23-c27 into c28, c19 into c29 (D-G9-4, D-G9-5). Gained #5201 c22 (typed forms). New row: the study rerun from the goal body.

criteria.text: A dated parity audit in Docs/audits lists every element of the reference frameworks named in the body, the best framework for each element, Jet's current state cited by code path and executable example, the gap, and each known downside of the best implementation with the Jet design that removes it.
Every owner choice the audit raises is on a Tower ballot with same-program alternatives, and every ratified choice has a child card under this card.

The framework name ballot is ratified, and no repository path, example name, or user-facing text uses a third-party framework's name for the Jet framework (Examples/features/web/tanstack_start is renamed in one cutover).

A repository scan for jet_web_framework, jet-web-framework and 'Jet Web framework' outside Docs/audits and Tower finds only the dated owner-feedback proposal heading (generic phrase in historical evidence). golden --filter web/jet_web: PASS o0/o1/o2; the renamed cases match their old-name baseline rows (graph KF #4830, browser REFUSED line 27). lane-check: CHECK OK. tanstack_start no longer exists in the tree.

cards.title: Native code faults (SIGSEGV at 0x0) seeking a handle bound by '&executables[i].file == .Val(input)' in store_reuse_executable_lease_members
cards.body: Repro (Linux, admitted compiler 657d0c5553 and HEAD 83c4c6521b runtime alike): assemble the Engine unit (JETPACK_BOOTSTRAP_AREAS=$(node Jetpack/Bootstrap/areas.mjs closure Engine) JETPACK_BOOTSTRAP_OWN_AREA=Engine node Jetpack/Bootstrap/assemble.mjs aot), then in its project run: jet test src/jetpack.jet "realize verified round trips". The claim 'store broker realize verified round trips through broker and fails closed on auth' (Jetpack/Store/Tests/Broker.jet) FAILs with Fault [SIGSEGV] invalid memory access at address 0x0; backtrace compiler_fs_error <- store_reuse_executable_lease_members (Jetpack/Store/Source, line '&input.seek(0)' after 'if &executables[index].file == .Val(input)') <- store_reuse_build_lease <- store_snapshot_lease_unlocked <- store_snapshot_lease <- store_realize_verified. Safe code must never fault (I1): either the borrowed-pattern binding of an Option field through an indexed borrow lowers a null handle, or the File handle in SnapshotFile is dropped early. The claim is not listed in Tools/testkit/known-failing.tsv. Found by Main while proving #6426.

log.text: QuickLead receipt, 2026-11-08 (seed a0_038, source dev 759775d626): the Engine-unit claim passes on every tier. Steps: Jetpack/Bootstrap/Assemble.jet areas closure Engine; Assemble.jet aot (560 sources, 559 claims, no E1271); then jet test --optimize=none,basic,full src/jetpack.jet "realize verified round trips" gives 1 passed, 0 failed at each of none, basic and full. The minimal repro is the b75e525782 case borrowed_list_of_optional_handles. Main reruns this exact proof before meeting c1.

b75e525782 repro half: cases --filter borrowed_list_of_optional_handles PASS 1/1 (seed-built d405d4cb6c + 8405a508b0). The Engine-unit claim (store broker realize verified round trips) still waits on a locked jetpack source (E1271).

a0_034: minimal repro of the faulting pattern (a [SnapshotFile] with FileReader? handles passed by value to a loop, then twice through '&executables[i].file == .Val(input)' seek+read) prints names 3 / bytes 12 / again 12 on O0, O1 and O2: no fault, handles stay open. The Engine-unit claim still needs its jetpack env run.

Likely root: #6677. The faulting statement compares '&executables[index].file == .Val(input)': it widens the borrowed FileReader into an Option union, and before 060bbcd0f1 and 8ac163916e the widened value was moved and dropped, which closes the caller's handle (the 'corrupt after' bisect). Re-run the claim with a0_034, the first seed carrying both fixes, before any other work on this card.
Deconfliction 2026-11-06: reworded to match I9 tiers O0, O1, O2 and web (D-EXEC1, D-EXEC2=A: no interpreter or JIT).

Bisect (assembled Engine unit, s1 of 60324f013d, scratch edits to the assembled copy only): the SnapshotFile FileReader is valid (stat ok) before store_reuse_create_exec_wrappers and corrupt after it; the corrupt handle sends seek/stat into compiler_fs_error, which faults at 0x0. The general FS error path works in the same unit (open of a missing path reports NotFound). A probe placed right after 'ready :: store_reuse_keeper_line(&child)' faults, a probe after the spawn hides the fault, and probes at every step hide it (claim passes). --checked-alloc also hides it (passes). So the damage happens in or around the first keeper_line call (loop line in child.stdout.lines() -> return line: early return out of a shared process-lines iterator, IterSources.jet iter_source_node shared clone/release) and is heap-layout dependent. A standalone repro of that pattern (spawn sh, keeper_line twice, stat a FileReader between) runs clean on jet run. Next: build that standalone with --checked-alloc and run to main return (sweep catches write-after-free), then shrink inside keeper_line. Parked for the owner's marker work.

cards.title: Types contain their impls: jet check --style flags a detached impl and jet fix --style moves it into the type body
cards.body:
Owner direction: across all Jet code (Core libraries, the compiler, Jetpack, examples, tests and tools), a struct or enum contains its own impls. A separate top-level impl is allowed only when it has to be somewhere else. Struct and enum bodies already accept methods and nested `impl Trait { … }` blocks (Compiler/JetParser/Source/Parser/Items.jet:1947-1952 and :2035-2042), so this needs no new syntax.

Census at dev 2d8aea4762: 1,335 top-level impls sit in the same file as their own struct or enum, in 580 files. By tree: Compiler 282, Core 368, tests 436, Examples 179, Jetpack 42, Tools 27, Docs 1.

Allowed exceptions (each must be named by the lint's own rule, not by an allow list): the type is declared in another file, module or package; an error conversion `impl A -> B`; a protocol side `impl X.Client` or `impl X.Server`; a target-specific impl; an impl a derive or generated source writes; an impl the type body cannot hold (for example `impl T.Trait using field` until the nested form accepts `using`).

Flag: `--style` turns on opt-in style checks on `jet check` and applies their fixes on `jet fix`. Impl placement is the first member. The marker cutover on #6039 already writes markers in the nested form.
cards.plan: 1. Parity: nested impl blocks accept everything a top-level impl does that a type body can hold (assoc types, constants, operator right-hand types, #Commutative, and `using` delegation if feasible). 2. Lint: a registered lint code with what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot. It is off by default and on under `jet check --style`, and it flags an `impl T` or `impl T.Trait` in the same file as `struct T` or `enum T` outside its body, unless an exception rule applies. 3. Fix: `jet fix --style` moves each flagged impl into the type body. Inherent methods become `fn` members and trait impls become nested `impl Trait { … }`, keeping comments and order. Re-check after the move, and skip it with a reason if checking fails. 4. Formatter keeps nested impls in place. 5. Sweep the whole tree with `jet fix --style` in collect-all mode, one commit per top-level tree. 6. One line of style guidance in Docs/spec/contributing/agent-engineering.md.

cards.title: Leak freedom is structural: safe Jet cannot leak
cards.body: Owner rule, 2026-11-05: Jet never leaks memory. Leak freedom is part of the memory-safety guarantee (I1); only an expert #Unsafe block may leak, so the language must structurally prevent leaks rather than fix them case by case. On 2026-11-05 three lowering families leaked in safe code (c8a 5037b3ce72: a reassign after a move; c8b 2d712dd94a: a field read off a fresh call result; c8c: a loop over or an index into a fresh List or Map), found only because jet repl grew 6.2 GB over 9 turns. This card makes such a defect impossible to ship: the compiler checks its own output, and the suites fail any program that leaks.
cards.plan: 1. An ownership verifier pass after IR lowering. 2. A leak gate in the golden and cases suites, plus the compiler itself, using the checked allocator. 3. Fix every leak the two find, by lowering family. 4. An audit of every construct that could leak in safe code (shared values and cycles, tasks parked at exit, channels, globals, closures) with a structural rule for each, or an owner ballot where the rule is a language choice. 5. I1 in AGENTS.md states leak freedom.

log.text: Golden leak-gate census, 2026-11-05 on dev 02602250cc (s1 with the checked allocator; runtime process roots tagged; under --checked-alloc the runtime runs the entry's drops instead of the exit shortcut): about 1170 of the golden programs leak (o0 1164, o1 1162, o2 1161 rows; about 100 more rows leak on only some tiers). On o0, 610 rows leak only runtime init roots (jet_rt_*_init, TLS keys), so the runtime frees or tags those at shutdown; 507 have real library or user leaks. Leak-gate rows: 3492 of 4715. Starting point for c2 and c3 when G19 is worked.

c3 progress (invariant fixes), f2ba7d34bf: the fresh-temporary-never-dropped family. loop x in make(), make()[i], make_map()[k], every non-mutating Map/Set builtin on a fresh receiver, and Set.from(make()) (buffer) now end the temporary. Before: 100-520 MB VmRSS per 40,000 rounds per shape on O0 and O2. Three new cases FAIL->PASS, one guard case PASS on both; every shape clean under --checked-alloc on O0 and O2; chain FIXED_POINT; golden A/B 267 = 267; cases A/B over 284 ids. Probe audit of the flat shapes (match, if pattern, struct method, String chains, ?. and ??, slices, tuple fields) is in the guard case.

criteria.text: After IR lowering, a verifier checks that every owned value, temporaries included, is dropped or moved exactly once on every path out of its scope, outside #Unsafe. It runs on every compile at O0, O1 and O2; a violation is an internal compiler error (exit 101), never a user diagnostic. A negative-control case shows it catching each of the 2026-11-05 leak shapes when the matching fix is reverted.

The golden and cases suites run their programs with the checked allocator and fail any row whose program exits with a live owned block allocated outside #Unsafe, at o0, o1 and o2. The compiler itself passes the same check: jet check and jet build over Core and over the compiler's own sources end with zero leaked blocks, and 9 jet repl turns of repl_core_data_query_plans_and_typed_joins stay flat.
Every leak the verifier or the leak gate finds is fixed at its root, per lowering family, each with a case per shape; the full suites then run with the leak gate on and show zero leak rows.

An audit, committed under Docs/audits, lists every construct that can keep memory alive in safe Jet (shared values and reference cycles, tasks or generators parked at exit, channels, globals and caches, closures and captures) and states the structural rule that prevents a leak for each, with a case; any rule that is a language choice goes to an owner ballot.
AGENTS.md I1 states that safe Jet cannot leak memory (only #Unsafe may), and Docs/spec/philosophy.md's memory-safety guarantee says the same.
criteria.evidence: 520bfbfa0f: AGENTS.md I1 says memory safety includes leak freedom: safe Jet cannot leak memory, and only code inside an #Unsafe block or function may. Docs/spec/philosophy.md design priority 1 says safe Jet cannot leak memory: every value it allocates is freed, and only #Unsafe code may leak.

criteria.text: (moved from #6035 c8) Root found by Prep 2026-11-04 for c7 (report $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/briefs/6035-c7-perf.md; measured at 5 jobs: ui 256 s, golden 678 s, cases OOM at 16G and 856 s for its last 826 entries at a 19.7 GiB peak). R1: jet repl keeps every turn's compile in memory (Repl.jet:338-348): 773 MiB at 1 turn grows to 5.6 GiB at 9, and suite repl cases reach 4.7-8.3 GB. Per-turn memory stays flat: 9 turns of repl_core_data_query_plans_and_typed_joins under 1 GiB, with a test. (Also #6543.)

A runtime leak and double-drop witness proves leak freedom per program: today JET_MEMORY_LEDGER records only unsafe sentry events (not leaks or double drops), and the counting allocator cap does not trip on String allocations (a 32 MB copy ran under a 48 MB cap; found by CoreCliLead-2 on #6677). A safe-Jet program run under the witness reports live allocations at exit = 0 and any double drop as a failure, on O0, O1 and O2. jet test and jet dev print the same witness: live allocations, unreleased foreign handles and Shared cycles with their sites on every level; release builds carry no tracking (was #3239 c49).

cards.title: Close rate: one source of truth per fact, structural checks, criteria sized to close
cards.body: Owner 2026-11-05: cards take too long to close; a well-designed codebase should take a change in one place. Measured on 2026-11-05: a compiler rebuild to fixed point takes about 5 minutes (147 s s1 + 132 s), and a lander batch averages 129 s over 111 batches, so build and landing are not the bottleneck. The causes are copies of one fact that drift (a diagnostic lives in the Prelude row, the generated DiagnosticRows, the coverage baseline, the snapshot, the explain page and spec prose: retiring two codes touched 10 files, and ui --coverage found 137 drift errors), checks that are found serially instead of structurally (three leak families found one at a time; 1170 leaking golden programs), unported Rust behavior that is porting work rather than edits (82 KF-UNPORTED ui rows over about 60 codes, 23 more Rust-only codes, 294 open G15 criteria), and criteria merged from old cards that each hold a whole feature.

log.text: c9 decision (Main, 2026-11-13): the release comparison (Tools/release/Admit.jet) covers every native suite in Tools/ci/TestShards.jet, including registries, and derives its list from that one home. Found 2026-11-10 by Lander2 on the t18a train: `jet test` leaks its per-run files. Host.jet names them `.test_<stem>.<pid>` (binary) and `.test_<stem>.<pid>.records.*` under the native test records dir, and nothing removes them when the run is killed (timeout, OOM, signal). 796 stale files filled the 6.2G XDG runtime tmpfs to 97%, and later runs failed with ENOSPC ("native test record I/O failed", rc 101), which looked like a test failure. Fix it at the root: the run removes its own files on every exit path, including a killed child, and each run sweeps files whose PID is no longer alive before it writes, without touching a live run. A case kills a run mid-test and shows that the next run leaves 0 stale files. An ENOSPC in record I/O reports its cause and path instead of a bare ICE.

cards.title: First jet cc pack install hashes the 450 MB tree about four times with pure-Jet SHA-256
cards.body: Found by Builder5 on dev b44941163a: the first jet cc toolchain pack install takes about 290 s, about 90% of it in the Store hashing the 450 MB unpacked tree about four times with core_crypto_sha256 (pkg_try_output_hash_of, store_record_realized_mode, publish_object, seal). Hash each tree once and reuse the digest across those steps, and bring core_crypto_sha256 throughput to the machine ceiling (SHA-NI where available) per the performance gate.

log.text: BoardPlanner review 2026-11-09 (dev 6a06b917cb). Speed or size card: moved from G4 to G11. Owner order 2026-11-09: all speed and size work is G11.

Main 2026-11-08 06:00: phase 2 landed as a08ffb93e2 (G1Lead). Core sha256 runs blocks through the runtime __sha256_blocks (SHA-NI where the CPU has it) in a private module. Receipt: release build, on a host with sha_ni, best of 3, 64 x sha256 over 1 MiB takes 0.38 s against 1.43 s on dev (3.8x). A differential of 302 inputs (lengths 0..299, 4109, 1048583) against node crypto shows 0 mismatches on none and release. Golden Crypto/ 39 PASS, Jetc 3 PASS, cases crypto 43 PASS (1 known-failing E2702, 1 SKIP-HOST), argon2id 2 PASS; 12 ratchets --check pass on a0_037. With phase 1 (591744cc94 hash-once, 3058b17fff SHA-NI) that completes the build. c1 still needs the timing: a first `jet cc` pack install under 60 s on the reference machine, measured on a quiet machine with the next seed (it must contain a08ffb93e2; a0_037 does not).

Main 2026-11-08 03:45: c1 progress by G1Lead. The hash-once half landed in 591744cc94. SHA-NI phase 1 landed in 3058b17fff: x64 SSE/SHA template forms (12 SDM encodings plus 3 rejections, tested), the leaf os_sha256_block_i64 behind cpuid with the scalar fallback kept, jet_crypto_sha256_blocks, and the core.crypto.__sha256_blocks row. Phase 2 (the Core sha2_256 and JETC2 stream through sha256_blocks) waits for a seed built from 3058b17fff or later, since the seed resolves Core dunders from its compiled-in rows. Lane rows with phase 2: SHA-256 of 16 MiB 435 ms -> 43-52 ms (about 9.4x); 302/302 differential rows against node sha256/sha224 at O0/O1/O2; crypto cases 43 PASS, 0 FAIL; jetc 5/5.

Main 2026-11-07: g13 landed as 591744cc94 (a cold fetch-toolchain hashes once; 20.6 s cold on the home NVMe, 1131 s before) and b1f1abe895 (the shared-CAS pass reseals a tree left writable). The Jetpack Engine+Environment aot jet test (seed a0_034): baseline eaa085b237 and fixed tree have the same 13 FAIL rows (empty diff), none from #6592: 2 lease recovery (recover_stale_leases and store_recover_hangar give 0, expected 1); 1 clean-plan quarantine (closure record has no dependency references); native runtime split (the test expects Rust `fn main()`, the generator emits `main: fn()`); 8 recipe sandbox rows (E1238 instead of E1236/E1237/E1275: the sandbox cannot start inside the test systemd scope); shared_hostile_corpus (Assemble does not copy tests/fixtures/build_sandbox/hostile-corpus.tsv). None is in the a0_034 full-profile run. Logs: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/PortsLead/g13/tests-base.log and tests-fix.log.

PortsLead-2 AFTER numbers, g13 batch (link CAS, parallel fsync pool, hashing on worker tasks, one tree pass with a memo), not yet landed. Cold `jetpack env fetch-toolchain --json` from an empty HOME and state: 20.6 s wall on the home NVMe; 43.4 s on the contended scratch NVMe, and 96.6 s on a rerun at load 10, where the fsync writeback of 442 MB dominates. BEFORE was 1131.1 s. Tree hash unchanged: sha256-700385c9c906 (5931 files, 442377517 B); CAS 4019 entries, linked. Scratch split: verify 2.2 s, untar 7.1 s, seal 1.2 s, parallel hash 16.6 s, publish fsync 24.1 s, hangar 0.6 s. core.crypto SHA-256 runs at 45-50 MB/s at O1/O2, about 10x slower than a scalar native implementation (~500 MB/s) and 40x slower than SHA-NI; that work is on #6681.

PortsLead-2 measured a cold fetch-toolchain before the fix at 135.6 s on its own s1. The c65 fresh run spent about 45 minutes in the same phase (17:10-17:55) under heavy machine load. The gap is unexplained: the per-file sync alone may not account for the 45 minutes.

Root cause of the 45-minute cold fetch-toolchain (c65 run 4df47ce6da, 17:10-17:55; PortsLead-2): AdmissionTransaction.publish_object → store_fsync_tree fsyncs every file and directory of the pack, about 1,900 journal commits at about 1.4 s each. Fix: write everything, one filesystem flush, then the publish rename. That needs a public Core function, because a Core  seam is reserved outside Core (Spellings.jet:13, Sema/Calls/Core.jet:514); ballot D-FS-SYNC1 (A: files.sync_filesystem, B: parallel fsync_tree, C: no API). Internal commit A (runtime syncfs export plus seam rows, no public surface) lands meanwhile; commit B (public function, store change, conformance case) waits on the ballot and the next seed.

cards.title: JSON event reader drains a document about 10x slower than parse
cards.body: Measured by GoldenRoots3 on dev aeeb2c479c (golden serde/json_selective, 1.05 MB document, --release): draining every event from the JSON reader takes 1.37 s against 80-123 ms for parse, and decode<Small> builds the whole Dyn tree before projecting (129 ms, 84 MB peak vs 67 MB for parse). Bring the event path to at least parse speed, let typed projection skip unselected fields without materializing them, and add a paired cell with a ceiling reference per the performance gate.

log.text: HELD by owner order 2026-11-11 (no small optimizations until the language is mostly stable; architecture and regression fixes go first, per #5479 c5-c8). These criteria stay open and unworked: c1 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c); c2 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c).

Main 2026-11-08 03:35: reader speed slice by G1Lead, landing now. On the 1.09 MB 20-field doc (CPU time), the reader drains in 51 ms against 52-72 ms for parse; it started at 1110 ms. Per kind, reader vs parse: ints 24/36 ms, strings 30/40, objects 88/94. Remaining plan, set aside for cheaper G3 criteria per the pareto order: (a) typed projection, about 2-3 h. A compiler-private intrinsic encoding.__decode_keys<T>() gives the generated Decode its demanded wire keys, wired through CoreSignatures, CoreCallRows, the Sema backing gate and JetIR lowering. __decode_typed then skips the other root fields with a validating, non-materializing skip. (b) the paired performance cell. A gauntlet entry (e.g. formats.json-kernel) with a fixture, expected.out, and peers in rust, c, zig, go, python and node, plus a hand-written Tools/perf/asm-parity ref.S ceiling, about several hours.

criteria.text: Draining every event from the JSON reader is at least as fast as parse on the 1.05 MB serde/json_selective document, typed projection skips unselected fields without building a Dyn tree, and a paired perf cell records it against its peers (Jet/peer below 1.00; the ceiling ratio is reported only). Proof: the cell's row in Tools/gauntlet/measurement-manifest.json and the gauntlet receipt.
json.parse on the 2.4 MB document from #4667 beats every matched peer (V8 JSON.parse included) in a paired perf cell (Jet/peer below 1.00); the ceiling ratio is reported only.

cards.title: Every CLI flag must also be a setting: non-build commands (registry publish --force and others) have no settings home
cards.body: Standing owner order: every CLI flag is also a setting. The only flag↔setting table is JET_BUILD_OPTIONS (build profiles, fn build, pins), which only build, run and dev read. jet registry publish --force (CLICommands.jet:796; it also gates E1218 per #6600) and every other non-build command flag have no setting. First census every registered CLI flag against its setting home. Then ballot where non-build command settings live (e.g. package.jet publish: {…} vs a per-command settings table in jet settings), with same-program alternatives. Then build it, with one flag↔setting mechanism for all commands.

log.text: meet-6606 (seed-b8, dev cc09d22cb9, 29 lines PASS-only) credits c2 only. c1: the cases rows cover four families (keep-going, trace, opt-dump, fmt --check). c1 asks for a row per command family and a census of every registered flag; the full family list and a row for each are needed. c4: rows cover keep-going, trace and opt-dump. Still missing: the disable, verify and SSA-stress hooks, the GC trace, the phase counters and the memory ledger, plus proof that AGENTS.md, the skills and the repository tools use the flag rather than the variable. c6: the text and --json snapshots pass, but the redaction test (Controls.jet "a URL's user and password never show") wasn't among the lines, and the criterion's 'every registered variable that is set' needs a line without --command. Routed to ScriptAPI-2.

Edge the ballot did not cover: a relative XDG_CONFIG_HOME. ScriptAPI-50 refused it, which broke roots-sh (parity 0/11 on b8) and cache_cli_status. Decision: jet ignores a relative value and falls back to the default, as the XDG Base Directory specification requires. ScriptAPI-62 makes that fix, with cases.

Criteria c3-c7 added on the owner's order (2026-11-10 ~21:00, G5): environment variables become one registry in code, every behavior control becomes a flag or setting first, transport moves to one channel, one listing command is added, and the D-ENV-SURFACE1 ballot gates the public spellings. The census script is in Main's scratch (envcensus.mjs, envdoc.mjs).
Owner ruling 2026-11-09 (BoardPlanner C-G4-6): moved to G5 (one settings table). ScriptLead-15r, already built, lands; further work waits for G5 in the owner goal order.

D-CLI-SETTINGS-HOME1 posted for the owner after a CLEAN adversarial review (sol-reviewer, 2026-11-09): the flat commands: keys are added as A. It is a home-format vote only, not an implementation receipt. D-SCRIPT-LINE-HELPERS1 and D-RUN-TIER1 came back NOT CLEAN (a0_042 already promotes plain jet run, and the helper size claim loses to Perl) and go back to ScriptLead.

Owner ruling 2026-11-08 (Q24 A): one registry. Every CLI command flag row gets a key <command>.<flag>, readable from package.jet settings and the user settings file; precedence flag, then package, then user (the JET_BUILD_OPTIONS mechanism). Destructive flags are marked not persistable and setting one is refused with a registered diagnostic. ScriptLead builds it.

Census (c1 first half), Main 2026-11-07, dev eb47eb7277 on seed a0_034. Method: jet help for all 49 commands and every action of the group commands (117 help pages), parsing each flag a usage line or flag row lists. A flag counts as homed when its long name is a JET_BUILD_OPTIONS row (Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/BuildOptions.jet, 7 rows) and its command reads that table (build, run, dev). Result: 429 command-flag rows over 76 commands and actions. 21 are homed: build, run and dev each have 7 (backtrace, bounds, inline, libs, optimize, os, small). The other 408 rows (157 distinct flags) have none. The most common homeless flags are --json x52, --color x44, --quiet x44, --live x8, --verbose x7, --profile x6, --set x6, -p x6, --gate x5, --release x5, --target x5, --threads x5, --trace x5, --dry-run x5 and --allow x4. Rows per command: test 57, build 34, run 32, dev 26, inspect 26, new 17, cc 16, c++ 16, jobs 15, check 12, fmt 11, self 11, budget 9; registry has 7, including publish --force and --no-sign. Flags with a neighbouring but non-flag-keyed home (--allow/--deny to package authority, --target to package targets, --profile to build profiles) count as homeless, because none goes through one flag-to-setting mechanism. The census is regenerated on demand by $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/burn/flags/{collect.sh,census.mjs} (scratch; the porting home is the CLI registry, not a committed table). Next: the ballot on where non-build command settings live, then one shared mechanism.

criteria.text: A census lists every registered CLI flag with its setting (or none); after the ratified ballot, every flag has exactly one setting through one shared flag-to-setting mechanism, with a cases row per command family proving that flag and setting have the same effect

Authority flags (--allow, -A, --gate, --token, --allow-unofficial) have no setting: the census marks them never persisted, and a package.jet or user settings key for one is refused with a registered diagnostic (owner 2026-11-09); a cases row proves the refusal.
criteria.evidence: Lander meet-6606 on seed-b8 at dev cc09d22cb9, each line judged PASS-only with its source printed. Line 8: tests/cases/cli_settings/permission_flags_are_never_settings.case, landed in fe4c65249b (ScriptAPI-66), shows that a package.jet commands block or the user settings file naming --allow, -A, --gate, --token or --allow-unofficial is refused with the registered E2117 before the program starts. Lines 19-20: the CommandSettings.jet census tests "no flag that gives permissions is a setting" and "a remembered destructive flag is refused as its CLI snapshot records" (ScriptAPI-49/50, 5263e2258c) mark them never persisted. D-ENV-SURFACE1 was ratified A on 2026-11-11.

criteria.text: Owner 2026-11-10 ~21:00: "seems like we rely heavily on env vars ... other languages just use build settings and build flags, not a ton of hidden envvars ... yes we need to fix that". Main's census on dev c2cecce162: code reads about 140 JET_/JETPACK_ variables (193 names in all), and Docs/spec/reference/environment.md, which calls itself the registry, lists 66 plus 3 wildcard families; 113 read names are on no list. One registry in code holds every environment variable that jet, jetpack, the runtime, Core or a repository tool reads. Each row gives the name, the owning module, its kind (user, automation, maintainer, transport between Jet processes, or test hook), its value type and default, and the flag or setting it overrides. A guard refuses a read of a name that has no row, across Compiler, Core, Jetpack and Tools. environment.md is generated from the registry, with a --check that the lane checks run. Zero unregistered reads.

Every user, automation or maintainer behavior control is a CLI flag or a settings key first, and its environment variable only overrides that setting, through the shared flag-to-setting mechanism of c1. The controls include keep-going and its report and skip lists, trace file and trace detail, the optimizer dump, disable, verify and SSA-stress hooks, the GC trace, phase counters and the memory ledger. AGENTS.md, the skills and the repository tools use the flag, not the variable. A cases row per family proves the flag, the setting and the variable have the same effect. The flag and setting spellings are ratified on the D-ENV-SURFACE1 ballot first (owner gate).

Transport between Jet-owned processes goes through one channel: argv, or one handoff file or descriptor that the parent passes to the child. It does not go through a separate environment name per value. The JET_FRONT_*, JET_DEVELOPMENT_RECEIPT_*, JET_DEVTOOLS_RELAY_*, JET_PROVE_*, JET_EVIDENCE_*, JET_TEST_SUITE_ROOT, JET_TEST_PLAN, JET_TEST_SETTINGS and JET_READ_SCOPE families are cut over in one greenfield cutover, with no old names kept. A launched user program inherits no Jet transport variable it does not own (a run case proves its environment).

One command prints every registered variable that is set, with its effective value, where that value came from (environment, setting, flag or default) and secret values redacted, in text and --json, with UI snapshots. It works like `go env`. Its spelling, and whether it is a new verb or part of an existing one (jet doctor, jet env), is ratified on the D-ENV-SURFACE1 ballot first (owner gate).

The D-ENV-SURFACE1 ballot is written and validated (Tools/agent/ballots/Validate.jet). It shows same-program alternatives for the c4 flag and setting spellings and for the c6 listing command, with beginner and expert paths, a comparison with Go (go env, go env -w), Cargo (config.toml mirrors CARGO_*), Zig and Python (-X flags), and an adversarial review of the recommended option. The owner ratifies it before c4 and c6 are built.
criteria.evidence: Meet g5a (Lander5 meetrun, 2026-11-12 03:19-03:3x) on dev 50a2cbc7e6 with seed-b11 jet@a0.0.45#3667b9a1 (built at 19333b2bb3); every line rc 0 with a judged PASS and zero FAIL/KF/UNEXPECTED-PASS/SKIP/ERROR/TIMEOUT. jet Tools/agent/ballots/Validate.jet --update on the board payload of D-ENV-SURFACE1 (ratified A, 2026-11-11; dumped from master board rev 99863) gives ok, rc 0. The payload carries the same-program alternatives, the beginner and expert paths, the go env / Cargo / Zig / Python -X comparisons and the adversarial review. Out: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Lander/loop/out/meet-g5a/3.out.

criteria.text: D-ENV-SURFACE1=A is built (owner ratified 2026-11-11): every hidden environment control becomes a normal concise flag and its existing command-qualified setting (for example `jet check --trace=trace.json` and `commands: { "check.trace": "trace.json" }` in package.jet or the user settings file, the file spelling ratified by D-CLI-SETTINGS-HOME1=A). `jet env vars [--command=C] [--json]` lists each control's effective value and its source (flag, setting or default) without launching anything. It extends the existing env group and adds no environment manager. Every in-repository caller of a retired variable migrates in one cutover, with no aliases. CLI #Tests prove the listing and each source.
criteria.evidence: 40e26406fc: jet test Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/CLIControls.jet -> 11 passed 0 failed; jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter cli_settings -> 44 PASS 0 FAIL (dev 98469bf0cf, seed-b14); jet test Compiler/JetCli/Tests/Controls.jet -> 144 passed 0 failed on a17e4f4491 + G5DevX2-fmt-manifest (landed 40e26406fc; the one earlier failure was a stale fmt-lossless pin for tests/ui/take_pattern_bad_hole.jet, refused by design since caf92fe112) (Lander holdsweep $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Lander/holds/14-6606-c8.out)

cards.title: Test suites run in seconds: fix the slow programs, the timeouts and the per-program cost
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-11-06: suites should finish in seconds or minutes, not take a long time; the golden suite once took about 15 minutes at most.

Measured on vb5 (dev 7f0b3d03ed, s1, 32 cores):
- golden: 4766 rows, about 4 minutes wall, median 0.28 s per row. The 4655 rows under 5 s alone sum to 74 CPU minutes, so per-program cost sets a floor of about 2.3 minutes even with perfect parallelism.
- cases: 4501 rows, about 13.5 minutes wall, median 0.10 s; 284 rows of 5 s or more account for 97 of 131 CPU minutes; 12 rows hit the 60 s wall-clock limit.
- ui: 2412 rows, about 1 minute wall.

Slowest golden programs (all tiers): concurrency/job_queue 248 s, foundations/storage 177 s, foundations/text 161 s, crypto/file_seal_jetc 153 s, game/raylib_indexed 148 s, foundations/realtime 100 s.
Timeouts: cffi/concurrent_bridges_share_one_target_publish_without_racing, cffi/ffi_capability_boundary_is_safe_only_inside_unsafe, ffi_rust/rust_extern_std_round_trip_uses_the_canonical_descriptor, fixtures_crypto_bridge_entropy/jetc_v2_record_boundaries_are_canonical, fmt_project/top_level_jet_fmt_delegates_non_jet_file_to_realized_formatter, jetpack_nix_index/index_backed_nixpkgs_repairs_only_missing_transitive_object, jetpack_nix_index/static_publication_resolves_signed_index_and_nix_objects, jetpack_tool/use_ephemeral_execs_inside_and_outside_project_without_path_projection, repl/repl_tty_prompts_and_reuses_exact_session_tuple, ui_fixes/ownership_ui_fixes_compile_ffi_companions, unsafe_and_runtime/ffi_capability_edge_uses_shared_sentry_prelude, web_dev/embedded_devserver_rejects_hardlinked_source.

For every slow row, first record where the time goes (compile front end, Core/Prelude re-check, code generation per tier, link, the program's own run, or a fixed sleep or timeout in the test), then fix that root. Never raise a limit, drop a tier or move a row out of the default profile to make a number.

log.text: Moved from G1 to G5 by owner ruling 2026-11-07. a0_033 release kit timings (parallel, under load): golden 1479 programs, median 528 ms, 420 at 5 s or more, rows sum 5037 s; cases 4637, median 156 ms, 524 at 5 s or more, sum 8201 s; ui 2252, median 66 ms, 9 at 5 s or more, sum 939 s. c4's shared per-run Core check is compiler work, the same as #6623 and #6647.

c4 progress: MechD-3's 59d955887b (store capacity checks replay a footprint tally instead of scanning every entry) cut golden wall from 1086 s to 118.7 s on fab74a230c s1, all rows passing (4318 PASS, 0 FAIL). The per-program median is 348 ms over 3 tiers, about 0.12 s per tier, against the 0.1 s target. About 90% of each tier is re-checking Core identically for every program; caching checked Core by content key is the remaining c4 lever, and df runs about 6 times per build. c5 still needs a run on the batch machine (118.7 s against the 90 s target).

criteria.text: Each of the six slow golden programs (concurrency/job_queue, foundations/storage, foundations/text, crypto/file_seal_jetc, game/raylib_indexed, foundations/realtime, or their successors after the Examples cutover) runs in under 5 s per tier on the batch machine, with the root cause of its old time recorded on this card.
The 12 cases rows that hit the 60 s wall-clock limit on vb5 are root-caused and each passes, or fails for a recorded unrelated reason, in under 10 s.
criteria.evidence: 85dea10ff4 (TestSystemLead-2). The 12 vb5 60 s rows, rerun at HEAD (release jetpack aaa6331fc067, cargo and bwrap on PATH). cards.title: Passing a read parameter to a method's owning argument copies silently, while a plain call reports E0201
cards.body:
Found by SyntaxOwner during the #6586 sweep (2026-11-06, dev 529e9d9ddd). With a read parameter `item: [Int]`, `rows.push(item)` is accepted silently: the list is copied into the owning argument. Passing the same value to a plain function whose parameter owns it, `keep(bag)`, reports E0201 MissingMoveMarker. One meaning must have one mechanism (I8): an owning argument position needs the same move or copy rule whether it belongs to a method call or a plain call, and sema decides it (I3).

Settled by the owner ruling of 2026-11-06 (A, calls never copy; card log): method owning arguments are take parameters, so a read parameter or a later-used name gives E0201/E0209 unless written .copy(). The cutover is the sema rule plus a collect-all codemod inserting .copy(), in one commit.

log.text: Both criteria are met.

Follow-up on c78da98b1b: the a0_030 candidate also rejects Core sites that the compiler build never reaches (Core/App/App.jet:307,310,312; Core/Web/Storage/Local.jet:22 and Session.jet:22; Core/Web/Browser.jet:1428), which broke 4 golden examples at o0-o2.  only reaches Core bodies a program calls (an import-everything probe, even with JET_DEBUG_LOWER_ALL=1, reports nothing), so no tool today can census a sema rule change across all of Core. Main is sweeping every Examples/ and tests/run program with the candidate s2 and lands one batch fix.

Owner ruling 2026-11-06: A, calls never copy. Method owning arguments (push/add/extend…) are take parameters like keep(item): a read parameter or later-used name gives E0201/E0209 unless written .copy(). This follows D-CALLSITE-MARK2=A ('a call never copies on its own'). Cutover: the sema rule plus a collect-all codemod inserting .copy() (>=958 sites at census), in one commit. [item] and Box{items: item} are not covered by this ruling.

cards.title: Tool symbol paths use `.`, not `::`: inspect, find, semindex, docs and the impact selector
cards.body:
Owner 2026-11-06 chose A: with `::` gone from source (D-DECL-COLON1=A, #6586), tool symbol paths switch from `module::name` to `.`, matching source qualification such as `alias.Type.method`. This changes the public JSON and text output of jet inspect, jet find, the semantic index and jet docs, and the user-typed selector of `jet inspect impact <file> <symbol>`. Greenfield cutover: no `::` reader stays behind.

Sites found by the syntax owner at c92bf872eb:
- User-typed: the jet inspect impact selector (Inspect.jet:1580).
- User-visible JSON or text: semindex identity, summary and call_path keys (SemIndexBuild.jet 149/1481/1526/1530/2151, Sema SemanticIndex.jet:422, InspectOutput.jet:32; the case semindex_projects_omitted_inferred_effects expects `inferred_effect_signature::announce`); inspect rights keys (InspectRights.jet 142/168/173); inspect shapes (InspectShapes.jet:422); find (Find.jet:308); docs `parent::name` (Docs.jet:279); codemod and try identities (Codemod.jet:1371, Try.jet:242).
- Internal parsing: ArchitectureAdvice.jet:47, Fill.jet:80, SemIndexBuild.jet:1797, and the ComptimeIR.jet:103 and Pipeline.jet:2712 cache keys.
- Real Rust paths in RustForeign.jet:210-232 are foreign syntax and stay.

Module paths contain dots (`core.process`), so a tool must know where the module path ends. The tools have the module graph, so a reader resolves the longest prefix that names a module, and the rest is the member path. Writers emit the same form.

log.text: Owner ruling 2026-11-06 (chat, second cut questions): c1 stands as written: every `::` in Compiler/ goes, internal keys included (~3,800 sites), not just the tool-visible paths.

criteria.text: Every tool output and selector listed in the body writes and reads symbol paths with `.` (for example `inferred_effect_signature.announce`), with no `::` writer, reader or fallback left except real Rust paths in RustForeign.jet; a repo search for `::` in Compiler/ outside Rust-foreign code and dated docs finds none.

Readers split a dotted path at the longest prefix that names a module in the program's module graph; a case proves `jet inspect impact <file> core.process.spawn`-style selectors and an ambiguous or unknown prefix gives a registered diagnostic with a UI snapshot.

The affected cases, snapshots and goldens (semindex_projects_omitted_inferred_effects and every inspect, find, docs, codemod and try row that names a symbol) are updated in the same commit and pass on the default tier; the spec text that documents these outputs shows the `.` form.

cards.title: Every effect is allowed by default; code denies, and a run warns when its effects change
cards.body: Owner ruling 2026-11-06 (chat): 'I think by default, we should consider all effects allowed. Packages, functions, types, etc can deny them. When a script or program is first run it warns about the effects that are used unless using the -A flag.' Approved with Main's four refinements: (1) the notice repeats whenever the program's effect set changes, not only on the first run; (2) a written authority row is a ceiling and silences the notice for what it lists; (3) jetpack records each dependency's effect row and reports widening, and --locked refuses it; (4) code run straight from a URL or the registry asks before its first run. Decision D-AUTH-DEFAULT1. This supersedes the prompt model of D-AUTH-AMBIENT1, D-AUTH-AMBIENT3 and D-SCRIPT-CONFIRM1 (spec.md 'Application authority'). Greenfield cutover: the prompt path, its diagnostics and every caller migrate in one change.

Its separate TTY prompt (once/session/deny) and the piped E1803 are removed in the same cutover. EffectsLead builds it with the c2 docs.

Ballot D-JET-RUN-REMOTE1 posted for the owner (Q25a B): the command that runs code straight from a URL or the registry and asks before its first run. Options A jet run <https-url|name#ver|name> (recommended), B a jet x verb, C jet fetch then run the stored path. c8 applies to the ratified form.

Owner rulings 2026-11-08 (Q25). a: B, ballot a command that runs URL or registry code (jet run <url> or pkg@ver) now; c8 applies to it. b: A, --allow=R acknowledges R (left out of the notice) and resource-qualified rows still confine through Landlock. c: A, the ambient floor (IO, Mem.Alloc, Exec.Args) stays inside every written ceiling and leaves only through an explicit deny. FYI items (jet new writes no authority row; scripts lose the #! -A rule; the notice omits floor effects) stand, no objection.

cards.title: D-HOST-LEAF1=E: the runtime is an ordinary library that Core uses
cards.body: Owner ratified D-HOST-LEAF1 option E on 2026-11-06. jet_runtime becomes an ordinary library: Core and any package write use rt: jet.runtime.time and call rt.sleep_ns(duration.ns). No marker, no symbol string, no hand-written manifest. Internals stay hidden by pub. Amended by the adversarial review (Docs/audits/2026-11-06-d-host-leaf1-option-e-review.md): a declared effect row on a pub runtime function introduces its effects, and the interface is generated from source with the runtime pack. This card builds the runtime side. The #6151 criteria (c4-c41) and #6111 c1/c2 that waited on the host-leaf ballot are unblocked by E and stay on their cards: they remove Core's privileges, which E's ordinary-library model makes possible.

log.text: Main decisions 2026-11-11 (TlsLead-3's open items): (1) the row_splits rows in RuntimeEffectRows (jet_time_raw_wall_sample via ssl_time, jet_random_os_entropy, jet_files_read_bytes_os, jet_fs_directory_open/close) stay until the owner ballot on whether a protocol root (Net) covers its host reads (Time, Rand, FS.Read); if it does not, the TLS entries declare the full rows in one cutover. (2) The F32 bit pair (core.math.__to_bits_f32/__from_bits_f32) has no runtime carrier: it is an IR-lowered pure intrinsic like sqrt, exempt here, pinned by a signaling-NaN round-trip case at O0/O1/O2. (3) tls.client is one declaration (tcp, server_name, config?, deadline?) -[Net, Time.Wait]> TLSStream NetError!; the host/port form and the sema arity/type dispatch are removed, and callers use tls.connect_host. (4) The 402 E3203 NonCAbiType errors come from seeds that predate the carrier commits (1e02b82ef1, 3bf0e43440, 8ff2c54775). No gate depends on them; the chain's last SUB checks the runtime binding package on the first batch compiler after it lands.

Ballot candidate (owner choice, not built): TLS certificate-validity checks read the wall clock (ssl_time via tls.__host_wall_sample). Today Net covers that read by a deliberate rule (Core/Net/SSL/Defs.jet:1501). Surfacing it as Time would add Time to about 60 SSL functions, the 10 Net callback fn types (Defs.jet:1054-1125), every Tls.jet engine fn and the public tls client/read/write/ready, http client/serve and ws upgrade rows (TlsLead3 cascade census, 2026-11-11). For #6615 the runtime binding declares Net under that rule, as an explicit exception row in RuntimeEffectRows. The open UI case: paint_state through a backend trait method needs Browser on the web backend only (effect-polymorphic trait methods); it keeps its route until decided.

Ballot NEW-D-HOST-CAP1 withdrawn 2026-11-11 after an adversarial rewrite (owner order: confusing or parallel ballots are redone, and questions an existing mechanism answers are decided rather than balloted). Decided: Preserve the existing UI needs contract in the checked runtime interface and propagate it through resolved calls; generate vocabulary from UICapability, not deleted call rows. It extends: origin/dev:Core/Ui/Host.jet:22-30 is the UI capability vocabulary. origin/dev:Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/CoreUsage.jet:445-480 checks declared needs; origin/dev:Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Loader.jet:256-260 currently derives valid names from Core call rows. D-HOST-LEAF1=E requires ordinary runtime library declarations and their checked interface. The full record is $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/ballots-v4/NEW-D-HOST-CAP1/verdict.md. Withdrawal decides the direction; it does not mean the build is done.

t22 landed (dev 5dc51a93f5): TlsLead-6615s4be (47d0ff8ba6, the text-cell and ETF-string decode scopes on jet.runtime.encoding) and TlsLead-6615s4bl (b48dfee798, core.log on jet.runtime.log, 15 bound leaves deleted). This is slice S4b of c5. CoreSourceRows and RuntimeEffectRows --check pass (0 differences), with no new case or core failures. c5 stays open for the remaining rows (c5a is staged).

t21 landed on dev 4a9268e62c (83b33f14dc..4a9268e62c): TlsLead-6615s3a/s3afix (jet.runtime.time binds all 13 raw time exports core.time calls, identity-keyed, so a user lookalike stays a C import with E3101/E3203/E1341), s4ar/s4arfix (48 handle-free term/log/encoding/process leaves bound with Option-of-tuple and tuple-of-Option carriers; the unchecked string_byte/bytes_into_text and coerce_now/coerce_emit stay Core-only behind E0510 until S7), s4bp (the dead core.process __signal_* leaves, records, dispatcher rows and IRRoute rows deleted, so jet.runtime.process is the only path) and s4bpfix (the unknown_module snapshot lists the 5 runtime modules). RuntimeEffectRows joins 59/59. Every test line passes after a clean census. c4 and c5 stay open: TlsLead3 census finds most S5-S8 leaves need Result/struct carriers (S11, go) or a Core-only visibility (ballot facts pending if no ordinary mechanism fits).

t19 landed TlsLead-6615c4 (0efcf91a49..97462b6d92), the c4 mechanism. A jet.runtime call lowers to the runtime export its interface row names at O0/O1/O2 and in a built binary, and Tools/agent/RuntimeEffectRows.jet --check (in VerifyFull) joins each interface function to its Core leaf by name with 0 differences. c4 stays open until every runtime function Core calls is bound this way (S3 onward).

Main ruling 2026-11-10 on S3, the time cutover (TlsLead3). Under D1 (the carrier projection ABI), each jet.runtime.<module> member is a body-less binding onto the runtime export that holds its one body. The binding is generated from the runtime export rows (the c3 interface), never hand-written, and lowered through a route derived from its Jet signature, so the hand IRRoute rows go. Sema admits carrier types (Option, tuple, List) only for bindings of the generated interface, keyed on its identity, not on a module name; a user `jet.runtime.*` module gets the ordinary C-law errors. The raw exports stay as each function's one far-side body, so they are not a twin, and c8 deletes the dispatcher rows and the compiler twin, not these exports.

Main rulings on the c3-c5 slice plan (TlsLead3, 16 slices, written up in its lane as 6615-plan.md). D1: a jet.runtime call uses the carrier projection of its Jet signature, computed on both sides from the one signature; no exported internal ABI. D2: `jet.runtime.<module>` is the spelling these criteria already name. `jet` is a compiler-provided namespace beside `core` and holds only `runtime`, with no other members. D3: c5 lands one module at a time (S3-S14). A module moves whole, with no dual path inside it, and its dispatcher rows, CoreCallRows, IRRoute rows and RuntimeStopExports go in the same SUB. c5 is met only when the last module lands and a census shows 0 dispatcher_row lines. Finding: c38-c40 on #6151 (core.build) are compiler comptime, not runtime, so jet.runtime does not unblock them.

t15a landed G6LeadC-11 (01b86931e7..8327f5ae47): c6 clause 2 (an ungated #Import(c) of a runtime export is E3101, UI snapshot runtime_import_needs_unsafe; a gated one works) and c7's interim clause (architecture.md limits the one-runtime claim to O0/O1/O2 and names the web tier's JavaScript runtime functions). c6 stays open for clause 1, and c7 for the web runtime itself.

Defect found by TestSystemLead-2 at 56e30acfcf: an #Import(c) call to the runtime symbol jet_rt_process_exit lowers into jet_rt_unreachable. The program prints 'internal error: entered unreachable code:' and exits 101 whatever code it passed. Repro: a 10-line program that imports raw_exit: fn(code: I64) = "jet_rt_process_exit" and calls it. Sites hit: Compiler Host.jet:1563 jet_cli_defect_exit, the JetTestKit fixture compiler.jet, and Compiler/JetTestKit/Assets/no_nix.jet. It belongs to c6 (reaching a runtime C symbol through #Import(c)): the imported call must exit with its argument and print nothing.

criteria.evidence: Landed on dev 97462b6d92 (train t19, 0efcf91a49..97462b6d92), SUB TlsLead-6615c3 + TlsLead-6615c3fix. The pack build's interface check fails on disagreement, and no hand-written copy exists. c3fix keys kept `jet run` records of the supplied interface sources by SHA-256, so program reuse holds (case run_rerun_reuses_the_kept_program_of_a_jet_runtime_import).

criteria.text: Every runtime function Core calls is a pub function of jet_runtime with a Jet name, Jet types (Int, not I64; typed handles) and a declared effect row. A generated comparison over every bound function proves each declared row equals the effect_kind and effect_leaf the compiler row held before the cutover, with zero differences.

Core reaches the runtime only through ordinary use of jet.runtime modules. The dispatcher_row lines in Compiler/Prelude/Core.jet, the bound CoreCallRows, the IRRoute carrier rows for those functions and their RuntimeStopExports entries are deleted, and every in-repository caller is migrated in one cutover. Goldens prove o0, o1 and o2 for one call in each Core module that called the runtime.

A safe package that names a runtime function that isn't pub fails with the ordinary visibility diagnostic, and reaching a runtime C symbol needs #Import(c) inside #Unsafe. Proof: a UI snapshot for each.

The web tier provides no runtime function as a JavaScript reimplementation: it runs jet_runtime compiled for the web, or its JavaScript host only marshals values into the same runtime code (I9). Until then, no public text says every tier runs one runtime.

Authority bypass found by TlsLead3, 2026-11-11: core.ui.host.clipboard clear and is_empty reach the host clipboard without the UI.Clipboard capability check (E2937). Both now refuse without `UI.Clipboard` in authority.needs, each with a UI snapshot, and a sweep confirms that every host-reaching core.ui.host* function carries its capability.

Every capability-only Core dispatcher row (Compiler/Prelude/Core.jet .with_ui_capabilities, 18 rows on dev 2dff7789f5 per TlsLead3's count: font shaping, ui.host open_file/save_file/shortcut/accessibility, clipboard x4, IME and drag-drop polls, shortcuts binding/register/dispatch/poll, accessibility attach/project, and others) and the internal CoreCallRecord.ui_capabilities field are the one remaining compiler-owned twin after c5 (Main, 2026-11-11, option A: kept as the capability carrier with vocabulary generated from UICapability, preserving every current requirement). They're deleted once a Core declaration can carry a UI capability itself. That needs a declaration-level spelling that no registered marker or effect row provides today (UI.* are not effect roots), which is new syntax and goes to a ballot only if the owner wants the twin gone. From the adversarial review of D-NET-HOSTREADS1 (sol-reviewer, 2026-11-11). If file-free sandboxed or embedded TLS is required, a scoped design proves separate precise entry paths or a complete provider API and lifetime design. A configuration value alone does not remove the conservative effects.

cards.title: Verify batches see self-compile miscompiles before a release does
cards.body: a0_030 (e32b979063) failed its release gate on an I2 regression that only the release's s2/s3 show: an ICE exits 1 instead of 101. Root (CoreCliLead): b4e29635ce made the runtime map a user program's process.exit(101) to status 1 (101 is reserved for ICEs). The compiler exits through the same Core call, so a jet linked with a pack built from post-b4e2 runtime source (s2/s3 link pack1) loses its 101. s1 links the seed's (a0_029) pack and still exits 101. Main's vb batches build and test s1 only, so every runtime change reaches the compiler's own behaviour unseen until the release run (33 minutes here). Fix the batch so a cheap probe runs on every batch: a jet linked with the batch's own runtime pack, on the rows most exposed to runtime changes in the compiler (ICE exit codes, process exit codes). Don't add a full s2 suite to each batch.

log.text: 2026-11-06 a0_030 retry on 2edea7b26a: census-snap preflight passed (rc=0) but the chain's s2 stopped with 19 jet.MissingMoveMarker errors in Core/Http, Core/Net/Tls and Core/Web. The rule came from c78da98b1b (#6611, calls never copy); the preflight and LaneCheck both check with the a0_029 seed, which lacks that rule, so a sema change that tightens Core is invisible until s2. Gap: the preflight needs a candidate pass (build s1, then a keep-going s1 check of Compiler, Core and Jetpack) before a release launches.

criteria.text: `jet Tools/agent/Land.jet batch` builds an s2 from the batch s1 (or uses one at the same commit) and runs the backend_ice cases plus a process-exit-code golden against it, failing the batch on any row that differs from s1.
A Land.jet batch on a commit carrying a known self-compile difference (the a0_030 ICE exit) reports it as a batch failure naming the s1/s2 split.

cards.title: Every --json command prints its machine envelope with the right exit status
cards.body: tests/cases/machine_output/every_json_report_door_uses_the_one_machine_envelope.case fails under a0_029 and every candidate since (vb8 on 690b182cb3, the e32b979063 release candidate) and has no known-failing line. TestSystemLead-2 ran each command by hand on s1 of dev 3e1b28f646 plus 976542d4b9: `jet build run.jet --json` (step build-effects) exits 0 with empty stdout and stderr where the case expects one {"action":"build.effects",...} status object; `jet budget check --json` exits 2 where the case expects 0; `jet inspect live 0 --json` exits 2 where it expects 1; hangar-generations exits 2 where it expects 0. Those three print a JSON report. perf-view and perf-export are unjudged. The other 31 commands are correct.

criteria.text: jet build FILE --json prints exactly one build.effects status object in the machine envelope
criteria.evidence: meet-G5a on dev c886c5e718 with seed-b9 (jet@a0.0.45), 2026-11-11 23:0x: jet test Compiler --profile cases tests/cases/machine_output/every_json_report_door_uses_the_one_machine_envelope.case: PASS 1, FAIL/KF/UP/SKIP-HOST/REFUSED/ERROR/TIMEOUT 0. Its build-effects step asserts exactly one status record, action build.effects, exit 0, empty stderr. A one-file jet build main.jet --json also printed exactly one line with action build.effects and ok true, rc 0.

criteria.text: jet budget check --json, jet inspect live N --json and hangar-generations --json exit with the status the case names, or the case is corrected with the reason the status is right
criteria.evidence: meet-G5a on dev c886c5e718 with seed-b9 (jet@a0.0.45), 2026-11-11 23:0x: same case, PASS 1 and every other count 0. jet budget check --json exits 0; the inspect step is jet inspect structure --live 1 --json, exit 1, with the case comment naming the E2105 refusal envelope; hangar generations --json exits 2, with the comment that Hangar is Jetpack's, so it is the E2101 unknown-command envelope.
