(was #3033) [#3032] A direct source without authentication needs interactive approval before the first artifact GET; `-y` and `--trust` cannot grant it. A grant binds source, metadata authority, repo, resolver, selector, asset policy, target, platform, proof floor and ordered HTTPS origins, and excludes mutable version, tag, digest and URL. A later candidate in an unchanged scope needs no new prompt. A new origin stops before the request. Any scope change invalidates the grant. Known pins check identity, grant and origins before the GET and the SHA-256 after it. Same identity with different bytes fails and preserves the working pin and generation. Release trust never authorizes builds, execution or elevation. Proof: `--area Trust --tests` CHECK OK with the ReleaseTrust claims. (was #4275 c135)

cards.title: Scripting speed and startup: beat Lua, LuaJIT, Python, Node, Bun, Deno and Perl
cards.body: Owner order 2026-11-06: Jet scripts beat every scripting language on run speed and startup.

log.text: HELD by owner order 2026-11-11 (no small optimizations until the language is mostly stable; architecture and regression fixes go first, per #5479 c5-c8). c6/c7 census by ScriptAPI (lanes/ScriptAPI/probe/g11-census.md, t22 lines): six cross-run compile caches are all on today. A1 is jet run's kept programs, A2 the jet build executable restore, A3 BuildExecutor action reuse, A4 the C dependency archives, A5 the C provisioning record and A6 the Rust FFI bridge. Two result caches go off too: B1, jet test result reuse (its --fresh flag is removed), and F3, Admit's suite and census caches. Main's ruling: every one is off by default, and its reuse code is unreachable until a ballot ratifies an opt-in spelling. The in-process memos C1/C2 stay on. ScriptAPI-22 builds it, and TierParity and scriptbench migrate in the same patch.

criteria.text: A matched script cell family (hello, a 50-line text-processing script, a JSON transform, a directory walk, a subprocess pipeline) runs `jet run` against Lua 5.4, LuaJIT, Python 3, Node, Bun, Deno and Perl, measuring exec-to-exit wall time, cycles and peak RSS, Jet compile included, cold and warm reported separately.
End metric: Jet wins every cell and metric against every peer (Jet/peer below 1.00), cold and warm; every loss names its root on a card.

(moved from #5072 c41 by the owner instruction of 2026-11-10 ~16:10) Peak memory: a small Jet tool's peak RSS is no higher than its original's on every PortBars entry. ScriptAPI-2 measured Jet at about 19-21 MB against bash's 7-12 MB on batch10, integrate10, streamb10 and verify-rows, and the cost is the runtime's baseline, not the twins. The fix goes in the general mechanism (runtime start-up, reserved heap or arena sizing, and eagerly mapped tables), and is proven on a second small program. PortBars shows peak memory PASS on all nine. Part 1 (ScriptAPI-3, image layout locality and the build key; it rides t16) took the warm small-script peak from 15.5 MB to 7.1-7.5 MB, and batch10, integrate10 and streamb10 still lose (11.8 against 10.6 MB, 12.9 against 8.6, 10.6 against 8.6), while verify-rows ties.

An uncached `jet file.jet` (a fresh cache dir: compile from cold, link and run from memory) beats python3 and node on wall time and peak memory, with no script cache, result cache or incremental state serving the run. Measured 2026-11-11 with GNU time on hello world (seed-t21): uncached `jet hello.jet` takes 30 ms and 36-40 MB, a script-cache hit 20-30 ms and 8.7-10.7 MB, the built O1 binary 0 ms and 256 KB, python3 10 ms and 13.1 MB, node 20 ms and 60 MB. Name where the uncached 30 ms and 37 MB go (front end, sema, lowering, emission, link, runtime start), fix them in those general mechanisms toward the 30M lines/s compile target, and prove it on hello world and on a repository tool twin.

Owner order 2026-11-11: the script cache is off by default. `jet file.jet` and `jet run` compile live every time, and no kept program, result cache or incremental state serves a run unless the user opts in. ScriptCache.jet's default flips. The opt-in spelling goes on a ballot (a flag or an environment variable) and nothing else changes until it is ratified. CLI #Tests prove a second run of unchanged sources compiles again by default (no read or write under the scripts dir). Every in-repository caller, doc and test that assumed a cache hit is migrated in the same patch.

Owner order 2026-11-11: build-action reuse (BuildExecutor's restored actions) and every other compile cache are off by default, so `jet build` and `jet test` compile live. Each cache that stays reachable only through an explicit opt-in has its spelling balloted. PortBars and the perf gates measure Jet with every cache off, and their receipts say so. A census lists every compile cache in Compiler, Jetpack and Tools with its default, and each one is off.
criteria.evidence: 6a80caeed7 (ScriptAPI-22c): the unreached native runtime cache and pack store are deleted with their tests and manifest rows; named proof lines pass on seed-t25a.

criteria.text: Child-process-bound workloads (found 2026-11-11 by G1Lead4's runtime-allocator twin: wall 0.92 inconclusive and peak memory 1.03 against node, with the same child processes run in sequence on both sides). Jet's spawn, wait and pipe path and its script start cost no more wall time or peak memory than node's child_process.spawnSync. A paired gauntlet cell that spawns 200 short children in sequence shows Jet below node and python on wall time and peak memory, live and uncached, and a second program that pipes a child's output proves the gain. This is a general runtime fix (process spawn, the runtime baseline), with nothing in the twin.

cards.title: Reasoning about code: Jet beats every language on how well readers and tools can reason about a program
cards.body: Owner order 2026-11-06: beat all other languages on the ability to reason about code.

criteria.text: A reasoning benchmark defines task families (predict the output, find every effect of a call, show two values never alias, find every caller, find what a change breaks, find where a failure can come from) over matched programs in Jet, Rust, Go, Python, TypeScript, Zig and C++.
Each task is scored for readers (human or model: accuracy and time) and for tools (what `jet inspect` and the language server answer mechanically versus each peer toolchain).
End metric: Jet scores best on every task family; every loss names its root on a card.

cards.title: Concision and builtins: the shortest correct code for common tasks
cards.body: Owner order 2026-11-06: lean toward less code for an equivalent task, with builtins good enough that common scripts are very short.

criteria.text: A matched task corpus of at least 50 common scripting, data, CLI and service tasks has idiomatic solutions in Jet, Python, Ruby, Lua, Go, Rust, TypeScript and Kotlin, measured in tokens and lines.
End metric: Jet is shortest or tied on every task family without giving up safety, diagnostics or clarity; every loss names the missing builtin or convenience on a card.

criteria.text: Every technique an asm-parity reference uses that Jet code cannot express (SIMD lanes, prefetch, alignment and layout control, branch and cold hints, non-temporal stores, syscall batching and others) is listed with the cells that use it.

Each missing technique gets an owner ballot with its plain and expert spellings (expert control by explicit opt-in) and a paired two-program cell; it ratifies only when it strictly beats the plain form.
End metric: every required cell can be written in Jet with its ceiling's technique, and codegen emits that technique.

cards.title: Transpile Jet to other languages through target libraries that implement one trait (C and Rust first-party, any language by a package)
cards.body:
Owner request 2026-11-07, re-scoped the same day: Jet transpiles a program to another language, and any language can be added as an ordinary Jet library implementing a target trait. Seeding and bootstrapping the compiler are a separate, frozen question on #6683; this card comes first.

Why: interop (Jet code inside C, Rust, Lua or JavaScript projects), reach (platforms with no Jet native writer), and the language-is-a-library priority.

Design: ballot D-EXPORT-TARGET1. The recommended shape: one shared pass makes every meaning explicit, and core.compiler exposes a versioned program view. A Target trait has required operation methods, host leaves and optional idiom hooks. Capabilities are checked first, and `jet test --to <target>` checks every executable example against `jet run`.

log.text: Ballot D-EXPORT-TARGET1 posted and ready. The fresh adversarial review (PortsLead-2, against dev 964e737fcc) broke the first draft's recommendation. Today's IR still leaves exact-Int spill, trap and stop meaning to each writer (X64Select.jet, Web/Select.jet). The runtime's platform layer is 75 #FFI(asm) leaves plus 383 raw x86-64 syscall sites. Comptime and the only native writer are x86-64, so a C seed cannot rebuild itself elsewhere. --target already means a platform. Recommended now: staged A, with a Wasm seed from the existing web writer (C syscall host, evaluator comptime), then a shared pass that makes every check explicit plus jet build --emit c, then third-party emit libraries once the form is declared stable. If ratified, the criteria follow the ruling.

Ballot D-EXPORT-TARGET1 drafted (owner request: challenge, refine, improve). Options: A target libraries over the compiler's final lowered form, with C and WebAssembly first and a C seed every release (recommended); B readable source-level transpilers per language; C WebAssembly seed only (Zig's approach); D prebuilt binaries only. It passes Tools/agent/ballots/Validate.jet except the review pass. Tower needs the adversarial review even for a draft, so the fresh review (PortsLead-2) is in progress, and the ballot is posted once its findings are folded in.

criteria.text: An adversarial design review in Docs/audits tests every claimed strength of the ratified D-EXPORT-TARGET1 design (library-defined targets for any language, one meaning across targets, readable output through idiom hooks, interop) against Haxe with Reflaxe, Fable, Kotlin's shared IR, Nim, Gleam and LLVM targets. Every gap it finds is on a card or ballot.

A ratified Tower ballot fixes the command's name and flags, the target-library API (what a target receives from the checked program and how it emits text), and the first-party targets, with same-program alternatives and beginner and expert paths.
criteria.evidence: D-EXPORT-TARGET1 ratified A (2026-11-07): one public core.compiler.target Target trait over the explicit program, with required op methods, host leaves and optional idiom hooks; capability errors before output; jet build --to <target>; jet test --to conformance; C and Rust first-party.

criteria.text: A target is an ordinary Jet library that any package can write, using only public compiler-library seams. A third-party test target built outside the repository exports a program as well as a first-party one does.

Exporting a program to C and building it with a stock C compiler gives the same stdout, stderr and exit code as jet run at O0, O1 and O2 for every executable example, with memory safety, fault reports and error behavior unchanged.

The 11-07 census found non-Jet scripts that no open card owns. cards.title: Test results are reused across runs: the full profile and the admit skip rows whose compiler and inputs are unchanged
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-11-07: card this; no cached or incremental work now.

Measured: a fresh-clone `jet test Compiler --profile full` took about 2 hours (engine 4 min, cold toolchain fetch 45 min, suites 64 min). The release admit then reruns every suite for the same commit, about 40 more minutes. Corpus rows total 248 CPU minutes (golden 160, cases 79, ui 9).

cards.title: The compiler's default thread count is fixed at start from the instantaneous load, so a build started on a busy host runs on one core
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-11-07: card this; do not build now.

`jet_cli_default_threads` (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Request.jet) reads procs_running from /proc/stat once at start and drops to one thread when the host is busy. The thread count then never grows. In the full profile, the hosted Jetpack engine build started beside four package runs took about 13 minutes on one core; it took 184 s when it started on a quiet host.

criteria.text: A build's parallel width follows free cores while it runs, instead of being fixed by the load at start.
The hosted Jetpack engine build started beside 8 concurrent package runs finishes within 1.5x of its quiet-host wall time, measured on the batch machine and recorded with the commit.
The quiet-host self-build wall time does not regress (compared on the same machine and commit range as #6527).

cards.title: core.crypto SHA-256 runs at 45-50 MB/s; a scalar native implementation does about 500 MB/s and SHA-NI about 2 GB/s
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-11-07: card this; do not build now.

Measured on #6592: pure-Jet core.crypto SHA-256 runs at about 45-50 MB/s at O1 and O2, and a hand-unrolled Jet version gives the same speed. The backend has no SHA-NI path. Toolchain install hashes about 450 MB, so hashing alone costs about 9 s per pass on one thread.

log.text: HELD by owner order 2026-11-11 (no small optimizations until the language is mostly stable; architecture and regression fixes go first, per #5479 c5-c8). These criteria stay open and unworked: c1 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c); c2 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c); c3 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c); c4 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c).

Measured on #6592 (PortsLead-2, 2026-11-07): pure-Jet core.crypto SHA-256 at 45-50 MB/s at O1 and O2; a hand-unrolled Jet version is no faster. Parallel hashing of the 442 MB toolchain tree still takes 16.6 s, the largest remaining fetch phase after fsync.

criteria.text: An asm-parity cell under Tools/perf/asm-parity is the SHA-256 ceiling reference: SHA-NI where the CPU reports it, and the best scalar code otherwise.
core.crypto SHA-256 at O1 and O2 meets that ceiling (Jet/ceiling at most 1.00 in cycles and bytes) on both paths, and beats every gauntlet peer.
The digest is identical on every tier (O0, O1, O2 and web), held by the existing SHA-256 conformance vectors.

Core crypto expert hashes (#3548): [#3870] SHA-512, BLAKE2b and Argon2id in Core/crypto/expert.jet run on U64 words, with no bigint spill and no per-block list allocation. Hash goldens are unchanged, with a perf receipt for password_hash. (was #3548 c13)

cards.title: Compiler/build.jet declares the whole project: every artifact, generated table, toolchain, chain stage and profile is one build graph
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-11-07: make full use of Jet's customizable build function for this project; card it, do not build it now.

Today Compiler/build.jet declares one target, the jet executable. Everything else is assembled outside the build graph, each piece in its own serial step: the self-host chain (Tools/agent/chain/chain.sh), the runtime pack (cc-pack and pack, with musl found through JET_PACK_MUSL_LIB), the Jetpack engine (Jetpack/Bootstrap/Assemble.jet, then a separate jet build inside the packages suite: 3 min quiet, 13 min under load), the generated registry tables (regenerated by hand and checked at precommit; a stale CoreEnumRows failed a landing on 2026-11-07), and the test and release tools.

The Build API already offers add_executable, add_library, add_test, add_package, add_publish, add_install, add_doc, action, generate, toolchain, probe, signing and embed, the registered build options, and core.build graph receipts with receipt_diff.

log.text: SpeedLead: build.jet cannot list a folder at plan time (b.find returns files only, walks into .jet, and is not recorded as a plan input; #4833 known-failing). So c6 keeps STAGE_FOLDERS and STAGE_FILES as a kernel.tsv row, plus a tests/guards check that every top-level entry of a split stage package (except Generated and dot entries) is listed, so the list cannot go stale silently. The .jet/deps alias hole touches 5 to 6 files in two packages and is now its own criterion; c6 does not depend on it.

c6 layout ruling (Main): the build-graph contract stays. SpeedLead moves the 4 kept generated sources into <pkg>/Generated/ (JetFoundation PreludeMarkers, JetSema PreludeDerives and PreludeUnits, JetLexer KeywordSpans). Stages read those packages top-level entries minus Generated/, derived at plan time, not a hand list, plus the kept files through .reads. The rejected alternative (narrow folders plus about 105 explicit files) would be a stale-prone closed list. Owner Q20 is withdrawn. Validator defect found by SpeedLead: both validators compare spelled folder paths, so a dependency bound at .jet/deps on the same real folder escapes the rule. It is fixed in the same patch by comparing resolved folders, with a #Test.

c6 blocker (SpeedLead): the self-host stages read the 17 Compiler folders whole, and the build-graph rule (Graph.jet:109-121, Jetpack Validation.jet:173-177, spec.md:5050, E3502) refuses step outputs inside them: the runtime step outputs under JetCli/.jet/build, and the c5 kept outputs (Prelude copies, KeywordSpans.jet). Main ruling: an output under a .jet or .git part being outside the folder read is a defect fix (one meaning with the folder snapshot, Cache.jet build_folder_skipped). SpeedLead lands it with a BuildGraphRules #Test. Allowing an output inside a read folder when the reader also reads it changes the spec contract, so it is owner Q20. SpeedLead is costing the keep-the-rule alternative.

It is the owner (A) stopgap shape (host cc plus musl), removed under #6687. On master as merge cb5a55054d, the exact tested dev tree. criteria.text: One build function declares jet, the runtime pack, jetpack, the docs site and the release package as targets, so `jet build` builds them concurrently from one graph and the packages suite reuses that jetpack instead of building its own.

Every generated registry table (CoreEnumRows, CoreStructureRows and the rest) comes from `b.generate` over its source registry, so it cannot be stale, and the precommit generator checks for those tables are deleted.

The self-host stages and the s2 == s3 byte-identical check are build actions in Compiler/build.jet, each run from cold, and Tools/agent/Chain.jet is deleted with every caller migrated. Proof: `jet build Compiler` runs the stages and the s2 == s3 check, and `git ls-files Tools/agent/Chain.jet` is empty.

Each compiler package (JetFoundation, JetLexer, JetParser, JetSema, JetIR, JetBackend, JetCli and the rest) is its own library target, and independent packages compile in parallel within one cold build. Depends on #6623. Proof: the `jet build Compiler` graph receipt shows the package targets overlapping in time.
Build profiles give a fast `dev` profile for targeted testing and a `ship` profile for release stages.

Every build records a core.build graph receipt with per-target wall time; receipt_diff between two commits shows the per-target time change, and the per-phase timeline for #6610 is read from it. Proof: `jet build Compiler` writes the receipt and receipt_diff of two commits' receipts lists every target with both times.

The step-output-in-read-folder rule (Graph.jet and Jetpack Validation.jet, spec.md:5050, E3502) compares resolved real folders, not spelled paths. A dependency bound at .jet/deps (or any other alias) that resolves to a folder holding a step output is refused. The project root and each dependency root are threaded into both validators and resolved through the host. A BuildGraphRules #Test covers the alias case.

[#2526] Scheduling is deterministic: identical start logs across runs of a 40-node graph, and stable diagnostics under randomized delays. Only the ratified pools exist (cpu, memory, linker, console, gpu), with a RAM-derived cpu cap. Ready nodes are ordered by longest remaining path, then by key. A failure cancels only its dependents, and keep-going continues the rest. (moved from #2514 c10)

[#2527] A TTY board of at most 8 lines redraws in place, with one final receipt line. cards.title: Portable seed: build a working Jet on a machine that has only a C compiler or a WebAssembly runtime
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-11-07: seeding and bootstrapping the compiler is a separate question from transpilation (#6675, D-EXPORT-TARGET1) and is frozen for the future. Transpilation comes first.

Goal: a machine with no Jet binary builds a current Jet from what it already has, so a seed never goes stale and a new platform is never stuck.

Candidate plan from the earlier D-EXPORT-TARGET1 draft, which is not ratified: compile the compiler with the existing WebAssembly writer, then turn that .wasm into C with a committed WebAssembly-to-C translator. A small C host answers the runtime's system calls on POSIX, and compile-time code runs on the IR evaluator instead of an x86-64 child. Every release checks that the seed rebuilds the release's own stage-2 bytes. Once the #6675 C target exists, exporting the compiler to C is the alternative route. Trust limit: a seed built from generated output still trusts the compiler that wrote it; only an independent Jet implementation removes that.

criteria.text: An adversarial design review in Docs/audits tests the seed's claims (durability, onboarding, trust) against existing bootstrap chains: Zig's WebAssembly seed, Nim's generated C, mrustc, and bootstrappable builds. Every gap it finds is on a card or ballot.
A ratified Tower ballot picks the seed route (WebAssembly translated to C, the #6675 C target, or prebuilt binaries only), with same-program alternatives and the trust limits stated.

Exporting the compiler's own source to C (and to Wasm) gives a compiler that, built with only a C compiler (or a Wasm runtime), compiles the same tree to a byte-identical stage-2 compiler: a portable seed for every release, linked with #6186.
Install docs describe building Jet from the exported seed with a stock C compiler, and a fresh machine with no Jet binary follows them to a working jet.

cards.title: The hosted Jetpack engine takes about 3 minutes to build on a quiet host while the whole compiler self-compiles in about 10 s
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-11-07: Pareto speed work for the fresh-clone full profile.

The packages suite builds the hosted Jetpack engine (Jetpack/Bootstrap/Assemble.jet hosted, then `jet build src/jetpack.jet`, in Compiler/test.jet jetpack_prepare). It took 184 s when it started on a quiet host and about 13 minutes on one core under load. The compiler, a larger codebase, self-compiles in about 10 s (#6527). The ratio points at something specific to the Jetpack build path (the assembled single unit, its optimization level, a pathological function, or a phase that grows superlinearly), not at code size.

log.text: Main 2026-11-07: SpeedLead landed 3412bcf62f (jet build cache entries, locks, leases and touches publish unsynced; reads verify digests, so a lost entry is a miss; the rlib cache, runtime pack, objects and LTO keep their syncs). The store publish tail went from 127.3 s/17.0 s to 8.4 s/5.0 s (fresh store, interleaved), with zero fsync calls during the build (strace). It also landed ef8a3f930d (L0534 copied the 12.5 MB engine module once per block: sema.finalize 149 s -> 5.8 s; sema.bodies 97 s -> 2.7 s; tests/ui_lint/map_group_round_trip.jet still prints L0534 at 10:9). Whole hosted engine build: 168 s -> 33.0 s at load 14 (28.6 s on a rerun); a cache hit takes 16.9 s. Proof by Main is pending (batch).

criteria.text: A per-phase profile of the hosted engine build (front end, sema, lowering, optimization, emission, link) names where the time goes, and it is recorded on this card with the commit.
criteria.evidence: Per-phase traces (jet build --trace; wall s / CPU s; 12 CPUs pinned on the busy 32-CPU host) of jet build src/jetpack.jet in the assembled hosted project (618 sources; one 12.5 MB module). dev eaa085b237: total 156.8-243.9 s wall, of which sema.finalize 98-149 s (sema.bodies 48-97 s wall / 547-928 CPU-s) and the store tail 17-127 s (fsync D-state); the front end 5-7 s, lowering 0.7-1.2 s, ir.opt 2.2-3.5 s, emission 0.7-0.9 s, link 0.15 s. Root cause 1: store fsyncs, fixed by 3412bcf62f (no fsync calls in strace). Root cause 2: the L0534 lint (10ce9aab90) copied the whole module bytes per block, fixed by ef8a3f930d. With both fixes: total 32.95 s wall / 49.7 CPU-s; sema.finalize 5.81 s; store tail 11.8 s under writeback throttling; cache hit 16.9 s. The table and the exact commands are in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/SpeedLead/6684-phases.md.

criteria.text: The root cause is fixed in the compiler or in Jetpack's assembly, and the hosted engine build on a quiet batch host takes at most 30 s, measured and recorded with the commit.
The built engine is byte-for-byte the same program as before the fix, or every packages-suite engine claim still passes.

cards.title: The Jetpack engine unit's claims all run serially because they share process state
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-11-07: card the remaining slow phases.

Compiler/test.jet jetpack_engine_rows runs `jet test src/jetpack.jet --serial` over the assembled engine unit (about 559 claims), because the claims share process state. Every claim waits for the one before it.

log.text: Main 2026-11-07, from SpeedLead measurements (hosted engine unit, after #6684 fixes; host busy, load 12-40): `jet test src/jetpack.jet --serial` took 243 s (compile 55 s, claims about 188 s); without --serial 195 s, with the same 807/22/15 and the same 22 known failures. One clean parallel run is evidence that the claims share no state, not proof; dropping the flag means editing jetpack_engine_rows. Compiling the unit alone at load 7 takes 15.7 s. 715 claims take under 0.1 s each; four take 102 of 225 s: StoreIngestLate.jet:42 "store closure readers are serialized with registration and compaction" 57.8 s, StoreIngestLate.jet:31 18.0 s, Lifecycle.jet:302 14.9 s, NixCache.jet:784 11.5 s. strace of the 57.8 s claim shows it is CPU-bound in the store, with no child processes and temp files on tmpfs: every closure-graph load re-verifies every record (producer and metadata decode, receipt rehash, seal checks), and 70 ingest+load pairs make that quadratic. Under 1 minute needs incremental verification in the store (a trust-design change), plus parallel claims. Ruled out: per-test module-scope copies in sema (5.7 s sema.bodies at low load).

criteria.text: The wall time of the engine unit's compile and its serial claim run are measured on the batch host and recorded with the commit.
Claims that share process state are isolated (each owns its state, or the shared state is per-claim), so the unit runs without --serial and every claim still passes.
The engine unit's claims finish in under 1 minute wall.

cards.title: Jet depends on no other language: port every C dependency (musl, libgcc, SQLite, mbedtls) to Jet
cards.body:
Owner order 2026-11-08: "We need to fix the issue blocking build.jet but also need to remove the C dependencies. Start by directly porting the functions being used but we also need full coverage of the libraries that are dependencies. Ensure all are tracked."

Census (Main, dev 9b21994eb3, seed a0_038): jet_runtime_jet.o has 55 undefined symbols, 54 from musl (33 math, 6 pthread, 4 DNS, 11 process, terminal and filesystem calls) plus jet_rt_fault_report. The source has 72 #Import(c) or #FFI(c) sites outside tests, fixtures, binders and examples: JetRuntime CompilerNeededMath.jet 29, RouteSys.jet 8, Thread.jet 6, HostNetResolver.jet 4, RouteTerm.jet 2, and TextFmt, Sync, ProcessSignal, NetRoutes and HostSpawn 1 each; JetDevserver WatchService.jet 7 and WebHost02.jet 4; JetCli Host.jet 2; JetTestKit RequireTool.jet and Assets/no_nix.jet 1 each; Tools/ci/CompiledWorkloadPeerLauncher.jet 1; and Tools/agent-eval/ffi-assurance 2 (a C-interop proof, which stays). The runtime pack links musl libc.a, libgcc.a and libgcc_eh.a (jet-runtime/foreign/platform). Vendored C: Core/Vendor/Sqlite3 (core.db) and Core/Vendor/Mbedtls (core.net TLS), together about 474k lines of C and headers. The clang C toolchain pack serves only users' C interop and `jet cc`, a feature that stays.

Order: first port the functions Jet uses today (math, threads, syscall wrappers, DNS, the compiler's and tools' own C imports), so the runtime pack drops musl and libgcc. Then port the vendored libraries in full: mbedtls, then SQLite. Each library port covers the whole library that the dependency provided, not only today's call sites. #6682 c4's fresh-clone C compiler requirement disappears once the runtime pack and every artifact jet build Compiler makes contain no C.

log.text: Every criterion met: no C dependency remains (musl, libgcc, SQLite and mbedtls are ported).
Reopened by the G1/G8 fresh-context closeout review (Review1); see the reopened criteria.

OWNER 2026-11-09 12:19: G1 is due by 16:00 today. G1 removes the C dependencies only. The full SQLite and mbedtls libraries move to G3 (#3550 and #6748 got the criteria), and #6693's size and startup measurement moves to G11 (#6736).
Owner refinement 2026-11-09: G4 and G8, and possibly G6, can run in parallel with each other. G1 keeps first claim on slots until it is finished.

Owner ruling 2026-11-09: goal order. Finish G1 first, then G4 (Best scripting language), then G8 (Effects on types), then G6 (Declarations as types and metaprogramming). The JetDevserver port (#5931, G5) is to be finished, not deleted, but not before these.

Audit 2026-11-09 (CFreeLead3, dev d4d45ded4b): what still links or calls C = (1) jet and jetpack through mbedtls (#6694); (2) the pack's vendored sqlite3 and mbedtls built with host cc/ar (#6694/#6695); (3) host nm in the pack build; (4) any program whose import graph reaches core.db or core.net.tls links musl, startup and pthreads even when it never calls C (ForeignDeps collects every checked module's providers). 21 of 25 gauntlet cells start at __jet_start with no musl.
Correction: #6735 folded into #6700 (G3); the debugger defects fold into #6730 (G5).

Owner ruling 2026-11-09: G1's No-C work only moves what Jet depends on from C libraries into native Jet so C leaves the dependencies; speed and size work (while speed is reasonable) belongs to G11 and building out full C-equivalent libraries to G3. New cards: #6735 (G3 math), #6736 (G11 speed), #6737 (G3 DTLS); #6700 moved to G3.

Agents follow best practices and idiomatic Jet, using Jet API-building features (typed records with defaults, traits and derives, typed config, Result errors), in the shape of existing Core modules. Other owner gates (syntax, commands, dependencies, invariant exceptions, scope) stay.
Owner Q8 ruling 2026-11-08: bwrap ships in the C toolchain pack as a stopgap; its removal (a Jet sandbox) is tracked on #6697, longer term.

Owner 2026-11-08: track full libc coverage too ("We should already have a lot of what libc covers just need to fill the gaps"), filed as #6696. Owner approved spawning leads for mbedtls (#6694) and SQLite (#6695).

Which artifacts need which C (SpeedLead, nm on the c4-built jet and on seed a0_038): jet links mbedtls (T mbedtls_ssl_setup, T jet_tls_new) through JetCli core.http.client (BuildHTTPTransport.jet, the HTTPS build fetch) and core.http.server tls (BuildWeb.jet), both reaching Core/Net/Tls.jet #Import c.mbedtls. jet links no sqlite (no sqlite3_* symbol, no core.db reached). jetpack links mbedtls and no sqlite. The runtime pack ships both foreign archives, which a user program links only when it reaches c.mbedtls or c.sqlite3 (ForeignLink.jet jet_cli_vendored_c_archive). So after #6693, mbedtls (#6694) is the only C that jet itself needs; SQLite (#6695) is needed only so the pack can serve user programs that use core.db. The fresh-clone criterion therefore needs #6693 and #6694 for jet, and #6695 for the pack.

cards.title: No C: port the mbedtls that Core uses to Jet (the pinned TLS 1.2 and 1.3 set, X.509, PSA crypto)
cards.body:
Owner order 2026-11-08: "We need to fix the issue blocking build.jet but also need to remove the C dependencies. Start by directly porting the functions being used but we also need full coverage of the libraries that are dependencies. Ensure all are tracked."

Core/Net/Tls.jet uses c.mbedtls (Core/Vendor/Mbedtls, 272 C and header files). Port the whole library the vendored configuration builds: TLS 1.2 and 1.3 client and server, X.509 parsing and verification, and every cipher, hash, MAC, KDF, key exchange and signature it provides (AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305, SHA-1 and SHA-2, HMAC, HKDF, ECDHE on X25519 and the NIST curves, ECDSA, RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 and PSS). Constant-time code is required where mbedtls is constant-time. Security closure (Docs/spec/contributing/security-closure.md) applies.

log.text: Every criterion met; the last proof was ctfix-d a800437c58 on batch compiler b3.
Reopened by the G1/G8 fresh-context closeout review (Review1); see the reopened criteria.

t17a landed TlsLead-72 (e75850d064..c2cecce162): B5 part 1, the timing admission (jet_rt_timing_admit before entry, refusal with the reason on unconfirmed hosts), __timing_host, E0744 jet.FixedTimingUnconfirmedTarget and the inspect plan row. c10 closes with TlsLead-72b (core.sys.timing_host() and the c10 proof) on t18b, built on integ/seed-t17a.

t16a landed TlsLead-68 and 69 (+69fix) (D-SECRET-CT1 B2b/B2c), TlsLead-70 (B3: the IR fixed bit and the timing.fixed lint after every pass) and TlsLead-71 (B4: the final-instruction validator for x86-64 DOIT and wasm32 CT-Wasm tables) (8327f5ae47..e75850d064). c10 stays open for B5: TlsLead-72 rides t17, and 72b follows the reseed.

D-SECRET-CT1 B5 is split in two. TlsLead-72 (B5a, t17) adds the policy.harden host admission (jet_rt_timing_admit), the __timing_host row and runtime probe, E0744 jet.FixedTimingUnconfirmedTarget for a hardened web or wasm32 build, and the inspect `timing host:` row, which shows the program`s admission plan. TlsLead-72b (after a reseed that carries 72) adds core.sys.timing_host() and TimingHost, plus the c10 closing proof. Decision (Main, recorded as fact): `jet inspect` shows no verdict for the build host, because the compiler calling the new export would need one more reseed. The host`s verdict comes from the one runtime probe at start-up. The c10(a) case constant_time_primitives_emit_no_secret_branch_or_index passes 1/1 on the 72 compiler.

t15a landed TlsLead-66r + 66rfix (D-SECRET-CT1 B1: the timing:/protects: tag fields and E0737, E0738, E0739) and TlsLead-67 + 67fix (B2a: total branches on timing: .Fixed values are masked; the total-method set is read from BUILTIN_METHOD_ROWS) (01b86931e7..8327f5ae47). c10 stays open: B2b/B2c (68), 69, B3 (70) and B4 (71) ride t16, and B5 (72, then 72b after a reseed) follows.

t14a landed TlsLead-65 (53805444ba..01b86931e7): the c10a emission case parses private keys, and their secret flows are fixed. c10 stays open for D-SECRET-CT1 B1-B5 (66r, 67, 68 and 69 ride t15 and t16).

t12c landed (4a5c0ec793..aaca1c8db2 (dev 00a2b37a42)): TlsLead-59r (c4 I-4b error-exit wipes), 60r (c10(a) emission coverage for RSA-PSS and core.crypto, c4 dudect rows), 62r (c10 TLS 1.2 RSA premaster under the emission case, c4 dudect rows). c4 waits for TlsLead-63 (t13a); c10 waits for part (b), D-SECRET-CT1.

c4 review half: the confirmation pass at dev c460ba91e5 (Docs/audits/2026-11-10-core-tls-crypto-security-rereview.md, "Confirmation 2026-11-10") closes F-ZERO-2 and I-3, and finds no new finding in TlsLead-51. One Info residual stays open, I-4b: in ECDSA.jet sign_core, four auto-propagated errors (derive_mpi, gen_privkey for k and t, ecp_mul) skip sign_failed, leaving the private-key limbs dl and work unwiped. TlsLead fixes it as TlsLead-59. c4 is met once that lands and the dudect coverage of every secret-dependent primitive is confirmed.

c4 re-review done (SecReview2, security-reviewer, read-only, on dev 76955986d0); the audit is committed on master as Docs/audits/2026-11-10-core-tls-crypto-security-rereview.md (db09b00e4f). F-ZERO-1, F-CT-1, F-TLS13-1, I-1, I-2 and the c14 dudect gaps are fixed; the c16 CBC/Lucky13 fix is correct. There is one new finding, F-ZERO-2 (Low): the DRBG seed is never wiped. It is c17, assigned to TlsLead3. Info residuals I-3 to I-6 do not block. c4 stays open until F-ZERO-2 lands and a reviewer confirms it.

c4 re-review done (SecReview2, security-reviewer, read-only, on dev 76955986d0); the audit is committed on master as Docs/audits/2026-11-10-core-tls-crypto-security-rereview.md. F-ZERO-1, F-CT-1, F-TLS13-1, I-1, I-2 and the c14 dudect gaps are fixed; the c16 CBC/Lucky13 fix is correct. There is one new finding, F-ZERO-2 (Low): the DRBG seed is never wiped. It is a new criterion, assigned to TlsLead3. Info residuals I-3 to I-6 (the unwiped gcd_modinv_odd copy, the early returns in sign_core that skip the wipe, the soak depth, and the record layer being outside the emission check) do not block. c4 stays open until F-ZERO-2 lands and the reviewer confirms it.

TlsLead-45 (audit finding I-1, the verified peer identity) and TlsLead-46 (c10(a) emission coverage: bitsliced AES, portable GHASH, HKDF, the TLS 1.3 key schedule) landed in ecf04d985a..76955986d0. TlsLead-50 (c16, the Lucky13 fixes: MAC length bound from public pre-padding length, ct_hmac wipes; dudect bad-pad |t| 1.38-1.75, negative control 8.57) landed too; c16 is met together with c15 (record layer in the emission check).
c11: TlsLead-41 (the close and release wipe) landed in ecf04d985a. It is met once TlsLead-41b (the failed-handshake release and its loopback #Test, in train 6) lands too.

c10 part (a) is done. TlsLead-36 (the emission-log check aid) and TlsLead-37 landed in 973d760c89. The case core_net_tls/constant_time_primitives_emit_no_secret_branch_or_index builds every secret-dependent primitive at O0, O1 and O2 and passes. Part (b) waits on D-SECRET-CT1, so c10 stays open.

c4 security review done (SecReview, a read-only security-reviewer). Verdict: fails, with F-ZERO-1 Medium, F-CT-1 Low, F-TLS13-1 Low and I-1, I-2 Info, and the dudect coverage gaps. Each finding is a new criterion on this card. c4 is met when they are all met and a fresh review records no open finding. Audit: Docs/audits/2026-11-09-core-tls-crypto-security-review.md (master c17bd85280). TlsLead owns the fixes.

Decision (Main, 2026-11-09) c10(a) ECP jac_add_mixed: the infinity cases use constant-time masks; the R==+-T doubling branch keeps one declassify line whose reason is the comb invariant (odd digits keep R off +-T for every valid scalar, so the branch outcome is fixed by construction), cited by file and line, with a case that runs random scalars and asserts the branch is never taken. Any caller where the invariant does not hold gets a fully constant-time addition (always-double-and-select or a complete formula, whichever is cheaper).

Decision (Main, 2026-11-09) for c10(a), reading the criterion as secret-dependent timing. (1) A stop branch (overflow, bounds, shift count, narrowing, tag drop) passes when its condition is public and is marked as a stop in the encoder log; it fails when its condition depends on a secret, and the fix is wrapping or explicit-width arithmetic at those Core/Crypto sites. (2) Leaks that mbedtls legacy Mpi accepts are removed where that is cheap: the private exponent is processed over the full modulus length with a fixed window. A declassify line in the check's spec is allowed only where the value carries no secret (an operand blinded by a fresh random, citing the blinding site), or once at key load for key checks that cannot run on public parts, each line stating its reason. Parity with mbedtls alone is never a reason.

Decision (Main, 2026-11-09) for c10(a): the emitted-code check is a post-optimizer IR taint pass joined with an emission log recorded at the x64 encoder, which tags every Jcc, Jmp, call and memory operand it writes with the IR instruction being lowered, at O0, O1 and O2. It does not use a hand-kept table of the branches instruction selection adds (that would describe the selector, not the emitted code), and it needs no x86 decoder. Inline asm in a secret function is refused and reported, never skipped. The JET_OPT_DUMP extension and the encoder log are separate SUBs; both variables are registered in the environment reference.

Decision (Main, 2026-11-09): c4 security review. security-closure.md governs Codex Security scan requests, and this card makes none, so c4 does not need an external scan. The review is a dated audit in Docs/audits by a fresh security reviewer that is not the author lane, covering every file on Core TLS and crypto path after TlsLead-30r2, 32, 33 and 34 land: secret-dependent timing (dudect and constant-flow results), memory safety of the parsers, handshake state machine, certificate validation, key and nonce handling and error paths. c4 is met when that audit records no open finding, or every finding is fixed and re-checked in the same audit.

OWNER 2026-11-09 ~12:40: Core's TLS is pinned to the modern set. TLS 1.3: AES-128/256-GCM and ChaCha20-Poly1305. TLS 1.2: ECDHE-ECDSA/RSA with AES-GCM and ChaCha20-Poly1305. Groups: x25519, P-256 and P-384. Signatures: ECDSA P-256/384, RSA-PSS and PKCS#1 with SHA-256/384/512. CBC, CCM, ARIA, Camellia, DHE, PSK, brainpool, x448 and ffdhe leave Core's policy; their code stays in the engine for G3 (#6748 c3). c2-c4 cover the pinned set.

Owner rulings 2026-11-09 on licenses: (1) The Jet translation of mbedtls is a derivative of Apache-2.0 code. Keep it for now under Apache-2.0, with its headers and mbedtls's NOTICE; later the crypto and TLS get rewritten from scratch, keeping the same module boundaries, so they can be MIT. (2) Test vectors: commit only public-domain NIST CAVP vectors. Fetch Wycheproof at test time, pinned by SHA-256. No Apache-2.0 vector files go in the repository.

Batch b6d landed on dev (0073f4fc47): TlsLead-5r 6bbde9ccfc (AES in every mode, CMAC, KW/KWP, GCM, CCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305; all applicable mbedtls 3.6.7 and Wycheproof vectors pass; bitsliced AES and carry-less GHASH) and 7r 449b255bc5 (bignum, 9090/0 mbedtls vectors). c2 and c4 are partial; 9r2 to 17 are in b7.
Landed in b5: f3300b44c9 (TlsLead-6r: c1 partial, the core.crypto.Hasher stream; Jetpack StreamingSHA256 wraps it) and f9f1be3aa5 (TlsLead-8r: c4 partial, AES-NI/PCLMULQDQ leaves).

Owner rulings 2026-11-08. Q10 A: public builtin U64.mul_wide(other) -> (U64, U64), lowered to one widening multiply on every tier. Q11 B: public core.net.dtls (DTLS 1.2) over the ported engine. Q12: agree, full functional coverage; mbedtls C plumbing (PSA key store, net_sockets, timing, threading, memory_buffer_alloc, debug strings) maps onto Jet own net, files, alloc and tasks.

S1 landed b53a78981d (TlsLead; precommit passed; queued for the Main batch). One hash engine (priv hashes in Crypto.jet) for SHA-1, SHA-2, SHA-3, HMAC, HKDF and PBKDF2; old copies in Crypto.jet, Expert.jet and Service.jet deleted; public surface unchanged. Case core_crypto_api/digests_macs_and_kdfs_match_the_mbedtls_and_wycheproof_vectors_on_every_tier passes on jet run, run --release and dev with 0 failures: mbedtls shax 589, md 100, hkdf 3, pkcs5 7; wycheproof hmac_sha256 174, hkdf_sha256 86, pbkdf2 60. Pins in input/vectors/UPSTREAM.md. Cases crypto 44/0, uuid 2/0, service 75/0. Perf against mbedtls 3.6.7 (load about 30, noisy): sha256 5x faster (SHA-NI), pbkdf2 3x faster; sha1 12x, sha512 3.2x and sha3 7.5x slower, and hmac 64 B 2.1 us against 943 ns. c5 is open on those. MD5 and RIPEMD-160 move to R1 (__core_crypto_hash).

TlsLead plan accepted 2026-11-08. Scope from the vendored mbedtls 3.6.7 default config (129,589 C lines in 117 files): every hash, MAC, KDF, cipher and mode, AEAD, DRBG, constant-time bignum, 13 ECC curves, RSA, DHM, LMS, ASN.1, PEM, PK, PKCS#5/7/12, X.509 parse, verify and write, TLS 1.2 and 1.3 client and server with every key exchange and extension built, and DTLS 1.2. Slices: S1 hashes, S2 AES with every mode, S3 AEAD, S4 AES-NI and PCLMULQDQ leaves, S5 ARIA, Camellia, DES and DRBG, S6 bignum, S7 ECC, S8 RSA, DHM and LMS, S9 ASN.1, PEM and PK, S10 X.509, S11 record layer and TLS 1.3 key schedule, S12 TLS 1.3, S13 TLS 1.2, S14 tickets and DTLS, S15 the one-commit cutover. Main rulings: G-a uses private runtime leaves for the wide multiply (a public U64.mul_wide is an owner question); G-c TlsLead owns the X64 crypto forms and JetRuntime crypto leaves; O1 ports full function and maps the C plumbing onto Jet facilities (told the owner); O2 DTLS public API is an owner question; O3 vectors go in-repo with upstream pins and the Apache-2.0 license. Existing Core/Crypto is about 10x off the mbedtls throughput (ChaCha20-Poly1305 51 ms/MiB, SHA-256 18 ms/MiB scalar), so its cores move to fixed inline arrays.
Assigned 2026-11-08 by Main to TlsLead (spawned with owner approval). The brief is in the Main lane scratch, briefs/TlsLead.md.
Assigned 2026-11-08 by Main: unstaffed: needs the owner's permission for another lead.

It requires the two-line header on each: SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0, then 'Translated from Mbed TLS 3.6.7 (...)'. It requires LICENSE-mbedtls and NOTICE-mbedtls in each folder; at c057ea659d both folders have them. It also refuses a file that names mbedtls but is not on the list. jet test tests/guards gave rc 0 in t2c (SqliteLead-15r2's test line).

criteria.evidence: 5ee8aa4dc8: the committed vectors are NIST CAVP only, and Wycheproof is fetched at test time, pinned by SHA-256 and cached outside the repository. At c057ea659d, git ls-tree finds no path containing wycheproof. The Lander integrated t2c on e4096a0f3b; landed as dev e4096a0f3b..c057ea659d.

criteria.text: Found 2026-11-09 (TlsLead): Core TLS and crypto masks are branch-free today on O0 and O2 (dudect, disassembly and callgrind agree), but nothing in lowering stops an optimizer from turning a mask into a branch. (a) A case builds every secret-dependent primitive at O0, O1 and O2 and fails if its emitted code has a branch or a secret-indexed load. (b) The language gets one mechanism that makes this a compiler guarantee; its spelling and behavior are fixed by an owner ballot before it is built.
criteria.evidence: TlsLead-6694ct1-d 740d40800c, ctb-d 76515fd6d2, ctc-d 3d21f3cb5d, s2-d 9b0dd64148, s3-d 9eb08a0831, s4-d faded48ebd, s5-d 0edce592a1 (8/8 proved), ctfix-d a800437c58 (5/5 proved on b3). (a) The case constant_time_primitives_emit_no_secret_branch_or_index builds every secret-dependent primitive at O0, O1 and O2 and passes on batch compiler b3 after ctfix-d made memcmp/memcmp_partial branch-free. (b) The mechanism is the ratified D-SECRET-CT1 #Secret fixed-timing check: Core's constant-time code takes secrets as #Secret parameters, the rule is in Docs/spec/spec.md, and tests/ui/taint/fixed_timing_secret_call_result_decides_an_error_return pins it. jet check Core, --filter=core_net_tls, ConstTime.jet and RSA.jet pass.

criteria.text: (c4 review, F-ZERO-1 Medium) Core TLS frees and wipes the engine secrets: __TLSState or SSLContext gets an impl Close that calls ssl_free and wipes buffer and pending. It runs on close and on handshake failure, and the TLS 1.3 handshake is freed at handshake wrapup. A case shows the session master, traffic secrets, IVs, premaster and record buffers are zeroed after close and after a failed handshake.
criteria.evidence: Landed on dev (train t6c, ecf04d985a..76955986d0), SUB TlsLead-41b. With TlsLead-41 (ecf04d985a): the failed handshake frees the engine and wipes its buffers; the loopback #Test passes.

criteria.text: (c4 review, F-CT-1 Low) ECDSA signing restores the mbedtls 3.6 t-blinding, s = (e + r*d)*t * (k*t)^-1 mod n, so no mod_mpi or mul_mpi sees an unblinded secret (Core/Crypto/ECDSA.jet:73-101). The CAVP and Wycheproof ECDSA vectors still pass.
criteria.evidence: Landed on dev ecf04d985a (train t5b, 973d760c89..ecf04d985a), SUB TlsLead-41. criteria.text: (c4 review, F-TLS13-1 Low) The TLS 1.3 CertificateVerify algorithm must satisfy ssl_tls13_sig_alg_for_cert_verify_is_supported: RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 is refused in TLS 1.3 (RFC 8446 4.4.3). The ECDSA code point must name the key curve, and the false comment at TLS.jet:2468 is corrected. Cases cover a PKCS#1 v1.5 CertificateVerify and a curve mismatch.
criteria.evidence: Landed on dev ecf04d985a (train t5b, 973d760c89..ecf04d985a), SUB TlsLead-41. cards.title: No C: full libc coverage in Jet (census libc against Core and the runtime, then fill every gap)
cards.body: Owner, 2026-11-08: "We should already have a lot of what libc covers just need to fill the gaps." Track full coverage of what a C libc provides (POSIX and C23: memory, strings, stdio and files, time and locale, process, signals, threads and sync, networking and name resolution, math, environment, users and groups, terminal, dynamic memory), as Jet-native Core or runtime surface. Step one is a census: every libc function family, with the Core or runtime API that already covers it, and the gaps. Then each gap is filled through normal Core review (new public API needs a ballot). Math is #6688; threads, syscalls and DNS are #6689 to #6691.

log.text: Batch b6d landed on dev (0073f4fc47): the G1 math rows; CFreeLead-5r2 2f31d91386 (ctype/wctype, memset_explicit, swab, a64l/l64a; group-A NotNeeded), 6r2 9a85b9d141 (Core type-method census checks; openat/renameat/statvfs Covered; ungetc/readv/writev/pathconf Language), 4r3 cd158d6233 (runtime signal hub), 6a3 b901f3c1fd, 7a3 b286f2b414, 8a3 6ad5cee938, 9a2 4b15c1e373, 10a a33b887631 (runtime leaves; their Core surfaces follow in the b parts, in b7). c1 and c2 are still in progress.

D-MAP-WRITE1 adversarial review done (Docs/audits/2026-11-08-D-MAP-WRITE1-review.md, dev 3eed4ae28a): A holds only as a direction; its SIGBUS recovery (Fault.jet is fatal-only, one-shot), shared atomics, durability and tier meaning are unproved, so the ballot is not posted. CFreeLead redesigns to close G2-G8 for a second review. Option E (non-shrinkable backing) was added. The read-only-map defect (G1) is on its own card.

Owner 2026-11-08 ruled A on CFreeLead's c2 gap list: accept all as not needed. (1) locale: *_l variants (124,127,135), setlocale/newlocale/nl_langinfo (346-348), strfmon (167), multibyte locale encodings and legacy iconv charsets (145-148,157); Jet text is UTF-8 and locale-independent. (2) message catalogs gettext/catopen (349-350): a library concern. (3) obsolete or insecure: crypt/encrypt/setkey DES (319-320), ctermid (183), utmpx (318), gethostent/getnetent/getprotoent iteration (330), System V IPC msg/sem/shm/ftok (336-339), aio (223), posix_devctl (224), typed memory objects (230), setbuf/setvbuf (178).
Split 2026-11-08 by Main: CFreeLead owns the non-math gaps; G1Lead keeps the math rows (with #6688 c3) and LibcCensus.jet.

Owner ruling 2026-11-08 (chat, Q18): reach parity coverage. Quote: i dont need to see every api design, just use best practices, idiomatic jet with excellent api, making use of jet s api features appropriately. So the libc gap fill needs no per-API ballot: each gap gets idiomatic Jet surface designed by the lead, using Jet features (effects, Result errors, typed handles, Close) rather than C shapes. New syntax, invariant exceptions and dependencies still go to the owner.
8b040ecdba (G1Lead): the census prints on demand; Docs/audits/libc-census.md is removed, matching the reworded c1. Queued for Main batch verification.

G1Lead landed 6dedd63f5a (Tools/agent/LibcCensus.jet plus Docs/audits/libc-census.md): 261 families, 1,482 functions, every POSIX.1-2024 function once plus the C23 additions; 119 covered, 40 partial, 23 language, 79 GAP. The committed generated doc breaks AGENTS.md, and the fault is in the Main criterion. c1 is reworded, and G1Lead is removing the doc and keeping the script on demand. GAP areas: math (rint family, issignaling, Bessel, C23 pi-trig, exp10 and log2p1 family, pown and rootn family, fromfp, fmaximum family, narrowing ops, canonicalize, totalorder, payload); all of fenv; complex elementary functions plus carg and cproj; isblank, isgraph, ispunct, isxdigit, the isw forms, wctype, wctrans and the _l variants; memset_explicit, swab; a64l, l64a; fdopen, fileno, ungetc, setbuf, setvbuf, ctermid; posix_fadvise, fallocate, readv, writev, mknod, statvfs, pathconf; dup family, isatty, ttyname, aio, posix_devctl; mlock and typed memory; posix_spawnattr and sched policy; signal sets and masks, sigwait, sigqueue, sigaltstack, pthread_kill; pthread attributes, mutex and cond attributes, rwlock, spin, once, TLS keys, atfork, semaphores; atomic fences; clock_settime and CPU-time clocks; set-uid and set-gid family, the group database, utmpx, crypt; sendmsg, recvmsg, socketpair, sockatmark, netdb iteration, if_nameindex; mq, shm_open, SysV IPC; tcgetpgrp, tcsetpgrp, pty functions; setlocale, locale_t, nl_langinfo, gettext, catgets, fmtmsg. Which gaps get Jet surface is an owner question (Q18); each new public API needs a ballot.
Assigned to G1Lead 2026-11-08, after #6688 c1 and c2 land: a committed census script listing every C23 and POSIX.1-2024 function family against Jet Core or runtime coverage.

criteria.text: A committed census script (Tools/agent/LibcCensus.jet) lists every libc function family (C23 and POSIX.1-2024) with the Jet Core or runtime API that covers it, or names it as a gap, and checks that every named Jet API exists. Every gap is either filled with idiomatic Jet surface in the shape of existing Core modules, or carries an owner ruling that Jet does not need it.

cards.title: No C: a Jet Linux sandbox replaces the bwrap binary shipped in the C toolchain pack
cards.body: Owner order 2026-11-08 (Q8): "B4 BUT that is a longer term card I dont want done now. for the time being, ship bwrap until the sandbox is built PROPERLY in jet, make sure this task is not lost so we dont forget to remove bwrap in the future." Context: #6686 found no bwrap on a NixOS host, so jet cc refused with E1275. The stopgap ships bwrap (a C binary) in the C toolchain pack. This card builds the sandbox in Jet (namespaces plus landlock or seccomp, ratified D-PORTABLE1=A: Jet own sandbox) and removes bwrap. Longer term: not to start before the owner says so. Related: #6687 (Jet depends on no other language), #4268 (authority and sandbox boundaries).

criteria.text: Process isolation for jet cc and every other sandboxed launch is done by Jet code (user, mount, pid and network namespaces, landlock rules or a seccomp filter) with the same confinement bwrap gave; a case proves each refused access.
The bwrap binary is gone from the C toolchain pack and from every launch path, with no fallback; the pack is re-pinned without it.
On a host without unprivileged user namespaces, the launch refuses with a registered diagnostic (what/why/fix and a UI snapshot) naming the missing kernel feature.

cards.title: Core math completeness: correctly rounded results (CORE-MATH grade) and all of C23 math.h
cards.body: Owner 2026-11-08: "it needs to be portable and accurate. we want people to use jet for EVERYTHING including mathematics, simulations". G1Lead audit (musl 1.2.5 worst cases reproduced against MPFR 4.2.2): under 1 ulp: exp .51, exp2 .51, pow .52, log .52, log2 .55, cbrt .67, log10 .81, sin/cos .83, atan .86, log1p .90, expm1 .91, acos .93, asin .98; over 1 ulp: tan 1.01, erf 1.02, cosh 1.03, hypot 1.03, atan2 1.55, atanh 1.80, sinh 1.87, asinh 1.91, tanh 2.22, acosh 2.24, erfc 3.72, exp10 4.14, tgamma 15.9, lgamma 4.4e15 near its zeros, Bessel j0/j1/y0/y1 1e14-1e15 near zeros. Plan: port CORE-MATH (MIT) binary64 and binary32 per function family into Jet, worst gaps first (lgamma, tgamma, erfc, tanh, acosh, exp10, atan2, then the rest), each replacing its musl port in one cutover; Bessel needs its own accurate design (no correctly rounded binary64 implementation exists). Estimate about 150 agent-hours serial.
cards.checkSteps: per function: a committed MPFR-generated corpus (CORE-MATH .wc hard cases plus random inputs) shows 0 mismatches against correctly rounded bits on O0, O1, O2 and web; jet test never calls MPFR; the census marks each function CR

log.text: c1 status (G1Lead-3, 2026-11-12): F32 exhaustive scan done for 26 of 36 fns, 0 misrounded (rsqrt(-0) convention aside); sinpi 189/256 chunks clean then OOM-killed at 4G and 10G with 16 parallel pipes; not run: rest of sinpi, cospi tanpi asinpi acospi atanpi exp2m1 exp10m1 log2p1 log10p1. Harness and commands: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/G1Lead-3/HANDOFF-6700.md. Next: find the sinpi memory hold on one chunk, then rerun with -P 4 in the heavy-job slot.
G1Lead-22b2 landed on dev cb6e8c33f6: math.fma is IEEE fused on every tier, hardware FMA3 behind a CPUID probe (c3 progress).

Criteria added from the card body and the slices so far. Landed in b6d: correctly rounded sinpi/cospi/tanpi (d8db0efaec), rsqrt/exp10 and the MPFR-CR harness (f0c28ff1e6). Slices 9-15 are in batch b7. G1Lead-2 owns this card.

criteria.text: binary32: every Core F32 elementary function (exp/log/pow/trig/hyperbolic/inverse, erf/erfc, tgamma/lgamma, cbrt, hypot, the pi variants) is correctly rounded to nearest, proven by an exhaustive scan of all 2^32 inputs against MPFR (f32scan receipts).
binary64: the same functions in F64 are correctly rounded, proven against MPFR on the CORE-MATH worst-case corpus plus at least 10^8 random inputs per function, with 0 misrounded results.
criteria.evidence: dev bcc9c4b023 (CORE-MATH ports, train 1; Core/Math fn bodies identical on 6cea1699f9 except Int abs and Decimal decode, neither scanned): MPFR 4.2.2 scan, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/G1Lead-3/f32mpfr ./run64.sh over 40 F64 fns (exp..atan2pi), CORE-MATH src/binary64/<fn>.wc corpus + 10^8 seeded random inputs each -> 0 misrounded finite results. Only diffs are conventions, not roundings: rsqrt(-0) = -inf (IEEE 754-2019, CORE-MATH agree; MPFR +inf) and sNaN operands to pow/hypot give qNaN (IEEE; MPFR has no sNaN). Receipt results64/SUMMARY; handoff HANDOFF-6700.md.

criteria.text: The musl ports they replace are deleted from Core and the runtime (one mechanism), and goldens show the same bits at O0, O1, O2 and on web.

On dev 0f193199cc the four deleted runtime files are absent, no libm_<elementary> fn remains in Compiler/JetRuntime/Source or Core, and from-musl text names only the exact Libm.jet primitives and the exact Core ports, so the CORE-MATH ports are the one implementation (comptime_module_calls_match_runtime PASS 37). Inputs where musl 1.2.5 differs are listed, with documented musl bugs (such as acosh of large negative inputs returning a number instead of NaN) named. cards.title: Native windows in pure Jet: a Wayland client that opens a window and presents frames, no external libraries
cards.body: Owner 2026-11-08: "i want jet to be able to draw to screen immediately with native windows using a full jet native framework/system asap no external dependencies. start with wayland support." Today the static native runtime never opens a window (RouteAGame.jet: the old bridge dlopened libraylib) and core.ui native is headless. Plan: a Wayland client written in Jet (wire protocol over the AF_UNIX socket at $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/$WAYLAND_DISPLAY, wl_registry, wl_compositor, wl_shm with a memfd buffer passed by SCM_RIGHTS, xdg_wm_base/xdg_surface/xdg_toplevel, frame callbacks, wl_seat pointer and keyboard, the compositor keymap parsed in Jet), presenting the existing Jet software rasterizer canvas; then core.game.raylib windows and the core.ui host on top. X11 follows as a separate card.
cards.checkSteps: jet run of an example opens a native Wayland window on a stock compositor (GNOME/KDE/sway), draws animated content from the Jet rasterizer, takes keyboard and pointer input, resizes and closes cleanly; the executable links no external library (symbol census); a headless-compositor case proves it on O0, O1 and O2

log.text: t15a landed G6LeadC-13 (01b86931e7..8327f5ae47): the Wayland wire part's `net: core.net` broke every web build that imports core.ui (E3304). Fixed at the root: the target socket check judges only the program's own `use`, and ui.open reaches the wire part only under a comptime Linux branch. Proof: cases web_build 31/0, including web_ui_open_answers_no_display.

c1 scope decision (Main, 21:45 EST). The raylib census covers code, examples, tests, tools, registries, specs, guides, env and flake inputs, and gauntlet entries. It excludes Docs/audits, Docs/research and Docs/proposals (evidence and rationale), the decision IDs and ballot history in syntax-decisions.md and Tools/slate/ballots.mjs (decision history, owned by Tower), and Tools/tower/.tower. Within scope: the CLI --renderer help and Bundle.jet become headless|ui; the agent-eval area-games pkg is ported to core.ui or deleted, and its captured run records are deleted; the gauntlet game-frame author becomes the maintaining lane; the dead raylib_window.jet row leaves authority-streamline-sites.tsv; syntax-decisions prose that presents raylib as current is marked superseded by #6701.

Owner ruling 2026-11-09 (D-UI-BLEND1, ruled directly from the chat summary before a Tower ballot existed: 'use recommendation for one rule'): core.ui composites with ONE rule, sRGB-space source-over on premultiplied bytes, d = s + d*(255-sa)/255, on every surface (canvas, sprites, text, core.ui.font.blend); the linear-light path is removed. Proof: a case that asserts alpha 20 over #0B0B0D gives #1E1E20 on every surface at O0/O1/O2.
Renderer speed is tracked on child #6718 (owner: fastest renderer).

Owner 2026-11-09, after running a dev native-window demo: 'it is extremely choppy and ugly. i dont like the unrasterized text default in the pane, the header bar is way too bulky and should be dark mode by default but adapt to the user theme. those need to be fixed asap. also, I wanted the logo to work for the app that shows up in the taskbar, not in the header bar itself by default.' Measured: a headless 900x600 frame with a full gradient, ~15 shapes and ~7 text lines takes ~140 ms at O0 and ~55 ms at O2, against a 16.7 ms budget. draw_text still uses the 5x7 bitmap font. Dispatched to WaylandLead3 as top priority: rasterizer speed (a few ms per 1080p frame at O0), anti-aliased Atkinson text by default (the 5x7 font deleted), a slim header bar that is dark by default and follows the portal color-scheme and accent, the icon via xdg-toplevel-icon in the taskbar and not in the drawn frame, and a new showcase demo.

AppReview6 (sol-reviewer) reviewed D-APP1 v6 and the FFI CARRIER1/SERIAL1 v6 ballots. ENGINEERED-AWAY=no for all three, with 15 open items O1-O15: the movable Win32 pump claim is invalid (the queue belongs to the thread that created it); the C model loses its in-foreign mark after nested callbacks; IME reconciliation drops deletions; event merging loses modifiers and phases; plus web, accessibility, FFI lifetime and machine-ceiling evidence gaps. It wrote repaired v7 drafts and an audit under '$JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AppReview6/'. Not buildable yet; the next step is a BallotLead redesign, then two consecutive clean fresh reviews.

D-APP1 v6 (BallotLead-2; scratch, not posted) answers AppReview5. It merges v5 A with G's fallback: JSPI where an executed check passes, otherwise Jet continuations, chosen before any app effect. R1-R27: 20 engineered away, 4 irreducible, 3 open, and 11 rows still have open parts. ENGINEERED-AWAY=no by its own count. A fresh sol-reviewer (AppReview6) is reviewing it together with the FFI v6 ballots. Nothing is built until two fresh reviews in a row are clean.

WaylandLead has answered the FrameReview matrix item by item in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/WaylandLead/FRAME-MATRIX.md.
- Proved by headless tests: tiling and maximized looks (square, no grips or shadow); whole-pixel sizing at fractional scales 120/150/180/210/240/300; title truncation at grapheme boundaries; contrast of the default palette (title 14.53:1 focused, 5.59:1 unfocused); no animation (reduced motion holds); keyboard button targets.
- Pending the 3b wiring: xdg-decoration server-side fallback.
- Blocked: portal color-scheme, accent and contrast, and following a portal restart, because Core has no D-Bus client. Also RTL shaping, and high-contrast detection.
- Partial: touch and pen targets are 46×36, below 44×44 on width.
- Every live-desktop check is listed for an owner session.
WaylandLead-3a (the __core_ui_frame part, nothing imports it yet) is queued for b8; 3b wires it to Wayland.

Four frame ballots posted (D-FRAME-STYLE1, TITLE1, ACCENT1, THEME1), repaired by a fresh sol review: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/FrameReview/2026-11-09-frame-ballots-review.md. Each originally failed on unsupported claims; each repaired ballot holds only within stated limits, and the reviewer rated ENGINEERED-AWAY=no. They are owner-choice proposals with their costs named, not certified solutions. Repairs: Classic-only and startup-accent options added; logical Start replaces physical Left (RTL); adaptive centering is an alternative; the System frame opt-in spelling is carried in STYLE1 and is not built. Still unproved, and required as build criteria after ratification: live GNOME/KDE/Sway/tiling-WM behaviour, touch, pen and keyboard window controls, screen reader, high contrast, reduced motion, fractional scale, portal absence and portal restart, and RTL title truncation. The pictured palette is not claimed WCAG-compliant. No public spelling is built until the owner rules.

criteria.text: Safe Jet: programs using ui need no #Unsafe, and Core/Ui (the Wayland client included) contains no #Unsafe; the OS primitives it needs (AF_UNIX connect, fd passing over SCM_RIGHTS as owned typed fds, a bounds-checked shared-memory buffer unmapped on drop, poll) are safe typed Core APIs whose single vetted edge lives in the runtime (owner 2026-11-08: "i want this to work in safe jet")

One implementation (owner 2026-11-08: "keep one implementation and just have it adapt to underlying linux"): one window, frame, buffer, input, keymap (XKB), renderer and event-loop model; each display server is a thin wire adapter chosen from the environment. Full-featured on Wayland first (multiple windows, resize, HiDPI scale, pointer, keyboard with layouts and repeat, text input, clipboard, cursor shapes, decorations, fullscreen), then X11 on the same implementation

Minimal trusted base: the OS edge is about 12 generic runtime leaves (open/close, read-at, size, shared create/resize/drop, copy in/out, unix send/receive with fds, readiness); no raw pointer or raw fd number reaches Core; the Wayland client, wire parser and XKB parser are safe Jet, so a hostile compositor can cause only typed errors.
criteria.evidence: dev d9e976ffd2 (WaylandLead-1a4), integration b5: census rc=0, tests pass.

criteria.text: Ownership makes misuse unwritable: Fd and SharedMemory are owned resources closed on drop (no double close, no use after close, no fd-reuse race across threads); offsets and lengths are range-typed (Int(lo..hi)) so sema proves bounds before a leaf runs.

Linux hazards removed by design, each with a case: shared memory is sealed (F_SEAL_SHRINK|F_SEAL_GROW) so a peer cannot SIGBUS us; received fds (keymap) are read with pread, never mapped; MSG_CTRUNC closes every received fd and reports a typed error; every leaf retries EINTR and handles partial sends; every fd is O_CLOEXEC.
