decisions.title: Where should a binary recipe select its upstream release asset?
decisions.gist: Choose whether release fields sit beside the source or wrap one existing installer.
decisions.lesson: A release feed lists several assets. Jetpack must choose one target, check its origin, hash its bytes and stage its format. Direct GitHub and custom feeds use explicit source trust. Existing authenticated providers keep their current protocol. Both placements reuse one existing installer and atomic activation.
decisions.story: Maya authors desktool without a catalog. She wants an explicit update to find its latest stable release, approve its origins, install the right asset and prepare the next launch without editing a hash.
decisions.inWild: Homebrew's AnyBar cask records a cask-calculated sha256, URL and app path. GitHub release metadata supplies tags, draft/prerelease status, assets, size and a same-channel optional digest. nvfetcher keeps a source declaration and generates version/hash facts.
decisions.detail:
D-RELEASE-RECIPE1 chooses only declaration placement. Both options use the same provider, direct-source trust, checksum, staging and atomic update lifecycle. Both examples are proposed surfaces, not shipped APIs.

Current boundary

`Pkg.adapt` supports local and Git sources with `Copy`, `Prebuilt` or `Build`. Source::Releases currently stops before staging. BuildStep.fetch still requires its locked digest. This ballot adds no second fetch and does not change that operation.

The two complete examples below describe the same `desktool` archive, source target, selector, origin scope and installer. A places fields beside source. B places them inside `Recipe.release`.

Declaration contract

A accepts `resolver` and `asset` only with `Source::Releases`. Its recipe remains exactly one existing installer. B accepts the same resolver and selector plus exactly one existing installer. Nested release wrappers, release fields on another source, duplicate selector fields and a second fetch are errors.

The finite proposed family is `ReleaseResolver`, `ReleaseFeed`, `ReleaseCandidate`, `ReleaseAsset`, `ReleaseAssetSelector`, `Sha256`, `ReleaseDecodeError`, `ReleaseAssetKind`, `ReleaseFormat` and `ReleaseEntryMode`. `Release.https` takes metadata, ordered HTTPS origins and a pure decoder. `Release.github()` takes no repository argument. It derives `owner/repo` from `owner/repo@releases#selector`.

The custom decoder maps a bounded UTF-8 body into every feed field. It performs no network, file, trust or execution action. Its feed checksum is raw text. Provider validation maps valid bare or prefixed text to canonical lowercase `Sha256{hex: String}`. Empty fields, invalid times, unsafe URLs, unsupported formats and oversized data fail before acquisition.

No public direct-feed signature, key or proof field exists. Direct GitHub and custom HTTPS sources therefore use D-RELEASE-TRUST1 when no existing authenticated-provider evidence applies. A recognized existing-provider failure is hard and never becomes a source-trust prompt.



Complete option A example

```jet
// Proposed A surface, not shipped.
Pkg.adapt(
  name: "desktool",
  source: "acme/desktool@releases#latest",
  resolver: Release.https(
    metadata: "https://downloads.acme.test/desktool/releases.json",
    origins: [
      "https://downloads.acme.test",
      "https://cdn.acme.test",
      "https://mirror.acme.test"
    ],
    decode: decode_acme),
  asset: Release.asset(
    target: "linux.x64",
    name: "desktool-{version}-linux-x64.tar.gz",
    kind: ReleaseAssetKind.Archive,
    format: ReleaseFormat.TarGz,
    root: Val("desktool-{version}"),
    entry: "desktool",
    mode: ReleaseEntryMode.Executable),
  recipe: Recipe.build(steps: [
    .install(src: "asset/desktool", dest: "bin/desktool")]))

use core.encoding.json as json

enum ReleaseResolver {
    Github
    Https(String, [String], fn(String) ReleaseFeed !ReleaseDecodeError)
}

enum ReleaseAssetKind {
    Raw
    Archive
    AppBundle
}

enum ReleaseFormat {
    Raw
    Zip
    Tar
    TarGz
    TarBz2
    TarXz
}

enum ReleaseEntryMode {
    Executable
    Data
}

struct ReleaseDecodeError {
    message: String
}

struct ReleaseFeed {
    releases: [ReleaseCandidate]
}

struct ReleaseCandidate {
    version: String
    tag: String
    stable: Bool
    draft: Bool
    prerelease: Bool
    published_at: ?String
    assets: [ReleaseAsset]
}

struct Sha256 {
    hex: String
}

struct ReleaseAsset {
    name: String
    url: String
    size: Int
    channel_sha256: ?String
}

struct ReleaseAssetSelector {
    target: String
    name: String
    kind: ReleaseAssetKind
    format: ReleaseFormat
    root: ?String
    entry: String
    mode: ReleaseEntryMode
}

module Release {
    pub fn github() ReleaseResolver -> ReleaseResolver.Github
    pub fn https(
        metadata: String,
        origins: [String],
        decode: fn(String) ReleaseFeed !ReleaseDecodeError
    ) ReleaseResolver -> ReleaseResolver.Https(metadata, origins, decode)
    pub fn asset(
        target: String,
        name: String,
        kind: ReleaseAssetKind,
        format: ReleaseFormat{ReleaseFormat.Raw},
        root: ?String{None},
        entry: String{"asset"},
        mode: ReleaseEntryMode{ReleaseEntryMode.Executable}
    ) ReleaseAssetSelector -> ReleaseAssetSelector{
        target: target,
        name: name,
        kind: kind,
        format: format,
        root: root,
        entry: entry,
        mode: mode,
    }
}

struct AcmeFeed {
    items: [AcmeRelease]
}

struct AcmeRelease {
    version: String
    tag: String
    channel: String
    draft: Bool
    prerelease: Bool
    published: String
    files: [AcmeFile]
}

struct AcmeFile {
    name: String
    url: String
    bytes: Int
    sha256: ?String
}

fn decode_acme(body: String) ReleaseFeed !ReleaseDecodeError -> {
    raw :: json.decode<AcmeFeed>(body) ?? return Err(ReleaseDecodeError{
        message: "invalid Acme release feed"
    })
    releases := [ReleaseCandidate]{}
    loop row in raw.items {
        assets := [ReleaseAsset]{}
        loop file in row.files {
            assets.push(ReleaseAsset{
                name: file.name,
                url: file.url,
                size: file.bytes,
                channel_sha256: file.sha256,
            })
        }
        releases.push(ReleaseCandidate{
            version: row.version,
            tag: row.tag,
            stable: row.channel == "stable",
            draft: row.draft,
            prerelease: row.prerelease,
            published_at: Val(row.published),
            assets: assets,
        })
    }
    return Ok(ReleaseFeed{releases: releases})
}
```

```jet
struct ReleaseCandidate {

    tag: String
    stable: Bool
    draft: Bool
    prerelease: Bool
    published_at: ?String
    assets: [ReleaseAsset]
}

struct Sha256 {
    hex: String
}

struct ReleaseAsset {
    name: String
    url: String
    size: Int
    channel_sha256: ?String
}

struct ReleaseAssetSelector {
    target: String
    name: String
    kind: ReleaseAssetKind
    format: ReleaseFormat
    root: ?String
    entry: String
    mode: ReleaseEntryMode
}

module Release {
    pub fn github() ReleaseResolver -> ReleaseResolver.Github
    pub fn https(
        metadata: String,
        origins: [String],
        decode: fn(String) ReleaseFeed !ReleaseDecodeError
    ) ReleaseResolver -> ReleaseResolver.Https(metadata, origins, decode)
    pub fn asset(
        target: String,
        name: String,
        kind: ReleaseAssetKind,
        format: ReleaseFormat{ReleaseFormat.Raw},
        root: ?String{None},
        entry: String{"asset"},
        mode: ReleaseEntryMode{ReleaseEntryMode.Executable}
    ) ReleaseAssetSelector -> ReleaseAssetSelector{
        target: target,
        name: name,
        kind: kind,
        format: format,
        root: root,
        entry: entry,
        mode: mode,
    }
}

struct AcmeFeed {
    items: [AcmeRelease]
}

struct AcmeRelease {
    version: String
    tag: String
    channel: String
    draft: Bool
    prerelease: Bool
    published: String
    files: [AcmeFile]
}

struct AcmeFile {
    name: String
    url: String
    bytes: Int
    sha256: ?String
}

fn decode_acme(body: String) ReleaseFeed !ReleaseDecodeError -> {
    raw :: json.decode<AcmeFeed>(body) ?? return Err(ReleaseDecodeError{
        message: "invalid Acme release feed"
    })
    releases := [ReleaseCandidate]{}
    loop row in raw.items {
        assets := [ReleaseAsset]{}
        loop file in row.files {
            assets.push(ReleaseAsset{
                name: file.name,
                url: file.url,
                size: file.bytes,
                channel_sha256: file.sha256,
            })
        }
        releases.push(ReleaseCandidate{
            version: row.version,
            tag: row.tag,
            stable: row.channel == "stable",
            draft: row.draft,
            prerelease: row.prerelease,
            published_at: Val(row.published),
            assets: assets,
        })
    }
    return Ok(ReleaseFeed{releases: releases})
}
```

Checksum and origin rules

One provider parser handles GitHub `assets[].digest` and custom `sha256` values. `None` stays absent. Bare 64-hex text and exact `sha256:<64-hex>` text normalize to lowercase `Sha256`. Whitespace, extra text, wrong length, non-hex data and unknown algorithms fail.

A channel checksum compares with acquired bytes. It does not authenticate a publisher. The provider authorizes metadata, artifact and redirect origins before each request or follow. A new origin stops first and needs explicit approval. A source grant never retroactively blesses a request.

Origin scenario

### metadata authority

- **issuer:** `Release.https` declaration.
- **object:** `https://downloads.acme.test/desktool/releases.json`.
- **check before action:** The initial HTTPS origin must be in `origins`. Each metadata redirect is checked before its next request.
- **prompt and authority:** No artifact source grant is needed for the declared metadata request. A new redirect origin needs interactive approval before follow. The declaration and existing origin grant are the authority.

### artifact origin

- **issuer:** selected `ReleaseAsset.url`.
- **object:** `https://cdn.acme.test/desktool-1.4.0-linux-x64.tar.gz`.
- **check before action:** The candidate origin must be in the declared or granted ordered origin scope before the first artifact GET.
- **prompt and authority:** A missing source grant needs approval before this GET. A later candidate under unchanged scope needs no new source-grant prompt. The source grant is the authority.

### redirect origin

- **issuer:** HTTPS `Location` response.
- **object:** `https://unexpected.acme.test/desktool-1.4.0-linux-x64.tar.gz`.
- **check before action:** The redirect origin is checked before follow. The provider never follows first and trusts later.
- **prompt and authority:** A new redirect origin needs interactive approval before follow. The expanded ordered origin grant is the authority.


The metadata request uses the declared authority and does not fetch an artifact. The artifact request uses the selected URL after its origin check. A redirect is followed only after its origin check. A later candidate under unchanged source, selector, asset, target, platform, proof floor and origin scope needs no new source-grant prompt.

First-install and update trace

For a project package, `jetpack update --deps` resolves the project channel lock. It does not realize packages. The existing project realization path consumes that lock and runs the release provider before atomic activation.

For a user tool, `jetpack use <ref> --prep` realizes a user profile. It is independent of project cwd and project lock. The existing user-tool update path, including `jetpack update --tools`, keeps its own profile and generation. Project package locks and user tool profiles never substitute for one another.

Both paths use one explicit plan for metadata, candidate ordering, origin checks, source trust, acquisition, hashing, staging and activation. Normal launch reads the exact lock or profile and performs no moving discovery. A failed first install leaves no active entry. A failed update preserves the previous generation and running process.

Candidate and staging contract

For moving selectors, retain stable, non-draft, non-prerelease records with present RFC3339 `published_at`. Normalize to UTC and sort descending. Reject duplicate tag/version identities. Fail only when distinct eligible candidates share the maximal timestamp. Older equal timestamps do not fail. Feed order, semantic-version order and `created_at` never break ties.

An exact tag selects exactly one matching tag and may select a prerelease. `#vN.x` filters the normalized major series and uses the same ordering. GitHub and custom feeds produce the same answer from equivalent canonical records.

Raw assets require `Raw`, no root, entry `asset` and executable mode. Archives admit only finite formats, one safe root and one relative entry. App bundles use Zip, one `.app` root and one executable entry. Paths are relative and link-safe. Existing installers consume the staged tree without a second fetch.

Shared lifecycle

1. Parse and validate the proposed declaration, source target, resolver, selector and origin policy.

2. Fetch bounded metadata and check every metadata redirect before follow.

3. Decode, normalize, order and select one exact candidate.

4. Check the candidate origin before the artifact GET and check every artifact redirect before follow.

5. Apply D-RELEASE-TRUST1 when existing authenticated-provider evidence is absent.

6. Acquire bytes, compute observed SHA-256, compare channel assertions and validate staging.

7. Recheck source, grant, candidate, artifact and generation facts under the existing commit lock.

8. Publish lock or pin, receipt, Store facts, generation and active entry through the existing atomic transaction.

Any metadata, origin, trust, acquisition, extraction, install, validation, cancellation or crash failure removes private partial state. It preserves the previous complete generation and running app. Only the next launch selects the verified new entry.

Authority boundaries

### source grant

- **issuer:** user, through an interactive approval.
- **object:** `release-trust-v1` with source, authority, resolver, selector, asset policy, target, platform, proof floor and ordered HTTPS origins.
- **check:** Exact scope match before an unsigned artifact GET and before any new request or redirect follow.
- **prompt:** First direct artifact use or a new origin requires approval. Same scope and a later candidate do not.
- **authority:** Existing `AUTH_PACKAGE` scoped grant and trust ledger.
- **exclusion:** It excludes mutable version, tag, observed hash, transient URL queries, Build steps and application launch.

### channel checksum

- **issuer:** configured feed issuer.
- **object:** candidate `channel_sha256` text from GitHub `digest` or custom `sha256`.
- **check:** Parse bare 64-hex or exact `sha256:` prefix to lowercase `Sha256`; compare with acquired bytes.
- **prompt:** None. A match never creates trust.
- **authority:** Same metadata channel only.
- **exclusion:** It is not publisher authentication, a source grant, build authorization or launch permission.

### observed hash

- **issuer:** Jet provider.
- **object:** SHA-256 of the exact acquired bytes and the concrete release pin.
- **check:** Compute after GET and compare with channel assertion and any known pin.
- **prompt:** None. A mismatch is a hard error.
- **authority:** Jet's lock, receipt and Store facts.
- **exclusion:** It proves byte identity only. It does not authenticate a publisher or authorize code.

### authenticated-provider evidence

- **issuer:** an existing provider protocol.
- **object:** provider-owned authenticated status.
- **check:** Verify the existing protocol before acquisition. A recognized failure stops.
- **prompt:** No downgrade prompt. Failure never becomes source trust.
- **authority:** Existing ratified provider authority and key policy.
- **exclusion:** Direct feed fields cannot manufacture it. It does not grant builds or launches.

### build authorization

- **issuer:** existing recipe and build approval policy.
- **object:** executable Build steps and locked `.fetch(url, sha256)` inputs.
- **check:** Preserve required hashes, sandbox, permits and confined outputs.
- **prompt:** Existing build approval prompt, when that policy requires one.
- **authority:** D-JPK-BUILDRECIPE1, D-JPK-SANDBOX2 and current build trust.
- **exclusion:** Release source trust, checksums and observed hashes do not authorize builds.

### application-launch permission

- **issuer:** user/runtime policy.
- **object:** launch of the activated app entry.
- **check:** Apply the existing launch policy after activation and on next launch.
- **prompt:** Only the existing launch-policy prompt, if any. Release acquisition never supplies it.
- **authority:** Existing RuntimePolicy and active generation.
- **exclusion:** Source grants, hashes and build approval do not launch an app.


This table is the contract. A checksum or observed hash cannot replace a source grant. A source grant cannot replace build approval or application-launch permission. Existing authenticated-provider evidence is not a direct-feed wire format.

The design removes platform guessing, catalog dependence, provider-specific installers, a second downloader, unsafe redirects, inferred roots and implicit executable modes. It keeps two genuine declaration placements and one provider lifecycle. Explicit asset identity is necessary in both options. A chooses wider flat fields to avoid B's wrapper; their placement is not a safety necessity.

decisions.title: Require one typed dispatch hole and keep Boolean guards
decisions.gist: Should dispatch tables require one typed `_` hole while keeping Boolean guards?
decisions.lesson: Each arm supplies a candidate for `_`. A guard adds a true-or-false check. The first successful arm wins; `->` selects its result. Here candidates are whole numbers (`Int`), and tests produce true or false (`Bool`). A pattern checks a value shape; `.Ok(_)` ignores its carried value.
decisions.story: User is improving Jet's FizzBuzz example. He wants one shared divisibility test and a clear list of divisors. He also wants per-arm checks such as ready without nesting another if.

options.name: Require one typed hole
options.detail:
Every non-else arm fills `_`. `2 && ready` requires both checks; `2 && ready || emergency` accepts an emergency alone. `2 && (ready || emergency)` always requires the candidate test.

Group Boolean candidates: `(ready && backup)`. Arm-level `|` separates candidates, not bits. Value-returning tables normally need `else`; action-only tables may do nothing. Omitting else requires plain equality, one immutable bound subject, and complete unguarded pattern coverage.

State the shared test once. Keep Boolean guards beside each candidate. Check one input type across the table.

Old headers and independent predicate arms need migration. Boolean candidates need grouping; bitwise-OR candidates need a named value. Header calls can repeat; unneeded candidate computations can be skipped.
options.technical:
Authority and scope

The owner chose a required typed `_`, one input, ordinary && and ||, and header evaluation per attempted arm. He also chose one candidate per non-else arm and candidate evaluation only when execution reaches `_`. The complete contract still requires this ballot's ratification.

Amend D-IFDIST1, D-IF3, D-MATCHARM1/2, and S68. Preserve D-ARMHEAD-PAREN1 grouping. Do not reopen unrelated syntax or the meaning of payload wildcards.

The feature is readability-motivated. No speedup, compile-time improvement, or measured peer advantage is claimed.

Header and typing

Write `if H[_] { candidate -> body }`. H[_] denotes a header with exactly one typed hole. Filling it must produce a Bool condition. Expression candidates and pattern candidates have the separate filling rules below.

The `_` is required for dispatch tables. Ordinary `if condition` and subjectless `if { condition -> body }` remain unchanged.

Reject zero-hole distributed headers and headers with multiple expression-hole occurrences. Repeated `_` does not name the same argument twice.

The hole has one static input type for the entire table. Infer it using existing expression, call, literal, and candidate constraints. Never specialize the header independently for each arm. For a pattern candidate, this is the type of value being matched, not a value produced by that pattern.

Ambiguous types receive a normal front-end diagnostic. Resolve ambiguity by typing an existing binding or named predicate. This ballot adds no `_` annotation spelling or conversion rule.

A single input may have any ordinary value type. Existing tuple or struct values remain one input. There is no automatic splitting into multiple arguments.

The hole belongs only to its own table header. It may occur inside ordinary operators, parentheses, receivers, indexing, or call arguments. It cannot cross into a nested callable, loop body, comprehension body, or another table. Those scopes could defer or repeat evaluation of the hole. Payload wildcard `_` remains a different syntactic role.

Header names keep their outer lexical bindings. Candidate pattern names cannot capture or rewrite names inside the header.

Candidate and Boolean grammar

The first arm operand is a candidate or a parenthesized candidate-alternative group. Its static type must fit the hole, regardless of whether that type is Bool.

Comparisons or Boolean expressions used as candidates must be parenthesized. Thus `(a < b)` supplies one Bool value, rather than bypassing the header.

After the candidate test, && and || take ordinary Bool operands with normal precedence. A bare trailing number is not another implicit candidate.

For `if n < _`, `2 && ready == true` means `(n < 2) && (ready == true)`.

`2 && ready || emergency` means `((n < 2) && ready) || emergency`. An emergency may select the arm when the candidate comparison is false.

`2 && (ready || emergency)` requires `n < 2` in both cases. The formatter preserves necessary grouping.

A candidate group uses existing `|`. `(1 | 2) && ready` means `(H[1] || H[2]) && ready`. A group next to && or || requires parentheses.

An explicit parenthesized alternative group may also occur after a Boolean operator. Every member still fills the same hole; no additional input is introduced.

The group stops at its first successful candidate. If its following guard then fails, continue to the next arm, not another candidate in that group.

At candidate-group level, | means alternatives, including inside parentheses. To supply a bitwise-OR result as one candidate, compute it in an ordinary binding or nested function argument first. No type-based grammar guessing is permitted.

A whole independent predicate belongs in a subjectless table. A Bool candidate is never silently reclassified as an independent predicate.

Evaluation and errors

There are two filling rules. An expression candidate x is substituted at the hole's expression position. This is not an eager runtime function call. Substitution preserves lexical bindings and ordinary evaluation order. A pattern candidate instead becomes the pattern operand of an existing equality pattern test. Its matching rule is specified below; it is not evaluated as an expression.

For each reached candidate, evaluate its completed header as an ordinary condition. An expression candidate is evaluated at most once, only if execution reaches the hole. A pattern candidate is matched only if execution reaches its equality pattern test.

For `if ready && accepts(_)`, a false ready skips an effectful candidate expression. For `if read() % _ == 0`, each reached candidate can call read again.

No table-wide caching is implied, even for an equality header. A user-written immutable binding provides one-time evaluation.

Stop after the first true complete arm head. Skip later candidates, guards, and bodies when their result is no longer needed. This skipping is short-circuiting. Evaluate only the selected body.

Errors and failures propagate exactly as in the expanded condition. They are not false matches. Do not hide division by zero or retry an error through later arms.

Existing effect, borrowing, and ownership rules apply. Do not add implicit cloning, copying, or deferred effects to make an otherwise-invalid repeated use compile.

Patterns, ranges, and bindings

A structural or range pattern may fill a hole that is an entire operand of an ordinary equality pattern test. `if result == _` and `if _ == result` are examples.

An enclosing Boolean expression retains ordinary pattern-test rules. Arithmetic and call input positions accept values, not binding patterns.

`if score == _ { 90..100 -> "A"; else -> "other" }` matches an inclusive band using the existing range-pattern mechanism.

`if n % _ == 0 { 2..5 -> ... }` does not search divisors. A Range cannot fill an Int hole. A function hole whose actual input type is Range may accept a Range value.

In `.Ok(value) && value > 0`, a successful pattern makes value available to the guard and selected body. The payload wildcard in `.Ok(_)` binds nothing.

Names are local to the arm. Keep the existing strict Boolean-OR rule: a pattern binding introduced beneath || is unavailable after that ||, including in the body. This remains true even when both Boolean branches bind the same name. A binding established before `(ready || emergency)` remains available; that nested OR does not introduce it.

Only structural | may merge pattern bindings across alternatives. Existing structural or-pattern rules require matching names, types, and binding modes across alternatives. They do not create multiple header inputs.

Read a pattern subject once within each candidate test. Range bounds and payload checks inspect that same value. A later candidate starts a new attempt.

Pending guards receive non-consuming read access to pattern-bound payloads. Sema rejects a guard that moves from or mutates the matched payload. Existing ordinary copying rules still apply to copyable values. Commit a permitted by-value pattern move only after the complete head selects the arm. Guard effects on unrelated state remain ordinary effects; there is no rollback.

Exhaustiveness and result types

Value tables require else unless existing structural coverage proves that some arm must succeed. Arm result types unify through existing rules. Effect tables may fall through without else.

Per-attempt subject evaluation makes type coverage alone insufficient. If next_result() returns .Err then .Ok, arms .Ok followed by .Err can both miss.

Use one explicit no-else proof rule. Ignoring parentheses, the whole header must be `subject == _` or `_ == subject`. The subject must be an immutable bound value. Unguarded structural pattern arms must cover its closed type using existing coverage rules.

Other guarded arms may be present but contribute no coverage. A Boolean conjunction or disjunction in the header requires else. A call, computed expression, or literal subject also requires else; bind it first to request structural coverage.

For example, `false && result == _` never becomes exhaustive merely because all result variants are listed. A result stored with `result :: next_result()` may use the ordinary unguarded variant-coverage proof. This proposal does not add a general stability or constant-folding prover.

Do not pretend arbitrary predicate tables are exhaustive by solving their conditions. No runtime fallback may stand in for a missing user else.

Cutover and implementation obligations

Migrate every in-repository caller, source producer, example, test, snapshot, formatter case, and affected explanation. Remove acceptance of the old holeless dispatch form.

Where old code relied on one evaluated subject, insert an explicit binding during migration unless single-evaluation equivalence is proven. Preserve observed meaning rather than mechanically adding `_`. The formatter handles layout after a source-aware semantic repair; it does not invent the repair.

Mixed tables with independent predicate arms must become subjectless tables. For example, retain `code == 200` and `ready == true` as separate written conditions. Preserve their ordering and any prior one-time subject binding. A bare unrelated predicate must not be forced into the hole or silently discarded.

Retain unrelated ordinary and subjectless if forms. Register the new contextual hole role in Syntax.rs against this decision. New or changed diagnostics need registered what, why, fix, and UI snapshots.

One semantic lowering must serve statement and value position, AOT, default run/dev, interpreter/deopt, web, and compile-time evaluation where applicable.

Lower to the existing typed conditional and pattern machinery. Do not introduce runtime closures, allocations, backend policy copies, or a compatibility parser.

Prove FizzBuzz, joined guards, OR bypass, grouped alternatives, skipped candidate effects, repeated header calls, changing-subject coverage, and pattern ownership. Compare them with explicit reference conditions.

Before closure, run affected golden, formatter, and diagnostic checks plus actual multi-mode programs. Do not claim these proposed examples have already passed.

Concrete reading and grammar examples

For an Int n, `n % divisor == 0` tests whether the divisor fits evenly. FizzBuzz returns "FizzBuzz" at 15 and "7" at 7.

For a Bool-taking accepts function, `ready && backup -> body()` means `accepts(ready) && backup` under `if accepts(_)`.

`(ready && backup) -> body()` instead means `accepts(ready && backup)`. The parentheses make the whole expression one candidate.

Likewise, write `(a < b)` to supply a comparison result as a Bool candidate. An unparenthesized whole comparison is not an independent predicate-arm escape.

At candidate-group level, `(Read | Write)` is still two alternatives. For a combined bitmask, first write `both :: Read | Write`, then use `both` as the candidate.

With read() returning 7, `if read() % _ == 0 { 3 -> hit(); 5 -> hit(); else -> miss() }` performs two reads.

With `n :: read()` before `if n % _ == 0`, the same candidates use one read. With a false condition before the hole, an effectful candidate is skipped.

These examples describe the proposed semantics. They are not compiler execution receipts.

decisions.title: Read complete enum values as compile-time metadata
decisions.gist: Should a payload-free enum expose its complete values as compile-time metadata?
decisions.lesson: A payload is data stored inside a case. A payload-free case is already a complete value. Jet has typed compile-time facts; this proposal derives values from the same enum declaration. A reads metadata, C creates an iterator, and B keeps manual lists. None invents payloads, integer conversions, or a second case registry.
decisions.story: Mina builds a complete direction selector and derives its count before the program runs. Adding East must update both from one declaration. She still uses an explicit list when she wants a subset or a different display order. The owner asked whether this should be an @ metadata reader instead of a generated method. A now makes that distinction explicit.
decisions.inWild:
enum Direction: CaseIterable { case north, south }
print(Direction.allCases.count) // 2; adding east makes 3.
decisions.detail:
## Answer to the owner question

Yes. Recommended A now uses T.@values through the existing typed compile-time fact reader. It replaces the proposed T.cases() operation rather than adding an alias beside it. B still means manual lists. C makes the original iterator design an explicit alternative. No option has been selected.

## Exact contract

For an eligible nominal enum T with N checked leaf cases, T.@values returns an ordinary immutable fixed array [T#N]. Each item is a real T value. The result is compile-time data, not CaseInfo, an erased Value, or a stored mutable iterator. It can feed normal collection operations or an explicit ordinary iterator conversion. Each iteration has ordinary independent cursor state.

The reader uses the existing @ grammar and registered fact mechanism. Register this reader and its typed result in the existing declaration/fact registry, not a parser special case or a second enum registry. No new token, keyword, nominal collection type, package, or dependency is proposed. A grammar change would require a full ballot before implementation.

Generate the value expressions from the same checked enum leaf rows used by matching, construction and D-ENUM-CASEMETA1. Do not cast discriminants to enum values or rediscover names through runtime reflection. N is the array's ordinary constant length; this does not let arbitrary metadata values mint types.

T.reflect().cases remains the D-ENUM-CASEMETA1 catalog of descriptions, including payload shapes. T.@values is the typed inhabited-value projection for the strictly payload-free subset. These are different questions over one declaration owner, not interchangeable names or independently maintained tables. This ballot does not change CaseInfo, Value.case(), or reflection capture authority.

All flattened leaf cases must have unit payloads. A single Bool payload still has multiple possible values. A zero-size payload type still requires a payload. Reject a payload-bearing or non-enum receiver in Jet; do not omit ineligible cases or synthesize defaults. Respect the existing enum validity rules, including whether an empty enum is legal. A legal empty domain produces an empty array; a singleton produces one value.

Emit every declared leaf once in declaration order. Groups contribute paths, not extra values. Sparse explicit discriminants do not create gaps or define indices. The array preserves T's nominal identity. Its order is not a wire ordinal, and its length is not an ABI or future-version promise. Existing non-exhaustive and visibility rules remain law.

A complete query uses ordinary source access checks. If the caller cannot access a required case, reject the complete query rather than returning a filtered domain. Publishing a lawfully obtained collection is ordinary intentional publication. This does not grant a foreign generator new access rights.

The @ reader is compiler-owned under the existing fact namespace. Do not shadow user members, silently replace a declaration, or reserve an unmarked values/cases method under A. Use the registered diagnostic machinery for invalid reads. Explicit application lists remain available for subsets and custom ordering.

Keep the array at compile time when it only supplies counts or generated code. Runtime use follows normal fixed-array ownership and lowering, without a mandatory Vec conversion or heap allocation. This is not a zero-copy or measured-speed claim. It introduces no performance-only surface waiver.

## Other complete designs

B adds neither a fact nor a method. The application owns completeness, subset and presentation order. Existing reflection law still applies, but B adds no automatic typed value enumeration.

C generates T.cases() returning a fresh ordinary Iter<T>. It follows the same eligibility, completeness, order, visibility and nominal-type rules as A. It uses the existing iterator protocol, with no required intermediate heap collection. A conflicting cases member receives the ordinary duplicate-member diagnostic. C adds no @values reader. No design ships both A and C as aliases.

## Proof after owner ratification

Exercise the same Direction program before and after East. Check actual typed items, declaration order, flattened groups, sparse codes, empty/singleton behavior where legal, two independent iterations, and source refusals. Prove compile-time use and runtime collection use across applicable I9 execution modes. Check generated artifacts for the chosen ordinary representation. Do not claim runtime parity or a speed win from this proposal.

## Evidence and retained law

The captured source/witness home remains docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-enum-f03-finite-case-values. Source owners are crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/core_surface.rs:964-1008 and crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerInfer/expr.rs:773-833,6905-6920. These prove existing fact routing and compile-time reflection, not the proposed @values implementation.

D-FACT-READ1=A as respelled by D-ONCE-AT1=D, D-META-CONST1=A, D-ENUM-CASEMETA1=A, D-UNIONTYPE1=A, D-TAG1, D-MAP-KEY1 and I1-I9 remain binding. This revision changes an unanswered proposal only.

decisions.title: Checked local obligations in existing tooling
decisions.gist: Should compiler tools show checked local obligations at a selected source point?
decisions.lesson: A local obligation is a checked duty at one source point, such as whether a name is being read before a write. A read window is the period in which that read still matters. A exposes the checker’s bounded record; B keeps today’s public facts. Neither turns missing data into permission.
decisions.story: Mina reads values in a loop and then calls values.push(3). At the point before push, she wants to know which binding owns values and whether a read is still active. A shows the checked write requirement and active views. B leaves her to reconstruct that answer from source and diagnostics.
decisions.detail:
## Complete technical contract

### mechanism

One additive typed payload within the existing SemIndex/canonical derivation projection; the existing checked compiler result carries that index. There is no core.compiler.index function, new command family, mutable compiler API or runtime core.compiler capability.

### fact boundary

Source content identity and exact before/after point; semantic binding identity, not spelling alone.

Reuse existing public type/mutability, target references and interface provenance.

Publish only checker-established access/move/view/invalidation/reachability/cleanup relations. Do not promise runtime values, exact alias sets or cleanup execution.

Retain current/unknown/unavailable/unsupported/stale/truncated distinctions and the static_derivation method.

No second analysis or independent fact store; selected facts come from existing check/projection producers.

Retain clean-check publication law. Invalid editor input has unavailable current data or an explicitly stale last-good record; no new privilege to publish recovered partial state as fresh valid facts.

### proof

READ-F10 requires actual selected-point outputs for shadowing, joins, moves, read-view last use, Fixed backing close, invalid input and stale edits. Coordinate BIG-F17 facade parity and READ-F16 nested schema authority.

### independent choice

READ-F01/D-READ-LOCAL1 may summarize current callable facts without this addition. Adding local fact records is independently decidable.

### distribution

Existing build/comptime-only core.compiler facade and developer tools. No new library or dependency; D-FOUND-COREAPI1’s eleven additions do not grant blanket future API approval.

### worked record

ballot-example-data.json binds the full source bytes, point and concrete JSON. Record is the proposed payload, not a complete current SemIndex document. Concrete definition/source IDs are fixture values; implementation reuses compiler-issued identities, not a new ID algorithm. Checked empty active views, unsupported cleanup, current/stale freshness and truncation remain distinct. Invalid input cannot publish this as current valid output.

### finite scope

READ-F10 enumerates all captured local fact planes in an availability matrix, including initialization, freezing, sendability, narrowing, typestate and compile-time string/path constraints. Reuse existing public facts; export only checker-established constraints. Unprojected/nonapplicable/unknown categories stay explicit and never mean no obligation. Raw runtime values are out of scope.

## corelib change

### library

core.compiler

### addition

checked local-obligation records through the existing checked-result semantic-index projection

### placement

existing immutable build/comptime-only facade and existing tooling

### dependency

none

### gate

D-READ-STATE1

## design away record

Reuse existing compiler-owned facts, identities, APIs and protocols; no second index, analyzer or dependency.

Keep ordinary source calls unchanged; request or expand detail only when needed.

Represent stale, redacted, unsupported and unavailable facts explicitly rather than invent values.

Retain source/build and captured-versus-executed limits; comparative usefulness and cost still require scoped proof.

## Recommendation reasoning

A gives Mina a bounded answer at the point before push while preserving unknown and unsupported states. B keeps the smallest API but leaves the local duty implicit.

Option B: B keeps existing facts but does not state the selected-point obligation. A exposes it without granting permission when data is missing.

decisions.title: Locate public compiler diagnostics in their source snapshot
decisions.gist: Should each compiler diagnostic identify the checked source snapshot for its byte span?
decisions.lesson: A byte span says which bytes were involved, but not which source file or text supplied them. A source snapshot is that exact checked input. Jet’s diagnostic has code, message, cause, fix and span, while imported diagnostics can lose their source identity. A stores optional origin data with the row; B keeps source context beside it. Neither changes program validity or the read-only facade.
decisions.story: Mira combines diagnostics from generated source. E0107 points to bytes 55–63, but a detached span does not say which input those bytes came from. A pairs the row with the known source digest and a null path for raw text. B leaves Mira to carry the path and digest in a sidecar. Both describe the same E0107.
decisions.detail:
Add optional origin to the existing read-only CompilerDiagnostic value, mirrored by the Rust DiagnosticView and existing compiler CLI JSON projection.

The proposed facade API/data version is2.

The origin is an optional structural record: path is optional text and source_digest is a lowercase64-character SHA256 of the exact UTF8 source bytes.

No new public type export, Core module, optional package, dependency or runtime compiler service is adopted.

A known raw source has a digest but may have path=null; never infer a physical path from a span.

Equal byte strings can have equal digests in different files/invocations, so this field is content provenance rather than universal declaration/request identity.

Reuse internal immutable source identity; do not recompute or copy the full source per diagnostic.

Keep build/comptime/E0956 restrictions.

Distinguish the compiler-facade API version from nested semantic-index/package schema versions.

Existing CLI/LSP source-origin repair is BIG-F08 regardless of this vote.

Exact proposed JSON value contract for CompilerDiagnostic.origin (a structural record, not invented Jet declaration syntax):
```json
{
  "type": [
    "object",
    "null"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "path": {
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "source_digest": {
      "type": "string",
      "pattern": "^[0-9a-f]{64}$"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "path",
    "source_digest"
  ],
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

Exact raw source supplied to the existing parser/check API in this illustrative case:
```jet
pub fn letter(score: Int, offset: Int) String -> {
    adjusted = score + offset
    return if {
        adjusted >= 90 -> "A"
        adjusted >= 80 -> "B"
        else -> "C"
    }
}
```
Its UTF8 SHA256 is ace012b6db1a7f594ec070db981636518b485595a5d47eb6238f5b847ce38283. The first adjusted occurrence is bytes55–63, zero-based UTF16 line1 characters4–12. The current/A/B examples are valid JSON data illustrations populated from this input and the observed E0107 text, not captured compiler-API outputs. B is explicitly a caller-owned context wrapper, not a new compiler return shape.

## Complete original normative metadata

This retained metadata preserves scope, evidence status, policy and provenance. It grants no implementation or dependency approval.

```json
{
  "source_fields": {
    "sourceFinding": "BIG-F20",
    "submissionStatus": "Complete unratified draft; Main assigns a focused card and checks uniqueness before submission.",
    "technical": "Add optional origin to the existing read-only CompilerDiagnostic value, mirrored by the Rust DiagnosticView and existing compiler CLI JSON projection. The proposed facade API/data version is2. The origin is an optional structural record: path is optional text and source_digest is a lowercase64-character SHA256 of the exact UTF8 source bytes. No new public type export, Core module, optional package, dependency or runtime compiler service is adopted. A known raw source has a digest but may have path=null; never infer a physical path from a span. Equal byte strings can have equal digests in different files/invocations, so this field is content provenance rather than universal declaration/request identity. decisions.title: How should a typed F32 list become a Tensor?
```
decisions.gist: Should a typed F32 list use from_list or a separately named F32 constructor?
decisions.lesson: F32 is a 32-bit floating-point value. A Tensor owns an array of such values. The current ordinary constructor follows Float/F64 source behavior. A preserves the input type through from_list; B adds from_list_f32. Both promise typed F32 storage and readback for the same one-value job, but neither has physical-storage proof yet.
decisions.story: Mira starts with the typed list [F32]{42.0}. A sends it through compute.from_list; B sends it through compute.from_list_f32. Both proposed jobs should return the typed list [42] from the Tensor. A uses the input type once; B repeats F32 in the operation name. Physical 4-byte storage remains a proof requirement, not a label.
decisions.inWild:
# CuPy adaptation; dtype is explicit; not run here.
import cupy as cp
x = cp.array([42.0], dtype=cp.float32)
assert x.dtype == cp.float32
assert x.nbytes == 4
print(cp.asnumpy(x))  # Intended:[42.].
decisions.detail:
A adds the typed F32 admission to the existing operation: `from_list(values:[F32]) Tensor<F32> !ComputeError`. B adds `from_list_f32(values:[F32]) Tensor<F32> !ComputeError` and leaves the old from_list route unchanged. Both use ordinary Core calls; neither adds parser syntax or a new tensor owner. The shown `show(values:[F32])` function makes the intended result element type explicit.

Both borrow the input for construction and return an owned rank-one tensor with the same F32 values and input length. The result cannot expose future mutation of the borrowed list as a hidden tensor mutation. Physical numeric storage remains32-bit across construction, device transfer and typed readback. There is no F64 staging, numeric narrowing or profile-only retagging. Existing allocation, size, finite-value and shape errors remain typed ComputeError results.

Empty typed input has shape[0], not an unknown dtype.

Existing ordinary Float input keeps its Float/F64 behavior. The current captured from_list takes Vec<f64> and builds Arc<Vec<f64>>. That source does not establish this new physical F32 path. The older constructor packet has current-line equality evidence but no historical file digest; the newer Core API packet records its captured source hashes. Neither is execution proof.

The source-facing choice is narrow: infer F32 from a typed list or also spell F32 in the function name. It does not admit authored U32 kernels, choose an atomic-cell constructor, alter the ratified launch, or approve a device compiler dependency. The separate U32 and Atomic drafts show their own exact admissions. Both F32 options must integrate with the same Tensor/View owner and target metadata.

The CuPy comparison establishes an explicit float32 constructor and physical byte-width check as a peer mechanism. Its script is an unexecuted adaptation, not a benchmark. In Jet, prove the returned [F32] consumer boundary, four-byte physical elements, shape and value preservation. Test non-finite rejection, actual allocation refusal, empty input, mixed typing and transfer/readback without assuming a profile string proves storage width.

Reading key. `use core.compute as compute` gives the compute library a short name. `fn` defines a function. A colon introduces a parameter type. The type after the parameter list is the result type. `->` introduces a one-expression body; braces group statements. `return` gives the caller a result. `::` binds a name that is not reassigned; `:=` binds a variable. `=` stores a new value. `+=` adds and stores. `loop i in 0..<n` repeats for positions zero through n minus one.

`xs[i]` reads position i, so a list of length two has positions zero and one. A comma-separated bracket selects one coordinate per dimension. `if condition -> statement` executes that statement only when the condition holds. `%` gives the remainder. `wrapping(expression)` explicitly permits fixed-width integer wraparound. `F32` is a 32-bit floating-point number; `U32` is an unsigned 32-bit integer. `Int` is Jet's ordinary exact integer. `[F32]{3,5}` is a list containing two F32 values.

A Tensor owns an array and its dimensions. A View borrows existing values; ViewMut is a writable loan. `#Kernel(.parallel)` marks an authored function whose runs may execute together. The launch supplies Invocation, the read-only facts for one run. Safe code cannot construct or edit those facts. `at.linear` is this run's zero-based position. `at.extent` is the number of logical runs. `resources: (xs,)` supplies one borrowed tensor resource. The trailing comma makes a one-item tuple.

`grid: [2]` requests two logical runs, not two hardware blocks. `output: ^buffer` moves an output owner into the call. `?? panic("{err}")` takes the successful result, or stops and shows the actual error. It is an example stop policy, not an automatic retry. `print` displays the value. All proposed programs and their intended results remain unexecuted.

Inherited launch constraints. The following applies to compute.launch, not to the ordinary default placement of tensor construction.

Preserved safety and execution contract. The compiler checks seven named matters: sendability, bounds, aliasing, captures, races, barriers, and control flow. Sendability means values can cross the worker boundary. Bounds mean every access names existing storage. Aliasing checks which names reach the same bytes. Captures must not bring unproved host state into device work. Race checks prevent conflicting simultaneous access. Barrier checks require every participant to reach the same meeting point. Control checks reject paths whose required execution cannot be proved.

These are required checks, not a claim that the current implementation proves the new examples. Naming seven matters does not require seven new fields or another checker.

The compiler proves relationships from source. The launch checks the actual shapes, lengths, offsets, strides, device capabilities and stream ownership required by those relationships. A failed source proof rejects before lowering. A failed runtime precondition returns the existing compute error before submission. Proposed diagnostic text below is illustrative wording, not a newly registered error code.

Omitting device, or choosing compute.device_auto(), requests a compatible real GPU. compute.device_cpu() explicitly chooses the reference path. compute.device_vulkan() explicitly requests Vulkan. No compatible device or capability returns an error. Neither a CPU substitute nor a requested-device label counts as GPU execution. Existing placement() and device() reports must describe actual work.

F32Strict preserves 32-bit source operations and their required rounding. Reproducible preserves the declared operation order and result policy. No hidden F64 staging, TF32/FP16 conversion, reassociation, contraction, or floating atomic sum may change that meaning. A specifically declared alternative numeric mode is a separate existing control; these examples do not select one. An unsupported provider rejects instead of changing the result policy.

A successful launch returns a completed Tensor, never a pending token. Inputs remain borrowed until completion. A moved preallocated output returns with the same semantic storage on success; permitted physical transfers remain disclosed. Moving output consumes the caller's owner even when validation or execution fails. The error does not return a partly written Tensor or restore that old name. The runtime retains submitted resource lifetimes until completion or safe device teardown. Retrying needs a new output allocation.

Device loss can also invalidate other storage on that device; recreate required inputs from retained host data or another valid owner. This is not transactional rollback of GPU bytes.

Only audited provider adapters may use the existing typed raw #Unsafe boundary. Unsafe foreign code is outside the compiler's safety theorem. A safe caller cannot obtain raw access by choosing a different launch option. Core source defines the operation meaning; provider adapters consume the shared checked program and its facts. No second GPU language checker, owner family, or launch engine is authorized.

Prerequisites. D-COMPUTE-TYPE1 remains the one Tensor/View owner law. D-GPU-COMPUTE-LAUNCH1 is unchanged. Every new spelling is a proposal. Required independent choices are not silently approved by appearing in another example.

It does not admit authored U32 kernels, choose an atomic-cell constructor, alter the ratified launch, or approve a device compiler dependency. The separate U32 and Atomic drafts show their own exact admissions. Both F32 options must integrate with the same Tensor/View owner and target metadata.

The CuPy comparison establishes an explicit float32 constructor and physical byte-width check as a peer mechanism. Its script is an unexecuted adaptation, not a benchmark. In Jet, prove the returned [F32] consumer boundary, four-byte physical elements, shape and value preservation. Test non-finite rejection, actual allocation refusal, empty input, mixed typing and transfer/readback without assuming a profile string proves storage width.

No new public operation name is added.

Reading key. `use core.compute as compute` gives the compute library a short name. `fn` defines a function. A colon introduces a parameter type. The type after the parameter list is the result type. `->` introduces a one-expression body; braces group statements. `return` gives the caller a result. `::` binds a name that is not reassigned; `:=` binds a variable. `=` stores a new value. `+=` adds and stores. `loop i in 0..<n` repeats for positions zero through n minus one.

`xs[i]` reads position i, so a list of length two has positions zero and one. A comma-separated bracket selects one coordinate per dimension. `if condition -> statement` executes that statement only when the condition holds. `%` gives the remainder. `wrapping(expression)` explicitly permits fixed-width integer wraparound. `F32` is a 32-bit floating-point number; `U32` is an unsigned 32-bit integer. `Int` is Jet's ordinary exact integer. `[F32]{3,5}` is a list containing two F32 values.

A Tensor owns an array and its dimensions. A View borrows existing values; ViewMut is a writable loan. `#Kernel(.parallel)` marks an authored function whose runs may execute together. The launch supplies Invocation, the read-only facts for one run. Safe code cannot construct or edit those facts. `at.linear` is this run's zero-based position. `at.extent` is the number of logical runs. `resources: (xs,)` supplies one borrowed tensor resource. The trailing comma makes a one-item tuple.

`grid: [2]` requests two logical runs, not two hardware blocks. `output: ^buffer` moves an output owner into the call. `?? panic("{err}")` takes the successful result, or stops and shows the actual error. It is an example stop policy, not an automatic retry. `print` displays the value. All proposed programs and their intended results remain unexecuted.

Inherited launch constraints. The following applies to compute.launch, not to the ordinary default placement of tensor construction.

Preserved safety and execution contract. The compiler checks seven named matters: sendability, bounds, aliasing, captures, races, barriers, and control flow. Sendability means values can cross the worker boundary. Bounds mean every access names existing storage. Aliasing checks which names reach the same bytes. Captures must not bring unproved host state into device work. Race checks prevent conflicting simultaneous access. Barrier checks require every participant to reach the same meeting point. Control checks reject paths whose required execution cannot be proved.

These are required checks, not a claim that the current implementation proves the new examples. Naming seven matters does not require seven new fields or another checker.

The compiler proves relationships from source. The launch checks the actual shapes, lengths, offsets, strides, device capabilities and stream ownership required by those relationships. A failed source proof rejects before lowering. A failed runtime precondition returns the existing compute error before submission. Proposed diagnostic text below is illustrative wording, not a newly registered error code.

Omitting device, or choosing compute.device_auto(), requests a compatible real GPU. compute.device_cpu() explicitly chooses the reference path. compute.device_vulkan() explicitly requests Vulkan. No compatible device or capability returns an error. Neither a CPU substitute nor a requested-device label counts as GPU execution. Existing placement() and device() reports must describe actual work.

F32Strict preserves 32-bit source operations and their required rounding. Reproducible preserves the declared operation order and result policy. No hidden F64 staging, TF32/FP16 conversion, reassociation, contraction, or floating atomic sum may change that meaning. A specifically declared alternative numeric mode is a separate existing control; these examples do not select one. An unsupported provider rejects instead of changing the result policy.

A successful launch returns a completed Tensor, never a pending token. Inputs remain borrowed until completion. A moved preallocated output returns with the same semantic storage on success; permitted physical transfers remain disclosed. Moving output consumes the caller's owner even when validation or execution fails. The error does not return a partly written Tensor or restore that old name. The runtime retains submitted resource lifetimes until completion or safe device teardown. Retrying needs a new output allocation.

Device loss can also invalidate other storage on that device; recreate required inputs from retained host data or another valid owner. This is not transactional rollback of GPU bytes.

Only audited provider adapters may use the existing typed raw #Unsafe boundary. Unsafe foreign code is outside the compiler's safety theorem. A safe caller cannot obtain raw access by choosing a different launch option. Core source defines the operation meaning; provider adapters consume the shared checked program and its facts. No second GPU language checker, owner family, or launch engine is authorized.

decisions.title: Observe remaining bounds with one runtime query
decisions.gist: Should remaining size use one runtime query rather than compile-time metadata?
decisions.lesson: A cursor changes as it yields items. Compile-time metadata cannot describe a live cursor’s changing remainder. A adds one non-consuming query returning lower and optional upper bounds. Equal bounds mean an exact count. B keeps consuming count only. Both retain existing compile-time facts and ordinary evaluation rules.
decisions.story: Ravi reads one record and then reserves space for the remainder. The size answer must fall from three to two without reading the next record. The owner asked whether this belongs in @ metadata. The answer separates stable compile-time facts from changing runtime state, while removing the previously proposed extra trait and exact-size method.
decisions.detail:
## Answer to the owner question

A changing remaining count is not an @ metadata field. @ reads compiler-known facts or demands evaluation of known inputs. It cannot inspect a live file, channel, predicate result or partially consumed runtime cursor before that state exists. A runtime property named with @ would give the mark a second meaning.

Stable declaration facts may still use the existing metadata mechanism. The ordinary evaluator may compute a size expression when all needed inputs and operations are available at compile time. Neither case requires a duplicate public @remaining API. This proposal does not widen compile-time effects or promise that every iterator runs in the evaluator.

## One public query, ordinary types

Recommended A adds size_hint() to the existing Iterator/Iter capability contract. It is a non-consuming observation returning the ordinary pair (lower: Int, upper: ?Int). Default knowledge is (0, None). Both numbers, when present, are nonnegative. A supplied upper must be at least lower. Equal bounds state an exact remaining yielded-item count; unequal or absent bounds do not.

Remove the earlier proposal's separate ExactRemaining capability and remaining_len() method. Consumers needing exactness inspect the same pair and handle absence normally. There is no new size wrapper, capability hierarchy, precision flag, or second public query. Ordinary len/count operations keep their existing consuming meanings.

The query must not call next, poll a live source, invoke mapping/filtering callbacks, or change cursor position. It reports knowledge about that source's current state, not its original input length. Source protocols preserve their existing ownership, effects and borrowing rules. A later advancing operation invalidates any application assumption that an earlier pair describes the new remainder.

An absent upper means unknown or not representable by the declared bound representation; it does not prove infinity. Bounds count yielded items, not bytes, memory usage, cost, or future success. A separate end-of-stream or cancellation contract is not encoded in this pair. A temporarily empty poll is not a permanently exhausted source.

A source may return conservative bounds. Safe user-provided hints never authorize unchecked indexing, uninitialized elements, or unchecked allocation arithmetic. Consumers remain memory-safe if an implementation gives a false hint. Internal proven facts may support optimization only under their existing proof rules.

## Propagation and boundaries

Map preserves cardinality when its existing contract yields one output per input. Filter and filter_map generally lower the guaranteed count to zero while retaining a lawful upper. Chain combines bounds with checked representability; overflow never wraps into a false exact count. Zip uses lawful minimum bounds. Take caps them. Exactness is the result of these ordinary rules, not a separate trait claim.

Mixed front/back advancement updates the same remaining range once that independently gated operation is implemented. No item may be duplicated. A permanently exhausted wrapper remains exhausted. Do not label a resumable source fused from an empty poll. Dynamic failures, stop and cancel retain their ratified distinct meanings.

The same internal cardinality knowledge should serve queries, adapter propagation and compiler analysis. Do not add a second public type hierarchy or require dynamic allocation to carry it. Reuse current copy/view provenance, callback ownership and Stream/task rules. Do not change extrema or top-k tie laws while implementing size propagation.

## Alternative B

B adds no non-consuming query. Existing metadata facts remain available, but they cannot answer live remaining state. Existing len/count consumes the source, invokes its normal effects, and may not terminate on an unbounded source. Explicit application tracking remains possible without acquiring a new core capability.

## Proof and scope

After ratification, run the same three-item cursor before and after next(). Check exact, filtered, unknown/live, empty, unbounded and checked-overflow cases. Ensure the query does not invoke callbacks or advance input. Check dishonest safe hints cannot compromise memory safety. Exercise mixed-direction behavior with its own approved dependency, rather than claiming that draft feature now works.

No new dependency, module, grammar or I1-I9 exception is proposed. AOT, default run and applicable interpreter/web paths must share meaning. This is a state-observation feature, not a measured speed claim. Comparing consuming and non-consuming programs cannot establish a matched performance win. Existing performance-gated drafts remain gated.

## Evidence

These are source observations, not runtime receipts.

Retain ITER-F005 and ITER-F022 evidence in docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md. D-FACT-READ1=A as respelled by D-ONCE-AT1=D, D-META-EFFECT1=A, D-ITER-HOOK, D-ITER-RESUME1=A, D-MEM-COPYSEM1 and I1-I9 govern implementation. This revision changes an unanswered proposal only.
