4. There is no public truncating integer conversion; Core keeps 12 private
   copies of `to_u8`. An unknown static method on a number type, such as
   `U8.truncate`, reports "Nothing named `U8` exists here".

No owner ballot is needed: every item above is either ratified or a small
addition inside an existing method family.

### Sources

- [Z-REF] Zig language reference, 0.15.2 and master, "Builtin Functions" and
  "Shadowing": <https://ziglang.org/documentation/0.15.2/#Builtin-Functions>,
  <https://ziglang.org/documentation/master/>
- [Z-0.11] Zig 0.11.0 release notes, "Rename Casting Builtins", "Cast
  Inference": <https://ziglang.org/download/0.11.0/release-notes.html>
- [Z-0.12] Zig 0.12.0 release notes, "@errorCast", "@abs":
  <https://ziglang.org/download/0.12.0/release-notes.html>
- [Z-0.14] Zig 0.14.0 release notes, "New @branchHint Builtin, Replacing
  @setCold", "Removal of @fence":
  <https://ziglang.org/download/0.14.0/release-notes.html>
- [Z-0.16] Zig 0.16.0 release notes, "@Type Replaced with Individual
  Type-Creating Builtin Functions" (proposal #10710), "@cImport Moving to
  Build System": <https://ziglang.org/download/0.16.0/release-notes.html>
- [PD] P. Dubroy, "Zig shadowing and builtins" (2025-06-08):
  <https://github.com/pdubroy/til/blob/main/zig/2025-06-08-Zig-shadowing-and-builtins.md>
- Jet: `Docs/spec/spec.md` "Compile-time names and staged syntax";
  `Docs/spec/reference/metaprogramming.md`; `Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md`
  (D-COMPILER-NS1, D-LAYOUT-FACTS1, D-NAME-SPLICE1); decisions D-JAI-SITE1,
  D-MARKER-DIAG1, D-UB-BOUNDARY1 (open), D-TAIL-CALL1.

sections.title: Primitives first, pareto wrappers on top: an API composition principle
sections.body:
# Primitives first, pareto wrappers on top: an API composition principle

Card #6367. Status: proposal, dev `59213de00f`. Owner choices are the two
ballots in §8. The full audit is
[`Docs/audits/api-composition-2026-10-30.md`](../audits/api-composition-2026-10-30.md);
this page summarises it, so you can read this page on its own.

## Plain summary

- **The rule.** Every API area has a complete, documented set of primitives that
  can do everything the area needs. On top of them sit a few high-quality
  wrappers for the common jobs. A wrapper is always a one-step composition of
  public primitives. When you need one option more than a wrapper offers, you
  step down one rung to the primitive. You never rewrite and you never copy
  Core's source.
- **Options, not siblings.** If two variants of an operation differ only in a
  policy, they become one function with a labelled, defaulted, enum-typed
  option: `base64.encode(data, alphabet: .Url)`, not `encode_url`. Separate
  names are for separate jobs: a different result type, failure type, safety
  level, effect, or call shape.
- **Use the call tools Jet already has.** Defaults, labels, label-only (`*`) and
  positional-only (`/`) zones, variadics and spreads make the common call the
  shortest one, and every other call is still a single call. Core barely uses
  them: 1.1% of its parameters have defaults, 2 functions are variadic, and 2
  documented top-level functions use a `*` zone.
- **What the audit found.** In 20 Core areas the documented surface is only
  wrappers, and the function that does the work is an undocumented helper with
  positional `Bool` flags. Examples are `base64` (no unpadded standard
  alphabet), `log` (no fields at a computed level) and `regex` (no "replace the
  first 3"). One module, `core.math.combinatorics`, ships 25 list functions
  that work only on `[Int]`, with a `Bool` where the predicate belongs. Core
  also has identical twins and names that promise behaviour the body does not
  have (`walk_parallel` is not parallel, `float32` does not round), and the
  language refuses options after a variadic.
- **How it stays true.** A ninth philosophy pillar, an eight-question API review
  checklist in the contributing docs, and an `api` lint group in `jet lint` for
  the rules a machine can check. The group starts with lint L2401, which is
  registered today but never fires.
- **Owner choices.** Two ballots: adopt the pillar (this also replaces the
  "siblings are the house style" law, which contradicts its own review table),
  and allow labelled options after a variadic parameter.

---

## 1. The principle (draft for `Docs/spec/philosophy.md`, pillar 9)

> **9. Primitives First, Pareto Wrappers On Top:** Every API area has a
> complete primitives layer that can express everything the area needs, and a
> small set of high-quality wrappers for the most common work. A primitive is
> documented, typed and stable; an undocumented helper is not a primitive. A
> wrapper is a documented composition of public primitives. It removes friction
> for the common case and never seals a path: if a wrapper can do something the
> primitives cannot, the primitives are incomplete. Stepping from a wrapper to
> its primitive is one rung on the same ladder, with the same names, types and
> errors. Variants of one operation are options on one function: labelled,
> defaulted and typed. Separate names are for separate jobs. APIs use the call
> tools the language provides (defaults, labels, positional-only and label-only
> zones, variadics, spreads) so the common call is the shortest one and every
> other call is still one call.

How it fits the existing pillars and priorities:

| Pillar | Relation |
|---|---|
| 1 Beginner magic, expert control | Wrappers and defaults are the magic; primitives and options are the control. Experts opt out by naming an option, as pillar 1 requires. |
| 2 Easy to read | A labelled option reads aloud at the call site: `encode(data, alphabet: .Url)` says as much as `encode_url(data)`, and it composes with the next option. |
| 3 Friction inverse to commonality | Wrappers exist only for common work. A rare need costs one more rung, not a fork. |
| 4 Ladders, not cliffs | Wrapper to primitive is a rung. An undocumented worker behind a wrapper is a cliff. |
| 5 The language is a library | Pillar 5 says "no names only Core may call" for the compiler. Pillar 9 says the same for every API: the worker a wrapper uses is one a user may use. |
| 7 Fewer layers | One function with options replaces a family of siblings. |
| 8 Explicit where quality depends on it | A choice that changes behaviour is a written label at the call; the default is the documented common case. |
| Priority 4, one mechanism | A wrapper is never a second mechanism; it expands into the first. |

It strengthens laws that are already in
[`stdlib-api-laws.md`](../spec/stdlib-api-laws.md): L-D ("beginner presets
compose small expert primitives; they do not fork them"), D3 ("defaulted
options replace overload families"), D4 (enum options, never `Bool` or string
flags), review row L9 (one root method with a label-only option enum), and Law
8 (one way to mean it). It replaces Law 9 ("sibling methods stay the house
style", D-STDLIB-OPTPARAM1=A), which contradicts L9 and D3 on the same page
(§7).

## 2. The rules

| Rule | Statement | Machine check |
|---|---|---|
| **P1 Complete primitives** | Each area names its primitives in its reference page. Everything a wrapper does is reproducible from documented primitives. A worker that is not meant to be a primitive lives in a `priv module`. | Partly: `api.constant_siblings` finds the wrapper families and names their shared worker |
| **P2 Wrappers are compositions** | A wrapper's body composes primitives and adds no behaviour of its own. Its doc names the primitive. | Partly |
| **P3 Options, not siblings** | Same operation with the same result, failure, safety and effect shape: one function with options. Otherwise a separate, plainly named job. | Yes: constant-forwarding sibling families |
| **P4 Typed options** | A policy is an enum or a typed value, never a `Bool` or a bare string. Every option has a default unless the caller must decide. | Yes: positional `Bool` (L2401), string compared only with literals |
| **P5 Use the call tools** | Four or more parameters, or two adjacent parameters of one type, put the later ones in a `*` zone. A list parameter usually called with a literal list is a variadic. An optional parameter defaults to `None`. | Yes |
| **P6 No twins, no name lies** | Two public names with identical behaviour, or a name that promises behaviour the body lacks, are defects. | Identical bodies: yes. Name lies: review |
| **P7 Generic before specific** | Do not ship an `[Int]`-only copy of an operation the language already offers generically. | Review |
| **P8 Wrappers earn their place** | A wrapper exists for work that is common in real programs: the competitive gate's frozen tasks (D-STDRUBRIC1) or counted call sites. | Review |

**When a sibling is still right.** The result type differs (`read` returns
`String`, `read_bytes` returns `[U8]`). The failure type differs. The safety
differs (an expert rung, as in D-ONCE-LAYER1=B). The effect row differs. Or the
call shape differs (a callback replacement such as `replace_all_with`). A
sibling is never right just because a constant differs.

## 3. Worked before and after (real Core and build code)

Every "today" line is a real signature at dev `59213de00f`. Every "after" is a
proposal under the rules above. The audit has the full lists.

### 3.1 `core.encoding.base64`: 31 documented names, worker undocumented (P1, P3, P4)

```jet
// Today: encode_alphabet(data, alphabet: String, padded: Bool) does the work.
// It is callable, but no reference page lists it and its flag is a bare Bool.
base64.encode(data)              // standard, padded
base64.encode_url(data)          // URL-safe, unpadded
base64.encode_url_padded(data)
base64.urlsafe_b64encode(data)   // a second name for encode_url
// Documented way to write unpadded standard base64: none.
```

```jet
// After: one primitive with typed options; the common call is unchanged.
base64.encode(data)
base64.encode(data, alphabet: .Url, padding: .Omit)
base64.encode(data, alphabet: .Custom(BCRYPT), padding: .Omit)
base64.decode(text, alphabet: .Url, whitespace: .Skip)
```

31 documented names become 4 (`encode`, `decode`, `pad`, `is_base64`), and
two jobs with no documented route get one.

### 3.2 `core.log`: five `_fields` twins and an undocumented `emit` (P1, P3, P5)

```jet
// Today
log.info("saved")
log.info_fields("saved", [log.field("user", id)])
// Fields at a level chosen at run time: only through undocumented log.emit.
```

```jet
// After: fields are a variadic tail; the level is an enum
log.info("saved")
log.info("saved", log.field("user", id), log.field("ms", ms))
log.log(level, "slow", log.field("ms", ms))
```

The level's string type is already carded as #6056 (log level ladder). This
example only removes the `_fields` twins and documents the primitive.

### 3.3 `core.regex`: `replace` and `replace_first` (Law 9's own example) (P3, P4)

```jet
// Today: both forward to replace_n(pattern, text, replacement, first_only: Bool).
regex.replace(re, text, "x")
regex.replace_first(re, text, "x")
// Replace the first three matches: no route.
```

```jet
// After
regex.replace(re, text, "x")
regex.replace(re, text, "x", limit: 1)
regex.replace(re, text, "x", limit: 3)
```

The callback form `replace_all_with` stays a sibling: its call shape differs.

### 3.4 `core.time.period`: three wrappers that pass zeros (P3, P5)

```jet
// Today
time.period(0, 0, 3)
time.period_days(3)
```

```jet
// After: label-only parameters with defaults
time.period(days: 3)
time.period(months: 1, days: 2)
```

### 3.5 `core.net`: a model the board already chose (P3)

```jet
// Today: a timeout needs a SocketAddr, and a host name cannot have one.
net.tcp_connect("db.local:5432")
net.tcp_connect_timeout(addr, 2000)
```

```jet
// After D-DEADLINE-ONE1=A (ratified, not yet built): one connect, one deadline block
#Deadline(2s) {
    conn :: net.tcp_connect("db.local:5432")?
}
```

This is pillar 9 at work: one composable mechanism (the deadline block) replaces
a timeout sibling on every waiting call. It needs no new ballot, only the
implementation card.

### 3.6 `fn build`: seven positional arguments, stringly typed (P4, P5)

```jet
// Today (spec "Programmable builds")
shell :: b.probe("shell", "find_program", "sh")
stamp :: b.action("stamp", ["assets/version.txt"], ["build/version.txt"],
    ["sh", "-c", "cp assets/version.txt build/version.txt"], ["Exec", "FS"], native, [shell])
app :: b.add_executable("app", ["main.jet"], [stamp])
```

```jet
// After
shell :: b.probe("shell", .Program("sh"))
stamp :: b.action("stamp", inputs: ["assets/version.txt"], outputs: ["build/version.txt"],
    run: ["sh", "-c", "cp assets/version.txt build/version.txt"], effects: [.Exec, .FS],
    toolchain: native, probes: [shell])
app :: b.add_executable("app", sources: ["main.jet"], deps: [stamp])
```

Three adjacent `[String]` lists can no longer be swapped silently, and the
effect and probe kinds are checked enums instead of strings.

### 3.7 Jetpack: four `_with_` wrappers that each pass `None` for the others (P3)

```jet
// Today: which wrapper takes a preset and an environment?
envmodel_evaluate_env(src, dir)
envmodel_evaluate_env_with_preset(src, dir, preset)
envmodel_evaluate_env_with_environment(src, dir, env)
envmodel_evaluate_env_with_selections(src, dir, preset, env)
```

```jet
// After
envmodel_evaluate_env(src, dir, preset: "ci", environment: "linux")
```

### 3.8 `core.math.combinatorics`: `[Int]`-only copies of generic operations (P7)

```jet
// Today: [Int] only, and a Bool where a predicate belongs
combinatorics.takewhile([3, 1, -2, 4], true)   // the only predicate is "x >= 0"
combinatorics.chain(a, b)                      // exactly two lists
```

```jet
// After: the generic list methods already exist (take_while, chunks, windows, zip, group_by)
xs.take_while(x -> x > limit)
combinatorics.chain(a, b, c)                   // variadic and generic
```

### 3.9 A language gap: options after a variadic (ballot D-VARIADIC-OPTS1)

```jet
fn join_path(parts: ...String, sep: String{"/"}) -> String
join_path("usr", "local", "bin")
join_path("C:", "Users", sep: "\\")
```

Today the declaration is `E1310 Variadic parameter 'parts' must be last`.
Python (keyword-only parameters after `*args`), Swift (a labelled parameter
after a variadic) and Kotlin (named arguments after a `vararg`) all allow it.
Without it, a variadic API cannot have options, so authors fall back to list
parameters or sibling families. That is the main reason Core has 2 variadics.

## 4. What the audit counted

Scope: all of `Core/` (167 files), `Jetpack/` (511 files), the `fn build` API,
and the Core surface ledger (1,180 user-facing names in 75 modules). Tests are
excluded. Ranked by severity, then reach:

| Rank | Finding | Count | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Undocumented workers behind documented wrappers | 20 areas | Promote the worker to a typed, documented primitive; reduce wrappers to one line or delete them |
| 2 | `[Int]`-only copies of generic operations | 25 functions, plus 4 second names for the same count | Delete; make `chain` and `cartesian` generic and variadic |
| 3 | Identical twins and names that lie | 10 groups (aliases are carded separately) | Fold or fix |
| 4 | Wrapper families that cannot be combined | 8 Core families; 148 suffix families in Jetpack | One function with label-only options |
| 5 | Call-tool gaps in the language | 3 (options after a variadic; function values drop labels; spreading a record into labels) | One ballot, one bug, one research item |
| 6 | `Bool` and string policy parameters | 197 Core and 380 Jetpack `Bool` parameters with no default | L2401 must fire; then enums |
| 7 | Long positional parameter lists | 352 Core and 981 Jetpack functions with 4 or more parameters | `*` zones, mechanically |
| 8 | Missing defaults | 100 of 9,067 Core parameters have one | Per site |

The audit also found five bugs (§6 of the audit), including L2401 never firing
and the retired trailing-block call form still being accepted.

## 5. Review checklist (for a new `Docs/spec/contributing/api-review.md`)

A reviewer answers each question for every new or changed public API. A "no"
blocks the change unless the review record explains why.

1. **Primitive named.** Which documented primitive does this area use? (P1)
2. **Wrapper expands.** Can you write this wrapper's body using only documented
   primitives, and does its doc name them? (P2)
3. **Same job, one name.** Is there a sibling that differs only in a constant?
   Fold it into an option. (P3)
4. **Typed options.** Does a `Bool` or a string pick a policy? Make it an enum.
   Does every option have a default unless the caller must decide? (P4)
5. **Call shape.** Are the later parameters label-only? Should a list parameter
   be a variadic? Do optional parameters default to `None`? (P5)
6. **No twins.** Does another public name already do this? Does the name
   promise only what the body does? (P6)
7. **Generic first.** Does a generic operation already exist? (P7)
8. **Earned.** Which frozen task or counted call sites justify this wrapper? (P8)

The review record in `stdlib-api-laws.md` gains one field, "Pillar 9 answers",
with the eight answers. The checklist page is the only copy; the laws page
links to it.

## 6. The `api` lint group (the mechanical rules)

D-STDRUBRIC1=A makes Core API laws "lints first", with the rubric generated
from lint metadata. These rules are mechanical and belong in `jet lint` as one
group. They run on Core and Jetpack under the same diagnostic ratchet as other
lints, and any package can turn them on (pillar 5).

| Lint | Detects | Example hit at HEAD |
|---|---|---|
| `positional_bool_parameter` (L2401, registered) | A `Bool` parameter outside a `*` zone with no default | `regex.replace_n(…, first_only: Bool)` |
| `api.constant_siblings` | Two or more public functions whose bodies are one call to the same callee, differing only in literal arguments. The fix hint names the callee as the primitive to promote. | `log.info` / `warn` / `debug` → `emit`; `base64.encode` / `encode_url` → `encode_alphabet` |
| `api.string_policy` | A `String` parameter compared only with string literals | `term.style(style: String, …)`, `b.probe(…, "find_program", …)` |
| `api.long_positional` | Four or more parameters with no `*` zone, or two adjacent parameters of one type | `b.action` (7), `net.dns_a_at(server, name, ms)` |
| `api.list_literal_param` | A list parameter that most call sites in the repo pass as a literal list | `ui.previews([phone, fallback])`, `ui.playgrounds([lab])` |
| `api.identical_twin` | Two public functions with identical bodies and signatures | `ui.previews` / `ui.playgrounds`, `files.walk` / `walk_parallel` |
| `api.copy_setter` | A function that copies a struct and changes one field, where struct field defaults would do | `tui.style_bold` |

The rules read declarations and one-call bodies (`api.list_literal_param` also
reads the package's call sites), so none needs a list of "documented" names.
The lints are ordinary compiler-API clients, so a third-party package gets the
same checks.

## 7. Conflicts this resolves

- **Law 9 against review row L9 and D3.** Law 9 says "do not add a mode
  parameter" and cites `replace` / `replace_first`. Row L9 says variants with
  the same result and safety shape "use one root method with a safe default and
  a label-only option enum". D3 says "defaulted options replace overload
  families". The same page asks for opposite things. Ballot D-API-COMPOSE1
  settles it for options.
- **Everything is public, but not everything is a primitive.** D-VIS-MODULE1
  makes every declaration public unless it is inside a `priv module`. Core has
  one `priv module` (in `core.db.sql`). So the 20 workers in rank 1 can already
  be called, but they are undocumented, untyped and unstable. Pillar 9 makes
  the choice explicit: promote the worker or make it private.

Already decided elsewhere, so not re-balloted here: Python alias spellings
(D-CORE-ONE-NAME1=A, carded as #5978 criterion 14), public `__` hooks (#5978
criterion 13), per-call timeouts (D-DEADLINE-ONE1=A), and the log level ladder
(#6056).

## 8. Owner ballots

| Ballot | Question | Options | Recommendation | Profile |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D-API-COMPOSE1 | Make "primitives first, pareto wrappers on top, options not siblings" philosophy pillar 9, enforced by a review checklist and an `api` lint group? It supersedes D-STDLIB-OPTPARAM1 (Law 9). | A: pillar 9 + checklist + lint group. B: primitives first only; sibling names stay the house style for variants. C: checklist guidance only, no pillar and no lints. | A | Short (stdlib group) |
| D-VARIADIC-OPTS1 | Allow label-only parameters after a variadic parameter? It amends D-VARIADIC1's "last parameter only" and E1310. | A: parameters after a variadic are label-only, as after Python's `*args` (`join_path("C:", "Users", sep: "\\")`). B: keep the variadic last; functions with options take a list. C: options go before the variadic, positionally. | A | Full (syntax group), so it needs a fresh adversarial review |

Reconcile D-VARIADIC-OPTS1 with D-CALLPOS1 (names are required in a `*` zone,
and the variadic acts as the zone opener), D-META-PARAMS1, and spreads
(`f(...xs, sep: "-")`). Peers for the comparisons: Python `base64.b64encode(s,
altchars=)` and keyword-only parameters after `*args`; Go
`base64.StdEncoding.WithPadding(base64.NoPadding)`; Swift labelled parameters
after a variadic; Kotlin named arguments after `vararg`.

## 9. Cards

The audit (§5) lists ten cards with the rows they fix. Four rest on laws that
are already ratified and can be filed now: retire the `[Int]` combinatorics
copies, fold the twins, make L2401 fire, and keep labels on function values.
Five wait on the ballots above, including promoting the base64, log and regex
workers, because folding wrappers into options reverses Law 9. One is a
research card on build outputs.

sections.title: API composition audit: Core, Jetpack and the build API
sections.body:
# API composition audit: Core, Jetpack and the build API

Card #6367, criterion 2. Dev `59213de00f`. The principle and its review rules
are in
[`Docs/proposals/api-primitives-and-wrappers-2026-10-30.md`](../proposals/api-primitives-and-wrappers-2026-10-30.md)
(rules P1 to P8).

## Plain summary

- **Scope.** All of `Core/` (167 source files), `Jetpack/` (511 files), the
  `fn build` API in the spec, and the Core surface ledger (1,694 rows in 75
  modules; 514 are `__` hooks, leaving 1,180 user-facing names). Tests are
  excluded.
- **The headline.** In 20 Core areas the documented surface is only wrappers.
  The function that does the work is an undocumented helper, usually with
  positional `Bool` or magic `Int` flags. It can be called, because every
  declaration is public unless it sits in a `priv module`, but no reference page
  lists it and nothing makes it stable. So a need just outside a wrapper has no
  supported route: unpadded standard base64, log fields at a level chosen at
  run time, or "replace the first three regex matches".
- **One module copies generic operations for `[Int]` only.**
  `core.math.combinatorics` has 25 list functions that accept only `[Int]`,
  several with a `Bool` where a predicate belongs, while generic list methods
  that do the same job already exist.
- **Call tools are almost unused.** 100 of Core's 9,067 parameters have a
  default (1.1%). Core has 2 variadics and Jetpack has none. 352 Core and 981
  Jetpack functions take four or more parameters, and Jetpack has 8 defaults in
  total.
- **Twins and name lies.** `files.walk_parallel` is `walk`, `math.float32`
  returns its argument unchanged, `ui.previews` and `ui.playgrounds` are the
  same function, and `crypto.publicdecrypt` takes a secret key.
- **Output.** Eight ranked finding classes (§3, §4), ten proposed cards (§5),
  five bugs with repros (§6). Items already decided or carded elsewhere are
  marked so they are not filed twice.

## 1. Method

| Measure | How | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Parameter census | A source scanner over every `fn` header (`census.mjs`): defaults, variadics, `*` and `/` zones, external names, `Bool` parameters, arity, sibling-name families | "Public-looking" means no `priv` and no `_` prefix. Core has one `priv module` (`core.db.sql`), so nearly everything is public; the surface ledger is used where "documented" matters. |
| Documented surface | `Compiler/Prelude/CoreSurfaceInventory.jet` `fixed_sig` rows | 1,694 rows; 1,180 without the `__` prefix |
| Constant-forwarding wrappers | A scanner (`wrappers.mjs`) for one-line bodies that call one function with at least one literal argument, grouped by callee and checked against the ledger | 204 wrappers; 27 callees have two or more (128 wrappers); 20 of those callees are not on the ledger |
| Behaviour probes | `jet check` / `jet run` with the published dev compiler on small programs | The repros in §6 and the language-gap rows in F5 |
| Decision cross-check | `stdlib-api-laws.md`, `philosophy.md`, spec "Programmable builds", Tower decisions and cards | Items already ratified or carded are marked "settled" |

The scanners read one-line headers and one-call bodies, so multi-line cases are
under-counted, never over-counted. The scripts and their raw output are in the
lane directory (`census.mjs`, `wrappers.mjs`, `census2/`).

## 2. Census

| | Core | Jetpack |
|---|---|---|
| Files / public-looking functions / their parameters | 167 / 6,096 / 9,067 | 511 / 9,713 / 16,640 |
| Parameters with a default | 100 (in 60 functions) | 8 (in 8 functions) |
| Variadic parameters | 2 (Prelude `min`, `max`) | 0 |
| Functions with a `*` / `/` zone | 13 / 7 | 0 / 0 |
| …of those on the documented top level | 2 (`ui.preview`, `ui.playground`) | |
| External parameter names (`timeout seconds:`) | 0 | 0 |
| `Bool` parameters with no default | 197 (in 174 functions) | 380 |
| Functions with ≥4 / ≥6 parameters | 352 / 79 | 981 / 264 |
| …documented top-level functions with ≥4 parameters and no `*` zone | 37 to 48 (by module-matched or bare-name ledger match) | |
| Sibling-name families (`x` and `x_with…`, `x_in`, `x_first`, …) | 122 | 148 |
| Constant-forwarding wrappers | 204 | not measured |

Per Core module, the 14 largest by public-looking functions:

| Module | Fns | Params | Defaults | `Bool` (no default) | ≥4 params |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Math | 844 | 989 | 0 | 3 | 27 |
| Encoding | 796 | 1,148 | 18 | 30 | 37 |
| Text | 436 | 728 | 0 | 28 | 12 |
| Web | 434 | 632 | 1 | 10 | 25 |
| Crypto | 381 | 795 | 0 | 6 | 65 |
| Net | 380 | 514 | 0 | 8 | 6 |
| Time | 332 | 443 | **46** | 5 | 21 |
| Files | 330 | 500 | 14 | 10 | 12 |
| Http | 286 | 345 | 7 | 2 | 9 |
| Data | 202 | 287 | 0 | 2 | 11 |
| Archive | 143 | 234 | 0 | 1 | 13 |
| Db | 141 | 203 | 2 | 2 | 10 |
| Service | 111 | 230 | 0 | 12 | 18 |
| Jobs | 102 | 258 | 2 | 9 | 25 |

Regex is smaller (102 functions) but has the most positional `Bool`s per
function: 22.

Good models already in Core, worth copying: `ui.preview(name, body, *,
viewport: UIPreviewViewport?{None})`, `time.until` / `since` (4 of 5 parameters
defaulted), `files.lock(path, timeout: Duration?{None})`,
`files.rename(from, to, if_exists:)`, `csv.reader` (4 of 5 defaulted), and
`cbor.reader` / `writer`.

## 3. Findings, ranked

Severity: **S1** a need just outside a wrapper has no supported route. **S2** a
duplicate, or a name that lies. **S3** a missed call tool (ergonomics). Rank is
severity first, then reach.

### F1 (S1, P1/P3/P4). Undocumented workers behind documented wrappers: 20 areas

Each row is a callee that two or more documented wrappers forward to with
literal arguments, where the callee itself is not on the surface ledger and not
documented. A probe confirms such a worker is callable today
(`base64.encode_alphabet(data, STD, false)` runs and prints `aGk/`), but users
cannot know it exists, its flags are untyped, and nothing keeps it stable.

| Area | Documented wrappers | Undocumented worker | No supported route for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `encoding.base64` | `encode`, `encode_url`, `encode_url_padded` (and base32 `encode`, `b32hexencode`) | `encode_alphabet(data, alphabet: String, padded: Bool)` | Unpadded standard alphabet; any custom alphabet |
| `encoding.base64` | `decode`, `decode_url`, `decodebytes` | `decode_strict(text, url: Bool, whitespace: Bool, relaxed: Bool)` | URL-safe with whitespace; relaxed decoding |
| `log` | `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`, `critical`, `fatal`, `log`, five `*_fields` | `emit(level: String, message, fields)` | Fields at a level chosen at run time |
| `regex` | `replace`, `replace_first` (and `sub`) | `replace_n(…, first_only: Bool)`; the name says *n*, the flag is a `Bool` | Replace the first *k* matches, even through the worker |
| `files` | `walk`, `walk_files`, `walk_parallel`, `walkdir` | `walk_impl(root, ignore, files_only: Bool)` | |
| `net.url` | `quote`, `quote_plus`, `quote_from_bytes`, `percent_encode` | `encode_component(text, allow_slash: Bool, plus_space: Bool)` | Keep `/` and encode spaces as `+` |
| `text.fmt` | `pad_left`, `pad_right`, `pad_center` | `pad_mode(…, mode: Int)` (0, 1, 2) | |
| `text.fmt` | `bin`, `oct`, `hex` | `radix_signed_width(n, base, width)` | Other bases; a width for `bin` and `oct` (`hex` requires one) |
| `text` | `pad_start`, `pad_end` | `pad_side` | |
| `text` | `remove_prefix`, `removeprefix`, `remove_suffix`, `removesuffix` | `strip_affix` | |
| `text` | `find`, `rfind` | `byte_find` | |
| `text.runtime` | `split_once`, `cut_last` | `split_at` | |
| `encoding` base85 | `b85encode`, `z85encode` / `b85decode`, `z85decode` | `base85_encode`, `base85_decode` (2 rows) | |
| `encoding.json` | `parse`, `parse_allow_duplicates` | `parse_json(text, allow_duplicates: Bool, limits)` | |
| `encoding.json` | `dumps`, `dump` | `render_json` | |
| `http` | `get`, `post` | `http.__request` | |
| `service` | `set_state_snapshot`, `set_state_event_log` | `select_state_adapter` | |
| `ui` | `open_request`, `save_request`; `node`, `node_color` | `transfer_request`; `transfer_node` (2 rows) | |

For each row, pillar 9 asks for one of two fixes: promote the worker to a
typed, documented primitive (enums for the flags, defaults for the common case)
and reduce the wrappers to one line or delete them; or, if the wrappers really
are the whole job, move the worker into a `priv module`.

### F2 (S1, P7). `[Int]`-only copies of generic operations: `core.math.combinatorics`

The module has 37 documented names. Nine are integer counts, which is real
math. The other 28 are sequence functions that work only on `Int`:

- 25 take `[Int]` lists: `accumulate`, `batched`, `cartesian`, `chain`,
  `combinations`, `combinations_with_replacement`, `compress`, `cycle`, `drop`,
  `dropwhile`, `filterfalse`, `flatten`, `groupby`, `islice`, `pairwise`,
  `permutations`, `powerset`, `product`, `reverse`, `starmap`, `takewhile`,
  `tee`, `unique`, `windows`, `zip_longest`. `count`, `count_from` and `repeat`
  produce only `Int`.
- `takewhile(items, pred_nonneg: Bool)`, `dropwhile` and `filterfalse` take a
  `Bool` where the predicate belongs; "x >= 0" is the only predicate there is.
- `starmap(items: [[Int]])` takes no function (it sums each row).
  `groupby(items)` takes no key.
- `chain(left, right)`, `cartesian(left, right)` and `zip_longest(left, right,
  fill)` take exactly two lists.
- Four of the nine counts are second names: `ncr` and `combinations_count` are
  `binomial`; `npr` and `falling_factorial` are `permutations_count`.

The generic list methods already exist. Probes at HEAD: `fold`, `flat_map`,
`group_by`, `any`, `position` and `sum` run; `take_while`, `skip_while`,
`chunks`, `windows` and `zip` resolve and return a one-pass `Iter`.
`text.combinators.take_while(src, predicate: String)` has the same defect: a
predicate written as a string.

### F3 (S2, P6). Identical twins and names that lie: 10 groups

| Names | Fact |
|---|---|
| `files.walk` / `walk_parallel` | Same signature, same body. Nothing runs in parallel. |
| `files.create_dir` / `create_dir_all` | Same body (`__create_dirs_os`); both create missing parents. Only the effect rows differ (`FS.Write` vs `FS`). |
| `math.float32` / `float64` | Both are `{ n }`. `float32` does not round to 32 bits. |
| `base64.decode_padded` | `{ decode(text) }` |
| `crypto.privatedecrypt` / `publicdecrypt` | Same body; both take an `X25519SecretKey`, so "public" is false. |
| `ui.previews` / `ui.playgrounds` | Same signature, same body (`preview_registry`). |
| `data.median` / `math.stats.median` | Same job, two contracts: `Float DataError!` and `Float?`. |
| `combinatorics.count` / `count_from` | `count` forwards unchanged. |
| `combinatorics.ncr` / `combinations_count` / `binomial` | One count, three names. |
| `combinatorics.npr` / `permutations_count` / `falling_factorial` | One count, three names. |

Settled elsewhere, not counted here: the Python alias spellings
(`b64encode`, `urlsafe_b64encode`, `hexlify`, `warning`, `sub`, `pwd`, `rm`, …).
D-CORE-ONE-NAME1=A deletes every alias and teaches the foreign spelling; the
deletion is #5978 criterion 14. They still ship at HEAD (for example
`Base64.jet:47`).

### F4 (S2, P3). Wrapper families that cannot be combined

| Family | Problem |
|---|---|
| `regex.replace` / `replace_first` | Law 9's own example. Folding into `replace(…, limit:)` also gives "first *k*", which no function offers. |
| `time.period` / `period_days` / `_months` / `_years` | Wrappers that pass zeros to `period(years, months, days)`. |
| `text.fmt.pad` / `pad_left` / `pad_right` / `pad_center` | `pad` is `pad_right`; the mode should be an option. |
| `hex.encode` / `encode_upper` / `encode_prefixed` / `encode_sep` | Case, prefix and separator are separate wrappers, so "uppercase with a separator" has no route. |
| `archive` gzip / zstd: `compress`, `compress_text`, `compress_file` per codec | The codec should be a value. `compress_file` returns `Bool` and an error. |
| `http.client` `session_header`, `_timeout`, `_retries`, `_redirects`, `_auth`, `_proxy`, `_cookie` | Seven copy-setters that rebuild all 8 fields; struct field defaults would do. `session_request(…, body: String)` has no per-request headers or byte body. |
| `tui.style_bold` / `style_dim` / … | Copy-setters, where struct field defaults would do. |
| `net.dns_a(name, ms)` / `dns_a_at(server, name, ms)` (× record kinds) | The server should be an option. Timeouts are settled by D-DEADLINE-ONE1=A (below). |
| Jetpack `envmodel_evaluate_env` + `_with_preset` / `_with_environment` / `_with_selections` / `_with_source_loader` | Each passes `None` for the others. The same shape: `cli_compose_env_scoped` / `_with_stats` / `_with_warm`, `run_command` / `_in`, `enter` / `_with_mode`, `plan` / `_with_default`, and `foundation_run_native_sandboxed` / `_with_mounts` / `_with_timeout_and_mounts`, where each new option multiplies the names. The census finds 148 suffix families in Jetpack; not all are constant-forwarders. |

Settled elsewhere: D-DEADLINE-ONE1=A (ratified, not yet built) retires every
per-call timeout argument and setter (`tcp_connect_timeout`,
`session_timeout`, the `ms` of the nine `dns_*` lookups, and others) in favour
of one `#Deadline(duration)` block. It is the model of pillar 9: one composable
mechanism instead of a timeout sibling per call.

### F5 (S3, language). Gaps in the call tools

| Gap | At HEAD (probed) | Peers |
|---|---|---|
| Options after a variadic | `fn join_path(parts: ...String, *, sep: String{"/"})` gives `E1310 Variadic parameter 'parts' must be last` | Python keyword-only after `*args`; Swift labelled parameter after a variadic; Kotlin named arguments after `vararg` |
| Function values keep labels and defaults | They lose them: `E0764` (bug 1) | D-APILABEL1=A requires that they keep them |
| Spreading a record into labelled arguments | `connect("h", ...opts)` gives `E1312 'connect' doesn't accept a spread argument`; into a `*` zone it gives `E0769` | Python `**kwargs`, JS object spread |

The first is ballot D-VARIADIC-OPTS1. The second is a bug against a ratified
decision. The third needs research before any ballot: an options-struct
parameter with defaults already covers most uses, and D-META-PARAMS1 covers
parameter-list pasting in markers.

### F6 (S3, P4). `Bool` and string policy parameters

197 Core and 380 Jetpack `Bool` parameters have no default; Regex has 22 of
them. Examples: `regex.replace_n(…, first_only: Bool)`,
`text.wrap.indent_with(text, prefix, predicate_nonblank: Bool)`,
`base64.decode_strict` (three), `net.url.encode_component` (two).

String policies: `log.log(level: String, …)` (carded as #6056),
`term.style(style: String, …)`, `b.probe(name, "find_program", …)`, and the
`b.action` effects list `["Exec", "FS"]`.

D4 in `stdlib-api-laws.md` already forbids these. The lint that should find the
`Bool` cases, L2401 `positional_bool_parameter`, is registered as active but
never emitted (bug 3).

### F7 (S3, P5). Long positional parameter lists and missing defaults

352 Core functions take four or more parameters (79 take six or more); Jetpack
has 981 (264). Of the documented Core top level, 37 to 48 take four or more
with no `*` zone. Examples:

- `b.action(name, inputs, outputs, argv, caps, toolchain, probes)`: three
  adjacent `[String]` lists that swap silently.
- `net.dns_a_at(server, name, ms)`: two adjacent `String`s.
- `text.parse.replace(text, old, new, count: Int)`: `count` is required.
- `files.walk(root, ignore: String?)`: `ignore` is optional but has no default.
- `files.read_at(path, offset, count)`: two adjacent `Int`s.
- `b.add_executable(name, sources, deps)`: `deps` is required; callers pass `[]`.

### F8 (S3, P5). Variadics unused

Core has 2 variadics (`min`, `max`) and Jetpack has none. Candidates: log
fields, `combinatorics.chain` / `cartesian` / `zip_longest` once generic,
`ui.previews` / `playgrounds` (every call site passes a literal list), set
`union`, path joining, and `b.default`. Most need options too, so they wait on
F5's first gap.

### Not ranked: build outputs declared two ways

`Output.Executable{…}` and its siblings (a closed sum of 9 kinds, D-SHAPE5b=A)
and `b.add_executable(…)` and its siblings (8 `add_*` methods in `fn build`)
both declare build products. Whether they are two mechanisms for one job, or a
package-product layer over a build-graph layer, needs research before it is a
finding. A closed sum also means a package cannot add a new output kind, which
pillar 5 questions. Proposed as a research card, not a ballot.

## 4. Ranking summary

| Rank | Finding | Count | Severity | Fix size |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | F1 undocumented workers | 20 areas | S1 | Medium: type and document the worker, reduce wrappers |
| 2 | F2 `[Int]`-only copies | 25 list functions + 3 generators + 4 duplicate counts | S1 | Small: delete; make `chain` / `cartesian` generic and variadic |
| 3 | F3 twins and name lies | 10 groups | S2 | Small |
| 4 | F4 unjoinable families | 8 Core families; 148 Jetpack suffix families | S2 | Medium |
| 5 | F5 language gaps | 3 (1 ballot, 1 bug, 1 research) | S3 | Language work |
| 6 | F6 `Bool` and string policies | 577 `Bool` parameters + 4 string policies | S3 | Large, mechanical once L2401 fires |
| 7 | F7 long lists, missing defaults | 1,333 functions | S3 | Large, mechanical: insert `*` zones |
| 8 | F8 variadics unused | about 8 candidates | S3 | Small after F5 |

## 5. Proposed cards

Main files these. Items 1 to 4 rest on laws that are already ratified and can
be filed now; items 5 to 9 wait on the ballots. Each card cites its rule and
the rows above.

1. **Retire the `[Int]` combinatorics copies (F2).** Delete the copies of
   generic list methods and the duplicate counts; make `chain` and `cartesian`
   generic. Fix `text.combinators.take_while(predicate: String)`. Rests on Law
   8 (one way to mean it).
2. **Twins and name lies (F3).** Fold `create_dir` / `create_dir_all`, delete
   `walk_parallel` or make it parallel, delete `float32` / `float64` or make
   `float32` round, fold `previews` / `playgrounds`, fix `publicdecrypt`, and
   pick one `median` contract. Rests on Law 8.
3. **Make L2401 fire (F6, bug 3).** The spec already promises it.
4. **Function values keep labels and defaults (F5, bug 1),** as D-APILABEL1=A
   already requires.
5. **Promote the undocumented workers (F1).** For each of the 20 rows, promote
   the worker to a typed, documented primitive or move it into a `priv module`.
   Start with base64, log and regex (`replace(…, limit:)`). Needs
   D-API-COMPOSE1, because folding the wrappers into options reverses Law 9.
6. **Fold the unjoinable families (F4)** into one function with label-only
   defaulted options: `period`, `pad`, `hex.encode`, archive codecs, http
   session fields, and the Jetpack `_with_` families starting with
   `envmodel_evaluate_env`. Needs D-API-COMPOSE1.
7. **Build API call shape (F6, F7).** Label-only `b.action` arguments, typed
   effects and probe kinds (D4 already requires the enums), defaulted `deps`.
   Needs D-API-COMPOSE1 for the label-only zone.
8. **Labelled options after a variadic (F5),** then the F8 variadics. Needs
   D-VARIADIC-OPTS1.
9. **The `api` lint group and the review checklist** (proposal §5 and §6):
   `Docs/spec/contributing/api-review.md`, the six `api.*` lints with their
   ratchet on Core and Jetpack, and Law 9 replaced in `stdlib-api-laws.md`.
   Needs D-API-COMPOSE1.
10. **Research: build outputs declared two ways (§3, not ranked).**

Already carded, so not filed again: the alias deletion (#5978 criterion 14),
public `__` hooks (#5978 criterion 13), the log level ladder (#6056). The
D-DEADLINE-ONE1 implementation should be checked for a card when Main files
these.

## 6. Bugs found (with repros)

Each repro was run with the published dev compiler at `59213de00f`.

1. **Function values lose labels.**
   ```jet
   fn greet(name: String, greeting: String{"Hello"}, punct: String{"!"}) -> String {
       "{greeting}, {name}{punct}"
   }
   fn run() {
       g :: greet
       print(g("Cy", punct: "~"))
   }
   ```
   `jet check` gives `E0764 'g' has no parameter labelled 'punct'`. D-APILABEL1=A
   says function values keep their labels and defaults.
2. **An unknown label on `print` is printed as a value.**
   `print("a", "b", sep: "-")` prints `a`, `b` and `-` on three lines and exits
   0. A user variadic with the same call shape, `total(1, 2, bogus: 3)`, gives
   `E0764 'total' has no parameter labelled 'bogus'`.
3. **L2401 is registered but never emitted.** `fn parse(text: String, strict:
   Bool)` called as `parse("abc", true)` gets only `L0102 unused_parameter`.
   L2401 is `active` in the diagnostic table and the spec says a positional
   `Bool` "earns advisory lint L2401", but no checker emits it.
4. **The retired trailing-block call form is still accepted.**
   `later() { 5 }` checks clean, although D-TRAILBLOCK2=A retired it (E0335).
   The UI `button` check still *requires* a trailing block
   (`Sema/Calls/UiHandles.jet:223`), and the spec still shows
   `b.generate(name) { ... }`.
5. **`String + String` gives a misleading diagnostic.** It reports `E0109
   Arithmetic needs matching number types`. It should teach interpolation
   (`"{a}{b}"`), since string `+` is intentionally absent.

The doc conflict between Law 9 and review row L9 in `stdlib-api-laws.md` is
settled by ballot D-API-COMPOSE1 (proposal §7).

sections.title: Projects and packages: one clean model for Jet's config files
sections.body:
# Projects and packages: one clean model for Jet's config files

Status: proposal for card #6368, 2026-10-30. Design only; nothing here is built.
Reads with: `Docs/research/2026-10-30-project-package-config-today.md` (the map of today's files, fields, words and confusions, and the peer comparison).
Owner choices: six ballots, listed in section 11. The workspace-to-project rename is already the owner's ruling and is not balloted.

## Summary

Jet's config is confusing because one file does four jobs and one fact has several homes. This proposal gives every fact exactly one home, chosen by one question.

- **Two kinds of folder.** A **package** is code that others can depend on: it has a `package.jet`. A **project** is the folder you work in, usually the repository root: it owns `project.jet`, the committed `jet.lock` and the disposable `.jet/` folder. A small program is both at once and needs only `package.jet`, or no file at all.
- **One question sorts every fact.** *Would someone who depends on this package need it?* Yes: `package.jet` (name, version, deps, outputs, the effects it needs, its lint rules). No, it is about how we work here: `project.jet` (which packages are in the project, build and test profiles, dev tools, toolchain pin, overrides, team policy). Only for this one run: a command-line flag.
- **Facts are data, work is code.** `package.jet` and `project.jet` hold values only. Code that computes or runs lives in three fixed files beside `package.jet`: `build.jet` holds `fn build`, `test.jet` holds `fn test`, `dev.jet` holds `fn dev`. Nothing is found by searching.
- **Primitives first, wrappers on top.** The data files and the entry code make the same Core values (`Output`, `BuildAction`, `BuildOptions`, `TestProfile`, `Environment`). One primitive call, `b.add(...outputs)`, can add any output; `b.add_executable("app", "run.jet", "util.jet", deps: [log])` is a one-line wrapper over it (the variadic sources form needs D-CALL-VARTAIL1=A; otherwise sources stay a list). Calls use positional arguments for what every call needs, a variadic tail for lists you type inline, and labels for every option.
- **One settings order.** stock → project → package (source markers, `package.jet`, `build.jet`) → flag. A pin anywhere, or a project `forbid`, refuses any conflicting value and names both lines.
- **"Workspace" leaves the package system.** No file, field, flag or message uses it. It keeps only its Jai meaning: one compilation with its own build options.
- **Custom linking (#5009).** A link hook returns a typed build action that Jet runs in place of its own link step for the outputs whose `link` option names it. A write hook may post-process the written file the same way. Both are option rows, so every one can be set, audited, pinned and forbidden. Programs that do not use them pay zero bytes.
- **Migration.** About 420 files change, almost all in `tests/` and `Examples/`. `jet fix` makes every move. A leftover old spelling is an error that names its new home.

## 1. The nouns

| Noun | What it is | Its file | Published? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **module** | a source file or folder of source files | any `.jet` | with its package |
| **package** | the unit you name, version, depend on and publish | `package.jet` (or an inline `package { }` block in a one-file program) | yes |
| **output** | one thing a package makes: one of the nine kinds of D-TARGET-ONE1 (Executable, Service, Library, Check, Bundle, Environment, Image, System, Fleet) | an `outputs:` entry or a `b.add(...)` call | with its package |
| **project** | the folder you work in: its packages, profiles, tools, lock, cache and policy | `project.jet` (optional), `jet.lock`, `.jet/` | never |

Rules that make these exact:

1. **Every command runs in exactly one project.** The project root is the nearest folder upward that holds `project.jet`. With no `project.jet`, it is the folder of the nearest `package.jet` (or the lone file's folder). So a one-package program is a project without writing one.
2. **A package belongs to one project.** A multi-package project lists its packages in `project.jet` `packages:`. A `package.jet` never lists other packages.
3. **Projects do not nest.** A `project.jet` inside another project's folder makes its own project; the outer project cannot list packages inside it. The error names both files.
4. **Nothing in `project.jet` is ever published or read by a consumer.** When your package is someone else's dependency, your `project.jet` does not exist for them. Cargo already behaves this way for profiles ("Profile settings defined in dependencies will be ignored", [Cargo profiles](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/profiles.html)); Jet makes it visible by giving those facts their own file.

The ladder (philosophy pillar 4) keeps every rung:

| Rung | Files | When |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `hello.jet` | a script; `jet run hello.jet` (D-ECO14) |
| 1 | `hello.jet` with a `package { }` block | a one-file program that needs a name, deps or effects |
| 2 | `package.jet` + source files (+ `build.jet`, `test.jet`, `dev.jet` when needed) | a package |
| 3 | `project.jet` + packages | custom profiles, dev tools, team policy, or more than one package |

Moving up a rung never rewrites a fact: the same field, with the same text, moves to the next file. `jet fix` and `jet init` do the move (D-LOOSE-GROW1).

## 2. Which file? The beginner's rule

Ask, in order:

1. **Is it only for this run?** → a flag (`jet build --profile release`, `--set port=9090`).
2. **Is it work, meaning code that computes something or runs a tool?** → `build.jet`, `test.jet` or `dev.jet`, beside the `package.jet` it serves.
3. **Would someone who depends on or installs this package need it?** → `package.jet`. Otherwise → `project.jet`.

That is the whole rule. Each line below is "X goes in F because …".

| Fact | File | Because |
|---|---|---|
| name, version, edition, license, description, repository | `package.jet` | it identifies the package to everyone who uses it |
| `jet: "0.4"` (the toolchain range the package needs) | `package.jet` | a consumer's toolchain must satisfy it |
| a dependency, `deps: { http: "1.4" }` | `package.jet` | the package does not compile without it |
| "every package here uses the same `http` version" | `project.jet` `catalog:`, and `deps: { http: project }` in each package | it is a team agreement; each package opts in explicitly |
| an output, `outputs: { app: .Executable{ entry: run } }` | `package.jet` | it is what the package makes |
| an output's own needs, such as `os: web` for a web build or a C library to link | `package.jet`, in that output's `options:` | the output is wrong without it, whoever builds it |
| which output bare `jet run` picks, `defaults: { run: cli }` | `package.jet` | it is a choice among the package's own outputs |
| effects the code uses, `authority: { allow: [IO] }`, and grants to its deps | `package.jet` | a consumer must approve them |
| effects `build.jet` needs (today `build: { allow: … }`) | `package.jet` `authority: { build: [FS, Exec] }` | a consumer runs that build code too |
| lint and code rules for this package (`policy:`, `boundaries:`) | `package.jet` | they describe this package's code |
| a test suite that is plain data (a golden folder), `suites:` | `package.jet` | the suite is part of the package, like an output |
| a test suite that needs code (a fuzz driver) | `test.jet`, `t.suite(...)` | it is work |
| generated code, a code-made output, a custom tool step | `build.jet` | it is work |
| dev-loop behaviour of one service (port, watch, reload) | `dev.jet`, or that output's `options:` | it belongs to that output |
| the packages in this repo, `packages:` | `project.jet` | a consumer never sees your repo layout |
| `version`, `edition`, `license` that every package shares | `project.jet` | a package that leaves one out takes the project's (D-CORE-HEADER1, now written in one place) |
| build profiles, `release: BuildOptions{ optimize: full }` | `project.jet` `profiles:` | how you choose to build; a consumer's build never reads yours |
| test profiles, `quick: TestProfile{ suites: [tests], time_limit: 60s }` | `project.jet` `profiles:` | how you choose to test; same namespace as build profiles (D-TEST-PROFILE1) |
| which profile bare `jet build` / `jet test` uses | `project.jet` `defaults:` | a team choice |
| dev tools, shells and local services (today `env.jet`) | `project.jet` `environments:` | they serve the people working here |
| the exact toolchain the team builds with | `project.jet` `toolchain:`; the resolved version goes in `jet.lock` | a team choice; `package.jet` `jet:` is only the range consumers need |
| a local replacement for a dependency (overlay, patch) | `project.jet` `overlays:` | it must never leak to consumers |
| team policy: forbid an option or effect, pin a value, allow a dependency's hooks | `project.jet` `policy:` | it is a ceiling over every package here |
| the resolved dependency graph and toolchain | `jet.lock` (written by Jet, committed) | D-LOCKFILE1 |
| build output, cache, generated files | `.jet/` (disposable, git-ignored) | D-WORKSPACE-CMD1 |
| `optimize: size` just this once | a flag | rule 1 |

`policy:` exists at both levels with the same shape: the package's block governs that package's code, the project's block is a ceiling over every package. The stricter one wins, and a conflict names both lines. `defaults:` also exists at both levels, but each level picks only among its own things: a package picks among its outputs, a project picks a package and profiles.

Large teams that want to split `project.jet` do not need a `configs:` mechanism. Both data files are Jet values, so a field can take a value from an ordinary module of the project: `environments: team_envs.all`. The special `Config{}` records and `configs:` lists retire.

## 3. Code files: `build.jet`, `test.jet`, `dev.jet`

- `fn build(b: Build)` lives in `build.jet`, `fn test(t: Test)` in `test.jet`, `fn dev(d: Dev)` in `dev.jet`, each beside its `package.jet`. One of each per package at most (D-CONF-ENTRY1's count rule, kept).
- The only other home is a program with no `package.jet` (rungs 0 and 1): there, everything is in the one file.
- `project.jet` has no entry functions. A project builds by building its packages, in dependency order (D-WORKSPACE-CMD1). A thing made from several packages, such as a release bundle, is an output of a small package that depends on them.
- `package.jet` and `project.jet` hold values only, so `jet env`, editors and policy checks read them without running project code (D-JPK-DEVCOMPOSE1).

Why fixed homes, when D-CONF-ENTRY1 allowed any file: `fn build`, `fn test` and `fn dev` run on the developer's machine, before the program exists, with powers such as `Exec` and `FS`. A reviewer must be able to see from a diff that build-time code changed. Cargo (`build.rs`), Zig (`build.zig`), Gradle (`build.gradle.kts`) and Bazel (`BUILD`) all give build code one name for this reason. It also removes discovery: today `Examples/features/tooling/build_entry_discovery` needs a README to say where its build lives.

`jet new --template overrides` stubs change from "replace the stock default" to the shape D-ENTRY-SHAPE1 ratified: the entry sets values, then the stock work runs once.

## 4. How settings combine

One list replaces the three in force today (D-CONF-MERGE1, D-SETTING-ORDER1, and D-BUILD-REUSESET1's root layer). Later wins:

1. **stock**: Jet's defaults and the stock profiles;
2. **project**: `project.jet`, including the profile selected by `--profile` or `defaults:`;
3. **package**: source markers, then `package.jet`, then `build.jet`, for that package's outputs. Inside this layer an output's own `options:` beat package-wide values (D-SETTING-ORDER1);
4. **deployment**: environment, system and fleet layers, for Image, System and Fleet outputs only (D-CONF-MERGE1);
5. **flag**: the command line.

Two rules sit across the list:

- **Pin.** `b.pin(...)`, a `pin:` in `package.jet`, or a `pin:` in `project.jet` policy fixes a value. Any other layer that sets a different value is an error naming both lines (D-JAI-BUILDOPT1). A package pins what its output cannot work without; a project pins what the team requires.
- **Forbid.** `project.jet` `policy: { forbid: [...] }` names options or effects that no layer in the project may set. The error names the policy line (the owner's build-options ruling: project or package policy can forbid any option).

Why the project sits under the package: the project sets the team's defaults and profiles, and a package's stated need for one of its outputs must not be overridden silently by a team default. When the project must win, it pins, and the conflict becomes a visible error instead of a silent override. This is D-BUILD-REUSESET1's order, with the profile moved into the project.

`jet explain setting optimize --output app` prints every layer that set the value, with file and line.

## 5. Composition: primitives first, wrappers on top

The owner's rule for every API applies here first: a strong set of primitives that can express everything, then high-quality wrappers for the common cases. In config this means:

### 5.1 One set of values

Data files and entry code build the same Core values, so a fact moves between them unchanged:

| Value | Written in data as | Made in code by |
|---|---|---|
| `Output` (nine kinds) | `outputs: { app: .Executable{ entry: run } }` | `b.add(.Executable{ name: "app", entry: run })` |
| `BuildOptions` | `profiles: { release: BuildOptions{ optimize: full } }` | `b.options()`, `b.profile("release")` |
| `TestProfile` | `profiles: { quick: TestProfile{ suites: [tests] } }` | `t.profile("quick")` |
| `Environment` | `environments: { dev: Environment{ tools: ["git"] } }` | (data only; `jet env` never runs code) |
| `BuildAction` | `options: { link: wasm.link }` (a function that returns one) | `b.action("stamp", run: [...], inputs: [...], outputs: [...])` |
| `Generated` | — | `b.generate("table") { ... }` (D-BUILD-GENVALUE1) |

### 5.2 The primitives

- `b.add(outputs: ...Output) -> [Output]`: add any outputs. A library can return `Output` values from ordinary functions and the caller adds them: `b.add(...web.targets("game", "editor"))`. This is the call every `add_*` wrapper reduces to.
- `b.output(name) -> &Output`: change a data-made or code-made output until the plan is sealed (D-TARGET-ONE1, D-JAI-CONFIG1).
- `b.action(name, *, run:, inputs:, outputs:, allow:, …)` → `BuildAction`: every field of a declared build action, by label (D-BUILD-CORE1, D-BUILDACTION1).
- `b.generate(name) { … }` → `Generated`: the generated code as a value. It can be passed anywhere a source is, so nobody types `.jet/generated/...` paths again.
- `b.pin(...)` and the generated setting methods, one per option row (D-SETTING-ORDER1).

### 5.3 The wrappers

Each wrapper is an ordinary Core function whose body is one primitive call. It has no power the primitive lacks, and its doc comment shows the expansion. `jet explain` prints it.

```jet
// Core/Build: a wrapper is one line over the primitive
fn add_executable(b: &Build, name: String, sources: ...Source, *,
                  deps: [Package]{[]}, options: BuildOptions{}, entry: Entry?{None}) -> Output BuildError! {
    b.add(.Executable{ name: name, sources: sources, deps: deps, options: options, entry: entry })[0]
}
```

The data files are the zero-code wrapper: an `outputs:` entry is the literal form of the value `b.add` takes. The stock defaults are the zero-file wrapper: no `package.jet` means `run.jet` is the program.

### 5.4 Argument shape rules for config and build APIs

These follow Jet's call rules (S61, D-CALLPOS1, D-VARIADIC1) and use them on purpose:

1. **What every call needs is positional:** the name, then the main input.
2. **A list you would type inline is a variadic tail:** sources, command arguments, suites. `b.add_executable("app", "run.jet", "util.jet")`, not `["run.jet", "util.jet"]`. Spread passes an existing list: `b.add_executable("app", ...find("src/**/*.jet"))`.
3. **Every option is label-only with a default:** `deps:`, `options:`, `entry:`, `link:`. Callers never count positions.
4. **No arity families.** One signature per method, never "5 or 7 to 15 positional arguments".
5. **A wrapper is one primitive call** (5.3).

Today the build handle breaks all five. The checker rejects every label with E0764 "`Build.{method}` takes positional arguments … the build method contract does not declare labels or variadic slots" (`Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/Build.jet:148`). `b.action` takes "5 or 7 to 15" positional arguments, and `add_*` takes "3 to 7" (`Build.jet:94-96`). D-BUILD-CORE1 already ratified labels; this section adds the variadic tail and the primitive.

Rule 2 needs one small language change. Jet requires a variadic parameter to be last (E1310), and a variadic after `*` becomes label-only. So `fn f(name: String, sources: ...String, *, deps: [String]{[]})` is E1310 today, and `fn g(name: String, *, deps: [String]{[]}, sources: ...String)` makes the call `g("app", "run.jet", deps: ["core"])` an E0769 (probed on dev; section 12). Python ([PEP 3102](https://peps.python.org/pep-3102/)), Swift ([Functions: variadic parameters](https://docs.swift.org/swift-book/documentation/the-swift-programming-language/functions/#Variadic-Parameters)) and Kotlin ([vararg](https://kotlinlang.org/docs/functions.html#variable-number-of-arguments-varargs)) all allow named parameters after a variadic one. Ballot D-CALL-VARTAIL1 asks whether label-only parameters may follow a variadic tail.

## 6. Before and after: four real projects

### 6.1 Hello

Before (`jet new hello` today, `Host.jet:1529-1531,1607,1618`):

```text
hello/package.jet   name, version, jet, description: "", license, repository: "",
                    authority: { allow: [IO, Mem.Alloc] }, deps: {}
hello/run.jet       fn run() { print("hello") }
hello/.jet/lock     written, and git-ignored by .gitignore
hello/.gitignore    .jet/build/  .jet/lock  .jet/cache/
```

After:

```text
hello/package.jet   name: "hello"
                    version: "0.1.0"
                    authority: { allow: [IO] }
hello/run.jet       fn run() { print("hello") }
hello/jet.lock      written by Jet, committed (D-LOCKFILE1)
hello/.gitignore    .jet/
```

No `project.jet`: the package folder is the project. Smaller still, `hello.jet` alone runs with `jet run hello.jet`. Changes: the lock is committed at the root, as ratified; empty placeholder fields are not written.

### 6.2 A library with tests

Before (D-TEST-PROFILE1's ratified shape, which today's parser rejects with E1206):

```jet
// textkit/package.jet
name: "textkit"
version: "0.3.0"
edition: "2026"
license: "MIT"
deps: { unicode: { git: "https://example.com/unicode", tag: "v1.2.0" } }
outputs: { textkit: .Library{ entry: textkit } }
build: { release: Build{ optimize: full } }
test: {
    quick: TestProfile{ suites: [tests], time_limit: 60s }
    full: TestProfile{ suites: [tests, golden], optimize: [none, full] }
}
suites: { golden: TestSuite{ golden_corpus: "tests/golden" } }
defaults: { test: quick }

// textkit/test.jet
fn test(t: Test) {
    t.suite("fuzz", fuzz_driver(seed: 7))
    t.run()
}
```

After:

```jet
// textkit/package.jet: what textkit is, needs and makes
name: "textkit"
version: "0.3.0"
edition: "2026"
license: "MIT"
deps: { unicode: { git: "https://example.com/unicode", tag: "v1.2.0" } }
outputs: { textkit: .Library{ entry: textkit } }
suites: { golden: TestSuite{ golden_corpus: "tests/golden" } }

// textkit/project.jet: how this team builds and tests it
profiles: {
    release: BuildOptions{ optimize: full }
    quick: TestProfile{ suites: [tests], time_limit: 60s }
    full: TestProfile{ suites: [tests, golden, fuzz], optimize: [none, full] }
}
defaults: { test: quick }

// textkit/test.jet: only the suite that needs code
fn test(t: Test) {
    t.suite("fuzz", fuzz_driver(seed: 7))
    t.run()
}
```

What a consumer of `textkit` sees is now exactly `package.jet`. The profiles stop looking like part of the library. `Build{ … }` becomes `BuildOptions{ … }` (D-ENTRY-NAMES1). A team that never customizes profiles has no `project.jet`.

### 6.3 A multi-package project: the Jet compiler

Before:

```jet
// env.jet (repo root): two of its environments
module env.compiler {
    sources: { default: NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable@github }
    packages: [ default.[ cargo, rustc, gcc, clang, lld, git, ripgrep, … ] ]
    prompt: "jet-compiler"
}

// Compiler/package.jet: a package named "compiler" that is also the root of 13 others
name: "compiler"
version: "0.0.1"
edition: "2026"
members: [ "JetFoundation", "JetLexer", …, "JetCli" ]

// Compiler/build.jet: makes the jet executable out of another package's file
fn build(b: Build) {
    jet :: b.add_executable("jet", ["JetCli/run.jet"], [])
    b.default(jet)
}

// Compiler/JetCli/package.jet
name: "jet_cli"
version: "0.0.1"
edition: "2026"
deps: { jet_foundation: ../JetFoundation, … }
authority: { allow: [Env, Exec, …] }
```

After:

```jet
// project.jet (repo root): the repo is the project
packages: [
    ...find("Compiler/*"),
    ...find("Jetpack/*"),
]
version: "0.0.1"
edition: "2026"
environments: {
    compiler: Environment{
        sources: { default: NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable@github }
        tools: [ default.[ cargo, rustc, gcc, clang, lld, git, ripgrep, … ] ]
        prompt: "jet-compiler"
    }
}

// Compiler/JetCli/package.jet: the package that owns the code owns the output
name: "jet_cli"
deps: { jet_foundation: ../JetFoundation, … }
outputs: { jet: .Executable{ entry: run } }
authority: { allow: [Env, Exec, …] }
```

`env.jet`, `Compiler/package.jet` and `Compiler/build.jet` are gone. `jet build` at the root builds every package; `jet build jet` builds the one output; `jet run jet -- --version` runs it. Members take `version` and `edition` from the project. The package named "compiler", which had no code of its own, no longer exists. That ends the case where a named root silently skips its own code (bug B1, section 12).

### 6.4 A project with build-time code generation

Before (`Examples/features/tooling/build_write_generated`):

```jet
// package.jet
name: "build_write_generated_example"
version: "0.1.0"
edition: "2026"
build: {
    inspect: Build{ write_generated: on },
}

// build.jet
fn build(b: Build) {
    b.generate("table") {
        fn table_size() -> Int { 5 }
    }
    app :: b.add_executable("run", ["run.jet", ".jet/generated/build_write_generated_example/table.jet"], [])
    b.default(app)
}
```

After:

```jet
// package.jet
name: "build_write_generated_example"
version: "0.1.0"
edition: "2026"

// project.jet
profiles: { inspect: BuildOptions{ write_generated: on } }

// build.jet
fn build(b: Build) {
    table :: b.generate("table") {
        fn table_size() -> Int { 5 }
    }
    app :: b.add_executable("run", "run.jet", table)
    b.default(app)
}

// The same build written with the primitive only:
fn build(b: Build) {
    table :: b.generate("table") {
        fn table_size() -> Int { 5 }
    }
    b.default(b.add(.Executable{ name: "run", sources: ["run.jet", table] })[0])
}
```

The generated code is a value, so the build no longer names a path inside `.jet/`, and the cache layout can change without breaking it. The trailing `[]` (an empty positional action list) is gone. The two spellings build the identical plan; `jet inspect build` cannot tell them apart.

## 7. Custom link and post-link steps (#5009)

D-JAI-EVENTS1=A (2026-10-17) added the stages `build.link(LinkInputs) -> Artifact`, `build.before_write(Artifact) -> replacement` and `build.after_write(Artifact) -> findings`, run as build actions. The owner asked for a ballot on whether a typed build action may replace one output's link step and post-process the written file. In this model the answer fits in three pieces:

1. **The hook returns a typed action; Jet runs it.** A `#On(build.link)` function receives `LinkInputs`: the object files, libraries, link arguments, the output path, and `default`, the exact `BuildAction` Jet would run. It returns a `BuildAction` (D-BUILDACTION1): a declared command with inputs, outputs and `Exec`/`FS` capabilities. Jet runs it in place of its own link step, checks that it wrote the declared file, and records it. A `#On(build.before_write)` function returns a `BuildAction` that turns the linked file into the final one (strip, compress, patch). `#On(build.after_write)` stays read-only and returns findings. Hooks never write files themselves, so every byte that reaches the output came from a declared, cached, recorded action.
2. **Which outputs use it is an option row.** `link: default | <hook>` and `post_link: [<hook>, …]` are rows of the one option table, so each has a flag (`--link=default`), a `package.jet` field (an output's `options:`), a `project.jet` profile field and a handle method (`b.output("game").link(wasm.link)`). Owner directive #4913 holds: no option without all three. Experts get full control: `LinkInputs.default` is the stock command, so a hook can edit one argument and keep everything else.
3. **Policy and audit.** `project.jet` or `package.jet` `policy: { forbid: [link, post_link] }` refuses both. A dependency's hook is held until `jet trust grant package-hook:<package>#<version>` records an exact grant in `policy.trust`, the grant every dependency hook already needs (D-HOOK-STAGES1, D-JPK-BUILDSCRIPT1). `jet inspect build` shows, per output, the link action's argv, its capabilities, and the line that chose it. A failed or missing link output is one registered build diagnostic naming the output, the hook and the setting line.

**Binary size (D-SIZE-PAYUSE1).** Hooks run at build time and nothing is linked into the program, so a program that does not use them is byte-for-byte unchanged. `LinkInputs.default` is the stock link command with all of Jet's link arguments, so a hook that edits one argument keeps the rest, including the ones that keep the file small. The build record reports the artifact size after the last post-link step, so size reports measure the file that actually ships.

```jet
// wasmtools/link.jet: a hook package
#On(build.link)
fn link(i: build.LinkInputs) -> BuildAction {
    build.action("wasm-ld",
        run: ["wasm-ld", "--no-entry", "--export-all", ...i.objects, "-o", i.output],
        inputs: i.objects,
        outputs: [i.output],
        allow: [.Exec])
}

#On(build.before_write)
fn optimize(a: build.Artifact) -> BuildAction {
    build.action("wasm-opt", run: ["wasm-opt", "-Oz", a.path, "-o", a.next], inputs: [a.path], outputs: [a.next], allow: [.Exec])
}

// game/package.jet: only the web output links with wasm-ld
outputs: {
    game_web: .Executable{ entry: run, options: { os: web, link: wasmtools.link, post_link: [wasmtools.optimize] } }
}

// a dependency's hook is held until granted once, recorded in policy.trust
$ jet trust grant package-hook:wasmtools#0.3
```

Ballot D-LINK-STEP1 has the options and the same program under each.

## 8. Words

- **project**: the folder you work in (section 1). It replaces "workspace" in the package system, in CLI help and diagnostics, and in Canvas's `"mode": "workspace"` (`Docs/spec/reference/canvas-workspace-architecture.md`).
- **workspace**: only its Jai meaning, one compilation with its own build options (`compiler_create_workspace`). In Jet that is one output built under one set of options (D-JAI-CONFIG1). No file, field or flag uses the word.
- **Jetspace** (D-ECO-ROOTNAME2=D) retires: "the project" names the checked graph of a project's packages.
- **packages:** is the `project.jet` field that lists packages (it replaces `members:`). The old `package.jet` `packages:` map of output kinds folds into `outputs:`.
- **profile**: a named `BuildOptions` or `TestProfile`, written only in `project.jet` `profiles:`. A platform preset in `targets:` says `platform:`, not `profile:`.
- **build**: the command, the `Build` handle and `build.jet`. The `build:` field retires (profiles moved), and so does `Build{ … }` as a record (D-ENTRY-NAMES1).
- **target**: the platform only (D-TARGET-ONE1).

Ballot D-PROJECT-WORDS1 settles the words that follow from the rename.

## 9. Migration and the `jet fix` story

Counts are `git ls-files` at `e784bb1ffe`.

| Today | After | Files | `jet fix` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace.jet` (`module workspace { members: X }`, overlays) | `project.jet` (`packages: X`, `overlays:`) | 22 | rename and reshape; a `fn` inside moves to its package's `build.jet`/`run.jet` |
| `env.jet` (`module env.<n> { packages: … }`) | `project.jet` `environments: { <n>: Environment{ tools: … } }` | 159 | merge; 154 sit where no `package.jet` exists and become `project.jet` files, not nameless packages |
| `members:` in `package.jet` | `project.jet` `packages:` | 5 | move; a named root with no code of its own is deleted after its outputs move to the package that owns the code |
| `build:` profiles in `package.jet` (35) and inline blocks (3) | `project.jet` `profiles:`; `build: { allow: }` → `authority: { build: }` | 38 | move; `Build{}` → `BuildOptions{}` |
| profile keys of `defaults:` | `project.jet` `defaults:` | ≤ 18 | split by key |
| `packages:` output map in `package.jet` | `outputs:` | 80 | rewrite each entry as an output value |
| `config.jet`, `configs:` files, `Config{}` records | the field's home in `package.jet` or `project.jet` | 32 + 5 | inline by field |
| `fn build`/`fn test`/`fn dev` outside its home, in a package with `package.jet` | `build.jet` / `test.jet` / `dev.jet` | 38 (21 in `run.jet`, 8 in `main.jet`, 3 in `package.jet`, 2 in `tools/build_entry.jet`, 4 others) | move the function; same package, so names still resolve |
| committed `.jet/lock` | `jet.lock` | 22 | move; `.gitignore` becomes `.jet/` |
| `pkg.jet` | `package.jet` | 5 | rename (already retired) |
| `jet new` templates and stubs | the new shapes | code | rewrite (`Host.jet:1513-1531`) |

Total: about 420 files, almost all fixtures under `tests/` and `Examples/`. Core's 604 inline `package { }` blocks are unchanged except 3 with `build:` and 3 with `configs:`. The 29 entry functions already in their home and the 104 in one-file programs do not move.

`jet fix` is mechanical for every row: each rewrite moves text between files without changing its meaning, and `jet fix --dry-run` prints the moves. After the cutover, every old spelling is a registered error that names its new home and the fix, for example: "`members:` belongs in project.jet as `packages:`. Run `jet fix`." There are no aliases and no fallback reads (clean cutover).
