## Morning report, 2026-10-04 09:00

### Stage 1: jetc0 now compiles the whole compiler

- **08:56: first complete L5 compile.** cand33f's jetc0 compiled the whole Jet compiler with zero errors in every phase and wrote out.rs (181 MB) plus the compiler image (111 MB). The pinned inputs match jetc0's own compiler unit (compiler_unit=same).
- **Classes fixed overnight:** R1/R2 (rustc), C1/C2 (lower), C3 (assemble), E1/E2 (emit), O1/O2 (optimize), M1 (MIR lint), P1/P2 (packaging), plus the lower-start out-of-memory. Also J1, RC1 and RC2 (below).
- **Found ahead of the chain** by three probes running alongside it:
  - **J1:** jetc1 would have failed while loading its image. Fixed in 0477acbf2; 3 jet-jit interface tests pass.
  - **RC1/RC2:** two rustc classes at L3 (E0499 ×14, E0502 ×1). Fixed in 779f82b45; isocheck rc=0.
  - **Runtime:** the Jet-compiled lexer and parser gave byte-identical output to the Rust-compiled ones on all 748 inputs.
  - **R2 (performance):** a dead deep copy on every forwarded `&` parameter makes the Jet-compiled parser quadratic. Stage 1 doesn't need it fixed; stage 2 does. FixR2Perf is working on it.
- **Now:** cand34f carries every fix and builds from about 08:57. L5 plus rustc should finish around 09:35, and the self-check (jetc1 compiles hello) around 09:50. RustcProbe is meanwhile running rustc across all of cand33f's L5 unit crates, to catch any L5-only rustc class first.
- **Stage 2:** the plan is ready (STAGE2-PLAN.md: fixedpoint --stages 3, about 1h20 to 2h20) and starts automatically after the self-check. The determinism audit found no nondeterminism. It needs R2 fixed to finish in a reasonable time.

### Your rulings handled overnight

- **One function arrow:** card #4512 (already D-SIG-AFTER1=A). The cutover is on branch fix/one-arrow (parser E0080, formatter, about 290 call sites) and its tests are running. It lands after the stage-2 inputs are pinned.
- **D-TERM-INCREMENTAL1:** your question is answered. Escape waits 0 ms on modern terminals (kitty keyboard protocol), 10 ms on older ones, and only when a lone Escape is the last byte available.
- **D-SIMD-NATIVE1:** your question is answered. Option A gives automatic safe vectorization by default and explicit expert opt-ins (exact widths, #Multiversion + core.arch, --cpu, #FFI(asm)), plus two new declinable spellings. It passed a beginner review and an adversarial review.
- **CoreLib/Prelude:** 1:1 port first, then an idiom pass, starting after stage 2. Native-floor and allocator ballots are queued for after stage 2, Zig-style (cross compile to every target from any host).

### Port

- The compiler 1:1 loop continues on port/compiler (savepoint a3b4fbea8), with about 8 writers.

### Waiting on you

- Decide the posted ballots (briefing "Ballots are ready to decide").
- Decide whether ~/.jet and ~/.local/share/jet move.

goals.title: Speed and size
goals.body:
The performance gate passes against every peer and the machine ceiling: measurement gate and dashboards, self-compile memory and time, codegen equal to hand-written assembly, and the smallest binaries (see G4, G10 and G12). Owner order 2026-11-08: G1, G4, G8, G6, G3, then G5, G7, G9, G10, G11 and G12 in their earlier order; this goal is tenth.

Merged from G4 (Self-compile in about 50 ms): The compiler checks and builds itself in about 50 ms, through per-phase throughput targets toward 500k lines per second.

Merged from G10 (Codegen beats C): Native codegen emits near-perfect machine code and beats C on every required perf cell (Jet/C < 1.00; Jet/Rust <= 1.05 on the same run) at --release, with identical output and one meaning on every tier. Exploit what C can't assume: no aliasing between distinct values, sema-proven bounds and loop facts, whole-program compilation, comptime specialization, automatic layout and per-chip builds. Epic card #6205; streams #3039 C6, #6201, #6203. Owner direction 2026-10-29.

Merged from G12 (Smallest binaries: every program within 1.5-2x of hand-written assembly): Owner order 2026-10-30. Jet default builds produce the smallest output of any language, for every program, by design: each program is within 1.5-2x (target 1.5x, hard bound 2x) of an optimized hand-written x86-64 assembly reference with the same behavior. The runtime is pay-for-what-you-use: the program reference graph alone decides what is linked, with lazy subsystem start, no unconditional startup, no unwind tables the runtime never uses, and symbols in a sidecar. Hello targets 504 B (floor 253 B). Plan: Docs/proposals/hello-size-architecture-2026-10-30.md.
